01Chapter 1 · Introduction to Building AI Applications with Foundation Models

Introduction to Building AI Applications

2020 ke baad AI ko ek hi shabd me describe karna ho to woh hai — scale. ChatGPT, Gemini aur Midjourney ke peeche jo models hain, woh itne bade hain ki duniya ki bijli ka ek bada hissa kha rahe hain, aur lagta hai ki internet ka publicly available data bhi khatam hone wala hai. Is scale ke do bade nateeje hue, aur wahi is book ki kahani hai.

Scale ke do nateeje

  • Models zyada powerful ho gaye: AI ab zyada kaam kar sakta hai, isliye naye applications ban rahe hain. Log aur teams AI se productivity badha rahe hain, economic value bana rahe hain aur quality of life improve kar rahe hain.
  • Training sirf kuch organizations kar sakti hain: bade language models ko train karne ke liye data, compute aur specialized talent chahiye — jo sirf kuch organizations afford kar sakti hain. Isliye model as a service aaya: ye organizations apne models ko service ke roop me deti hain, aur koi bhi unhe use karke application bana sakta hai, bina model banane me upfront invest kiye.

Short me: AI applications ki demand badh gayi, aur unhe banane ka entry barrier kam ho gaya. Isi liye AI engineering — readily available models ke upar applications banane ka process — sabse tezi se badhne wali engineering discipline ban gayi hai.

AI applications naye nahi hain

ML models ke upar applications banana naya nahi hai. LLMs ke mashhoor hone se bahut pehle bhi AI applications chala raha tha — product recommendations, fraud detection, churn prediction jaise kaam. Production me AI le jaane ke bahut se principles wahi hain. Lekin bade, readily available models nayi possibilities aur nayi challenges laate hain — wahi is book ka focus hai.

Is chapter me kya hai?

  • Pehle foundation models ka overview — AI engineering ke peeche ka key catalyst.
  • Phir successful AI use cases ki range — har ek batata hai ki AI kis me achha hai aur kis me abhi nahi.
  • Aakhir me AI stack ka overview — foundation models ke saath kya badla, kya wahi raha, aur aaj ke AI engineer ka role traditional ML engineer se kaise alag hai.

Book ka approach fundamentals par hai, kisi ek tool ya API par nahi — tools jaldi outdated ho jaate hain, fundamentals zyada tikte hain. Ye book tutorial bhi nahi hai aur ML theory book bhi nahi: iska kaam hai real-world problems solve karne ke liye foundation models ko adapt karne ka framework dena.

Yaad rakho: AI engineering ka matlab model banana nahi hai — matlab hai kisi aur ke banaye hue powerful model ko apne kaam ke liye adapt karna. Yahi ek shift poori book ko chalata hai.
SOURCESource: Huyen, AI Engineering, O'Reilly, Chapter 1 — Introduction to Building AI Applications with Foundation Models

01.1Chapter 1 · Introduction to Building AI Applications with Foundation Models

LM se LLM, Foundation Models, AI Engineering tak

ChatGPT aur GitHub Copilot achanak nahi aaye — ye dashakon ki technology advancements ka nateeja hain. Pehle language models 1950s me aaye, phir self-supervision ne unhe bada banaya (LLM), phir unme aur modalities judi (foundation models), aur phir unke upar applications banane ka kaam ek discipline ban gaya (AI engineering).

Language model kya hai?

Language model ek ya zyada languages ke baare me statistical information encode karta hai — matlab, kisi context me kaunsa shabd aane ki kitni sambhavna hai. Example: context "My favorite color is __" ho to model "blue" ko "car" se zyada likely bolega.

Languages ki statistical nature sadiyon se jaani jaati hai. 1905 ki Sherlock Holmes kahani "The Adventure of the Dancing Men" me Holmes ne English ke statistics se code toda tha — English me sabse common letter E hai, to sabse common stick figure E hi hoga. Baad me Claude Shannon ne Second World War me dushman ke messages decode karne ke liye statistics use kiye, aur unka 1951 ka landmark paper "Prediction and Entropy of Printed English" aaj bhi language modeling ki buniyaad hai — entropy jaise concepts wahi se aaye.

Token aur tokenization

Language model ki basic unit hai token. Token character bhi ho sakta hai, word bhi, ya word ka hissa bhi (jaise -tion). GPT-4 phrase "I can't wait to build AI applications" ko 9 tokens me todta hai — "can't" do tokens banta hai: can aur 't.

  • Text ko tokens me todne ko tokenization kehte hain. GPT-4 me ek average token lagbhag 3/4 word ke barabar hota hai — 100 tokens lagbhag 75 words.
  • Model jitne tokens ke saath kaam kar sakta hai, woh uska vocabulary hai. Mixtral 8x7B ka vocabulary 32,000 hai, GPT-4 ka 100,256. Tokenization method aur vocabulary size model developers tay karte hain.
  • Non-English languages me ek Unicode character kabhi-kabhi multiple tokens ban jaata hai.

Token hi kyun, word ya character kyun nahi?

  1. Meaningful components: character se behtar — "cooking" ko "cook" + "ing" me tod sakte ho, dono ka matlab banta hai.
  2. Chhota vocabulary: unique tokens unique words se kam hote hain, isliye model zyada efficient hota hai.
  3. Unknown words: bana hua word jaise "chatgpting" ko "chatgpt" + "ing" me tod kar model uski structure samajh sakta hai.

Tokens words se kam units aur characters se zyada meaning ka balance hain.

Do tarah ke language models

Masked language model: sequence me kahin bhi missing tokens predict karta hai, aage aur peeche dono taraf ka context use karke — jaise fill in the blank. Example: "My favorite __ is blue" me blank likely "color" hai. Famous example BERT (Devlin et al., 2018). Aaj ye non-generative tasks — sentiment analysis, text classification, code debugging — me use hote hain, jahan poora context samajhna zaroori hai.

Autoregressive language model: sirf pehle wale tokens se next token predict karta hai, aur ek ke baad ek token generate karke lambi text bana sakta hai. Aaj text generation ke liye yehi models pasand kiye jaate hain — masked models se bahut zyada popular hain. Is book me jab tak alag se na kaha jaye, "language model" ka matlab autoregressive model hi hai.

Completion machine aur generative AI

Language model ke outputs open-ended hote hain — fixed, finite vocabulary se infinite possible outputs ban sakte hain. Isi liye inhe generative kehte hain, aur yahi generative AI hai.

Language model ko completion machine samjho: text (prompt) do, woh use complete karne ki koshish karta hai. Prompt "To be or not to be" ho to completion ", that is the question." ho sakti hai. Completions predictions hain, probabilities par based — sahi hone ki guarantee nahi. Yahi probabilistic nature inhe exciting bhi banati hai aur frustrating bhi (Chapter 2 me detail).

Completion simple lagta hai, par bahut powerful hai. Translation, summarization, coding, math problems — bahut se tasks completion ki tarah frame kiye ja sakte hain. Prompt "How are you in French is …" ka completion "Comment ça va" ho to woh translation ban gaya. Aur prompt "Question: Is this email likely spam? … Answer:" ka completion "Likely spam" ho to wohi model spam classifier ban gaya.

Lekin completion conversation nahi hai — sawaal poochho to model jawab dene ke bajaye ek aur sawaal jod sakta hai. Model ko user ki request par sahi tareeke se respond karwana post-training ka kaam hai (Chapter 2).

Self-supervision — scale ka raaz

Language models ko center me kis cheez ne laaya? Self-supervision. Bahut se models ko supervision chahiye hoti hai — labeled data, jo mehenga aur slow hota hai. AlexNet (2012) supervised tha: ImageNet ke 1 million+ images, 1,000 categories me classify karna. Labeling ka kharch dekho: ek image label karne me 5 cents lage to 1 million images ke $50,000; do logon se cross-check karvao to double; 1 million categories tak badhao to $50 million. Aur cancer wale CT scan jaise labels to astronomical mehenga hota hai.

Self-supervision me model labels input data se hi infer kar leta hai. Language modeling self-supervised hai kyunki har input sequence labels bhi deta hai aur context bhi. Sentence "I love street food." se 6 training samples bante hain — har baar agla token predict karna hai, context pehle wale tokens hain. <BOS> aur <EOS> sequence ki shuruaat aur ant mark karte hain; <EOS> khaas taur par zaroori hai taaki model ko pata chale kab rukna hai.

Yaad rakho: self-supervised learning unsupervised learning se alag hai — self-supervised me labels input se infer hote hain, unsupervised me labels ki zaroorat hi nahi hoti.

Text sequences har jagah hain — books, blog posts, articles, Reddit comments — isliye massive training data banana possible hua, aur language models scale karke LLM ban gaye. "Large" koi scientific term nahi hai: model ka size uske parameters se naapa jaata hai (training me update hone wale variables). GPT (June 2018) 117 million parameters ke saath "large" tha; GPT-2 (Feb 2019) 1.5 billion ke saath aaya to 117 million "small" ho gaya; book likhte waqt 100 billion parameters "large" mana jaata hai.

Bade models ko zyada data kyun chahiye? Unki capacity zyada hoti hai, to performance maximize karne ke liye zyada training data chahiye. Bade model ko chhote dataset par train karna compute ki barbaadi hai — wahi ya behtar result chhote model se mil jaata.

LLM se foundation models tak

Language models sirf text tak limited the. Hum duniya ko sirf bhasha se nahi, vision, hearing, touch se bhi samajhte hain — real world me kaam karne ke liye aur modalities zaroori hain. GPT-4V aur Claude 3 images aur text dono samajhte hain; kuch models video, 3D assets, protein structures bhi samajhte hain. OpenAI ne GPT-4V system card (2023) me kaha tha ki image inputs jaisi modalities jodna AI research ka key frontier hai.

Jo model ek se zyada modality ke saath kaam kare, woh multimodal model hai; generative multimodal model ko large multimodal model (LMM) kehte hain. Language model next token sirf text tokens se predict karta hai; multimodal model text + image tokens dono se. Pehle AI research modalities se bata hua tha — NLP sirf text, computer vision sirf vision. Foundation models ne ye deewaar todi.

Multimodal models ko bhi scale ke liye data chahiye, aur self-supervision wahan bhi kaam karti hai. OpenAI ne CLIP (2021) ko natural language supervision se train kiya: internet par co-occur karne wale (image, text) pairs dhoondhe aur bina manual labeling ke 400 million pairs ka dataset banaya — ImageNet se 400x bada. CLIP generative nahi hai — ye embedding model hai, text aur image ke joint embeddings banata hai (embeddings Chapter 3 me detail me).

Foundation models ek aur shift laaye: task-specific se general-purpose tak. Pehle sentiment analysis wala model translation nahi kar sakta tha. Foundation models scale aur training ki wajah se bahut se tasks kar lete hain — Super-NaturalInstructions benchmark ke tasks ki range iska saboot hai. Out-of-the-box model bahut se tasks me decent hai, aur use specific task ke liye tweak bhi kiya ja sakta hai.

Example: retailer ke liye product descriptions generate karni hain. Out-of-the-box model accurate description de sakta hai par brand ki voice pakad na paye, marketing clichés bhar de. Teen tareeke hain use adapt karne ke: prompt engineering (detailed instructions + desirable descriptions ke examples), RAG (customer reviews ka database jod do), ya finetuning (high-quality descriptions par aur train karo). Teeno poori book me detail me aayenge.

Existing powerful model ko adapt karna scratch se model banana se bahut aasan hai — jaise 10 examples aur ek weekend vs 1 million examples aur 6 mahine. Kitna data chahiye, ye technique par depend karta hai. Lekin task-specific models ke bhi fayde hain — woh chhote hote hain, isliye faster aur cheaper. Buy-or-build ka faisla har team ko khud karna hai.

Foundation models se AI engineering tak — 3 factors

Factor 1: General-purpose AI capabilities. Foundation models sirf purane tasks behtar nahi karte — woh naye tasks kar sakte hain jo pehle impossible lagte the. AI ab likh sakta hai — kabhi-kabhi insaan se behtar — to communication wala har kaam automate ya partially automate ho sakta hai: emails, customer requests, contracts samjhana. Koi bhi computer wala instant customized images/videos bana sakta hai — marketing, headshots, book illustrations. AI training data synthesize kar sakta hai, algorithms bana sakta hai, code likh sakta hai — jo aage aur powerful models train karne me madad karega.

Factor 2: Increased AI investments. ChatGPT ki success ke baad VC aur enterprise investment tezi se badha. AI applications saste aur jaldi market me aane lage to ROI attractive hua. Matt Ross (Scribd) ke hisaab se unke use cases ki AI cost April 2022 se April 2023 me do orders of magnitude gir gayi. Goldman Sachs ka estimate: 2025 tak US me $100 billion aur globally $200 billion AI investment. FactSet: Q2 2023 me S&P 500 ki ek me se ek company ne earnings call me AI mention kiya — pichhle saal se 3x. WallStreetZen: AI mention karne wali companies ke stock me average 4.6% badhotri, baaki me 2.4% — causation hai ya correlation, ye unclear hai.

Factor 3: Low entrance barrier. OpenAI aur dusre providers ne model as a service popular kiya: models APIs ke through milte hain, ek API call me powerful model. Bina API ke model host aur serve karne ka infrastructure chahiye hota. Upar se AI khud code likh deta hai, aur models se plain English me kaam hota hai, programming language me nahi — ab koi bhi AI application bana sakta hai, bina ek line code likhe bhi.

Foundation models banana sirf bade corporations (Google, Meta, Microsoft, Baidu, Tencent), governments (Japan, UAE) aur well-funded startups (OpenAI, Anthropic, Mistral) ke bas ka hai. Sam Altman (Sept 2022) ne kaha tha ki zyadaatar logon ke liye sabse bada opportunity hai in models ko specific applications ke liye adapt karna.

Growth ke numbers hairan karne wale hain: sirf 2 saalon me 4 open-source AI engineering tools (AutoGPT, Stable Diffusion web UI, LangChain, Ollama) ne GitHub stars me Bitcoin ko peeche chhod diya, aur React aur Vue jaise popular web frameworks ko bhi peeche chhodne ke raaste par hain. LinkedIn survey (Aug 2023): "Generative AI", "ChatGPT", "Prompt Engineering" jaise terms profile me add karne walon ki sankhya har mahine average 75% badhi. ComputerWorld ne kaha — "teaching AI to behave is the fastest-growing career skill".

"AI Engineering" naam kyun?

  • ML engineering kyun nahi? Foundation models ke saath kaam traditional ML models se kaafi alag hai (page 39 par detail) — ML engineering ye difference capture nahi karta. Lekin ML engineering dono processes ko cover karne ke liye achha umbrella term hai.
  • *Ops wale terms kyun nahi? (MLOps, AIOps, LLMOps) — operational components to hain, par focus zyada engineering/tweaking par hai: foundation model ko woh karvana jo tum chahte ho.
  • Author ne 20 logon se survey kiya jo foundation models par applications bana rahe the — zyadaatar ne AI engineering pasand kiya. Isliye book ne logon ki pasand chuni.
Yaad rakho: language model → self-supervision se LLM → modalities judkar foundation model → unke upar applications banane se AI engineering. Har step me scale aur accessibility badhi, aur barrier gira.
SOURCESource: Huyen, AI Engineering, O'Reilly, Chapter 1 — Introduction to Building AI Applications with Foundation Models

01.2Chapter 1 · Introduction to Building AI Applications with Foundation Models

Foundation Model Use Cases

Foundation models se kya-kya ban sakta hai, ye list karna impossible hai — theresanaiforthat.com par Sept 2024 tak 14,688 tasks ke liye 16,814 AIs listed the. Author ne use cases samajhne ke liye 50 companies se interview kiye, 100+ case studies padhe, aur 205 open-source AI applications (GitHub par kam se kam 500 stars) examine kiye — aur unhe 8 categories me baanta.

Use cases categorize karna hi mushkil hai

Har survey alag categorization use karta hai. AWS ne enterprise generative AI use cases ko 3 buckets me baanta: customer experience, employee productivity, process optimization. 2024 O'Reilly survey me 8 categories theen: programming, data analysis, customer support, marketing copy, other copy, research, web design, art. Deloitte ne value capture se categorize kiya: cost reduction, process efficiency, growth, accelerating innovation. Gartner ka ek category hai business continuity — organization AI adopt na kare to business se bahar ho jaye; 2023 me survey kiye 2,500 executives me se 7% ne yehi motivation bataya.

Kaun se occupations AI se sabse zyada exposed hain?

Eloundou et al. (2023) ne ek task ko exposed mana agar AI uska time kam se kam 50% kam kar de. 100% ya uske kareeb exposure wale occupations: interpreters and translators, tax preparers, web designers, writers (mathematicians bhi 100%). Dusri taraf koi exposure nahi: cooks, stonemasons, athletes. Ye study achha idea deti hai ki AI kis kaam me achha hai.

8 categories — consumer aur enterprise examples

Ek application ek se zyada category me aa sakta hai — bot companionship bhi de aur information bhi aggregate kare; PDF se structured data bhi nikaale aur uske baare me sawaal bhi jawab de. 205 open-source apps me distribution dekhne par education, data organization aur writing ke chhote percentages ka matlab ye nahi ki ye use cases popular nahi hain — bas ye applications open-source nahi hain, enterprise me zyada bante hain.

Enterprise duniya kam risk wale applications pehle deploy karti hai. 2024 a16z report: companies internal-facing applications (internal knowledge management) external-facing (customer support chatbots) se jaldi deploy karti hain — internal apps se AI engineering expertise banti hai, data privacy, compliance aur catastrophic failure ka risk kam rehta hai. Aur foundation models open-ended hain, phir bhi bahut si applications close-ended hi banti hain, jaise classification — kyunki evaluate karna aasan hai, to risk estimate karna aasan hai.

1. Coding — sabse popular use case

Har generative AI survey me coding sabse upar hai — AI coding me achha bhi hai, aur early AI engineers khud coders hain jo coding challenges se rubaru hain. Sabse pehle production successes me se ek: GitHub Copilot, jiska annual recurring revenue launch ke 2 saal me $100 million paar kar gaya. AI coding startups ne hundreds of millions raise kiye — Magic ne $320 million aur Anysphere ne $60 million (dono Aug 2024). Open-source tools gpt-engineer aur screenshot-to-code ko ek saal me 50,000 stars mile.

Specialized coding tasks ke examples:

  • Web pages aur PDFs se structured data nikaalna (AgentGPT)
  • English se code banana (DB-GPT, SQL Chat, PandasAI)
  • Design ya screenshot se website ka code generate karna (screenshot-to-code, draw-a-ui)
  • Ek programming language/framework se dusre me translate karna (GPTMigrate, AI Code Translator)
  • Documentation likhna (Autodoc), tests banana (PentestGPT), commit messages likhna (AI Commits)

Kya AI software engineering ko poori tarah automate kar dega? Ek taraf Jensen Huang (NVIDIA CEO) kehte hain AI human software engineers ko replace kar dega aur bachhon ko code seekhna band kar dena chahiye; AWS CEO Matt Garman ke leaked recording me kehte hain ki aane wale time me zyadaatar developers coding band kar denge — matlab software developers khatam nahi, unka kaam badal jayega. Dusri taraf bahut se engineers maante hain woh kabhi replace nahi honge — technical aur emotional, dono reasons se.

McKinsey researchers ke hisaab se AI developers ko documentation me 2x productive aur code generation/refactoring me 25–50% zyada productive banata hai — lekin highly complex tasks me minimal improvement. Kai AI coding tool developers ne bataya ki AI frontend development me backend se bahut behtar hai. AI engineers ko replace kare ya na kare, unhe zyada productive zaroor bana sakta hai — companies kam engineers se zyada kaam kar sakti hain, aur outsourcing industry disrupt ho sakti hai kyunki outsourced tasks aksar simple hote hain.

2. Image aur Video Production

AI apni probabilistic nature ki wajah se creative tasks me bahut achha hai (Chapter 2 me detail). Sabse successful AI startups me creative applications hain: Midjourney (image generation), Adobe Firefly (photo editing), Runway, Pika Labs, Sora (video generation). Midjourney ne dedh saal ki umar me $200 million annual recurring revenue generate kiya. Dec 2023 me Apple App Store ke top 10 free Graphics & Design apps me se aadhe ke naam me "AI" tha — jaldi hi graphics apps me AI default hoga aur naam me "AI" ki zaroorat hi nahi padegi.

Log AI se social media profile pictures banate hain — LinkedIn se TikTok tak. Kai candidates maante hain AI-generated headshots se job milne ke chances badhte hain. Perception badal gaya hai: 2019 me Facebook ne AI-generated profile photos wale accounts safety reasons se ban kiye the; 2023 me bahut si social media apps khud AI profile photo tools deti hain.

Enterprises me ads aur marketing ne AI jaldi apnaya — company ke budget ka average 11% marketing par kharch hota hai, to automation se badi bachat hoti hai. AI promotional images/videos directly generate kar sakta hai, ideas brainstorm kar sakta hai, human experts ke liye first drafts bana sakta hai, multiple ads generate karke test kar sakta hai ki kaunsa audience ke liye behtar hai, aur seasons/locations ke hisaab se variations bana sakta hai — jaise fall me patton ka rang badalna ya winter me zameen par snow add karna.

3. Writing

Writing AI ke liye ideal application hai: hum bahut likhte hain, ye tedious hota hai, aur galtiyon ke liye tolerance high hai — model ka suggestion pasand na aaye to ignore kar do. Smartphone ka autocorrect aur auto-completion bhi AI hi hai.

MIT study (Noy and Zhang, 2023): 453 college-educated professionals ko occupation-specific writing tasks diye, aadhe ko ChatGPT diya. ChatGPT walon ka time 40% kam hua aur output quality 18% badhi. ChatGPT workers ke beech quality ka gap kam karta hai — matlab jinhe likhna kam aata hai, unhe zyada fayda. Experiment ke 2 hafte baad ChatGPT wale workers real job me use karne ki 2x zyada report karte the, 2 mahine baad 1.6x.

Consumer use cases: gusse wala email pleasant banana, bullet points se poore paragraphs banana, important email AI se improve karvaye bina na bhejna. Students essays likh rahe hain, writers books likh rahe hain — startups AI se children's, fan fiction, romance aur fantasy books generate kar rahe hain. AI-generated books interactive ho sakti hain — plot reader ki preference se badal sakta hai; children's reading app jin words me bachha atak raha hai, un par centered stories generate karta hai.

Google Docs, Notion, Gmail jaise apps writing improve karne me AI use karte hain; Grammarly model ko finetune karta hai taaki writing fluent, coherent aur clear ho. Managers performance reports likhne me AI use karte hain; cold outreach emails, ad copywriting, product descriptions; HubSpot aur Salesforce jaise CRM apps web content aur outreach emails generate karte hain.

Abuse bhi hai: 2023 me New York Times ne report kiya ki Amazon AI-generated travel guidebooks se bhar gaya — author bio, website aur rave reviews, sab AI-generated. AI SEO me khaas taur par achha lagta hai, shayad kyunki bahut se models internet data par train hote hain jo SEO-optimized text se bhara hai. Isse content farms ki nayi peedhi bani: junk websites banao, AI content se bharo, Google par rank karvao, ad spots becho. June 2023 me NewsGuard ne 141 popular brands ke lagbhag 400 ads junk AI websites par paye; ek junk website din me 1,200 articles produce karti thi. Author ki hypothesis: hum internet content par itna distrust karne lagenge ki sirf un logon ya brands ka content padhenge jin par bharosa hai.

4. Education

ChatGPT down hote hi OpenAI ke Discord server par students homework complete na kar paane ki shikayat karne lagte hain. New York City Public Schools aur Los Angeles Unified School District ne cheating ke dar se ChatGPT ban kiya, par kuch mahino me hi decision reverse kar diya.

Ban karne ke bajaye schools AI se students ko tezi se seekhne me madad kar sakte hain: textbooks summarize karna, har student ke liye personalized lecture plans banana. Ads personalized hote hain kyunki hum sab alag hain — par education nahi. Auditory learners materials ko loud padhva sakte hain; jinhe animals pasand hain woh visualizations me zyada animals la sakte hain; jineh math equations se zyada code padhna aasan hai woh equations ko code me translate karva sakte hain.

AI language learning me khaas helpful hai — alag-alag practice scenarios roleplay karva sakta hai. Duolingo ke Pajak aur Bicknell (2022) ne paya ki course creation ke 4 stages me AI ko sabse zyada fayda lesson personalization stage me hai. AI quizzes generate kar sakta hai (multiple-choice aur open-ended) aur answers evaluate kar sakta hai; debate partner ban sakta hai — ek hi topic par alag views dene me average insaan se behtar hai. Khan Academy students ko AI-powered teaching assistants aur teachers ko course assistants deta hai. Ek innovative method: teachers AI-generated essays assign karte hain jisme students ko mistakes dhoondhni aur correct karni hoti hain.

Lekin kai education companies ka lunch AI kha gaya: Chegg ka share price ChatGPT launch (Nov 2022) par $28 se gir kar Sept 2024 me $2 ho gaya, kyunki students homework help ke liye AI ki taraf mud gaye. Risk yahi hai ki AI bahut si skills replace kar de; opportunity ye hai ki AI kisi bhi skill ko seekhne ke liye tutor ban sakta hai.

5. Conversational Bots

Conversational bots versatile hain: information dhoondhna, concepts samjhana, ideas brainstorm karna, companion aur therapist banna, kisi ki bhi personality emulate karna — digital girlfriends aur boyfriends bahut kam time me weirdly popular ho gaye; kai log bots se insaano se zyada baat karne lage hain. Research me log conversational bots ke group se society simulate karke social dynamics par studies karte hain (Park et al., 2023).

Enterprises me sabse popular bots customer support bots hain — cost bachte hain aur customer experience behtar hota hai kyunki human agents se pehle respond karte hain. AI product copilots bhi ban sakta hai jo customers ko insurance claims file karna, taxes karna ya corporate policies dhoondhna jaise painful tasks me guide kare.

Text ke alawa bhi interfaces hain: Google Assistant, Siri, Alexa jaise voice assistants saalon se hain (author ko hairani hai ki Apple aur Amazon generative AI ko Siri/Alexa me itna slow kyun incorporate kar rahe hain — shayad quality aur compliance ka bar zyada hai). 3D conversational bots games me common hain aur retail/marketing me traction le rahe hain — smart NPCs (non-player characters, NVIDIA ke Inworld aur Convai demos) — bina AI ke NPCs scripted hote hain, limited dialogues ke saath; AI unhe bahut smarter bana sakta hai aur The Sims aur Skyrim jaise games ki dynamics badal sakta hai, plus naye games enable kar sakta hai.

6. Information Aggregation

Hamari success useful information ko filter aur digest karne ki ability par depend karti hai, lekin emails, Slack messages aur news se keep up karna overwhelming ho sakta hai. Salesforce 2023 Generative AI Snapshot Research: 74% generative AI users use karte hain complex ideas distill karne aur information summarize karne ke liye.

Consumers ke liye: documents (contracts, disclosures, papers) ko process karke conversational tareeke se information nikaalna — is use case ko talk-to-your-docs bhi kehte hain. AI websites summarize kar sakta hai, research kar sakta hai, chosen topics par reports bana sakta hai. Book likhte waqt author ko AI papers summarize aur compare karne me helpful laga.

Enterprises ke liye information aggregation aur dissemination se organization leaner ho sakti hai — middle management ka burden kam hota hai. Instacart ne jab internal prompt marketplace launch kiya to sabse popular template nikla "Fast Breakdown" — meeting notes, emails aur Slack conversations ko facts, open questions aur action items me summarize karna; action items automatically project tracking tool me daal kar sahi owners ko assign kiye ja sakte hain. AI potential customers ke baare me critical information surface kar sakta hai aur competitors par analysis chala sakta hai.

7. Data Organization

Future me hum aur zyada data produce karenge — smartphone users photos/videos lete rahenge, companies apne products, employees aur customers ke baare me sab log karti rahenge, saal me billions of contracts banenge. Photos, videos, logs aur PDFs sab unstructured ya semistructured data hain — inhe aise organize karna zaroori hai ki baad me search kiya ja sake.

AI images aur videos ke baare me text descriptions generate kar sakta hai, ya text queries ko matching visuals se mila sakta hai. Google Photos AI se search query se match karne wali images surface karta hai (author ke 40,000+ photos/videos bina AI ke search karna near-impossible hota). Google Image Search ek kadam aage: agar koi existing image user ki need se match nahi karti to woh generate kar sakta hai.

AI data analysis me bahut achha hai: data visualization ke programs likh sakta hai, outliers identify kar sakta hai, revenue forecasts jaise predictions bana sakta hai — aur confusing graphs ko explain bhi kar sakta hai.

Enterprises AI se unstructured data se structured information extract kar sakti hain: credit cards, driver's licenses, receipts, tickets, email footers se contact information — simple cases; contracts, reports, charts se data — complex cases. IDP (intelligent data processing) industry 2030 tak $12.81 billion tak pahunchne ka estimate hai, har saal 32.9% growth ke saath.

8. Workflow Automation

Aakhir me AI ko jitna ho sake automate karna chahiye. End users ke liye: restaurants book karna, refunds request karna, trips plan karna, forms bharna jaise boring daily tasks. Enterprises ke liye: lead management, invoicing, reimbursements, customer requests manage karna, data entry jaise repetitive tasks.

Ek khaas exciting use case: AI models se data synthesize karna, jo phir models ko hi improve karne me use ho (Chapter 8 me data synthesis). AI se apne data ke labels banva sakte ho, humans ko loop me rakh kar labels improve kar sakte ho.

Bahut se tasks ke liye external tools ki access chahiye: restaurant book karne ke liye search engine kholna, phone se call karna, calendar me appointment add karna. Jo AIs plan bana sakti hain aur tools use kar sakti hain, unhe agents kehte hain. Agents ke aas-paas interest obsession ki hadd tak hai, par poori tarah bina wajah nahi — AI agents har person ko vastly zyada productive bana sakte hain aur vastly zyada economic value generate kar sakte hain. Agents Chapter 6 ka central topic hain.

Yaad rakho: internet ke early days me kisi ne nahi socha tha ki social media dominating use case ban jayega. AI ka dominating use case bhi humein surprise kar sakta hai — ummeed hai achha surprise hoga.
SOURCESource: Huyen, AI Engineering, O'Reilly, Chapter 1 — Introduction to Building AI Applications with Foundation Models

01.3Chapter 1 · Introduction to Building AI Applications with Foundation Models

Planning AI Applications

AI ki seemingly limitless potential dekh kar seedha building me koodna tempting hai. Sirf seekhne aur maze ke liye hai to kood jao — building seekhne ka sabse achha tareeka hai, aur early days me kai AI heads ne teams ko experiment karne ko encourage kiya taaki upskill hon. Lekin agar ye tumhari rozi-roti hai, to ek kadam peeche hat kar sochna faydemand hai: kyun bana rahe ho, aur kaise? Foundation models se cool demo banana aasan hai; profitable product banana mushkil hai.

Use case evaluation — pehla sawaal: kyun?

AI application banana business decision hai — aksar risks aur opportunities ka jawab. Risk ke 3 levels, high se low:

  1. Existential threat: agar ye nahi kiya to AI wale competitors tumhe obsolete kar denge. Gartner 2023 study me 7% ne business continuity ko AI apnane ki wajah bataya. Ye document processing aur information aggregation wale businesses me zyada common hai — financial analysis, insurance, data processing — aur creative kaam me bhi: advertising, web design, image production. OpenAI study "GPTs are GPTs" (Eloundou et al., 2023) se dekho ki industries AI exposure me kahan rank karti hain.
  2. Profit aur productivity ka opportunity: zyadaatar companies isi liye AI apnati hain. AI lagbhag har business operation me madad kar sakta hai — behtar copywriting, product descriptions aur promotional visuals se user acquisition sasta; customer support aur customized user experience se retention zyada; sales lead generation, internal communication, market research, competitor tracking.
  3. Peeche na reh jayein: abhi pata nahi AI business me kahan fit hoga, par leap lene me der nahi karni. Kodak, Blockbuster aur BlackBerry ne bahut der tak wait karke galti ki. Transformational technology ka business par impact samajhne me resources lagana bura idea nahi hai, agar afford kar sakte ho. Badi companies me ye R&D ka hissa ho sakta hai; chhoti startups ke paas ek person bhi "look around" ke liye nahi hota.

Reason mil jaye to ye bhi socho ki khud banana hi zaroori hai ya nahi. Agar AI existential threat hai to in-house karna chahiye, competitor ko outsource karne ke bajaye. Lekin agar profit/productivity boost chahiye to bahut se buy options time, paisa bacha sakte hain aur behtar performance bhi de sakte hain.

Application me AI aur humans ka role

AI product me kis role me hai, isse development aur requirements dono tay hote hain. Apple ke document se 3 key points:

  • Critical ya complementary: agar app AI ke bina bhi chal sakta hai to AI complementary hai. Face ID AI-powered facial recognition ke bina kaam nahi karega, jabki Gmail Smart Compose ke bina bhi chalega. AI jitna critical hai, AI part ko utna hi accurate aur reliable hona chahiye. Log galtiyan zyada accept karte hain jab AI core nahi hota.
  • Reactive ya proactive: reactive feature user ke request/action par respond karta hai (jaise chatbot); proactive feature opportunity dekh kar khud respond karta hai (jaise Google Maps ke traffic alerts). Reactive features ko usually fast hona chahiye; proactive features precompute kiye ja sakte hain, to latency kam important hai. Lekin users ne proactive feature manga nahi hota, to low quality par woh intrusive ya annoying lagta hai — isliye proactive predictions/generations ka quality bar zyada hota hai.
  • Dynamic ya static: dynamic features user feedback se continually update hote hain (jaise Face ID — chehre badalte hain to update chahiye); static features periodically update hote hain (jaise Google Photos me object detection — sirf app upgrade par). AI me dynamic ka matlab ho sakta hai har user ka apna model, unke data par continually finetune hota hua, ya ChatGPT ki memory feature jaise personalization mechanism; static me ek shared model sab users ke liye, jo shared model update hone par hi badalta hai.

Humans ka role bhi clarify karna zaroori hai. AI humans ko background support dega, directly decisions lega, ya dono? Customer support chatbot ka example:

  • AI kai responses dikhata hai jinhe human agents reference karke tezi se jawab likh sakte hain.
  • AI sirf simple requests ka jawab deta hai, complex requests humans ko route karta hai.
  • AI sab requests ka jawab directly deta hai, bina human involvement ke.

AI ke decision-making me humans ko involve karna human-in-the-loop kehlata hai. Microsoft (2023) ne gradually AI automation badhane ka framework diya — Crawl-Walk-Run: (1) Crawl — human involvement mandatory; (2) Walk — AI internal employees se directly interact kar sakta hai; (3) Run — zyada automation, external users se direct AI interaction bhi. Humans ka role time ke saath badal sakta hai jaise AI system ki quality improve hoti hai — shuru me AI human agents ke liye suggestions generate kare; agar acceptance rate high hai (jaise simple requests ke 95% AI-suggested responses human agents verbatim use karte hain), to un simple requests ke liye customers ko AI se direct interact karne do.

AI product defensibility — moat kya hai?

Agar AI applications standalone products ke roop me bech rahe ho to defensibility sochna zaroori hai. Low entry barrier blessing bhi hai aur curse bhi — jo tumhare liye banana aasan hai, competitors ke liye bhi aasan hai. Tumhara moat kya hai?

Foundation models ke upar application banana matlab un models ke upar ek layer provide karna (early days ka joke: AI startups sirf OpenAI ya Claude wrappers hain). Agar underlying models ki capabilities badh gayi to tumhari layer models me subsumed ho sakti hai aur application obsolete ho jaye. Example: ye maan kar PDF-parsing application banao ki ChatGPT PDFs achhe se parse nahi kar sakta ya scale par nahi kar sakta — agar ye assumption galat ho gayi to compete karna mushkil hoga. Lekin open-source models ke upar bana PDF parser phir bhi sense bana sakta hai, un users ke liye jo models in-house host karna chahte hain.

Ek major VC firm ke general partner ne bataya ki unhone bahut si startups dekhi hain jinka poora product Google Docs ya Microsoft Office ka ek feature ho sakta tha. Agar unka product chal nikla to Google ya Microsoft ko 3 engineers ko 2 hafte allocate karke replicate karne se kya rokega?

AI me aam taur par 3 tarah ke competitive advantages hote hain: technology, data, aur distribution (product ko users tak pahunchane ki ability). Foundation models ke saath zyadaatar companies ki core technologies similar hongi. Distribution advantage likely badi companies ke paas hoga. Data advantage zyada nuanced hai: badi companies ke paas zyada existing data hoga, lekin agar startup pehle market me aakar kaafi usage data gather kar le aur products ko continually improve kare to data hi unka moat ban jayega. User data se models directly train na bhi kar sako, usage information se user behaviour aur product shortcomings ke baare me invaluable insights milte hain, jo data collection aur training process ko guide karte hain — isiliye book likhte waqt author ko har AI startup se "data flywheel" phrase sunne ko milta tha.

Phir bhi bahut si successful companies shuru me badi products ka ek feature theen jinhe bade competitors ne overlook kiya tha: Calendly Google Calendar ka feature ho sakta tha, Mailchimp Gmail ka, Photoroom Google Photos ka. Kai startups bade competitors ko peeche chhod deti hain, ek aisa feature bana kar jo bade competitors ne miss kiya. Shayad tumhara product agla ho.

Setting expectations — success kaisi dikhegi?

Decide kar liya ki khud banana hai, to agla step hai success define karna — use kaise measure karoge? Sabse important metric business par impact hai. Customer support chatbot ka example:

  • Customer messages ka kitna percentage chatbot automate kare?
  • Chatbot se kitne zyada messages process kar paoge?
  • Kitni jaldi respond kar paoge?
  • Kitna human labor chatbot bacha lega?

Chatbot zyada messages ka jawab de sakta hai, par iska matlab ye nahi ki users khush honge — isliye customer satisfaction aur customer feedback bhi track karna zaroori hai (feedback system design Chapter 10 me).

Product customers ke saamne laane se pehle usefulness threshold clear rakho — kitna achha hona chahiye tabhi useful hoga. Threshold me ye metric groups ho sakte hain:

  • Quality metrics — chatbot ke responses ki quality measure karne ke liye.
  • Latency metrics — TTFT (time to first token), TPOT (time per output token), total latency. Acceptable latency use case par depend karti hai — agar abhi humans median 1 ghante me respond karte hain to usse fast kuch bhi kaafi ho sakta hai.
  • Cost metrics — per inference request kitna kharcha.
  • Baaki metrics — jaise interpretability aur fairness.

Abhi sure nahi ho ki kaunsi metrics use karni hain to chinta mat karo — baaki book me kai metrics cover hongi.

Milestone planning — last mile challenge

Measurable goals tay karne ke baad unhe achieve karne ka plan chahiye. Kahan se shuru kar rahe ho, is par depend karta hai. Existing models ko evaluate karo taaki unki capabilities samajh aayein — off-the-shelf models jitne strong hain, utna kam kaam tumhe karna padega. Example: goal 60% customer support tickets automate karna hai aur off-the-shelf model pehle se 30% automate kar sakta hai, to effort usse kam hoga jaise woh 0% automate karta ho.

Goals evaluation ke baad badal bhi sakte hain — jaise pata chale ki usefulness threshold tak pahunchne ke resources potential return se zyada hain, to pursue karna hi band kar do.

AI product planning me last mile challenge ka hisaab rakho. Foundation models ke saath initial success misleading ho sakti hai. Base capabilities pehle se impressive hain, to fun demo banane me zyada time nahi lagta — lekin achha demo achhe end product ki guarantee nahi deta. Demo banane me ek weekend lag sakta hai, product banane me mahine, saal bhi lag sakte hain.

UltraChat paper (Ding et al., 2023) me likha hai: "0 se 60 tak ka safar aasan hai, 60 se 100 tak badhna exceedingly challenging hota hai." LinkedIn (2024) ne wahi sentiment share kiya: unhe chahiye hue experience ka 80% achieve karne me 1 mahina laga. Is initial success ne unhe grossly underestimate karva diya ki aage kitna time lagega — 95% se upar jaane me 4 aur mahine lage. Bahut time product ke kinks fix karne aur hallucinations se deal karne me gaya. Har agle 1% gain ki slow speed discouraging thi.

Maintenance — bullet train par sawaari

Planning goals achieve karne par khatam nahi hoti. Socho product time ke saath kaise badlega aur maintain kaise hoga. AI product ki maintenance me AI ke fast pace ki extra challenge hai — AI space pichhle decade me incredibly fast move kiya hai, aur agle decade bhi shayad karega. Aaj foundation models par build karna matlab is bullet train par sawaari karne ka commitment hai.

Bahut se changes achhe hain: models ki limitations address ho rahi hain, context lengths lambi ho rahi hain, outputs behtar ho rahe hain, inference faster aur cheaper ho raha hai. Figure 1-11 me 2022–2024 ke beech MMLU performance aur inference cost ka evolution dikhta hai — reasoning ki cost tezi se gir rahi hai.

Lekin achhe changes bhi workflows me friction laate hain. Har technology investment ka cost-benefit analysis karte rehna padega. Aaj ka best option kal ka worst ban sakta hai. Tum in-house model banane ka decide karo kyunki model providers se sasta lagta hai, aur 3 mahine baad providers apni prices aadhi kar dein to in-house mehenga option ban jaye. Kisi third-party solution me invest karo aur infrastructure uske aas-paas tailor karo, aur provider funding na milne par band ho jaye.

Kuch changes adapt karna aasan hai: model providers same API par converge ho rahe hain, to ek model API ko dusre se swap karna aasan ho raha hai. Lekin har model ki apni quirks, strengths aur weaknesses hoti hain — naye model ke saath developers ko workflows, prompts aur data adjust karne padenge. Bina proper versioning aur evaluation infrastructure ke ye process bahut headaches de sakta hai.

Kuch changes adapt karna mushkil hai, khaas taur par regulations ke aas-paas. AI se judi technologies kai countries ke liye national security issues mani jaati hain — compute, talent aur data heavily regulated hain. Europe ke GDPR ko compliant hone me businesses ko $9 billion ka estimate tha. Compute availability overnight badal sakti hai jab naye laws compute khareedne-bechne par restrictions lagayein (US October 2023 Executive Order dekho). Agar tumhara GPU vendor achanak tumhare country ko GPUs bechne se ban ho jaye to mushkil hai.

Kuch changes fatal bhi ho sakte hain: intellectual property (IP) aur AI usage ke aas-paas regulations abhi evolve ho rahe hain. Agar tumhara product kisi aise model par bana hai jo dusre logon ke data par train hua hai, to kya tum sure ho sakte ho ki tumhare product ki IP hamesha tumhari hi rahegi? Kai IP-heavy companies, jaise game studios, is dar se AI use karne me hesitate karti hain ki baad me apni IP kho na dein.

Yaad rakho: demo banana aasan hai, product banana mushkil — 0 se 60 aasan hai, 60 se 100 tak ka safar hi asli kaam hai. Plan me usefulness threshold, milestones aur maintenance — teeno pehle se rakho.
SOURCESource: Huyen, AI Engineering, O'Reilly, Chapter 1 — Introduction to Building AI Applications with Foundation Models
