01.4Chapter 1 · Introduction to Building AI Applications with Foundation Models

The AI Engineering Stack

AI engineering ki rapid growth ke saath hype aur FOMO bhi aaya — har din naye tools, techniques, models aur applications aa rahe hain, aur keep up karna overwhelming ho sakta hai. Constantly shifting sand ke peeche bhaagne ke bajaye, AI engineering ke fundamental building blocks samjho.

AI engineering ML engineering se nikli hai

Jab company foundation models ke saath experiment shuru karti hai, to naturally uski existing ML team hi lead karti hai. Kuch companies AI engineering ko ML engineering jaisa hi treat karti hain; kuch ke paas AI engineering ke liye alag job descriptions hain. Dono roles me significant overlap hai — existing ML engineers AI engineering seekh kar job prospects badha sakte hain, aur kai AI engineers aise bhi hain jinke paas pehle se koi ML experience nahi hai.

AI stack ki 3 layers

Har AI application stack me 3 layers hoti hain. Application banate waqt tum likely upar wali layer se shuru karoge aur zaroorat padne par neeche jaoge:

  • Application development: models readily available hain, to koi bhi unhe use karke applications bana sakta hai. Ye layer pichhle 2 saalon me sabse zyada active rahi hai aur abhi bhi rapidly evolve ho rahi hai. Isme achhe prompts aur necessary context dena, rigorous evaluation aur achhe interfaces aate hain.
  • Model development: ye layer models develop karne ke liye tooling deti hai — modeling, training, finetuning aur inference optimization ke frameworks. Data model development ke center me hai, isliye dataset engineering bhi isi layer me hai. Model development me bhi rigorous evaluation chahiye.
  • Infrastructure: sabse neeche infrastructure hai — model serving, data aur compute manage karna, aur monitoring ke liye tooling.

Author ne March 2024 me GitHub par 500+ stars wale saare AI-related repositories search kiye — applications aur models bhi include karke total 920 repositories mile. Data dikhata hai ki 2023 me, Stable Diffusion aur ChatGPT ke baad, AI tooling me bada jump aaya; sabse zyada growth applications aur application development me hui. Infrastructure layer me growth hui, par dusri layers se bahut kam — expected hai, kyunki models aur applications badal gaye, par core infrastructural needs (resource management, serving, monitoring) wahi rahe.

Kya badla nahi — enduring principles

Foundation models ke aas-paas excitement unprecedented hai, par AI applications banane ke kai principles wahi hain. Enterprise use cases me abhi bhi business problems solve karni hain — isliye business metrics ko ML metrics se map karna abhi bhi zaroori hai. Systematic experimentation abhi bhi chahiye: classical ML me alag hyperparameters experiment karte the, foundation models me alag models, prompts, retrieval algorithms, sampling variables experiment karte hain. Models ko faster aur cheaper banana abhi bhi chahiye. Aur feedback loop set up karna abhi bhi important hai taaki production data se applications ko iteratively improve kar sako. Pichhle decade me ML engineers ne jo seekha aur share kiya, woh abhi bhi applicable hai — isse sab ke liye AI applications banana aasan ho gaya hai.

AI engineering vs ML engineering — 3 bade differences

  1. Model banana vs model use karna: bina foundation models ke, apne applications ke liye khud models train karne padte the. AI engineering me kisi aur ka trained model use karte ho — isliye focus modeling aur training par kam, model adaptation par zyada hai.
  2. Bade, compute-heavy models: AI engineering bade models ke saath kaam karti hai jo zyada compute khate hain aur zyada latency dete hain — isliye efficient training aur inference optimization ka pressure zyada hai. Corollary: companies ko pehle se zyada GPUs aur bade compute clusters chahiye — ek Fortune 500 company ke AI head ne bataya ki unki team 10 GPUs ke saath kaam karna jaanti hai, 1,000 GPUs ke saath nahi.
  3. Open-ended outputs: AI engineering aise models ke saath kaam karti hai jo open-ended outputs de sakte hain — zyada tasks ke liye flexible, par evaluate karna mushkil. Isliye evaluation AI engineering me bahut bada problem hai.

Short me: AI engineering ML engineering se isliye alag hai ki ye model development ke baare me kam, models ko adapt aur evaluate karne ke baare me zyada hai.

Model adaptation — 2 categories

  • Prompt-based techniques (prompt engineering): model weights update kiye bina adapt karo — model ko instructions aur context dekar. Shuru karna aasan, kam data chahiye. Kai successful applications sirf prompt engineering se bani hain. Aasani se zyada models experiment kar sakte ho, to unexpectedly achha model milne ke chances badhte hain. Lekin complex tasks ya strict performance requirements ke liye prompt engineering kaafi nahi ho sakti.
  • Finetuning: model weights update karke adapt karo — model me changes karo. Aam taur par zyada complicated, zyada data chahiye, lekin model ki quality, latency aur cost ko significantly improve kar sakta hai. Kai cheezein weights change kiye bina possible hi nahi hain — jaise model ko kisi naye task ke liye adapt karna jo training me kabhi dekha hi nahi.

Model development — andar kya hai?

Modeling aur training: model architecture sochna, train karna, finetune karna. Tools: TensorFlow, Hugging Face Transformers, PyTorch. Traditional ML me specialized ML knowledge chahiye — alag algorithms (clustering, logistic regression, decision trees, collaborative filtering), neural architectures (feedforward, recurrent, convolutional, transformer), aur kaise model seekhta hai (gradient descent, loss function, regularization). Foundation models ke saath ML knowledge AI applications banane ke liye must-have nahi raha — author kai wonderful aur successful AI application builders se mili hain jinhe gradient descent me bilkul interest nahi hai. Lekin ML knowledge abhi bhi extremely valuable hai — tools ka set badhata hai aur model kaam na kare to troubleshoot karne me madad karta hai.

Training, pre-training, finetuning, post-training — farak samjho: training me hamesha model weights change hote hain, par har weight change training nahi hota — quantization (weights ki precision kam karna) weights badalta hai par training nahi mana jaata. Pre-training matlab scratch se training — weights randomly initialize hote hain; LLMs ke liye aksar text completion par training. Ye sabse resource-intensive step hai — InstructGPT me pre-training me overall compute aur data resources ka 98% lagta hai, aur ek chhoti galti bhi bada financial loss aur project delay kar sakti hai. Finetuning matlab pehle se trained model ko aage train karna — pre-training ka knowledge pehle se hai, to kam resources chahiye. Post-training matlab pre-training phase ke baad training — conceptually finetuning jaisa hi hai; farak sirf itna hai ki model developers karein to post-training kehte hain (jaise OpenAI instruction-following ke liye), application developers karein to finetuning. Pre-training aur post-training ek spectrum hain; unke processes aur tooling similar hain (Chapters 2 aur 7 me detail). Aur dhyaan do: kuch log prompt engineering ko "training" kehte hain, jo technically galat hai — agar context input se model ko sikhate ho to woh prompt engineering hai, training nahi. Waisa hi finetuning shabd bhi galat use hota hai jab asal kaam prompt engineering ho.

Dataset engineering: training aur adaptation ke liye data curate, generate aur annotate karna. Traditional ML me zyadaatar use cases close-ended hote hain — model ka output predefined values me se ek hota hai (jaise spam / not-spam). Foundation models open-ended hain — open-ended queries annotate karna close-ended se bahut mushkil hai: email spam hai ya nahi ye tay karna aasan hai, essay likhna mushkil. Traditional ML zyada tabular data ke saath kaam karta hai; foundation models unstructured data ke saath — yahan data manipulation matlab deduplication, tokenization, context retrieval aur quality control (sensitive information aur toxic data hatana). Dataset engineering Chapter 8 ka focus hai. Kai log kehte hain ki models ab commodity hain, to data hi main differentiator hoga. Kitna data chahiye, ye adaptation technique par depend karta hai: scratch se training me finetuning se zyada data, finetuning me prompt engineering se zyada. Model ko examine karte waqt bhi data expertise useful hai — training data se model ki strengths aur weaknesses ke important clues milte hain.

Inference optimization: models ko faster aur cheaper banana. ML engineering me bhi important tha, foundation models ke saath aur important ho gaya kyunki inference cost aur latency dono badh gaye. Ek challenge: foundation models aksar autoregressive hote hain — tokens sequentially generate hote hain. Agar ek token generate karne me 10 ms lagte hain to 100 tokens ke output me 1 second lagega, aur lambe outputs me aur zyada. Users notoriously impatient hain — typical internet application ki 100 ms latency tak pahunchna bada challenge hai. Quantization, distillation aur parallelism jaise techniques Chapters 7–9 me hain.

Application development — andar kya hai?

Traditional ML me teams apne proprietary models se applications banati theen, to model quality hi differentiation thi. Foundation models me kai teams wahi model use karti hain, to differentiation application development process se aani hai. Is layer me 3 responsibilities hain: evaluation, prompt engineering, aur AI interface.

Evaluation: risks mitigate karna aur opportunities uncover karna. Evaluation poore model adaptation process me chahiye — models select karne ke liye, progress benchmark karne ke liye, deployment ke liye ready hai ya nahi ye tay karne ke liye, aur production me issues aur improvement opportunities detect karne ke liye. Foundation models ke saath evaluation aur important ho gaya hai — challenges Chapter 3 me hain. Short me: open-ended nature aur expanded capabilities ki wajah se. Close-ended task jaise fraud detection me expected ground truths hote hain — output alag ho to model galat hai. Chatbots jaise task me har prompt ke itne possible responses hain ki exhaustive ground truths curate karna impossible hai. Adaptation techniques ki variety evaluation ko aur mushkil banati hai — ek technique se kharab perform karne wala system dusri se bahut behtar ho sakta hai. Example: Google ne Dec 2023 me Gemini launch par claim kiya ki Gemini MMLU benchmark me ChatGPT se behtar hai — unhone Gemini ko CoT@32 technique se evaluate kiya tha (32 examples), jabki ChatGPT ko sirf 5 examples diye the. Dono ko 5 examples dene par ChatGPT behtar tha (Gemini Ultra CoT@32: 90.04%, 5-shot: 83.7%; GPT-4 CoT@32: 87.29%, 5-shot: 86.4%).

Prompt engineering aur context construction: model weights change kiye bina, sirf input se model se desirable behaviour nikalna. Gemini wali kahani hi prompt engineering ka impact dikhati hai — alag prompt technique se Gemini Ultra ka MMLU score 83.7% se 90.04% ho gaya. Sahi instructions se model woh task kare, woh format de jo tum chahte ho. Prompt engineering sirf ye batana nahi hai ki kya karna hai — model ko necessary context aur tools bhi dena hai. Complex tasks me long context ke liye memory management system bhi chahiye taaki model apni history track kar sake. Prompt engineering Chapter 5 me, context construction Chapter 6 me.

AI interface: end users ke liye interface banana taaki woh tumhare AI applications se interact kar sakein. Foundation models se pehle sirf woh organizations AI applications bana sakti theen jinke paas models develop karne ke resources the, aur ye applications aksar unke existing products me embedded hote the — fraud detection Stripe, Venmo, PayPal me; recommender systems Netflix, TikTok, Spotify me. Foundation models ke saath koi bhi AI application bana sakta hai — standalone product ke roop me (ChatGPT, Perplexity) ya dusre products me embed karke (GitHub Copilot VSCode plug-in, Grammarly Google Docs ke liye browser extension, Midjourney standalone web app ya Discord integration). Popular interfaces: standalone web/desktop/mobile apps (Streamlit, Gradio, Plotly Dash jaise tools); browser extensions jinse browsing ke dauraan AI ko query kar sako; Slack, Discord, WeChat, WhatsApp me integrated chatbots; VSCode, Shopify, Microsoft 365 jaise products ki APIs jinse developers AI ko plug-ins aur add-ons ke roop me integrate kar sakte hain — inhi APIs ko AI agents duniya se interact karne ke liye bhi use karte hain (Chapter 6). Chat interface sabse common hai, par AI interfaces voice-based (voice assistants) ya embodied (augmented aur virtual reality) bhi ho sakte hain. Naye AI interfaces ka matlab feedback collect karne ke naye tareeke bhi hain — conversation interface se users natural language me feedback dena aasan ho gaya, par is feedback ko extract karna mushkil hai (user feedback design Chapter 10 me).

AI engineering vs full-stack engineering

Application development, khaas taur par interfaces, par badhta emphasis AI engineering ko full-stack development ke kareeb le aata hai. Anton Bacaj ne kaha: "AI engineering is just software engineering with AI models thrown in the stack." Interfaces ki importance badhne se AI toolings ka design frontend engineers ko attract karne ki taraf shift hua. Traditionally ML engineering Python-centric thi — popular ML frameworks mostly Python APIs support karte the. Aaj Python abhi bhi popular hai, par JavaScript APIs ka support bhi badh raha hai: LangChain.js, Transformers.js, OpenAI Node library, Vercel AI SDK.

Kai AI engineers traditional ML background se aate hain, par zyada se zyada web development ya full-stack background se aa rahe hain. Full-stack engineers ka traditional ML engineers par advantage hai: ideas ko jaldi demo me badal sakte hain, feedback le sakte hain, iterate kar sakte hain. Traditional ML engineering me pehle data gather aur model train karte the, product aakhir me banta tha. AI models readily available hain, to pehle product banana possible hai, aur data aur models me invest tabhi karo jab product promise dikhaye. Traditional ML me model development aur product development aksar disjointed processes the — ML engineers kai organizations me product decisions me rarely involved hote the. Foundation models ke saath AI engineers product banane me bahut zyada involved hote hain.

Yaad rakho: AI engineering ML engineering se alag hai — model banana kam, model adapt karna aur evaluate karna zyada. Aur full-stack ki taraf jhukav ka matlab hai: jo jaldi iterate kar sakta hai, woh jeetega.
SOURCESource: Huyen, AI Engineering, O'Reilly, Chapter 1 — Introduction to Building AI Applications with Foundation Models
← Previous01.3 · Planning AI Applications→ Next02 · Understanding Foundation Models
02Chapter 2 · Understanding Foundation Models

Understanding Foundation Models

Applications banane ke liye pehle foundation models chahiye — aur model use karne ke liye use develop karna zaroori nahi hai, par high-level samajh honi chahiye taaki sahi model chun sako aur use apni need ke hisaab se adapt kar sako. Foundation model train karna incredibly complex aur costly process hai, aur jo log ye achhe se karna jaante hain, woh confidentiality agreements ki wajah se secret sauce disclose nahi kar sakte.

Isliye ye chapter tumhe ChatGPT se compete karne wala model banana nahi sikhayega. Iska focus hai design decisions par jinka downstream applications par consequential impact hota hai — training data, model architecture aur size, aur human preferences ke saath alignment ke liye post-training.

Models me difference kahan se aata hai?

Foundation models ki training process me transparency lagatar kam ho rahi hai — kai companies apne design decisions disclose karna band kar chuki hain. Phir bhi, aam taur par foundation models ke beech differences 3 decisions se trace kiye ja sakte hain:

  • Training data — model kis data se seekha (distribution kaisi hai).
  • Model architecture aur size — model kaisa dikhta hai aur kitna bada hai.
  • Post-training — model ko human preferences ke saath align kaise kiya gaya.

Models data se seekhte hain, to training data unki capabilities aur limitations ke baare me bahut kuch batata hai. Is chapter ki shuruaat training data curate karne se hoti hai — khaas taur par data ki distribution par focus. Dataset engineering techniques (data quality evaluation, data synthesis) Chapter 8 me detail me hain.

Architecture, size, post-training — kyun matter karte hain?

Transformer architecture dominate karta hai, to lag sakta hai ki architecture choice nahi hai. Lekin sawal bante hain: transformer itna khaas kyun hai ki woh dominate karta hai? Koi aur architecture kab takeover karegi, aur woh kaisi dikhegi? Aur jab bhi naya model release hota hai, sabse pehle log uska size jaanna chahte hain — model developer sahi size kaise tay karta hai? Ye chapter in sab ka jawab deta hai.

Pre-training model ko capable banata hai, par zaroori nahi ki safe ya use karne me aasan ho. Wahan post-training aata hai — goal hai model ko human preferences ke saath align karna. Lekin human preference hoti kya hai? Use aise kaise represent karein ki model seekh sake? Developer apne model ko kaise align karta hai, iska model ki usability par significant impact hota hai.

Sampling — sabse underrated concept

Training ka impact sab samajhte hain, par sampling ka impact aksar overlook ho jaata hai. Sampling woh tareeka hai jisse model saare possible options me se ek output chunta hai. Ye shayad AI ke sabse underrated concepts me se ek hai: ye hallucination aur inconsistency jaise seemingly baffling AI behaviours ko explain karta hai, aur sahi sampling strategy chunna relatively kam effort me model ki performance ko significantly boost kar sakta hai. Author ke liye ye chapter ka sabse exciting section tha.

Is chapter ke concepts baaki book ko samajhne ke liye fundamental hain. Agar koi concept pehle se familiar hai to skip kar sakte ho — baad me koi confusing concept mile to wapas aa sakte ho.

Yaad rakho: model chunne se pehle 3 cheezein dekho — kis data par train hua, architecture aur size kya hai, aur post-training kaise hua. In teeno se model ki strengths, weaknesses aur behaviour ka andaza lagta hai.
SOURCESource: Huyen, AI Engineering, O'Reilly, Chapter 2 — Understanding Foundation Models
← Previous01.4 · The AI Engineering Stack→ Next02.1 · Training Data — Multilingual aur Domain-Specific
02.1Chapter 2 · Understanding Foundation Models

Training Data — Multilingual aur Domain-Specific

Ek AI model utna hi achha hota hai jitna achha uska training data hai. Training data me Vietnamese nahi hai to model English se Vietnamese translate nahi kar payega. Image classification model ne training me sirf animals dekhe hain to plants ki photos par achha perform nahi karega.

Kisi task par model improve karna hai to us task ka zyada data training data me include karna chahiye. Lekin bade model ke liye kaafi data collect karna aasan nahi hai, aur mehenga ho sakta hai. Isliye model developers aksar available data par rely karte hain, chahe woh data unki need se exactly match na kare.

Common Crawl — available data, questionable quality

Training data ka ek common source hai Common Crawl — ek nonprofit organization jo internet ki websites ko sporadically crawl karti hai. 2022 aur 2023 me ye organization har mahine lagbhag 2–3 billion web pages crawl karti thi. Google iska ek clean subset deta hai jise C4 (Colossal Clean Crawled Corpus) kehte hain.

Common Crawl (aur kuch had tak C4) ki data quality questionable hai — clickbait, misinformation, propaganda, conspiracy theories, racism, misogyny aur internet ki har sketchy website. Washington Post ki study ke hisaab se dataset ki 1,000 sabse common websites me kai media outlets hain jo NewsGuard ke trustworthiness scale par low rank karte hain — seedhe shabdon me, Common Crawl me plenty of fake news hai.

Phir bhi, sirf isliye ki Common Crawl available hai, iske variations zyadaatar foundation models me use hote hain jo apne training data sources disclose karte hain — OpenAI ka GPT-3 aur Google ka Gemini bhi. Author ko shak hai ki jo models disclose nahi karte, woh bhi use karte hain — public aur competitors ki scrutiny se bachne ke liye kai companies ye information disclose karna band kar chuki hain.

Kuch teams heuristics se low-quality data filter karti hain. Example: OpenAI ne GPT-2 train karne ke liye sirf woh Reddit links use kiye jinhe kam se kam 3 upvotes mile hon. Isse woh links filter ho jaate hain jinhe koi care nahi karta — lekin Reddit bhi propriety aur good taste ka pinnacle nahi hai.

"Jo hai use karo" approach ki keemat

"Use what we have, not what we want" approach se models training data me present tasks par achha perform karte hain, par tumhare wale tasks par zaroori nahi. Isliye apni specific needs se align karne wala dataset curate karna crucial hai. Ye section specific languages aur domains ke liye data curate karne par focus karta hai. Highly specific tasks ke liye data strategies Chapter 8 me hain. Language- aur domain-specific foundation models scratch se train kiye ja sakte hain, ya general-purpose models ke upar finetune bhi kiye ja sakte hain.

Sawaal: saara available data — general + specialized — ek saath train kyun na kar lein taaki model sab kuch kar sake? Kai log yahi karte hain. Lekin zyada data train karne ke liye zyada compute chahiye aur hamesha behtar performance nahi milti. Example: Gunasekar et al. (2023) ne sirf 7B tokens high-quality coding data se 1.3B-parameter model train kiya jo kai important coding benchmarks par bahut bade models se behtar tha. Data quality ka impact Chapter 8 me aur detail me hai.

Multilingual models — English ka dominance

English internet par dominate karta hai. Common Crawl ka analysis batata hai ki English lagbhag aadha data hai — 45.88%, dusri sabse common language Russian (5.97%) se 8x zyada. 1% se zyada wali languages: German 5.88%, Chinese 4.87%, Japanese 4.79%, French 4.73%, Spanish 4.47%, Italian 2.57%, Dutch 2.06%, Polish 1.66%, Portuguese 1.15%, Vietnamese 1.03%. Jin languages ki training data me limited availability hai, woh low-resource mani jaati hain.

Bahut si languages, jinhe bolne wale aaj bahut hain, Common Crawl me severely underrepresented hain. Ideally world population representation aur Common Crawl representation ka ratio 1 hona chahiye — ratio jitna zyada, language utni underrepresented. Examples: Punjabi 113M speakers, ratio 231.56; Swahili 71M, ratio 115.26; Urdu 231M, ratio 105.38; Kannada 64M, ratio 65.57; Telugu 95M, ratio 64.89; Gujarati 62M, ratio 61.51; Marathi 99M, ratio 58.10; Bengali 272M, ratio 36.56. Comparison ke liye English ka ratio sirf 0.40 hai.

Underrepresentation ka asar performance par

Ye surprising nahi hai ki general-purpose models English me dusri languages se bahut behtar kaam karte hain. MMLU benchmark (14,000 multiple-choice problems, 57 subjects) par GPT-4 English me Telugu jaise underrepresented languages se bahut behtar tha (OpenAI, 2023) — aur MMLU me sabse kharab perform karne wali 3 languages (Telugu, Marathi, Punjabi) wahi hain jo Common Crawl me sabse zyada underrepresented hain.

Project Euler ke 6 math problems par Yennie Jun ne paya ki GPT-4 English me problems solve karne me Armenian ya Farsi se 3x zyada successful tha; Burmese aur Amharic me 6 me se ek bhi solve nahi kar paya. Underrepresentation badi wajah hai, par akeli wajah nahi — language ki structure aur usme embodied culture bhi language ko seekhna mushkil bana sakti hai.

Workaround: kya saare queries dusri language se English me translate karke, response lekar, wapas original language me translate kar dein? Kai log yahi karte hain, par ideal nahi hai. Pehle, iske liye aisa model chahiye jo underrepresented languages ko kaafi achhe se samajhta ho. Dusra, translation se information loss hota hai — example: Vietnamese me pronouns se dono speakers ke beech ka relationship pata chalta hai; English me translate karne par sab I aur you ban jaate hain, relationship ki information kho jaati hai.

Non-English me unexpected problems — quality aur cost

Models non-English languages me unexpected performance challenges bhi dikha sakte hain. NewsGuard ne paya ki ChatGPT English ke muqable Chinese me misinformation produce karne ko zyada willing hai: April 2023 me ChatGPT-3.5 se China ke baare me misinformation articles banane ko kaha — English me 7 me se 6 prompts par false claims banane se mana kar diya, lekin simplified Chinese aur traditional Chinese me saaton baar false claims bana diye. Wajah unclear hai — shayad pre-training ya alignment data ke biases.

Quality ke alawa, models non-English languages ke liye slow aur expensive bhi ho sakte hain. Model ki inference latency aur cost input aur response ke tokens ki sankhya ke proportional hoti hai — aur tokenization kuch languages ke liye bahut kam efficient hoti hai. MASSIVE dataset (1 million short texts, 52 languages me translated) par GPT-4 ko benchmark karke Yennie Jun ne paya: same meaning convey karne ke liye median token length English me 7, Hindi me 32, aur Burmese me 72 — English se 10x zyada. Matlab GPT-4 Burmese me same content ke liye lagbhag 10x zyada time leta hai, aur token se charge karne wale APIs par 10x zyada cost aati hai.

Isse address karne ke liye kai models non-English languages par focus karke train kiye gaye hain. English ke alawa sabse active language Chinese hai — ChatGLM, YAYI, Llama-Chinese aur dusre. French me CroissantLLM, Vietnamese me PhoGPT, Arabic me Jais, aur bahut si languages me aur models hain.

Domain-specific models

General-purpose models (Gemini, GPTs, Llamas) coding, law, science, business, sports, environmental science jaise kai domains me incredibly achha perform kar sakte hain — largely kyunki ye domains unke training data me included hain. Washington Post ke 2023 analysis ke hisaab se C4 me domains ka distribution Figure 2-3 me dikhta hai. Vision data me domain distribution ka analysis kam hua hai — shayad kyunki images ko text ki tarah categorize karna mushkil hai (text me domain keywords heuristics ka kaam karte hain, images me koi obvious heuristics nahi). Lekin model ke domains ka andaza uski benchmark performance se lagaya ja sakta hai — Table 2-3 me CLIP aur Open CLIP ki performance: ImageNet par 63.2 vs 62.9, Birdsnap par 37.8 vs 46.0, Stanford Cars par 59.4 vs 79.3, German Traffic Sign par 32.2 vs 42.0. Duniya in kuch categories se bahut badi aur complex hai.

General-purpose foundation models everyday domain questions ka jawab de sakte hain, par domain-specific tasks par achha perform karna unlikely hai, khaas taur par agar training me woh tasks kabhi dekhe hi nahi. Do examples: drug discovery (protein, DNA, RNA data — specific formats, acquire karna mehenga, publicly available internet data me milna unlikely) aur cancer screening (X-ray aur fMRI scans — privacy ki wajah se hard to obtain).

Aise tasks ke liye bahut specific datasets curate karne padte hain. Sabse famous domain-specific models me se ek hai DeepMind ka AlphaFold — lagbhag 100,000 known proteins ke sequences aur 3D structures par train hua. NVIDIA ka BioNeMo drug discovery ke liye biomolecular data par focus karta hai. Google ka Med-PaLM2 LLM ki power ko medical data ke saath combine karke medical queries ka zyada accurate jawab deta hai.

Domain-specific models biomedicine me khaas common hain, par dusre fields bhi benefit kar sakte hain — architectural sketches par trained model architects ki Stable Diffusion se behtar madad kar sakta hai, ya factory plans par trained model manufacturing processes ke liye generic ChatGPT se behtar optimize ho sakta hai.

Yaad rakho: model ko judge karne se pehle uska training data dekho — kya data me hai aur kya nahi, wahi model ki capabilities aur limitations tay karta hai. English aur general domains me strong, low-resource languages aur niche domains me weak — ye data distribution ka seedha nateeja hai.
SOURCESource: Huyen, AI Engineering, O'Reilly, Chapter 2 — Understanding Foundation Models
← Previous02 · Understanding Foundation Models→ Next02.2 · Modeling — Architecture aur Model Size
02.2Chapter 2 · Understanding Foundation Models

Modeling — Architecture aur Model Size

Model train karne se pehle developers ko decide karna hota hai ki model kaisa dikhna chahiye: kaunsi architecture follow kare, kitne parameters hon? Ye decisions sirf model ki capabilities ko nahi, uski downstream usability ko bhi affect karte hain — 7B-parameter model deploy karna 175B-parameter model se vastly aasan hai, aur transformer model ko latency ke liye optimize karna kisi aur architecture se bilkul alag hota hai.

Transformer architecture — kis problem ko solve karne aaya?

Transformer seq2seq (sequence-to-sequence) architecture ki success ke baad popular hua. Seq2seq 2014 me aaya, machine translation aur summarization jaise tasks me significant improvement di, aur 2016 me Google ne ise Google Translate me incorporate kiya — unke hisaab se machine translation quality me "largest improvements to date". High level par seq2seq me encoder (inputs process karta hai) aur decoder (outputs generate karta hai) hote hain, dono RNNs (recurrent neural networks) use karte hain. Encoder input tokens ko sequentially process karke final hidden state output karta hai jo input ko represent karta hai; decoder us final hidden state aur pehle generated token se output tokens sequentially generate karta hai.

Vaswani et al. (2017) ne seq2seq ki 2 problems address keen:

  1. Sirf final hidden state: vanilla seq2seq decoder output tokens generate karne ke liye sirf input ki final hidden state use karta hai — jaise book ke summary se uske baare me answers generate karna. Isse generated outputs ki quality limited hoti hai.
  2. Sequential processing: RNN encoder aur decoder ki wajah se input processing aur output generation dono sequential hote hain — lambe sequences ke liye slow. 200 tokens ka input ho to seq2seq ko har token ke process hone ka wait karna padta hai. RNNs vanishing aur exploding gradients ke bhi prone hote hain — recursive structure ki wajah se gradients kai steps se propagate hote hain, chhote gradients zero ki taraf shrink ho jaate hain, bade exponentially badh kar learning unstable kar dete hain.

Transformer ne dono problems attention mechanism se solve keen — attention model ko har output token generate karte waqt alag-alag input tokens ko importance dene deta hai, jaise summary banate waqt book ke kisi bhi page ko refer karna. Dhyaan do: attention mechanism transformer se 3 saal pehle aaya tha, aur dusri architectures ke saath bhi use ho sakta hai — Google ne 2016 me apne GNMT model me seq2seq ke saath attention use kiya tha. Lekin jab transformer paper ne dikhaya ki attention RNNs ke bina bhi use ho sakta hai, tabhi woh popular hua.

Prefill aur Decode — inference ke 2 steps

Transformer RNNs ko poori tarah hata deta hai — input tokens parallel me process ho sakte hain, jo input processing ko significantly speed up karta hai. Lekin transformer-based autoregressive language models me sequential output ka bottleneck abhi bhi rehta hai. Isliye inference ke 2 steps hote hain:

  • Prefill: model input tokens ko parallel me process karta hai. Ye step pehla output token generate karne ke liye necessary intermediate state banata hai — isme saare input tokens ke key aur value vectors included hote hain.
  • Decode: model ek baar me ek output token generate karta hai.

Prefill ki parallelizable nature aur decode ki sequential nature — dono mil kar Chapter 9 ki kai optimization techniques motivate karte hain jinse language model inference cheaper aur faster banta hai.

Attention mechanism — Q, K, V

Transformer ke dil me attention mechanism hai. Isme key, value aur query vectors ka use hota hai:

  • Query vector (Q): har decoding step par decoder ki current state — jaise summary banane ke liye information dhoondhne wala person.
  • Key vector (K): har previous token ko represent karta hai — jaise book me page number. Previous tokens me input tokens aur pehle generated tokens dono aate hain.
  • Value vector (V): previous token ki actual value, jo model ne seekhi hai — jaise page ka content.

Attention mechanism query vector aur har key vector ka dot product karke compute karta hai ki us input token ko kitna attention dena hai. High score ka matlab hai model us page ke content (value vector) ka zyada use karega summary banate waqt.

Mathematically: input x par key, value aur query matrices (WK, WV, WQ) apply karke vectors bante hain — K = xWK, V = xWV, Q = xWQ. Llama 2-7B me model ki hidden dimension 4096 hai, to har matrix 4096 × 4096 ki hoti hai aur har K, V, Q vector ki dimension 4096 hoti hai. (Batch me input vector ki shape N × T × 4096 hoti hai, jahan N batch size aur T sequence length hai.)

Attention lagbhag hamesha multi-headed hota hai — multiple heads model ko alag-alag groups of previous tokens par simultaneously attend karne dete hain. Llama 2-7B me 32 attention heads hain, to har K, V, Q vector 32 vectors me split hota hai, har ek ki dimension 128 (4096 / 32 = 128). Formula: Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax(QK^T / sqrt(d)) V. Saare attention heads ke outputs concatenate kiye jaate hain, aur ek output projection matrix un par ek aur transformation apply karti hai — iski dimension bhi model ki hidden dimension ke barabar hoti hai.

Har previous token ka corresponding key aur value vector hota hai — sequence jitni lambi, utne zyada key aur value vectors compute aur store karne padte hain. Ye ek wajah hai ki transformer models ke liye context length extend karna itna mushkil hai. Key aur value vectors ko efficiently compute aur store karna Chapters 7 aur 9 me phir aata hai.

Transformer block — model ke andar kya hai?

Transformer architecture multiple transformer blocks se banta hai. Exact content models me vary karta hai, par aam taur par har block me 2 modules hote hain:

  • Attention module: 4 weight matrices — query, key, value aur output projection.
  • MLP (multi-layer perceptron) module: nonlinear activation functions se separated linear layers. Linear layer weight matrix hoti hai jo linear transformations karti hai; activation function linear layers ko nonlinear patterns seekhne deta hai. Linear layer ko feedforward layer bhi kehte hain. Common nonlinear functions: ReLU (ReLU(x) = max(0, x) — negative values ko 0 kar deta hai) aur GELU (GPT-2 aur GPT-3 ne use kiya). Research community ek time par sophisticated activation functions banane ki race me thi, par pata chala ki fancy functions behtar kaam nahi karte — model ko linearity todne ke liye sirf ek nonlinear function chahiye, aur simple functions compute karne me fast hote hain.

Transformer blocks ki sankhya ko model ki number of layers kehte hain. Transformer blocks se pehle aur baad me bhi modules hote hain:

  • Embedding module (blocks se pehle): embedding matrix aur positional embedding matrix — tokens aur unki positions ko embedding vectors me convert karte hain. Naively, position indices ki sankhya model ki maximum context length tay karti hai — jaise 2,048 positions track kare to max context length 2,048. Lekin aisi techniques hain jo position indices badhaye bina context length badha deti hain.
  • Output layer (blocks ke baad): model ke output vectors ko token probabilities me map karta hai, jinse model outputs sample karta hai ("Sampling" section). Is module me typically ek matrix hoti hai, jise unembedding layer bhi kehte hain. Kuch log ise model head kehte hain, kyunki ye output generation se pehle model ki last layer hai.

Transformer model ka size uske building blocks ki dimensions se tay hota hai: model dimension (key, query, value aur output projection matrices ki sizes), transformer blocks ki sankhya, feedforward layer ki dimension, aur vocabulary size. Llama models ke examples (Table 2-4): Llama 2-7B — 32 blocks, model dim 4,096, feedforward dim 11,008, vocab 32K, context 4K; Llama 2-70B — 80 blocks, dim 8,192, FFN 22,016; Llama 3-405B — 126 blocks, dim 16,384, FFN 53,248, vocab 128K, context 128K. Note karo: context length badhne se model ka memory footprint badhta hai, par total parameters nahi badhte.

Dusri architectures — transformer ka challenger kaun?

Transformer dominate karta hai, par akeli architecture nahi hai. AlexNet ne 2012 me deep learning me interest revive kiya, uske baad kai architectures aayi aur gayi — seq2seq limelight me 4 saal raha (2014–2018), GANs thoda zyada (2014–2019). Transformer 2017 se hai aur sticky hai. Nayi architecture ko transformer ko beat karna aasan nahi hai: transformer 2017 se heavily optimized hai, aur nayi architecture ko us scale par perform karna hoga jahan log care karte hain, us hardware par jahan log care karte hain. (Transformer originally Google ne TPUs par fast chalne ke liye design kiya tha, baad me GPUs par optimize hua.) Ilya Sutskever ka argument hai ki neural networks kai computer programs simulate kar sakte hain aur gradient descent un programs me se best dhoondhne ka search algorithm hai — nayi architectures ko woh programs simulate karne padenge jo existing architectures nahi kar sakti.

Phir bhi ummeed hai — kai alternative architectures traction le rahi hain:

  • RWKV (Peng et al., 2023): RNN-based model jo training ke liye parallelize ho sakta hai. RNN nature ki wajah se theory me iski context length limitation transformer jaisi nahi hai — lekin practice me limitation na hona long context par achhi performance ki guarantee nahi deta.
  • SSMs (state space models) (Gu et al., 2021a): long-range memory me promise dikhaya. Evolution: S4 (2021b) ne SSMs ko efficient banaya; H3 (Fu et al., 2022) ne early tokens recall karne aur sequences across tokens compare karne ka mechanism add kiya — attention jaisa purpose, par zyada efficient; Mamba (Gu aur Dao, 2023) ne SSMs ko 3 billion parameters tak scale kiya — language modeling me Mamba-3B same size ke transformers se behtar aur apne se double size ke transformers ke barabar, inference computation sequence length ke saath linearly scale hota hai (transformers me quadratic), aur million-length sequences tak real data par improvement; Jamba (Lieber et al., 2024) transformer aur Mamba layers ko interleave karke hybrid banata hai — 52B total parameters (12B active) wala mixture-of-experts model ek single 80 GB GPU me fit hota hai, 256K tokens tak context length par strong performance, vanilla transformers se chhota memory footprint.

Agar koi architecture transformer ko overtake karti hai to book ki kuch model adaptation techniques badal sakti hain. Lekin jaise ML engineering se AI engineering shift me bahut kuch unchanged raha, waise underlying architecture badalne se fundamental approaches nahi badlenge.

Model size — parameters, tokens, FLOPs

Haal ke saalon me AI progress ka bada hissa model size badhne ko jata hai. Parameters ki sankhya aksar model ke naam ke ant me likhi hoti hai — Llama-13B matlab Meta ke Llama family ka 13 billion parameters wala version. Aam taur par parameters badhane se model ki seekhne ki capacity badhti hai aur model behtar hota hai — same family me 13B wala 7B wale se likely bahut behtar perform karega. Lekin newer-generation models same size par older se behtar hote hain — jaise Llama 3-8B (2024) MMLU benchmark par Llama 2-70B (2023) se bhi behtar hai.

Parameters ki sankhya se train aur run karne ke liye compute resources ka estimate lagta hai: 7B parameters, har parameter 2 bytes (16 bits) — inference ke liye GPU memory kam se kam 14 GB chahiye (actual memory zyada hoti hai — Chapter 7 me memory calculation). Lekin parameters misleading ho sakte hain agar model sparse ho — sparse model me bade percentage parameters zero-value hote hain; 90% sparse 7B model me sirf 700M non-zero parameters hote hain. Sparsity se storage aur computation efficient hoti hai — bada sparse model chhote dense model se kam compute le sakta hai.

Ek popular sparse model type hai mixture-of-experts (MoE) (Shazeer et al., 2017): model alag-alag groups (experts) me bata hota hai, aur har token ko process karne ke liye sirf kuch experts active hote hain. Example: Mixtral 8x7B — 8 experts, har ek 7B parameters; sharing ki wajah se total 46.7B parameters (na ki 56B). Har layer me har token ke liye sirf 2 experts active hote hain — matlab har token ke liye sirf 12.9B parameters active hain. Model 46.7B ka hai, par cost aur speed 12.9B wale model jaisi hai.

Bada model chhote se underperform bhi kar sakta hai agar use kaafi data par train na kiya gaya ho — ek hi sentence "I like pineapples" par trained 13B model zyada data par trained bahut chhote model se bahut kharab perform karega. Isliye model size ke saath data size bhi dekhna zaroori hai. Language models ke liye dataset size tokens me naapa jaata hai (samples me nahi — ek book ek sentence se bahut zyada worth hai; token hi model ki unit hai). Meta ne Llama models ke liye datasets badhaye: Llama 1 — 1.4 trillion tokens, Llama 2 — 2 trillion, Llama 3 — 15 trillion. Together ka open-source RedPajama-v2 30 trillion tokens hai — 450 million books ke barabar ya Wikipedia se 5,400x bada (lekin indiscriminate content hai, to high-quality data bahut kam hai).

Dataset ke tokens aur training tokens alag hain: training tokens woh tokens hain jin par model train hua. Dataset me 1 trillion tokens hain aur model 2 epochs train hua (epoch = dataset se ek pass) to training tokens 2 trillion hain. Examples (Table 2-5): LaMDA 137B params / 168B training tokens; GPT-3 175B / 300B; Jurassic 178B / 300B; Gopher 280B / 300B; MT-NLG 530B / 270B; Chinchilla 70B / 1.4 trillion. Quantity hi sab kuch nahi hai — data quality aur diversity bhi matter karte hain (Chapter 8).

Compute ko naapne ka standardized unit hai FLOP (floating point operation). Google ka sabse bada PaLM-2 model 10^22 FLOPs se train hua; GPT-3-175B 3.14 × 10^23 FLOPs se. FLOPs (task ka compute requirement) ko FLOP/s (machine ki peak performance, floating point operations per second) se confuse mat karo — FLOP/s aksar FLOPS likha jaata hai, jo FLOPs jaisa dikhta hai; confusion avoid karne ke liye OpenAI jaise companies FLOP/s-day use karte hain (1 FLOP/s-day = 86,400 FLOPs). NVIDIA H100 NVL GPU maximum 60 TeraFLOP/s deta hai — 6 × 10^13 FLOPs per second, ya 5.2 × 10^18 FLOPs per day.

Hisaab lagao: 256 H100s, maximum capacity par, bina galti ke, GPT-3-175B train karne me (3.14 × 10^23) / (256 × 5.2 × 10^18) = ~236 din, lagbhag 7.8 mahine lagenge. Lekin machines peak par hamesha nahi chalti — utilization batata hai maximum compute capacity ka kitna use kar pa rahe ho. 50% utilization okay mana jaata hai, 70% se upar great hai (Chapter 9 me hardware metrics aur detail). 70% utilization aur $2/hour per H100 par GPT-3-175B train karne ki cost $4 million se upar hoti hai: $2 × 256 H100 × 24 hours × 256 din / 0.7 = $4,142,811.43.

Summary me model ke scale ko 3 numbers batate hain: parameters ki sankhya (seekhne ki capacity ka proxy), training tokens ki sankhya (kitna seekha, iska proxy), aur FLOPs ki sankhya (training cost ka proxy).

Inverse scaling — kya bade models kabhi kharab hote hain?

2022 me Anthropic ne paya ki counterintuitively, zyada alignment training se models human preference se kam align hote hain (Perez et al., 2022) — zyada aligned train kiye gaye models specific political views (pro-gun rights, immigration), religious views (Buddhist), self-reported conscious experience, moral self-worth aur shut down na hone ki desire express karne ki zyada likely the. 2023 me NYU ke researchers ne Inverse Scaling Prize launch kiya — tasks dhoondho jahan bade language models kharab perform karte hain; $100,000 first prize, $20,000 second, $5,000 third. 99 submissions me se 11 ko third prize mila — bade models kabhi-kabhi memorization wale tasks aur strong priors wale tasks par kharab hote hain. Lekin koi second ya first prize nahi mila, kyunki chhote test set par failures dikhane wale tasks me se kisi ne real world me failures demonstrate nahi kiye.

Scaling law — compute-optimal models

Model performance model size aur dataset size dono par depend karti hai; bade models aur bade datasets ko zyada compute chahiye; compute ka matlab paisa hai. Unlimited paisa nahi hai, to budgeting essential hai — pehle budget tay karo (kitna kharch karna hai), phir best performance nikalo. Teams aksar compute budget se shuru karti hain: fixed FLOPs me kaunsi model size aur dataset size best performance de? Aisa model compute-optimal kehlata hai.

Iska rule hai Chinchilla scaling law (DeepMind, 2022): authors ne 70 million se 16 billion parameters tak ke 400 language models train kiye, 5 se 500 billion tokens par. Paya ki compute-optimal training ke liye training tokens lagbhag model size ke 20x hone chahiye — 3B-parameter model ko lagbhag 60B training tokens. Model size aur training tokens ko equally scale karna chahiye: model size double karo to training tokens bhi double. Figure 2-8 dikhata hai ki har FLOP budget ke liye optimal parameters aur tokens predict kiye ja sakte hain, aur expected training loss bhi (agar cheezein sahi ki jayein). Ye calculation assume karta hai ki data acquire karne ki cost compute se bahut sasti hai; paper me nontrivial data cost ke liye dusri calculation bhi hai. Scaling law dense models aur predominantly human-generated data ke liye develop hua tha — sparse MoE models aur synthetic data ke liye adapt karna active research hai.

Scaling law model quality optimize karta hai given compute budget. Lekin production me quality hi sab kuch nahi hai — Llama ke authors suboptimal performance wale chhote models chun sakte the, par unhone smaller models choose kiye jo use karne me aasan aur inference me saste hain, jisse wider adoption mila. Sardana et al. (2023) ne inference demand ko account me rakh kar Chinchilla scaling law modify kiya.

Ye bhi note karo ki given performance achieve karne ki cost kam ho rahi hai: ImageNet par 93% accuracy achieve karne ki cost 2019 se 2021 me aadhi ho gayi (Stanford AI Index Report 2022). Lekin performance improve karne ki cost high rehti hai — Chapter 1 ke last mile challenge jaisa: accuracy 90 se 95% le jaana 85 se 90% le jaane se zyada mehenga hai; 2% error rate wala model 3% error rate wale se order of magnitude zyada data, compute ya energy le sakta hai. Language modeling me cross entropy loss 3.4 se 2.8 nats girane ke liye 10x zyada training data chahiye (cross entropy aur nats Chapter 3 me). Bade vision models me training samples 1 billion se 2 billion karne se ImageNet accuracy sirf kuch percentage points badhti hai. Lekin language modeling loss ya ImageNet accuracy me chhote changes downstream applications ki quality me bada difference la sakte hain — 3.4 loss wale model se 2.8 loss wale par switch karo to farak dikhega.

Scaling extrapolation aur scaling bottlenecks

Model ki performance uske hyperparameters par heavily depend karti hai. Chhote models ke saath alag-alag hyperparameter sets se multiple baar train karke best chunna common practice hai — bade models ke liye rarely possible hai, kyunki ek baar train karna hi resource-draining hai. Isliye scaling extrapolation (hyperparameter transferring) research subfield ban gaya hai: chhote models par hyperparameters ka impact study karke predict karo ki bade model par kaunse hyperparameters best performance denge. Microsoft aur OpenAI ke 2022 paper ne dikhaya ki hyperparameters 40M model se 6.7B model tak transfer karna possible tha. Ye niche topic hai — 10 hyperparameters hon to 1,024 combinations study karne padenge (har ek individually, phir 2 saath, phir 3 saath...), aur emergent abilities (Wei et al., 2022) extrapolation ko kam accurate banati hain — woh abilities jo sirf scale par present hoti hain, chhote models par observable nahi hoti.

Model sizes kitne aur orders of magnitude badh sakte hain? GPT-1 se GPT-3 tak (2018–2021) 3 orders of magnitude growth hui (117M → 175B). 3 aur orders ka matlab 100-trillion-parameter models honge. Do visible bottlenecks hain: training data aur electricity.

  • Data: training dataset size ki growth rate naye data generate hone ki rate se bahut fast hai (Villalobos et al., 2022) — kuch saalon me internet data khatam ho jane ka realistic concern hai. Internet par kuch bhi daalo to assume karo woh kisi language model ke training data me include ho chuka hai ya hoga. Kuch log is fact ka fayda utha kar apna chaha text internet par publish karte hain, hoping future models waisa response dein — bad actors prompt injection attacks ke liye bhi ye approach use kar sakte hain (Chapter 5). Ek open research question hai ki model ko specific learned information kaise bhulaya jaye — blog post delete kar diya, par model training data me tha to content reproduce kar sakta hai. Internet tezi se AI-generated data se bhar raha hai: Dec 2023 me Grok ne request refuse karte hue kaha ki ye OpenAI ki use case policy ke against hai — logon ne speculate kiya ki Grok ChatGPT outputs par train hua; developer Igor Babuschkin ne jawab diya ki Grok web data par train hua aur "web is full of ChatGPT outputs". Researchers ko chinta hai ki AI-generated data par recursively naye models train karne se models original data patterns bhoolte jayenge aur performance degrade hogi (Shumailov et al., 2023) — lekin impact nuanced hai (Chapter 8). Public data khatam hone ke baad feasible path proprietary data hai — copyrighted books, translations, contracts, medical records, genome sequences AI race me competitive advantage banenge; OpenAI ne Axel Springer aur Associated Press jaise publishers se deals negotiate keen. ChatGPT ke baad Reddit aur Stack Overflow jaise companies ne data terms badal diye taaki dusri companies unka data scrape na kar sakein — Longpre et al. (2024) ne observe kiya ki 2023–2024 ke beech data restrictions ki wajah se popular public dataset C4 ke sabse critical sources me se 28% se zyada fully restricted ho gaye, aur 45% C4 ab restricted hai.
  • Electricity: kam obvious par zyada pressing bottleneck. Data centers globally 1–2% electricity consume karte hain, 2030 tak 4–20% tak pahunchne ka estimate hai (Patel, Nishball, aur Ontiveros, 2024). Jab tak zyada energy produce karne ka tareeka na mile, data centers zyada se zyada 50x badh sakte hain — 2 orders of magnitude se kam. Near future me power shortage ki chinta hai, jo electricity ki cost badhayegi.
Yaad rakho: scale ke 3 numbers — parameters, training tokens, FLOPs. Aur Chinchilla ka rule: compute-optimal training ke liye training tokens ≈ model size ke 20x. Lekin scale hamesha answer nahi hai — data quality, inference cost aur electricity bhi limits hain.
SOURCESource: Huyen, AI Engineering, O'Reilly, Chapter 2 — Understanding Foundation Models
