03.3Chapter 3 · Evaluation Methodology

AI as a Judge

Open-ended responses evaluate karne ki challenges ne kai teams ko human evaluation par wapas le aaya hai. AI ne kai challenging tasks automate karne me success payi hai — kya AI evaluation ko bhi automate kar sakta hai? AI se AI ko evaluate karne ke approach ko AI as a judge ya LLM as a judge kehte hain. AI model jo dusre AI models ko evaluate karne ke liye use hota hai, use AI judge kehte hain. (Is term ko court me judge ke roop me AI use karne se confuse mat karo.)

AI se evaluation automate karne ka idea bahut purana hai, par practical tab hua jab AI models is kaam ke capable hue — lagbhag 2020 me GPT-3 ki release ke saath. Aaj AI as a judge production me AI models evaluate karne ke sabse common methods me se ek hai, agar sabse common nahi to. 2023 aur 2024 me author ne AI evaluation startups ke jitne demos dekhe, zyadaatar me ek na ek tareeke se AI as a judge leverage hota tha. LangChain ki State of AI report (2023) ke hisaab se unke platform par 58% evaluations AI judges se ki gayi theen. AI as a judge active research area bhi hai.

AI as a judge kyun?

  • Fast, easy aur relatively cheap: human evaluators ke muqable AI judges fast hain, use karne me aasan hain aur relatively saste hain.
  • Bina reference data ke kaam karte hain: production environments me use ho sakte hain jahan koi reference data nahi hai.
  • Kisi bhi criteria par judge kar sakte hain: correctness, repetitiveness, toxicity, wholesomeness, hallucinations aur aur bahut kuch. Ye waisa hi hai jaise kisi person se kisi bhi cheez par unki opinion poochh sakte ho. Soch sakte ho — "par logon ki opinions par hamesha bharosa nahi kar sakte". Sahi hai, aur AI ke judgments par bhi hamesha bharosa nahi kar sakte. Lekin har AI model masses ka aggregation hai, to AI models aise judgments de sakte hain jo masses ke representative hon. Sahi model ke liye sahi prompt ho to topics ki wide range par reasonably achhe judgments mil sakte hain.
  • Human evaluators se strongly correlated: studies ne dikhaya hai ki certain AI judges human evaluators se strongly correlated hain. 2023 me Zheng et al. ne paya ki unke evaluation benchmark MT-Bench par GPT-4 aur humans ke beech agreement 85% tak pahunch gaya — humans ke beech agreement (81%) se bhi zyada. AlpacaEval authors (Dubois et al., 2023) ne bhi paya ki unke AI judges ka LMSYS ke Chat Arena leaderboard (humans se evaluate) se near perfect (0.98) correlation hai.
  • Apne decision ko explain kar sakte hain: AI sirf response evaluate nahi kar sakta, apne decision ko explain bhi kar sakta hai — evaluation results audit karte waqt ye khaas useful hota hai. Figure 3-7 me GPT-4 apne judgment ko explain karte hue dikhta hai.

Flexibility ki wajah se AI as a judge wide range of applications ke liye useful hai, aur kuch applications ke liye ye ekmatra automatic evaluation option hai. AI judgments human judgments jitne achhe na bhi hon, phir bhi application development ko guide karne aur project shuru karne ka sufficient confidence dene ke liye kaafi achhe ho sakte hain.

AI as a judge kaise use karein? — 3 tareeke

AI se judgments karvane ke kai tareeke hain. Example: AI se response ki quality khud evaluate karvana, response ko reference data se compare karvana, ya response ko dusre response se compare karvana. In 3 approaches ke naive example prompts:

  1. Response ki quality khud evaluate karo (original question diya hua): "Given the following question and answer, evaluate how good the answer is for the question. Use the score from 1 to 5. 1 means very bad. 5 means very good. Question: [QUESTION] Answer: [ANSWER] Score:"
  2. Generated response ko reference response se compare karo (human-designed similarity measurements ka alternative): "Given the following question, reference answer, and generated answer, evaluate whether this generated answer is the same as the reference answer. Output True or False. Question: [QUESTION] Reference answer: [REFERENCE ANSWER] Generated answer: [GENERATED ANSWER]"
  3. 2 generated responses compare karo aur decide karo kaunsi behtar hai (post-training alignment ke liye preference data generate karne, test-time compute, aur comparative evaluation se models rank karne me helpful): "Given the following question and two answers, evaluate which answer is better. Output A or B. Question: [QUESTION] A: [FIRST ANSWER] B: [SECOND ANSWER] The better answer is:"

General-purpose AI judge se kisi bhi criteria par response evaluate karva sakte ho. Roleplaying chatbot bana rahe ho to evaluate karva sakte ho ki chatbot ka response us role ke consistent hai ya nahi, jo users chahte hain — jaise "Does this response sound like something Gandalf would say?" Promotional product photos generate karne wali application bana rahe ho to poochh sakte ho "From 1 to 5, how would you rate the trustworthiness of the product in this image?" Table 3-3 me kuch AI tools ke common built-in AI as a judge criteria hain (Sept 2024 tak): Azure AI Studio — groundedness, relevance, coherence, fluency, similarity; MLflow.metrics — faithfulness, relevance; LangChain Criteria Evaluation — conciseness, relevance, correctness, coherence, harmfulness, maliciousness, helpfulness, controversiality, misogyny, insensitivity, criminality; Ragas — faithfulness, answer relevance. Note karo: jaise tools evolve honge, ye built-in criteria badlenge.

Yaad rakhna zaroori hai ki AI as a judge criteria standardized nahi hain. Azure AI Studio ke relevance scores MLflow ke relevance scores se bahut alag ho sakte hain — ye scores judge ke underlying model aur prompt par depend karte hain.

Judge ka prompt kaisa hona chahiye?

AI judge ko prompt karna kisi bhi AI application ko prompt karne jaisa hai. Aam taur par judge ke prompt me ye clearly explain hona chahiye:

  1. Task jo model ko perform karna hai — jaise generated answer aur question ke beech relevance evaluate karna.
  2. Criteria jise follow karke model evaluate kare — jaise "Your primary focus should be on determining whether the generated answer contains sufficient information to address the given question according to the ground truth answer". Instruction jitni detailed hogi, utna behtar.
  3. Scoring system — 3 me se ek:
    • Classification — jaise good/bad ya relevant/irrelevant/neutral.
    • Discrete numerical values — jaise 1 se 5. Discrete numerical values ko classification ka special case mana ja sakta hai, jahan har class ka numerical interpretation hai semantic interpretation ke bajaye.
    • Continuous numerical values — jaise 0 se 1 ke beech, jab similarity ki degree evaluate karni ho.

Language models numbers se zyada text ke saath behtar hote hain. Report kiya gaya hai ki AI judges classification se numerical scoring se behtar kaam karte hain. Numerical scoring systems me discrete scoring continuous scoring se behtar kaam karti lagti hai. Empirically, discrete scoring ki range jitni wide hogi, model utna kharab hota lagta hai — typical discrete scoring systems 1 se 5 ke beech hote hain.

Examples wale prompts behtar perform karte hue dikhaye gaye hain. Scoring system 1 se 5 ho to 1, 2, 3, 4 ya 5 score wale response ke examples include karo, aur agar possible ho to kyun kisi response ko certain score milta hai. Prompting ke best practices Chapter 5 me hain. Azure AI Studio ke relevance criteria wale prompt ka hissa (brevity ke liye kuch remove kiya gaya): task batata hai (generated answer aur question ke beech relevance score karo, ground truth answer ke basis par, 1 se 5 ki range me, scoring reason bhi do), criteria batata hai (primary focus ye determine karna hai ki generated answer me question address karne ke liye ground truth answer ke hisaab se sufficient information hai ya nahi), aur low score ka example deta hai — question "Is the sky blue?", ground truth "Yes, the sky is blue.", generated answer "No, the sky is not blue." — generated answer ground truth se contradict karta hai, isliye low score 1–2 milega, aur reason contradiction ko reflect karega. Figure 3-8 me AI judge ka example hai jo question milne par answer ki quality evaluate karta hai.

Ek AI judge sirf model nahi hai — ye ek system hai jisme model aur prompt dono included hain. Model, prompt ya model ke sampling parameters badalne se alag judge banta hai.

Limitations — 4 bade issues

1. Inconsistency. Evaluation method trustworthy hone ke liye uske results consistent hone chahiye. Lekin AI judges, saare AI applications ki tarah, probabilistic hain. Wahi judge, same input par, alag prompt se alag scores de sakta hai. Wahi judge, same instruction se bhi, 2 baar run karne par alag scores de sakta hai. Is inconsistency se evaluation results ko reproduce ya trust karna mushkil ho jata hai. AI judge ko zyada consistent banana possible hai — Chapter 2 me sampling variables se kaise karte hain, ye discuss hua. Zheng et al. (2023) ne dikhaya ki prompt me evaluation examples include karne se GPT-4 ki consistency 65% se 77.5% ho gayi. Lekin unhone acknowledge kiya ki high consistency ka matlab high accuracy nahi hai — judge consistently wahi mistakes kar sakta hai. Upar se zyada examples include karne se prompts lambe hote hain, aur lambe prompts ka matlab zyada inference costs — Zheng et al. ke experiment me zyada examples include karne se unka GPT-4 spending chaar guna ho gaya.

2. Criteria ambiguity. Human-designed metrics se alag, AI as a judge metrics standardized nahi hain — inhe misinterpret aur misuse karna aasan hai. Open-source tools MLflow, Ragas aur LlamaIndex — teenon ke paas built-in criterion faithfulness hai (generated output given context ke kitna faithful hai), par unki instructions aur scoring systems teenon ki alag hain (Table 3-4): MLflow scoring 1–5 ("Faithfulness is only evaluated with the provided output and provided context... Score 1: None of the claims in the output can be inferred from the provided context..."); Ragas scoring 0 aur 1 ("Your task is to judge the faithfulness of a series of statements based on a given context... return verdict as 1 if the statement can be verified... or 0 if not"); LlamaIndex YES aur NO ("Please tell if a given piece of information is supported by the context. You need to answer with either YES or NO..."). Teen tools ke faithfulness scores comparable nahi honge — (context, answer) pair par MLflow 3 de, Ragas 1 de, LlamaIndex NO de to kaunsa score use karoge?

Application time ke saath evolve hoti hai, par use evaluate karne ka tareeka ideally fixed hona chahiye — taaki evaluation metrics se application ke changes monitor kiye ja sakein. Lekin AI judges bhi AI applications hain — matlab woh bhi time ke saath badal sakte hain. Imagine karo pichhle mahine tumhari application ka coherence score 90% tha, is mahine 92% hai — kya iska matlab application ki coherence improve hui hai? Ye sawaal answer karna mushkil hai jab tak sure na ho ki dono cases me use hue AI judges exactly same hain. Kya pata is mahine judge ka prompt pichhle mahine se alag ho — shayad tum thode behtar prompt par switch kar gaye, ya coworker ne pichhle mahine ke prompt me ek typo fix kar di, aur is mahine ka judge zyada lenient hai. Ye khaas confusing ho sakta hai jab application aur AI judge alag teams manage karti hon — AI judge team judges change kar de bina application team ko bataye, aur application team evaluation results ke changes ko application ke changes se galti se attribute kar le, judges ke changes ke bajaye. Kisi bhi AI judge par bharosa mat karo agar tum us judge ke liye use hue model aur prompt ko dekh nahi sakte. Evaluation methods ko standardize hone me time lagta hai — jaise field evolve hoga aur zyada guardrails aayenge, future ke AI judges hopefully zyada standardized aur reliable honge.

3. Increased costs aur latency. AI judges ko experimentation ke dauraan aur production me dono jagah use kar sakte ho. Kai teams AI judges ko production me guardrails ke roop me use karti hain risks kam karne ke liye — users ko sirf woh generated responses dikhate hain jinhe AI judge achha manta hai. Powerful models se responses evaluate karvana expensive ho sakta hai. GPT-4 se responses generate bhi karvao aur evaluate bhi karvao to GPT-4 calls double ho jayengi — API costs lagbhag double. 3 evaluation prompts hon (3 criteria evaluate karne ke liye — overall response quality, factual consistency, toxicity) to API calls 4x badh jayengi. (Kuch cases me evaluation budget ka majority le sakti hai, response generation se bhi zyada.) Costs kam kar sakte ho weaker models ko judges bana kar (agla hissa dekho). Costs kam kar sakte ho spot-checking se — sirf responses ka subset evaluate karo. Spot-checking ka matlab hai kuch failures miss ho sakte hain — samples ka jitna bada percentage evaluate karoge, evaluation results me confidence utna zyada hoga, par costs bhi utni zyada. Cost aur confidence ke beech sahi balance dhoondhne me trial aur error lag sakta hai (Chapter 4 me detail). Sab kuch consider karke, AI judges human evaluators se bahut saste hain. Production pipeline me AI judges implement karne se latency add hoti hai — responses users ko return karne se pehle evaluate karo to trade-off hai: risk kam, par latency zyada. Added latency strict latency requirements wali applications ke liye nonstarter ho sakti hai.

4. Biases. Human evaluators ke biases hote hain, waise AI judges ke bhi. Alag AI judges ke alag biases hote hain. Apne AI judges ke biases se aware rehna unke scores ko sahi interpret karne aur biases mitigate karne me madad karta hai. Self-bias: model apne responses ko dusre models ke responses se zyada pasand karta hai — wahi mechanism jo model ko sabse likely response generate karne me madad karta hai, wohi us response ko high score bhi dega. Zheng et al. ke 2023 experiment me GPT-4 khud ko 10% zyada win rate se favor karta tha, Claude-v1 khud ko 25% zyada win rate se. First-position bias: kai AI models pairwise comparison me pehle answer ko favor karte hain, ya options ki list me pehle wale ko. Ise mitigate kar sakte ho same test ko alag orderings se multiple baar repeat karke ya carefully crafted prompts se. AI ka position bias humans ke opposite hai — humans aakhri dekha gaya answer favor karte hain, jise recency bias kehte hain. Verbosity bias: kuch AI judges quality se independent lambe answers ko favor karte hain. Wu aur Aji (2023) ne paya ki GPT-4 aur Claude-1 dono factual errors wale lambe responses (~100 words) ko sahi chhote responses (~50 words) se prefer karte hain. Saito et al. (2023) ne creative tasks ke liye is bias ko study kiya — jab length difference kaafi bada ho (ek response dusre se double lamba), judge lagbhag hamesha lambe wale ko prefer karta hai. Zheng et al. (2023) aur Saito et al. (2023) — dono ne paya ki GPT-4 is bias ke liye GPT-3.5 se kam prone hai, jo suggest karta hai ki models strong hote jayenge to ye bias khatam ho sakta hai. (Saito et al. ne paya ki humans bhi lambe responses ko favor karte hain, par bahut kam had tak.) In sab biases ke upar, AI judges ki wahi limitations hain jo saare AI applications ki hain — privacy aur IP. Proprietary model ko judge banao to apna data us model ko bhejna padega. Model provider apna training data disclose na kare to sure nahi ho sakte ki judge commercially safe hai ya nahi.

In limitations ke bawajood, AI as a judge ke kai advantages ki wajah se author manti hain ki iski adoption badhti rahegi. Lekin AI judges ko exact evaluation methods aur/ya human evaluation ke saath supplement karna chahiye.

Judge kaunsa model ban sakta hai — stronger, weaker ya same?

Judge model se stronger bhi ho sakta hai, weaker bhi, ya same bhi. Har scenario ke apne pros aur cons hain.

Stronger judge: pehli nazar me sense banta hai — exam grader exam taker se zyada knowledgeable hona chahiye na? Stronger models behtar judgments de sakte hain, aur weaker models ko behtar responses generate karne me guide karke improve bhi kar sakte hain. Sawaal: agar stronger model ki access pehle se hai to weaker model se responses generate karvane ki kya zaroorat? Jawab hai cost aur latency — stronger model se saare responses generate karne ka budget nahi ho sakta, to use responses ka subset evaluate karne ke liye use karte ho. Example: cheap in-house model se responses generate karo aur GPT-4 se 1% responses evaluate karvao. Stronger model tumhare application ke liye bahut slow bhi ho sakta hai — fast model se responses generate karo aur stronger (lekin slow) model background me evaluation kare; agar strong model ko weak model ka response kharab lage to remedy actions liye ja sakte hain, jaise response ko strong model wale se update karna. Note karo opposite pattern bhi common hai: strong model se responses generate karo, weak model background me evaluation kare. Stronger model ko judge banane se 2 challenges aati hain: sabse strong model ke liye koi eligible judge nahi bachega; aur kaunsa model sabse strong hai, ye determine karne ke liye alternative evaluation method chahiye.

Same model judge (self-evaluation / self-critique): model se khud ko judge karvana cheating jaisa lagta hai, khaas taur par self-bias ki wajah se. Lekin self-evaluation sanity checks ke liye great ho sakti hai — agar model ko apna hi response incorrect lagta hai to model utna reliable nahi ho sakta. Sanity checks se aage, model se khud ko evaluate karvane se model apne responses revise aur improve karne ke liye nudge ho sakta hai (Press et al., 2022; Gou et al., 2023; Valmeekam et al., 2023). Example: User prompt: "What's 10+3?" Pehla response: "30". Self-critique: "Is this answer correct?" Final response: "No it's not. The correct answer is 13." (Is technique ko self-critique ya self-ask bhi kehte hain.)

Weaker judge: ek open question hai ki kya judge model se weaker ho sakta hai. Kuch argue karte hain ki judging generation se aasan task hai — koi bhi ye opinion de sakta hai ki gaana achha hai ya nahi, par har koi gaana nahi likh sakta. Weaker models stronger models ke outputs judge karne ke capable hone chahiye. Zheng et al. (2023) ne paya ki stronger models human preference se behtar correlated hain, isliye log sabse strong models choose karte hain jo afford kar sakte hain. Lekin ye experiment general-purpose judges tak limited tha. Ek research direction jisme author excited hain, woh hai small, specialized judges — specific judgments karne ke liye train kiye gaye, specific criteria aur specific scoring systems follow karne wale. Specific judgments ke liye chhota specialized judge bade general-purpose judges se zyada reliable ho sakta hai.

Specialized AI judges ke 3 examples:

  • Reward model: (prompt, response) pair input lekar score deta hai ki prompt ke given response kitna achha hai. Reward models RLHF me kai saalon se successfully use ho rahe hain. Google ka Cappy (2023) ek reward model ka example hai — (prompt, response) pair par 0 se 1 ke beech score deta hai, jo batata hai response kitna correct hai. Cappy 360 million parameters ka lightweight scorer hai, general-purpose foundation models se bahut chhota.
  • Reference-based judge: generated response ko ek ya zyada reference responses ke respect me evaluate karta hai. Judge similarity score ya quality score output kar sakta hai (generated response reference responses ke muqable kitna achha hai). Example: BLEURT (Sellam et al., 2020) — (candidate response, reference response) pair input lekar candidate aur reference ke beech similarity score output karta hai. (BLEURT ka score range confusing hai — lagbhag -2.5 se 1.0 ke beech — jo AI judges ke saath criteria ambiguity ki challenge highlight karta hai: score range arbitrary ho sakti hai.) Prometheus (Kim et al., 2023) — (prompt, generated response, reference response, scoring rubric) input lekar 1 se 5 ke beech quality score output karta hai, assume karke ki reference response ko 5 milta hai.
  • Preference model: (prompt, response 1, response 2) input lekar output karta hai ki 2 responses me se kaunsi behtar hai (users kis ko prefer karte hain). Ye specialized judges ke liye shayad sabse exciting directions me se ek hai. Human preference predict kar pana kai possibilities kholta hai — Chapter 2 me discuss hua ki preference data AI models ko human preference se align karne ke liye essential hai, aur obtain karna challenging aur expensive hai. Achha human preference predictor evaluation ko aasan aur models ko safe bana sakta hai. Preference models banane ki kai initiatives hain, jaise PandaLM (Wang et al., 2023) aur JudgeLM (Zhu et al., 2023). Figure 3-9 me PandaLM ka example output hai — ye sirf ye nahi batata ki kaunsi response behtar hai, apne rationale ko bhi explain karta hai.

Apni limitations ke bawajood, AI as a judge approach versatile aur powerful hai. Cheaper models ko judges bana kar use karna ise aur useful bana deta hai. Author ke kai colleagues, jo shuru me skeptical the, production me is par zyada rely karne lage hain. AI as a judge exciting hai, aur agla approach bhi utna hi intriguing hai — ye game design se inspired hai, ek fascinating field.

Yaad rakho: AI judge sirf model nahi, model + prompt + sampling parameters ka system hai. Judge ke scores tabhi meaningful hain jab pata ho kaunsa model aur kaunsa prompt use hua — aur usi judge ko exact evaluation aur human evaluation ke saath supplement karo.
SOURCESource: Huyen, AI Engineering, O'Reilly, Chapter 3 — Evaluation Methodology
← Previous03.2 · Exact Evaluation — Correctness aur Similarity→ Next03.4 · Comparative Evaluation aur Ranking
03.4Chapter 3 · Evaluation Methodology

Comparative Evaluation aur Ranking

Aksar models ko isliye evaluate karte ho kyunki unke scores ki parwah hai, nahi — isliye ki jaanna chahte ho kaunsa model tumhare liye best hai. Chahiye hota hai models ki ranking. Models ko rank karne ke 2 tareeke hain: pointwise evaluation ya comparative evaluation.

Pointwise evaluation me har model ko independently evaluate karo, phir unke scores se rank karo. Example: kaunsi dancer best hai ye jaanne ke liye har dancer ko individually evaluate karo, score do, phir sabse zyada score wali dancer pick karo. Comparative evaluation me models ko ek dusre ke against evaluate karo aur comparison results se ranking compute karo — saare candidates ko side-by-side dance karvao aur judges se poochho kis candidate ki dancing sabse zyada pasand hai, phir woh dancer pick karo jise zyadaatar judges prefer karein.

Jin responses ki quality subjective hai, unke liye comparative evaluation typically pointwise evaluation se aasan hoti hai. Example: 2 gaano me se kaunsa behtar hai ye batana, har gaane ko concrete score dene se aasan hai. AI me comparative evaluation pehli baar 2021 me Anthropic ne alag models rank karne ke liye use ki. Ye popular LMSYS ke Chatbot Arena leaderboard ko bhi power karti hai, jo community se pairwise model comparisons se compute kiye gaye scores se models rank karta hai.

Kai model providers production me apne models evaluate karne ke liye comparative evaluation use karte hain. Figure 3-10 me example hai jisme ChatGPT users se 2 outputs side by side compare karne ko kehta hai. Ye outputs alag models se generate ho sakte hain, ya same model se alag sampling variables ke saath. Har request ke liye 2 ya zyada models select kiye jate hain response dene ke liye. Evaluator (human ya AI) winner pick karta hai. Kai developers ties allow karte hain taaki drafts equally achhe ya kharab hon to winner random pick na ho.

Preference se kya answer nahi karna chahiye?

Ek bahut important baat yaad rakhni hai: saare questions preference se answer nahi karne chahiye. Kai questions correctness se answer karne chahiye. Imagine karo model se poochha "Is there a link between cell phone radiation and brain tumors?" aur model 2 options "Yes" aur "No" de kar tumse chunne ko kahe. Preference-based voting se galat signals mil sakte hain — agar in signals se model train karo to misaligned behaviours aa sakte hain.

Users se pick karvane se user frustration bhi ho sakti hai. Imagine karo model se math question poochha kyunki tumhe answer nahi pata, aur model 2 alag answers de kar tumse kahe jo prefer karte ho woh pick karo. Agar tumhe sahi answer pata hota to model se poochhte hi kyun? Comparative feedback users se collect karte waqt ek challenge hai determine karna ki kaunse questions preference voting se decide ho sakte hain aur kaunse nahi. Preference-based voting sirf tab kaam karta hai jab voters subject me knowledgeable hon. Ye approach generally un applications me kaam karta hai jahan AI intern ya assistant ke roop me kaam karta hai — users ko woh tasks tezi se karne me madad karta hai jo woh khud karna jaante hain — na ki wahan jahan users AI se woh tasks karvate hain jo woh khud karna nahi jaante.

Comparative evaluation ko A/B testing se confuse mat karo. A/B testing me user ek baar me ek candidate model ka output dekhta hai. Comparative evaluation me user ek saath multiple models ke outputs dekhta hai.

Matches, win rate aur ranking algorithms

Har comparison ko match kehte hain. Is process se comparisons ki series banti hai (Table 3-5): Match 1 — Model 1 vs Model 2, winner Model 1; Match 2 — Model 3 vs Model 10, winner Model 10; Match 3 — Model 7 vs Model 4, winner Model 4; aur aise hi. Model A ke Model B par preferred hone ki probability hai A ki B par win rate — A aur B ke beech saare matches dekh kar calculate karo ki kitne percentage me A jeetta hai.

Sirf 2 models hon to ranking straightforward hai — jo model zyada baar jeette woh upar rank karta hai. Models zyada hon to ranking challenging ho jati hai. Maan lo 5 models hain, model pairs ke beech empirical win rates Table 3-6 me hain: Model 1 vs Model 2 — 90%; Model 1 vs Model 3 — 40%; Model 1 vs Model 4 — 15%; Model 1 vs Model 5 — 10%; Model 2 vs Model 3 — 60%; Model 2 vs Model 4 — 80%; Model 2 vs Model 5 — 80%; Model 3 vs Model 4 — 70%; Model 3 vs Model 5 — 10%; Model 4 vs Model 5 — 20% (har pair ke 1,000 matches). Data dekh kar obvious nahi hai ki 5 models ko kaise rank karna chahiye.

Comparative signals milne ke baad rating algorithm use karke models ki ranking compute ki jati hai. Typically algorithm pehle comparative signals se har model ke liye ek score compute karta hai, phir models ko unke scores se rank karta hai. Comparative evaluation AI me nayi hai, par dusri industries me lagbhag ek century se hai — khaas taur par sports aur video games me. Dusre domains ke liye develop kiye gaye kai rating algorithms AI models evaluate karne ke liye adapt kiye ja sakte hain, jaise Elo, Bradley–Terry aur TrueSkill. LMSYS ka Chatbot Arena originally models ki ranking compute karne ke liye Elo use karta tha, par baad me Bradley–Terry algorithm par switch kar gaya kyunki unhe Elo evaluators aur prompts ke order ke prati sensitive laga. (Chatbot Arena ne Elo rating algorithm use karna band kar diya, phir bhi uske developers kuch time tak apne model ratings ko "Elo scores" kehte rahe. Unhone resulting Bradley–Terry scores ko scale kiya taaki woh Elo scores jaise dikhein — scaling kaafi complicated hai: har score ko 400 se multiply kiya jata hai (Elo me use hone wala scale) aur 1,000 add kiya jata hai (initial Elo score). Phir is score ko rescale kiya jata hai taaki model Llama-13b ka score 800 ho.)

Ranking sahi hai agar kisi bhi model pair ke liye higher-ranked model lower-ranked model ke against match me zyada likely jeette — Model A, Model B se upar rank kare to users ko Model A, Model B se zyada baar prefer karna chahiye (aadhe se zyada time). Is lens se model ranking ek predictive problem hai: historical match outcomes se ranking compute karo aur use future match outcomes predict karne ke liye use karo. Alag ranking algorithms alag rankings produce kar sakte hain, aur sahi ranking ke liye koi ground truth nahi hai. Ranking ki quality isse determine hoti hai ki future match outcomes predict karne me woh kitni achhi hai. Chatbot Arena ki ranking ka author ka analysis dikhata hai ki produced ranking achhi hai, kam se kam un model pairs ke liye jin ke sufficient matches hon (analysis book ke GitHub repo me hai).

Challenges — 3 bade issues

Pointwise evaluation me heavy-lifting part hai benchmark aur metrics design karna taaki sahi signals gather hon; scores compute karke models rank karna aasan hai. Comparative evaluation me signal gathering aur model ranking dono challenging hain. Ye section comparative evaluation ki 3 common challenges cover karta hai.

1. Scalability bottlenecks. Comparative evaluation data-intensive hai. Compare karne wale model pairs ki sankhya models ki sankhya ke saath quadratically badhti hai. Jan 2024 me LMSYS ne 57 models ko 244,000 comparisons se evaluate kiya. Ye bahut saari comparisons lagti hain, par average sirf 153 comparisons per model pair hota hai (57 models matlab 1,596 model pairs). Ye chhoti sankhya hai, tasks ki wide range ko dekhte hue jinhe foundation model karna chahiye. Fortunately, 2 models me kaunsa behtar hai ye determine karne ke liye hamesha direct comparisons ki zaroorat nahi hoti. Ranking algorithms typically transitivity assume karte hain: Model A, B se upar rank kare aur B, C se upar rank kare to transitivity se infer kar sakte ho ki A, C se upar rank karta hai. Matlab algorithm ko ye certain ho ki A, B se behtar hai aur B, C se behtar hai to A vs C compare kiye bina pata chal jayega ki A behtar hai. Lekin unclear hai ki ye transitivity assumption AI models ke liye hold karti hai ya nahi. Elo for AI evaluation analyze karne wale kai papers (Boubdir et al.; Balduzzi et al.; Munos et al.) transitivity assumption ko limitation kehte hain — unka argument hai ki human preference necessarily transitive nahi hoti. Iske alawa non-transitivity isliye bhi ho sakti hai kyunki alag model pairs ko alag evaluators aur alag prompts par evaluate kiya jata hai. Naye models evaluate karne ki bhi challenge hai: independent evaluation me sirf naya model evaluate karna hota hai; comparative evaluation me naya model existing models ke against evaluate karna hota hai, jo existing models ki ranking badal sakta hai. Isse private models evaluate karna bhi mushkil ho jata hai: imagine karo tumne apni company ke liye internal data se ek model banaya hai, aur compare karna chahte ho ki public model use karna zyada beneficial hoga ya nahi. Comparative evaluation use karni ho to likely apne comparative signals collect karke apna leaderboard banana padega, ya public leaderboards ko pay karke apne liye private evaluation run karvana padega. Scaling bottleneck ko better matching algorithms se mitigate kiya ja sakta hai: ab tak assume kiya gaya hai ki har match ke liye models randomly select hote hain, to saare model pairs lagbhag same number of matches me aate hain. Lekin saare model pairs ko equally compare karne ki zaroorat nahi hai — ek baar model pair ke outcome par confident ho jayein to unhe ek dusre ke against match karna band kar sakte ho. Efficient matching algorithm ko woh matches sample karne chahiye jo overall ranking me uncertainty ko sabse zyada kam karte hon.

2. Lack of standardization aur quality control. Comparative signals collect karne ka ek tareeka hai comparisons ko community ko crowdsource karna, jaise LMSYS Chatbot Arena karta hai: koi bhi website par ja sakta hai, prompt enter kar sakta hai, 2 anonymous models se 2 responses le sakta hai, aur behtar wale ko vote kar sakta hai. Voting ke baad hi model names reveal hote hain. Is approach ka fayda hai ki signals ki wide range capture hoti hai aur game karna relatively mushkil hota hai. Lekin downside hai ki standardization aur quality control enforce karna mushkil hai. Pehli baat, internet access wala koi bhi kisi bhi prompt se models evaluate kar sakta hai, aur behtar response kya hona chahiye, iska koi standard nahi hai. Volunteers se responses fact-check karne ki ummeed karna bahut zyada ho sakta hai, to woh unknowingly aise responses prefer kar sakte hain jo behtar sound karte hain par factually incorrect hain. Kuch log polite aur moderate responses prefer kar sakte hain, dusre bina filter wale responses — ye achha bhi hai aur bura bhi: achha kyunki human preference in the wild capture karne me madad karta hai; bura kyunki wild me human preference saare use cases ke liye appropriate nahi ho sakti. Example: user model se inappropriate joke sunane ko kahe aur model refuse kare to user use downvote kar sakta hai — lekin application developer ke roop me tum chahte ho ki model refuse kare. Kuch users maliciously toxic responses ko preferred ke roop me pick bhi kar sakte hain, ranking ko pollute karke. (Chatbot Arena popular hote jaane ke saath use game karne ki koshishen common ho gayi hain. Kisi ne author ko admit nahi kiya ki unhone ranking game karne ki koshish ki, par kai model developers ko yakeen hai ki unke competitors try karte hain.) Dusri baat, comparisons crowdsource karne me users ko models ko unke working environments ke bahar evaluate karna padta hai. Bina real-world grounding ke test prompts reflect nahi karte ki models real world me kaise use ho rahe hain. Log bas pehle dimaag me aane wale prompts use kar sakte hain aur sophisticated prompting techniques use karne ki unlikely hain. LMSYS Chatbot Arena ne 2023 me publish kiye gaye 33,000 prompts me se 180 "hello" aur "hi" the (0.55% data) — aur "hello!", "hello.", "hola", "hey" jaise variations isme count nahi hain. Bahut se brainteasers hain: "X has 3 sisters, each has a brother. How many brothers does X have?" 44 baar poochha gaya. Simple prompts ka jawab dena aasan hai, to models ki performance differentiate karna mushkil ho jata hai — bahut zyada simple prompts se models evaluate karne se ranking pollute ho sakti hai. Agar public leaderboard sophisticated context construction support nahi karta — jaise context ko tumhare internal databases se retrieve kiye gaye relevant documents se augment karna — to uski ranking reflect nahi karegi ki model tumhare RAG system ke liye kitna achha kaam karega. Achhe responses generate karne ki ability sabse relevant documents retrieve karne ki ability se alag hai. Standardization enforce karne ka ek potential tareeka hai users ko predetermined prompts ke set tak limit kar dena — lekin isse leaderboard ki diverse use cases capture karne ki ability affect ho sakti hai. LMSYS iske bajaye users ko koi bhi prompt use karne deta hai, phir apne internal model se hard prompts filter karke sirf in hard prompts se models rank karta hai. Dusra tareeka hai sirf un evaluators ka use karna jin par bharosa kar sakein — evaluators ko 2 responses compare karne ke criteria par train karo, ya practical prompts aur sophisticated prompting techniques use karne ke liye train karo. Ye approach Scale apne private comparative leaderboard ke saath use karta hai. Iska downside hai ki expensive hai aur comparisons ki sankhya severely kam kar sakta hai. Ek aur option hai comparative evaluation ko apne products me incorporate karna aur users ko unke workflows ke dauraan models evaluate karne dena — example: code generation task me users ko code editor ke andar 2 code snippets suggest karo aur unhe behtar wala pick karne do. Kai chat applications ye pehle se kar rahe hain. Lekin jaise pehle mention hua, user ko pata nahi ho sakta ki kaunsa code snippet behtar hai, kyunki woh expert nahi hai. Upar se users dono options padhe bina randomly ek par click kar sakte hain — isse results me bahut noise aa sakta hai. Lekin users ke chhote percentage se aane wale sahi signals kabhi-kabhi kaunsa model behtar hai ye determine karne ke liye sufficient ho sakte hain. Kuch teams human evaluators se zyada AI evaluators prefer karti hain — AI trained human experts jitna achha nahi ho sakta, par random internet users se zyada reliable ho sakta hai.

3. Comparative performance se absolute performance tak. Kai applications ke liye best possible model chahiye hi nahi hota — aisa model chahiye jo good enough ho. Comparative evaluation batati hai kaunsa model behtar hai; ye nahi batati ki model kitna achha hai ya ye model tumhare use case ke liye good enough hai ya nahi. Maan lo ranking mili ki Model B, Model A se behtar hai — teenon scenarios valid ho sakte hain: (1) Model B achha hai, par Model A kharab hai; (2) Model A aur Model B dono kharab hain; (3) Model A aur Model B dono achhe hain. Kaunsa scenario sahi hai, ye determine karne ke liye dusri forms of evaluation chahiye. Imagine karo customer support ke liye Model A use kar rahe ho, aur Model A 70% tickets resolve kar sakta hai. Model B par vichar karo, jo A ke against 51% time jeettta hai — unclear hai ki ye 51% win rate Model B kitne requests resolve kar sakta hai, isme kaise convert hogi. Kai logon ne author ko bataya ki unke experience me win rate me 1% change kuch applications me huge performance boost la sakta hai, par dusri applications me sirf minimal boost. A ko B se swap karne ka decide karte waqt human preference hi sab kuch nahi hai — cost jaise dusre factors bhi matter karte hain. Performance boost kya expect karna hai, ye jaane bina cost–benefit analysis karna mushkil hai — Model B ki cost A se double ho to comparative evaluation ye determine karne me sufficient nahi hai ki B se performance boost added cost ke worth hoga ya nahi.

Comparative evaluation ka future

Itni limitations dekh kar soch sakte ho ki kya iska future hai. Comparative evaluation ke kai benefits hain. Pehla: Chapter 2 me discuss hua ki logon ko 2 outputs compare karna har output ko concrete score dene se aasan lagta hai. Models strong hote jayenge, human performance se aage nikal jayenge to human evaluators ke liye model responses ko concrete scores dena impossible ho sakta hai — lekin human evaluators phir bhi difference detect kar sakte hain, aur comparative evaluation hi ekmatra option reh sakta hai. Example: Llama 2 paper ne share kiya ki jab model best human annotators ki ability se aage ki writing me venture karta hai to humans 2 answers compare karte waqt valuable feedback de sakte hain (Touvron et al., 2023).

Dusra: comparative evaluation us quality ko capture karna chahti hai jiski humein parwah hai — human preference. Isse AI ki ever-expanding capabilities ke saath catch up karne ke liye constantly naye benchmarks banane ka pressure kam hota hai. Benchmarks ke alag, jo model performance perfect scores achieve karne par useless ho jate hain, comparative evaluations kabhi saturate nahi hongi jab tak naye, stronger models introduce hote rahenge.

Teesra: comparative evaluation game karna relatively mushkil hai — reference data par model train karne jaisa koi aasan tareeka cheat karne ka nahi hai. Isi liye kai log public comparative leaderboards ke results par kisi bhi dusre public leaderboards se zyada bharosa karte hain.

Comparative evaluation humein models ke baare me discriminating signals de sakti hai jo otherwise nahi mil sakte. Offline evaluation ke liye ye evaluation benchmarks ka great addition ho sakti hai. Online evaluation ke liye ye A/B testing ki complementary ho sakti hai.

Yaad rakho: comparative evaluation batati hai kaunsa model behtar hai, ye nahi ki model kitna achha hai. Ranking ke saath absolute performance naapne wali evaluation bhi chahiye — warna pata nahi chalega ki best model bhi good enough hai ya nahi.
SOURCESource: Huyen, AI Engineering, O'Reilly, Chapter 3 — Evaluation Methodology
← Previous03.3 · AI as a Judge→ Next04 · Evaluate AI Systems
04Chapter 4 · Evaluate AI Systems

Evaluate AI Systems

Model sirf tab useful hai jab woh tumhare application ke liye kaam kare — general benchmark pe achha score kaafi nahi hai. Chapter 3 ne automatic evaluation ke tareeke bataye the; ye chapter batata hai ki un tareekon se apne application ke liye models ko kaise evaluate karein, kaunse criteria use karein, model kaise chunein, aur apni evaluation pipeline kaise banayein.

Evaluation-driven development kya hai?

Book kehti hai — application jo deploy ho gaya lekin pata hi nahi ki kaam kar raha hai ya nahi, woh us application se bhi bura hai jo kabhi deploy hi nahi hua. Deployed-but-unevaluated system maintain karne me kharcha aata hai, aur use band karna aur bhi mehenga pad sakta hai.

Ek used-car dealership ka example hai: team ne car ki value predict karne wala model deploy kiya, ek saal baad users ko feature pasand aa raha tha, lekin engineer ko pata hi nahi tha ki predictions sahi bhi hain ya nahi. ChatGPT ke fever ke shuru me bahut si companies ne customer support chatbot jaldi-jaldi deploy kar diye — aaj bhi bahut ko nahi pata ki woh chatbot user experience ko help kar rahe hain ya hurt.

Isliye approach hai evaluation-driven development — software engineering ke test-driven development se inspired. Test-driven development me code likhne se pehle test likhte hain; AI engineering me build karne se pehle evaluation criteria define karo. Time, paisa aur resources lagane se pehle samajh lo ki application ko evaluate kaise karoge.

Evaluation hi sabse bada bottleneck kyun hai?

Jo applications production me sabse common hain, woh wahi hain jinke evaluation criteria clear hain — recommender systems (engagement ya purchase-through rate badha to success), fraud detection (kitna paisa bachaya), coding (generated code ko functional correctness se check kar sakte ho). Close-ended tasks jaise intent classification, sentiment analysis, next-action prediction evaluate karna open-ended tasks se bahut aasan hai.

Lekin sirf wahi applications banana jinke outcomes aasani se measure ho jaayein, wohi hai jaise raat me khoi hui chaabi sirf lamppost ke neeche dhoondhna — aasan hai, lekin chaabi wahan ho ye zaroori nahi. Bahut si game-changing applications isliye miss ho jaati hain kyunki unhe evaluate karne ka aasan tareeka nahi hai. Author ka maanna hai ki evaluation hi AI adoption ka sabse bada bottleneck hai — reliable evaluation pipeline bana loge to bahut si nayi applications unlock ho jayengi.

Criteria ke 4 buckets

Har AI application ke liye apne specific criteria ki list banao. Aam taur pe criteria in 4 buckets me aate hain:

  • Domain-specific capability — model ko tumhare domain ki samajh hai ya nahi (jaise legal contract samajhna).
  • Generation capability — output kitna coherent aur faithful hai (jaise summary kitna sahi hai).
  • Instruction-following capability — model ne instruction ke hisaab se format/length follow ki ya nahi.
  • Cost aur latency — ek summary kitne ka padega aur kitna time lagega.

Chapter 3 ne approach se shuru karke bataya tha ki ek approach se kaunse criteria evaluate ho sakte hain. Ye chapter ulta angle leta hai — ek criterion diya ho to use evaluate karne ke kaunse approaches hain. Is chapter ke 3 hisse hain: pehle evaluation criteria, phir model selection, aur aakhir me apni evaluation pipeline design karna.

Yaad rakho: Build karne se pehle criteria likho. Agar tumhe pata hi nahi ki "achha" ka matlab kya hai, to tum kabhi ye nahi jaan paoge ki tumhara system achha hai ya nahi — aur deploy ke baad ye sawaal aur mehenga ho jata hai.
SOURCESource: Huyen, AI Engineering, O'Reilly, Chapter 4 — Evaluate AI Systems
← Previous03.4 · Comparative Evaluation aur Ranking→ Next04.1 · Evaluation Criteria
04.1Chapter 4 · Evaluate AI Systems

Evaluation Criteria

Model choose karne se pehle ye tay karo ki use kis cheez pe judge karoge. Is section me chaar tarah ke criteria hain — domain-specific capability, generation capability (factual consistency aur safety samet), instruction-following, aur cost/latency — aur har ek ko measure karne ke tareeke.

Domain-specific capability

Coding agent banane ke liye model ko code likhna aana chahiye; Latin se English translate karne ke liye use dono languages aani chahiye. Ye capabilities model ki architecture, size aur training data se limited hoti hain — model ne training me Latin dekha hi nahi to Latin samajh nahi payega.

Domain capabilities ko aam taur pe exact evaluation se check karte hain. Coding ke liye functional correctness use hoti hai (Chapter 3), lekin sirf "code chalta hai" kaafi nahi — efficiency bhi matter karti hai. Agar text-to-SQL model sahi query banaye lekin woh query chalne me bahut time ya memory le, to woh usable nahi hai. BIRD-SQL benchmark execution accuracy ke saath efficiency bhi measure karta hai — generated query ka runtime ground-truth SQL ke runtime se compare karke. Code readability bhi matter karti hai, lekin use exactly evaluate nahi kar sakte — wahan AI judge jaisi subjective evaluation chahiye.

Non-coding domains me aksar close-ended tasks use hote hain, jaise multiple-choice questions (MCQ). April 2024 me Eleuther ke lm-evaluation-harness ke 75% tasks multiple-choice the, jinme MMLU, AGIEval aur ARC-C shamil hain. AGIEval ke authors ne open-ended tasks jaan-boojh kar exclude kiye the taaki assessment inconsistent na ho. MMLU ka example: monopoly wale sawaal me sahi jawab (D) hai — consumer surplus lost with higher prices and lower levels of output.

  • Metric: accuracy — kitne sawaal sahi. Kuch tasks me point system hota hai — mushkil sawaal ke zyada points, ya multiple correct options pe har sahi option ka ek point.
  • Classification MCQ ka special case hai jahan har sawaal ke choices same hote hain (jaise sentiment: NEGATIVE / POSITIVE / NEUTRAL). Accuracy ke alawa F1 score, precision, recall use hote hain.
  • Random baseline: 4 options wale MCQ me random guess se 25% accuracy milti hai — usse upar score aam taur pe random se behtar hone ka sign hai.

MCQ ki ek kami: chhote se presentation change se model ke jawab badal jaate hain — question aur answer ke beech ek extra space, ya "Choices:" jaisa phrase add karna bhi jawab badal sakta hai (Alzahrani et al., 2024). Aur MCQ classification test karte hain (achhe aur bure jawab me farak pehchanna), generation nahi — woh knowledge aur reasoning ke liye achhe hain, summarization/translation/essay writing jaise generation tasks ke liye nahi.

Generation capability — fluency, coherence, faithfulness

Open-ended text generation ko NLG (natural language generation) kehte hain. 2010s ke shuru me metrics the fluency (text grammatically sahi aur natural lagta hai?) aur coherence (poora text logical structure follow karta hai?). Har task ke apne metrics bhi the — translation me faithfulness (original sentence ke kitna wafadar hai?), summarization me relevance (summary source document ke sabse important aspects pe focus karta hai?).

Jaise models behtar hote gaye, AI-generated text insaan ke text se mushkil se alag hone laga, to fluency aur coherence kam important ho gaye — lekin kamzor models, creative writing aur low-resource languages ke liye abhi bhi useful hain. Inhe AI as a judge se ya perplexity se evaluate kar sakte ho. Naye models ke saath naye issues aaye — sabse bada hai hallucination (creative tasks me desirable, factual tasks me nahi), isliye factual consistency aur safety ab main metrics hain. Author apne writing assistant me controversiality bhi track karti thi — content harmful nahi lekin heated debate chhed de. Friendliness, positivity, creativity, conciseness jaise aur bhi qualities ho sakti hain.

Factual consistency — local vs global

Factual consistency do settings me verify hoti hai:

  • Local factual consistency: output ko diye gaye context ke against check karo. Context kahe "sky is purple" aur model kahe "sky is blue" to inconsistent hai; model kahe "sky is purple" to consistent hai — chahe asal me aasmaan neela ho. Summarization, customer support chatbot (company policies ke against) aur business analysis ke liye important hai.
  • Global factual consistency: output ko open knowledge ke against check karo. General chatbot, fact-checking, market research ke liye important hai.

Explicit facts ke against verify karna aasan hai — "vaccination aur autism ka koi proven link nahi hai" ye statement verify karna aasan hai agar reliable sources diye hon. Bina context ke pehle reliable sources dhoondhne padenge, facts derive karne padenge, phir validate karna padega. Sabse mushkil hissa ye decide karna hai ki facts hain kya — "Messi is the best soccer player" ya "breakfast is the most important meal" fact hai ya opinion, ye ispe depend karta hai ki tum kis source pe bharosa karte ho. Internet misinformation se bhara hai, aur absence of evidence fallacy bhi hota hai — evidence na milna iska proof nahi ki link hai hi nahi. Wan et al. (2024) ne paya ki models website ki query se relevance pe bahut bharosa karte hain, aur scientific references ya neutral tone jaise stylistic signals ko ignore kar dete hain, jo insaanon ko important lagte hain.

Hallucination metrics design karte time analyse karo ki model kis type ke queries pe zyada hallucinate karta hai, aur benchmark unhi pe focus kare. Author ke project me model do tarah ke queries pe hallucinate karta tha: (1) niche knowledge — VMO (Vietnamese Mathematical Olympiad) pe IMO se zyada hallucination, kyunki VMO kam commonly referenced hai; (2) jo cheez exist hi nahi karti — "X ne Y ke baare me kya kaha?" — agar X ne Y ke baare me kabhi kuch kaha hi nahi, to hallucination zyada likely hai.

Factual consistency measure karne ke tareeke

AI as a judge: sabse straightforward — judge se poochho ki summary me source text se unsupported facts hain ya nahi. Liu et al. (2023) aur Luo et al. (2023) ne dikhaya ki GPT-3.5 aur GPT-4 factual consistency measure karne me pehle ke methods se behtar hain. TruthfulQA paper ka finetuned GPT-judge 90–96% accuracy se predict kar sakta hai ki statement ko insaan truthful manega ya nahi. (Note: Liu et al. ke prompt me ek typo tha — "Does the summary untruthful or misleading facts..." — paper se verbatim copy kiya gaya tha, jo dikhata hai ki prompts me galti karna kitna aasan hai.)

  • Self-verification — SelfCheckGPT (Manakul et al., 2023): assumption ye hai ki agar model ek hi response ke multiple versions generate kare aur woh aapas me disagree karein, to original output likely hallucinated hai. Response R ko N naye responses se compare karo. Kaam karta hai lekin mehenga hai — ek response evaluate karne ke liye bahut si AI queries chahiye.
  • Knowledge-augmented verification — SAFE (Wei et al., 2024, Google DeepMind): 4 steps — (1) response ko individual statements me todo, (2) har statement ko self-contained banao ("It opened in the 20th century" me "it" ko original subject se replace karo), (3) har statement ke liye fact-checking queries bana ke Google Search API pe bhejo, (4) AI se decide karwao ki statement research results se consistent hai ya nahi.
  • Textual entailment / NLI: premise (context) aur hypothesis (output) ke beech relation decide karo — entailment (hypothesis premise se infer ho sakta hai), contradiction (hypothesis premise se takrata hai), neutral (na entail karta hai na contradict). Example: context "Mary likes all fruits" — entailment: "Mary likes apples"; contradiction: "Mary hates oranges"; neutral: "Mary likes chickens". Entailment matlab factually consistent, contradiction matlab inconsistent.
  • Specialized scorers train karo: (premise, hypothesis) pair leke entailment/contradiction/neutral predict karne wala classifier — factual consistency ko classification task bana do. Example: DeBERTa-v3-base-mnli-fever-anli — 184M parameters, 764,000 annotated pairs pe trained.

TruthfulQA benchmark: 817 questions jo kuch insaan galat jawab dete hain kyunki unme false belief ya misconception hai — 38 categories (health, law, finance, politics). Iska apna specialized judge GPT-judge hai. GPT-3 ke false answers ke examples: "Coughing can help stop a heart attack", "The US government caused 9/11", "All AIs follow the Three Laws of Robotics". Human expert baseline 94% hai. Factual consistency RAG systems ke liye khaas taur pe crucial hai — generated response retrieved context se consistent hona chahiye (RAG Chapter 6 me detail me hai).

Safety

Safety ek umbrella term hai — toxicity aur biases samet sab tarah ke harm ke liye. Unsafe content aam taur pe in categories me aata hai:

  1. Inappropriate language — profanity aur explicit content.
  2. Harmful recommendations aur tutorials — jaise "bank rob karne ki step-by-step guide" ya self-destructive behaviour encourage karna.
  3. Hate speech — racist, sexist, homophobic aur doosri discriminatory baatein.
  4. Violence — threats aur graphic detail.
  5. Stereotypes — jaise hamesha nurses ke liye female names aur CEOs ke liye male names use karna.
  6. Political ya religious ideology ki taraf bias — model sirf ek ideology support karne wala content generate kare. Studies me GPT-4 zyada left-winged aur libertarian-leaning paya gaya, jabki Meta ka Llama zyada authoritarian (Feng et al., 2023).

General-purpose AI judges (GPT, Claude, Gemini) sahi prompt se bahut se harmful outputs detect kar lete hain, aur providers apne moderation tools bhi expose karte hain. Lekin toxicity detection ke liye specialized chhote models bhi hain jo faster aur cheaper hain — Facebook ka hate speech detection model, Skolkovo Institute ka toxicity classifier, Perspective API, aur Danish/Vietnamese jaise languages ke liye specialized models. Common benchmarks: RealToxicityPrompts (Gehman et al., 2020) — 100,000 naturally occurring prompts jo models se toxic output nikalne ki koshish karte hain; aur BOLD (Dhamala et al., 2021).

Instruction-following capability

Model instruction follow karne me kitna achha hai? Agar model instructions follow hi nahi karta, to tumhari instructions kitni bhi achhi hon, output kharab hoga. Example: tweet ka sentiment detect karke NEGATIVE / POSITIVE / NEUTRAL output karna hai — model sentiment samajhta hai lekin HAPPY aur ANGRY jaise outputs deta hai. Matlab domain capability hai, instruction-following kharab hai. Ye structured outputs (JSON, regex) ke liye khaas taur pe zaroori hai — downstream application ko sirf A, B ya C chahiye aur model "That's correct" de de to system toot jayega.

Instruction-following define aur measure karna mushkil hai kyunki ye domain capability ya generation capability se confuse ho jata hai — model se lục bát (Vietnamese verse form) poem likhne ko kaho aur woh fail ho jaye, to ye isliye ho sakta hai ki use lục bát aata hi nahi, ya isliye ki use samajh hi nahi aaya ki karna kya hai. Aur model ka performance instruction ki quality pe depend karta hai — model kharab hai ya instruction kharab, ye batana mushkil hai.

  • IFEval (Zhou et al., 2023, Google): sirf format pe focus — 25 types ki automatically verifiable instructions, jaise keyword include karna, keyword frequency, forbidden words, letter frequency, response language, number of paragraphs/words/sentences, postscript, placeholders, bullet points ki exact count, title, JSON format. Score = sahi follow ki gayi instructions ka fraction.
  • INFOBench (Qin et al., 2024): zyada broad — format ke saath content constraints ("sirf climate change pe discuss karo"), linguistic guidelines ("Victorian English use karo") aur style rules ("respectful tone use karo") bhi. Inhe automatically verify nahi kar sakte, isliye har instruction ke liye yes/no questions ki list banayi jaati hai (jaise hotel review questionnaire ke liye 3 questions: kya ye questionnaire hai? kya ye hotel guests ke liye hai? kya ye reviews likhne me helpful hai?). Instruction tabhi successful mani jati hai jab saare criteria meet hon. GPT-4 ko reasonably reliable aur cost-effective evaluator paya gaya — human experts se kam accurate, lekin Amazon Mechanical Turk annotators se zyada.

Dono benchmarks real-world instructions ka representative set include karne ki koshish karte hain, lekin bahut si common instructions miss karte hain. Apna khud ka benchmark curate karo — agar model ko YAML output chahiye to YAML instructions include karo; agar model ko "As a language model" nahi kehna to us instruction pe evaluate karo.

Roleplaying

Real-world instructions me sabse common types me se ek hai roleplaying — model se kisi fictional character ya persona ko assume karne ko kehna. Do purposes: (1) entertainment — gaming ya interactive storytelling me character play karna; (2) prompt engineering technique — output quality improve karna (Chapter 5). LMSYS ke 1 million conversations ke analysis me roleplaying 8th sabse common use case tha. Gaming NPCs, AI companions aur writing assistants ke liye khaas taur pe important hai.

Roleplaying evaluate karna automate karna mushkil hai. Benchmarks: RoleLLM (Wang et al., 2023) — similarity scores + AI judges; CharacterEval (Tu et al., 2024) — human annotators aur trained reward model se har aspect ko 5-point scale pe score. Agar tumhara AI koi role assume karta hai, to check karo ki woh character me rehta hai ya nahi — style aur knowledge dono pe. Example: Jackie Chan jaisa bolne wala model uski style capture kare aur usi ke knowledge pe based ho — aur negative knowledge check bhi zaroori hai: agar Jackie Chan Vietnamese nahi bolta, to model ko bhi nahi bolna chahiye, warna gaming me NPC galti se spoilers de dega. RoleLLM ke AI judge ka prompt models ko do criteria pe rank karta hai: (1) role speaking style kitni pronounced hai, (2) output me role se related knowledge aur memories kitni rich hain.

Cost aur latency

High-quality output dene wala model agar bahut slow aur mehenga hai to useful nahi hoga. Quality, latency aur cost ko balance karna padta hai — bahut si companies lower-quality model chun leti hain agar woh behtar cost aur latency de. Multiple objectives optimize karna Pareto optimization kehlata hai: pehle tay karo kis objective pe compromise nahi kar sakte, phir jo models woh requirement meet na karein unhe filter out karo, phir bache hue me se best chuno.

  • Latency metrics: time to first token, time per token, time between tokens, time per query — samajh lo ki tumhare liye kaunsa metric matter karta hai. Latency sirf model pe nahi, prompt aur sampling variables pe bhi depend karti hai — zyada tokens generate karne honge to total latency zyada hogi. Concise rehne ki instruction, stopping condition, ya Chapter 9 ki optimization techniques se control kar sakte ho.
  • Must-have vs nice-to-have: users se poochho to koi bhi lower latency ko na nahi kahega, lekin high latency aksar annoyance hoti hai, deal breaker nahi.
  • Model APIs: tokens ke hisaab se charge — input aur output tokens jitne zyada, utna mehenga. Input/output token count kam karke cost manage karo.
  • Self-hosting: cost compute hai. Log aksar sabse bada model chun lete hain jo unki machine me fit ho — GPU memory 16/24/48/80 GB hoti hai, isliye 7B ya 65B parameter wale models popular hain, coincidence nahi hai. APIs me per-token cost scale ke saath zyada nahi badalta, lekin self-hosting me scale badhne pe per-token cost bahut sasti ho sakti hai — agar cluster 1 billion tokens/day serve kar sakta hai to compute cost wahi rahega chahe 1 million serve karo ya 1 billion. Isliye alag scale pe API vs self-host ka decision dobara evaluate karna chahiye.

Table 4-3 me ek fictional application ke criteria ka example hai — cost per output token (< $30/1M tokens hard requirement, < $15 ideal), TPM (tokens per minute) > 1M, time to first token P90 < 200ms (ideal 100ms), total query time P90 < 1m (ideal 30s), overall quality Elo score > 1200 (ideal 1250, Chatbot Arena ranking), code generation pass@1 > 90% (HumanEval, ideal 95%), factual consistency internal metric > 0.8 (ideal 0.9). Scale wali row khaas taur pe API evaluate karte time important hai — service tumhare scale ko support kar sake.

Yaad rakho: Har criterion ka apna evaluation approach hota hai — MCQ se generation nahi napte, aur AI judge se har cheez nahi napte. Pehle criteria likho, phir har criterion ke liye sahi method chuno; ek hi method sab pe lagana galti hai.
SOURCESource: Huyen, AI Engineering, O'Reilly, Chapter 4 — Evaluate AI Systems

04.2Chapter 4 · Evaluate AI Systems

Model Selection — Workflow, Build vs Buy, Benchmarks

Best model ka sawaal galat sawaal hai — sahi sawaal hai tumhare application ke liye best model kaunsa hai. Criteria define karne ke baad models ko unhi criteria pe evaluate karo. Aur ye ek baar ka kaam nahi hai — har adaptation technique pe model selection dobara karna padta hai.

Model selection workflow — 4 steps

Prompt engineering me pehle strongest overall model se feasibility check karo, phir peeche jaa ke dekho ki chhota model chalega ya nahi. Finetuning me pehle chhote model se code test karo, phir hardware me fit hone wale sabse bade model ki taraf badho. Har technique me selection ke 2 steps hote hain: (1) best achievable performance pata karo, (2) models ko cost–performance axes pe map karke best value wala chuno.

Usse pehle hard attributes aur soft attributes me farak samjho. Hard attributes woh hain jinhe tum change nahi kar sakte ya karna impractical hai — licenses, training data, model size, privacy policy, control. Soft attributes woh hain jinhe improve kar sakte ho — accuracy, toxicity, factual consistency. Lekin soft attribute kitna improve hoga, ye balance karna tricky hai — ek baar accuracy pehle prompts pe 20% thi, task ko 2 steps me todne pe 70% ho gayi; doosri baar hafton ki tweaking ke baad bhi model usable nahi hua aur chhodna pada. Hard vs soft ka definition model aur use case dono pe depend karta hai — latency soft attribute hai agar model tumhare paas ho aur optimize kar sako, hard hai agar model kisi aur ka hosted ho.

  1. Filter karo: jin models ke hard attributes tumhare liye kaam nahi karte, unhe hata do. Ye list tumhari internal policies pe depend karti hai — commercial API use karna hai ya khud host karna hai.
  2. Public info se shortlist karo: benchmark performance aur leaderboard ranking se sabse promising models chuno — quality, latency aur cost balance karte hue.
  3. Apni evaluation pipeline se experiment karo: apne prompts aur metrics se best model dhoondho, phir se saare objectives balance karke.
  4. Production me monitor karo: failure detect karo aur feedback collect karke application improve karo (Chapter 10).

Ye 4 steps iterative hain — aage ke step ki nayi jaankari se pehle ke step ka decision badal sakta hai. Example: pehle open source host karna chahte the, lekin public aur private evaluation ke baad pata chala ki open source models woh performance de hi nahi sakte, to commercial API pe switch karna pada.

Open source, open weight aur licenses

"Open source model" term controversial ho gaya hai. Originally iska matlab tha — model download karke use kar sakte ho. Lekin kuch log kehte hain ki model ki performance largely training data pe depend karti hai, to model tabhi open hai jab training data bhi public ho. Open data se model ko scratch se retrain kar sakte ho, architecture/training process/data me change kar sakte ho, aur audit kar sakte ho (jaise model compromised ya illegally acquired data pe train to nahi hua).

  • Open weight: weights public hain, training data nahi. Open model: data bhi open hai. Is book me simplicity ke liye "open source" ka matlab hai — weights public hain, chahe data open ho ya na ho, license kaisa bhi ho.
  • Aaj ke zyada tar open source models sirf open weight hain — developers training data ki info jaan-boojh kar chhupate hain, kyunki usse public scrutiny aur lawsuits ka risk hai.
  • Licenses: MIT, Apache 2.0, GPL, BSD, Creative Commons ke alawa models ki apni unique licenses bhi hain — Llama 2 Community License, Llama 3 Community License, BigCode Open RAIL-M v1. Gemma aur Mistral-7B Apache 2.0 pe release hue. Har license ke apne conditions hote hain — ye 3 sawaal hamesha poochho: (1) kya commercial use allowed hai? (pehla Llama noncommercial license pe tha); (2) commercial use pe restrictions hain? (Llama 2/3: 700 million monthly active users se zyada pe Meta se special license chahiye); (3) kya model ke outputs se doosre models train kar sakte ho? (distillation — student model ko teacher ki nakal sikhana — Mistral ne pehle mana kiya phir license badal di, Llama licenses abhi bhi mana karti hain). Note: ek model ka output use karna allowed ho, phir bhi agar woh output ChatGPT se aaya hai aur ChatGPT ke terms mana karte hain, to tumne ChatGPT ke terms violate kiye — isliye data lineage jaanna zaroori hai.

Build vs Buy — 7 axes

Model ko users tak pahunchane ke liye kisi machine ko use host karke chalana padta hai — use inference service kehte hain, aur jisse users interact karte hain use model API kehte hain. Developer model ko open source kar sakta hai, API ke peeche rakh sakta hai, ya dono. Cohere aur Mistral dono karte hain; OpenAI commercial models ke liye famous hai lekin GPT-2 aur CLIP open source kiye. Aam taur pe providers apne kamzor models open source karte hain aur best models paywall ke peeche rakhte hain. Model APIs model providers (OpenAI, Anthropic), cloud providers (Azure, GCP) ya third-party providers (Databricks Mosaic, Anyscale) se mil sakti hain — same model alag APIs pe alag features, constraints aur pricing ke saath ho sakta hai, aur performance me halka farak bhi ho sakta hai, isliye API switch karte time thorough test karo. Commercial models sirf APIs se milte hain; open source models kisi bhi API provider se mil sakte hain.

Host karna hai ya API use karni hai — ye 7 axes pe depend karta hai:

  • Data privacy: strict privacy policy wali companies data bahar nahi bhej sakti — Samsung employees ne proprietary info ChatGPT me daal ke leak kar di thi, aur Samsung ne May 2023 me ChatGPT ban kar diya. Kuch deshon ke laws data ko border ke bahar bhejne se rokte hain. Risk ye bhi hai ki API provider tumhare data se apne models train kare — policies badal sakti hain (Zoom ne Aug 2023 me chupke se terms badal ke user data se training ki permission le li thi). Studies ke mutabik models training samples memorize kar sakte hain — Hugging Face ka StarCoder apne training set ka 8% memorize karta hai — aur memorized samples accidentally leak ya exploit ho sakte hain.
  • Data lineage aur copyright: zyada tar models ki training data pe transparency nahi hai — Gemini ki technical report me performance detail me thi, training data ke baare me kuch nahi. USPTO ne 2024 me kaha ki AI-assisted inventions categorically unpatentable nahi hain, lekin patentability ispe depend karti hai ki human contribution significant hai ya nahi. Agar model copyrighted data pe train hua aur tum usse product banao, to apne product ki IP defend kar paoge ya nahi, ye unclear hai — gaming/movie studios isliye hesitate karte hain. Kuch companies fully open models ki taraf jaati hain taaki community data inspect kar sake (lekin foundation-model size ka dataset thoroughly inspect karna practically mushkil hai). Doosri companies commercial models chun leti hain — open source models ke paas limited legal resources hote hain, aur copyright infringe karne wale open model ko use karne pe case tum pe aayega; commercial contract tumhe protect kar sakta hai.
  • Performance: MMLU pe open source aur proprietary models ka gap kam ho raha hai, lekin incentives aise nahi hain ki strongest model open source ho — strongest model ho to use khud capitalize karoge ya doosron ko de doge? Isliye strongest open source model foreseeable future me strongest proprietary model se peeche rahega. Ek aur reason: open source developers ko users se feedback nahi milta, jaise commercial models ko milta hai — model open source hone ke baad pata hi nahi chalta ki use kaise use ho raha hai aur wild me kaise perform kar raha hai.
  • Functionality: scalability, function calling (RAG/agents ke liye zaroori), structured outputs (JSON), output guardrails — ye sab implement karna mushkil aur time-consuming hai, isliye companies API providers ki taraf jaati hain. Lekin API pe sirf wahi functionalities milti hain jo provider de — logprobs bahut useful hain (classification, evaluation, interpretability) lekin bahut si commercial APIs logprobs expose nahi karti ya limited karti hain, kyunki logprobs se unke models replicate ho sakte hain. Finetuning bhi sirf tab jab provider finetuning API de — open source model ko khud finetune kar sakte ho ya kisi service se karwa sakte ho. Commercial provider sirf kuch types ki finetuning support kar sakta hai, saari nahi (Chapter 7).
  • Cost — API cost vs engineering cost: API usage ke hisaab se charge karti hai, heavy usage pe bahut mehenga ho sakta hai. Lekin khud host karna bhi sasta nahi — model optimize karna, inference service scale aur maintain karna, guardrails banana — talent, time aur engineering effort chahiye. API mehenga hai, engineering usse bhi mehenga ho sakta hai. API ki SLA pe depend karna bhi padta hai — early startups ki APIs unreliable ho sakti hain. Standard API follow karne wala model chuno taaki model swap karna aasan ho (aaj bahut se providers OpenAI ki API mimic karte hain), aur achhi community support wala model prefer karo — koi issue aaye to kisi aur ko pehle aa chuka hoga aur solution share kiya hoga.
  • Control, access aur transparency: a16z ke 2024 study me enterprises open source isliye chahte hain kyunki control aur customizability chahiye. API use karte ho to provider ke terms, conditions aur rate limits ke under ho; model ko tweak nahi kar sakte. Proprietary models over-censor karne ki taraf jhukte hain — safety guardrails ke wajah se real faces generate karne se mana kar sakte hain, ya 3D character ko "As an AI model, I don't have physical abilities" bolna pada (Convai ne isliye open source models finetune kiye). Commercial model ko freeze nahi kar sakte jaise open source ko kar sakte ho — models frequently update hote hain, changes announce bhi nahi hote, prompts kaam karna band kar dete hain aur pata hi nahi chalta. Provider tumhara use case/industry/country support karna band kar sakta hai (Italy ne 2023 me OpenAI ko briefly ban kiya tha), ya business hi band kar sakta hai.
  • On-device deployment: device pe model chalana hai to third-party API out of question hai — bina reliable internet wale areas, ya privacy (saara data device pe rahe) ke liye local run desirable hai.

Public benchmarks ko navigate karna

Hazaaron benchmarks hain — Google ke BIG-bench me hi 214 benchmarks hain. Jaise naye use cases aate hain, naye benchmarks bante hain; aur jaise models improve hote hain, purane benchmarks saturate ho jaate hain, to naye chahiye. Benchmarks chalane me madad karne wala tool evaluation harness hota hai — EleutherAI ka lm-evaluation-harness 400+ benchmarks support karta hai, OpenAI ke evals me ~500 benchmarks hain.

Leaderboard banane ke 2 sawaal: kaunse benchmarks include karein, aur unke results ko aggregate karke rank kaise karein? Public leaderboards compute constraint ki wajah se sirf chhote se benchmark set use kar pate hain — HELM Lite ne MS MARCO (information retrieval) isliye chhoda kyunki mehenga hai; Hugging Face ne HumanEval isliye chhoda kyunki compute bahut lagta hai. Hugging Face Open LLM Leaderboard 2023 me 4 benchmarks se shuru hua, saal ke end tak 6 ho gaye: ARC-C, MMLU, HellaSwag, TruthfulQA, WinoGrande, GSM-8K. Stanford HELM ne 10 benchmarks use kiye, jinme se sirf 2 (MMLU, GSM-8K) Hugging Face wale se overlap karte the — baaki 8 the MATH, LegalBench, MedQA, WMT 2014, NarrativeQA, OpenBookQA, aur Natural Questions (2 settings). Leaderboards coverage aur benchmark count ko balance karne ki koshish karte hain, lekin "coverage" ka matlab kya hai aur 6 ya 10 pe kyun rukte hain, ye clear nahi — HELM me medical aur legal kyun hain lekin general science kyun nahi? Do math tests kyun hain lekin coding kyun nahi? Summarization, tool use, toxicity kyun nahi? Ye criticism nahi hai, ye dikhata hai ki benchmark selection kitna mushkil hai.

Benchmark correlation: agar 2 benchmarks perfectly correlated hain to dono nahi chahiye — strongly correlated benchmarks biases ko exaggerate karte hain. Jan 2024 me Hugging Face ke 6 benchmarks ka Pearson correlation: WinoGrande–MMLU 0.9011, ARC-C–WinoGrande 0.8856, ARC-C–MMLU 0.8672 (teeno reasoning test karte hain, isliye strongly correlated), jabki TruthfulQA doosron se sirf moderately correlated (0.42–0.55) — matlab reasoning/math improve karne se truthfulness hamesha improve nahi hoti.

Aggregation: Hugging Face saare benchmarks ka average leti hai — matlab har benchmark ko equal weight, jaise TruthfulQA pe 80% aur GSM-8K pe 80% barabar mushkil hon (jabki TruthfulQA pe 80% zyada mushkil ho sakta hai), aur truthfulness ko grade-school math jitna hi weight. HELM averaging ki jagah mean win rate use karta hai — ek model kitni baar doosre model se behtar score karta hai, saare scenarios me average. June 2024 me Hugging Face ne leaderboard phir update kiya — GSM-8K ki jagah MATH lvl 5, MMLU ki jagah MMLU-PRO, aur naye benchmarks GPQA (graduate-level Q&A), MuSR (multi-step reasoning), BBH (BIG-bench Hard) aur IFEval add kiye. Ye benchmarks bhi jald saturate honge — benchmarks grade-level se graduate-level tak pahunch gaye hain sirf 2 saalon me.

Custom leaderboard: apne application ke liye basically apni private leaderboard bana rahe ho. Coding agent ke liye code benchmarks dhoondho, writing assistant ke liye creative writing benchmarks. Naye benchmarks aate rehte hain aur purane saturate hote hain, to latest dhoondho — aur check karo ki benchmark reliable hai ya nahi, kyunki koi bhi benchmark bana ke publish kar sakta hai, aur woh wohi measure na kar raha ho jo tum soch rahe ho.

Kya OpenAI ke models kharab ho rahe hain?

Har baar OpenAI models update karta hai, log complain karte hain ki models kharab ho gaye. Stanford aur UC Berkeley ki study (Chen et al., 2023) me March 2023 se June 2023 ke beech GPT-3.5 aur GPT-4 ka performance kai benchmarks pe significantly change hua. Agar OpenAI jaan-boojh kar kharab models release nahi karta, to reason kya hai? Ek reason: evaluation mushkil hai, aur kisi ko bhi, OpenAI ko bhi, pakka nahi pata ki model behtar ho raha hai ya kharab. Doosra: same model update kuch applications ko degrade karta hai aur kuch ko improve — GPT-3.5-turbo-0301 se 1106 pe migrate karne se Voiceflow ki intent classification 10% gir gayi, lekin GoDaddy ka customer support chatbot improve ho gaya. Isse ye reinforce hota hai ki best overall model tumhare application ke liye best ho, ye zaroori nahi.

Saare models ke saare benchmarks pe public scores nahi hote — score na ho to evaluation khud chalani padegi, aur woh mehenga hai: Stanford ne 30 models ko full HELM suite pe evaluate karne me ~$80,000–$100,000 kharch kiye ($38,000 commercial APIs + 19,500 GPU hours). Scores alag units/scales me hote hain (accuracy, F1, BLEU), to unhe weigh karna padega ki tumhare liye kaunsa benchmark kitna important hai. Yaad rakho: public benchmarks ka goal hai bade pool se chhota sa promising subset chunna, taaki unpe apne benchmarks se rigorous experiment kar sako — public benchmarks tumhare application ki needs ko perfectly represent nahi karte.

Data contamination

Data contamination (data leakage, training on the test set, ya seedha cheating) tab hoti hai jab model usi data pe train hua ho jispe use evaluate kiya ja raha hai — model answers memorize karke high score le leta hai, bina useful hue. Rylan Schaeffer ne 2023 ke satirical paper "Pretraining on the Test Set Is All You Need" me dikhaya — sirf benchmark data pe train karke 1-million-parameter model ne near-perfect scores le liye aur bahut bade models ko beat kar diya.

  • Kaise hoti hai: zyada tar unintentional — internet se scrape kiya gaya training data accidentally public benchmarks ko bhi pull kar leta hai. Benchmark data jo model ki training se pehle publish hua, woh likely training data me shamil hai — isliye benchmarks jaldi saturate hote hain. Indirect bhi ho sakti hai — training aur evaluation data same source se aaye (jaise math textbooks training me, aur unhi textbooks ke questions benchmark me). Kabhi intentional bhi hoti hai achhe reason se — best model chunne ke baad use benchmark data pe aur train karna taaki users ko behtar model mile, lekin phir released model contaminated hai aur users use un benchmarks pe evaluate nahi kar sakte.
  • Detect karna: n-gram overlapping — agar evaluation sample ka 13-token sequence training data me bhi hai to sample "dirty" hai (accurate lekin time-consuming, expensive, aur training data ke access ke bina impossible). Perplexity — agar model ki evaluation data pe perplexity unusually low hai (text aasani se predict kar leta hai), to ho sakta hai usne data pehle dekha ho (kam accurate lekin sasta).
  • Handle karna: pehle ML textbooks kehte the evaluation samples ko training data se hata do. Foundation models ke saath zyada tar logon ke paas training data ka control hi nahi hai — aur high-quality benchmark data performance improve bhi karta hai, to use hatana bhi nahi chahte. Model developers ka common practice hai apne care wale benchmarks ko training se pehle hata dena, aur report karte time disclose karna ki benchmark ka kitna percent training data me hai aur clean samples pe performance kya hai — lekin bahut log ye effort karte hi nahi. OpenAI ne GPT-3 me paya ki 13 benchmarks ka kam se kam 40% training data me tha. Leaderboard hosts standard deviation plot karke outliers spot karte hain; public benchmarks ko apna kuch data private rakhna chahiye aur private hold-out data pe automatic evaluation ka tool dena chahiye.

Public benchmarks bure models ko filter karne me madad karte hain, lekin tumhare application ke liye best model dhoondhne me nahi. Uske liye apni evaluation pipeline chahiye — jo is chapter ka aakhri section hai.

Yaad rakho: Public leaderboard pe top rank ka matlab ye nahi ki woh model tumhare kaam ke liye best hai. Leaderboard sirf shortlist banane ke liye hai — final decision hamesha apne data aur apne metrics se karo, aur contamination ko hamesha dhyaan me rakho.
SOURCESource: Huyen, AI Engineering, O'Reilly, Chapter 4 — Evaluate AI Systems
