06.1Chapter 6 · RAG and Agents

RAG Architecture aur Retrieval

RAG system ke 2 components hote hain — retriever jo external memory sources se information retrieve karta hai, aur generator jo retrieved information ke basis pe response generate karta hai (Figure 6-2). RAG system ki success uske retriever ki quality pe depend karti hai.

RAG architecture — indexing aur querying

Original RAG paper (Lewis et al.) me retriever aur generative model ko saath me train kiya gaya tha. Aaj ke RAG systems me ye 2 components aksar alag se train hote hain, aur bahut si teams off-the-shelf retrievers aur models se apne RAG systems banati hain. Lekin poore RAG system ko end-to-end finetune karne se performance significantly improve ho sakti hai.

Retriever ke 2 main functions hain: indexing (data ko aise process karo ki baad me jaldi retrieve ho sake) aur querying (query bhej ke usse relevant data retrieve karo). Data ko kaise index karna hai, ye ispe depend karta hai ki use baad me kaise retrieve karna hai.

Example workflow: external memory ek database hai documents ki — company ke memos, contracts, meeting notes. Ek document 10 tokens ka bhi ho sakta hai aur 1 million tokens ka bhi. Poore documents retrieve karna context ko arbitrarily lamba bana dega, isliye har document ko manageable chunks me split karo (chunking strategies aage discuss hain). Har query ke liye goal hai us query se most relevant data chunks retrieve karna. Phir minor post-processing se retrieved chunks ko user prompt ke saath join karke final prompt banaya jata hai, jo generative model ko feed hota hai. Is chapter me "document" term se "document" aur "chunk" dono refer hote hain — technically ek document ka chunk bhi ek document hai, aur ye classical NLP aur information retrieval (IR) ki terminology se consistent hai.

Retrieval algorithms — term-based vs embedding-based

Retrieval RAG ke liye unique nahi hai — information retrieval century-old idea hai (1920s me Emanuel Goldberg ke "statistical machine" patents se), aur search engines, recommender systems, log analytics ki backbone hai. Retrieval ka core kaam hai documents ko query se unki relevance ke hisaab se rank karna. Algorithms isme differ karte hain ki relevance scores kaise compute karte hain.

Literature me retrieval ko sparse vs dense me divide kiya jata hai — sparse retrievers sparse vectors use karte hain (zyada tar values 0), dense retrievers dense vectors (zyada tar values non-zero). Lekin book term-based vs embedding-based division use karti hai, kyunki SPLADE (Sparse Lexical and Expansion) jaise algorithms sparse embeddings use karte hain — sparse/dense division me SPLADE term-based algorithms ke saath group ho jata hai, jabki uski operations, strengths aur weaknesses dense embedding retrieval ke zyada similar hain.

Term-based retrieval (lexical retrieval)

Sabse straightforward tareeka hai keywords se relevant documents dhoondhna. Query "AI engineering" ho to woh saare documents retrieve karo jinme "AI engineering" hai. Lekin 2 problems hain: (1) bahut se documents me woh term ho sakta hai, aur model ke context me saare fit nahi honge — heuristic hai woh documents include karo jinme term sabse zyada baar aaya ho (assumption: term jitni baar aaye, document utna relevant; term ke document me aane ki count ko term frequency, TF kehte hain); (2) prompt lamba ho sakta hai aur usme bahut se terms ho sakte hain, kuch zyada important hote hain — "Easy-to-follow recipes for Vietnamese food to cook at home" me 9 terms hain, lekin "vietnamese" aur "recipes" "for" aur "at" se zyada informative hain. Intuition: jitne zyada documents me ek term ho, utna kam informative hai — term ki importance us document count ke inversely proportional hai, is metric ko inverse document frequency, IDF kehte hain. 10 documents hon aur 5 me ek term ho to us term ki IDF = 10/5 = 2. IDF jitna high, term utna important.

TF-IDF in dono metrics ko combine karta hai: document D ka query Q ke liye score = sum over query terms of IDF(t) × f(t, D), jahan f(t, D) term t ki document D me frequency hai aur IDF(t) = log(N / C(t)), N total documents aur C(t) woh documents jinme t hai.

  • Elasticsearch (Shay Banon, 2010, Lucene pe built): inverted index naam ki data structure use karta hai — terms se un documents ka dictionary jinme woh terms hain (Table 6-1: "banana" 2 documents me — (10, 3), (5, 2) — matlab document 10 me 3 baar, document 5 me 2 baar). Index me term frequency aur document count bhi store ho sakta hai, jo TF-IDF scores compute karne me madad karta hai.
  • Okapi BM25 (Robertson et al., 1980s, 25th generation of Best Matching): TF-IDF ka modification — term frequency scores ko document length se normalize karta hai, kyunki lambe documents me term aane aur high TF hone ki possibility zyada hoti hai. BM25 aur uske variants (BM25+, BM25F) aaj bhi industry me widely use hote hain aur modern sophisticated algorithms ke against formidable baselines hain. Perplexity ke CEO Aravind Srinivas ne tweet kiya tha ki "Making a genuine improvement over BM25 or full-text search is hard".
  • Tokenization: query ko individual terms me todne ka process. Simplest method hai words me split karna, lekin multi-word terms ka matlab kho sakta hai — "hot dog" split hoke "hot" aur "dog" ho jaye to dono me original term ka matlab nahi rehta. Mitigation: common n-grams ko terms treat karo. Lowercase karna, punctuation hatana aur stop words ("the", "and", "is") hatana bhi common hai — term-based solutions ye automatically handle karte hain. NLTK, spaCy aur Stanford CoreNLP jaise classical NLP packages bhi tokenization offer karte hain. N-gram overlap se bhi retrieve kar sakte ho (Chapter 4 me lexical similarity) — ye tab best kaam karta hai jab query aur documents similar length ke hon; documents bahut lambe hon to unme query ke n-grams hone ki likelihood badh jati hai aur truly relevant documents distinguish karna mushkil ho jata hai.

Embedding-based retrieval (semantic retrieval)

Term-based retrieval relevance ko lexical level pe compute karta hai, semantic level pe nahi — text ka appearance uska meaning capture nahi karta. Query "transformer architecture" pe electric device ya Transformers movie ke documents aa sakte hain. Embedding-based retrievers documents ko is basis pe rank karte hain ki unka meaning query ke meaning se kitna closely align karta hai — isse semantic retrieval bhi kehte hain.

Indexing me ek extra function hai: original data chunks ko embeddings me convert karna. Jahan generated embeddings store hote hain use vector database kehte hain. Querying 2 steps me hoti hai (Figure 6-3): (1) embedding model query ko embedding me convert karta hai — wahi embedding model jo indexing me use hua tha; (2) retriever k data chunks fetch karta hai jinki embeddings query embedding ke closest hon. k kitna ho, ye use case, generative model aur query pe depend karta hai. Real-world semantic retrieval systems me aur components bhi ho sakte hain — reranker (retrieved candidates ko rerank karne ke liye) aur caches (latency kam karne ke liye). Embedding-based retriever tabhi kaam karta hai jab embedding model achha ho.

Vector search: vector database me store karna easy part hai, hard part hai vector search — query embedding ke close vectors dhoondhna aur return karna. Vectors ko aise index aur store karna padta hai ki vector search fast aur efficient ho. Vector search generative AI ke liye unique nahi hai — search, recommendation, data organization, clustering, fraud detection — har application me use hota hai jahan embeddings use hote hain. Aam taur pe ise nearest-neighbor search problem ke roop me frame kiya jata hai — query ke k nearest vectors dhoondho.

  • Naive kNN (k-nearest neighbors): (1) query embedding aur database ke saare vectors ke beech similarity scores compute karo (jaise cosine similarity), (2) saare vectors ko similarity se rank karo, (3) top k return karo. Precise hai lekin computationally heavy aur slow — sirf chhote datasets ke liye use karo.
  • ANN (approximate nearest neighbor): bade datasets ke liye vector search typically ANN algorithms se hoti hai. Popular libraries: FAISS (Facebook AI Similarity Search, Johnson et al., 2017), Google ka ScaNN (Scalable Nearest Neighbors, Sun et al., 2020), Spotify ka Annoy (Bernhardsson, 2013), aur Hnswlib (Malkov aur Yashunin, 2016). Application developers aam taur pe vector search khud implement nahi karenge, isliye sirf quick overview: vector databases vectors ko buckets, trees ya graphs me organize karte hain; algorithms isme differ karte hain ki similar vectors ke paas hone ki likelihood kaise badhate hain; vectors ko quantize (precision kam) ya sparse bhi kar sakte hain taaki kaam computationally sasta ho.
  • LSH (locality-sensitive hashing) (Indyk aur Motwani, 1999): similar vectors ko same buckets me hash karke similarity search fast karta hai — accuracy ke badle efficiency. FAISS aur Annoy me implemented hai.
  • HNSW (Hierarchical Navigable Small World) (Malkov aur Yashunin, 2016): multi-layer graph banata hai jahan nodes vectors hain aur edges similar vectors ko connect karte hain — graph edges traverse karke nearest-neighbor search hoti hai. FAISS aur Milvus me implemented hai.
  • Product Quantization (Jégou et al., 2011): har vector ko multiple subvectors me decompose karke bahut simple lower-dimensional representation me reduce karta hai — distances lower-dimensional representations se compute hote hain, jo bahut faster hai. FAISS ka key component hai aur lagbhag saari popular vector search libraries me supported hai.
  • IVF (inverted file index) (Sivic aur Zisserman, 2003): K-means clustering se similar vectors ko same cluster me organize karta hai — aam taur pe clusters aise set karte hain ki har cluster me average 100–10,000 vectors hon. Querying me query embedding ke closest cluster centroids dhoondho, un clusters ke vectors candidate neighbors ban jate hain. Product quantization ke saath IVF FAISS ki backbone banata hai.
  • Annoy (Approximate Nearest Neighbors Oh Yeah) (Bernhardsson, 2013): tree-based approach — multiple binary trees banata hai, har tree vectors ko random criteria se clusters me split karta hai (jaise randomly line draw karke 2 branches me split). Search me in trees ko traverse karke candidate neighbors gather karte hain. Spotify ne implementation open source ki hai.
  • Aur bhi algorithms hain — Microsoft ka SPTAG (Space Partition Tree And Graph) aur FLANN (Fast Library for Approximate Nearest Neighbors). Vector search ke baare me aur seekhne ke liye Zilliz ki excellent series hai. Aur dhyaan rakho: vector databases RAG ke rise ke saath apni category bane, lekin koi bhi database jo vectors store kar sakta hai, use vector database kaha ja sakta hai — bahut se traditional databases ne vector storage aur vector search support extend kiya hai ya karenge.

Retrieval algorithms compare karna

Term-based retrieval indexing aur query dono me embedding-based se bahut faster hai — term extraction embedding generation se faster hai, aur term se documents map karna nearest-neighbor search se kam computationally expensive hai. Term-based out of the box achha kaam karta hai — Elasticsearch aur BM25 ne bahut si search/retrieval applications power ki hain — lekin simplicity ka matlab hai kam components jinhe tweak karke performance improve kar sako. Embedding-based retrieval ko time ke saath significantly improve kar sakte ho — embedding model aur retriever ko alag se, saath me, ya generative model ke saath finetune karke — aur term-based se outperform kar sakta hai. Lekin data ko embeddings me convert karne se keywords obscure ho sakte hain, jaise specific error codes (EADDRNOTAVAIL (99)) ya product names, jisse unhe baad me search karna mushkil ho jata hai — is limitation ko term-based retrieval ke saath combine karke address kar sakte ho (hybrid search, aage).

Retriever ki quality retrieved data ki quality se evaluate hoti hai. RAG evaluation frameworks me 2 metrics common hain: context precision (retrieved documents me se kitne percent query se relevant hain — context relevance bhi kehte hain) aur context recall (query se relevant saare documents me se kitne percent retrieve hue). Compute karne ke liye evaluation set curate karo — test queries aur documents ki list; har test query ke liye har test document ko relevant ya not relevant annotate karo (humans ya AI judges se); phir precision aur recall compute karo. Production me kuch RAG frameworks sirf context precision support karte hain, context recall nahi — context recall ke liye database ke saare documents ki har query se relevance annotate karni padti hai; context precision simple hai — sirf retrieved documents ko query se compare karna hai, jo AI judge kar sakta hai. Agar retrieved documents ki ranking matter karti hai (zyada relevant documents pehle rank hone chahiye) to metrics use karo — NDCG (normalized discounted cumulative gain), MAP (Mean Average Precision) aur MRR (Mean Reciprocal Rank).

Semantic retrieval ke liye embeddings ki quality bhi evaluate karni hai — Chapter 3 ke hisaab se embeddings achhe hain agar zyada similar documents ki embeddings closer hon. MTEB benchmark (Muennighoff et al., 2023) embeddings ko broad range ke tasks pe evaluate karta hai — retrieval, classification, clustering. Retriever ko poore RAG system ke context me bhi evaluate karo — ultimately retriever achha hai agar woh system ko high-quality answers generate karne me madad kare (generative outputs ki evaluation Chapters 3 aur 4 me hai). Semantic retrieval pursue karna worth hai ya nahi, ye cost aur latency priorities pe depend karta hai — RAG latency ka zyada hissa output generation se aata hai, khaas taur pe lambe outputs ke liye, to query embedding generation aur vector search ki added latency total ke comparison me minimal ho sakti hai — phir bhi user experience pe impact pad sakta hai. Cost bhi concern hai — embeddings generate karna paisa leta hai, khaas taur pe agar data frequently change hota hai aur embeddings regenerate karne padte hain (100 million documents ke embeddings roz generate karna socho!). Vector storage aur vector search queries bhi expensive ho sakte hain — kisi company ki vector database spending uski model API spending ka one-fifth ya half bhi ho sakti hai.

Table 6-2 side-by-side comparison: term-based — querying speed much faster, performance typically strong out of the box lekin improve karna mushkil, term ambiguity se galat documents retrieve ho sakte hain, cost much cheaper. Embedding-based — query embedding generation aur vector search slow ho sakte hain, finetuning se term-based ko outperform kar sakta hai, semantics pe focus karne se zyada natural queries allow karta hai, embeddings/vector storage/vector search expensive ho sakte hain.

Indexing vs querying trade-off: index jitna detailed, retrieval utna accurate, lekin indexing slow aur memory-consuming. Detailed index jaise HNSW high accuracy aur fast query times deta hai lekin build karne me significant time aur memory chahiye; simpler index jaise LSH jaldi aur kam memory me banta hai lekin queries slow aur kam accurate hoti hain. ANN-Benchmarks website alag ANN algorithms ko multiple datasets pe 4 metrics se compare karti hai: recall (nearest neighbors ka kitna fraction mila), QPS (queries per second — high-traffic applications ke liye crucial), build time (index build karne ka time — frequent updates ke liye important), index size (scalability aur storage ke liye). BEIR (Thakur et al., 2021) retrieval ke liye evaluation harness hai — 14 common retrieval benchmarks pe retrieval systems support karta hai. Summary: RAG system ki quality ko component by component aur end to end — dono tareeke se evaluate karo: (1) retrieval quality, (2) final RAG outputs, (3) embeddings (embedding-based retrieval ke liye).

Retrieval algorithms combine karna — hybrid search

Alag retrieval algorithms ke distinct advantages ki wajah se production retrieval system typically kai approaches combine karta hai. Term-based aur embedding-based retrieval combine karna hybrid search kehlata hai. Algorithms ko sequence me use kar sakte ho: pehle cheap, less precise retriever (jaise term-based) candidates fetch karta hai, phir zyada precise lekin zyada expensive mechanism (jaise k-nearest neighbors) un candidates me se best dhoondhta hai — is doosre step ko reranking kehte hain. Example: term "transformer" ho to pehle saare documents fetch karo jinme "transformer" hai — electric device, neural architecture ya movie, koi bhi ho — phir vector search se unme se woh dhoondho jo tumhari transformer query se actually related hain. Doosra example: query "Who's responsible for the most sales to X?" — pehle keyword X se X se associated saare documents fetch karo, phir vector search se "Who's responsible for the most sales?" se associated context retrieve karo.

Algorithms ko parallel me ensemble ke roop me bhi use kar sakte ho — retriever documents ko relevance scores se rank karta hai; multiple retrievers se candidates ek saath fetch karo, phir alag rankings combine karke final ranking banao. Rankings combine karne ka ek algorithm hai reciprocal rank fusion (RRF) (Cormack et al., 2009): har document ko uski ranking ke basis pe score milta hai — pehle rank pe ho to score 1/1 = 1, doosre pe ho to 1/2 = 0.5. Document ka final score saare retrievers ke scores ka sum hai — ek retriever pe pehle aur doosre pe doosre rank pe ho to score 1 + 0.5 = 1.5 (ye oversimplification hai). Actual formula: Score(D) = sum over i of 1 / (k + r_i(D)), jahan n ranked lists ki sankhya hai, r_i(D) retriever i ke hisaab se document ka rank hai, aur k ek constant hai jo division by zero avoid karta hai aur lower-ranked documents ke influence ko control karta hai — typical value k = 60.

Retrieval optimization — 4 tactics

1. Chunking strategy

Data ko kaise index karna hai, ye ispe depend karta hai ki use baad me kaise retrieve karna hai. Sabse simple strategy: documents ko equal length ke chunks me split karo — characters, words, sentences ya paragraphs ke hisaab se (jaise 2,048 characters ya 512 words ke chunks, ya har chunk me fixed number of sentences, jaise 20 sentences, ya har paragraph apna chunk). Documents ko recursively bhi split kar sakte ho — pehle sections me, section lamba ho to paragraphs me, paragraph lamba ho to sentences me — isse related texts arbitrarily tootne ka chance kam hota hai. Specific documents ke liye creative strategies bhi hain — alag programming languages ke liye special splitters, Q&A documents ko question-answer pair ke hisaab se split karna (har pair ek chunk), Chinese texts ko English texts se alag tareeke se split karna.

Bina overlap ke split karne pe chunks important context ke beech me cut ho sakte hain — text "I left my wife a note" ko "I left my wife" aur "a note" me split karo to dono me se koi bhi original text ki key information convey nahi karta. Overlapping ensure karta hai ki boundary ki important information kam se kam ek chunk me ho — chunk size 2,048 characters ho to overlap 20 characters rakh sakte ho. Chunk size generative model ki maximum context length se zyada nahi honi chahiye; embedding-based approach me chunk size embedding model ki context limit se bhi zyada nahi honi chahiye. Tokens se bhi chunk kar sakte ho — generative model ke tokenizer se documents tokenize karo, phir tokens ko boundaries bana ke split karo — isse downstream models ke saath kaam karna aasan hota hai, lekin downside hai ki agar doosre generative model pe switch karo jiska tokenizer alag hai to data reindex karna padega.

Chunk sizes matter karte hain: chhota chunk size zyada diverse information allow karta hai — chunk size half karo to context me double chunks fit honge, model ko wider range ki information milegi aur behtar answer de payega. Lekin chhote chunks se important information loss ho sakta hai — document me topic X ke baare me information poore document me hai, lekin X sirf pehle half me mention hua hai, to document ko 2 chunks me split karne pe second half retrieve nahi hoga aur model uski information use nahi kar payega. Chhote chunks computational overhead bhi badhate hain — embedding-based retrieval me chunk size half karne ka matlab double chunks index karne hain, double embedding vectors generate aur store karne hain, aur vector search space double bada hoga, jisse query speed kam hogi. Koi universal best chunk size ya overlap size nahi hai — experiment karke dhoondho ki tumhare liye kya kaam karta hai.

2. Reranking

Retriever ki initial document rankings ko aur accurate banane ke liye rerank karo — khaas taur pe jab retrieved documents ki sankhya kam karni ho, ya to model ke context me fit karne ke liye ya input tokens kam karne ke liye. Common pattern "Combining retrieval algorithms" me discuss hua: cheap less precise retriever candidates fetch karta hai, phir zyada precise expensive mechanism unhe rerank karta hai. Documents ko time ke basis pe bhi rerank kar sakte ho — recent data ko higher weight do — time-sensitive applications ke liye useful hai, jaise news aggregation, emails ke saath chat, ya stock market analysis. Context reranking traditional search reranking se isme alag hai ki exact position kam critical hai — search me rank (pehla ya paanchva) crucial hai; context reranking me documents ka order abhi bhi matter karta hai kyunki woh affect karta hai ki model unhe kitni achhi tarah process karta hai (models beginning aur end ke documents ko behtar samajhte hain, Chapter 5) — lekin jab tak document include hai, uske order ka impact search ranking ke comparison me kam significant hai.

3. Query rewriting

Query rewriting ko query reformulation, query normalization aur kabhi query expansion bhi kehte hain. Conversation example: User: "When was the last time John Doe bought something from us?" AI: "John last bought a Fruity Fedora hat from us two weeks ago, on January 3, 2030." User: "How about Emily Doe?" — aakhri question context ke bina ambiguous hai; is query ko verbatim retrieve karne ke liye use karo to likely irrelevant results milenge. Query ko rewrite karna chahiye taaki woh reflect kare ki user asal me kya poochh raha hai — nayi query apne aap me sense banani chahiye: "When was the last time Emily Doe bought something from us?"

Query rewriting RAG ke liye unique nahi hai — traditional search engines me ye heuristics se kiya jata hai; AI applications me doosre AI models se bhi kar sakte ho, aise prompt se: "Given the following conversation, rewrite the last user input to reflect what the user is actually asking" (Figure 6-4 me ChatGPT ne query rewrite ki). Query rewriting complicated ho sakta hai, khaas taur pe jab identity resolution ya doosri knowledge chahiye — user poochhe "How about his wife?" to pehle database query karke pata karna padega ki uski wife kaun hai; agar woh information nahi hai to rewriting model ko acknowledge karna chahiye ki ye query solvable nahi hai, naam hallucinate karke galat jawab dene ki jagah.

4. Contextual retrieval

Idea hai har chunk ko relevant context se augment karna taaki relevant chunks retrieve karna aasan ho jaye. Simple technique: chunk ko metadata se augment karo — tags aur keywords. Ecommerce me product ko uski description aur reviews se augment kar sakte ho; images aur videos ko unke titles ya captions se query kar sakte ho. Metadata me chunk se automatically extracted entities bhi shamil ho sakti hain — document me specific terms hon jaise error code EADDRNOTAVAIL (99), to unhe document ke metadata me add karne se system use keyword se retrieve kar sakta hai, document ko embeddings me convert karne ke baad bhi.

Har chunk ko un questions se bhi augment kar sakte ho jinka woh jawab de sakta hai. Customer support ke liye har article ko related questions se augment karo — password reset karne wala article "How to reset password?", "I forgot my password", "I can't log in", ya "Help, I can't find my account" jaise queries se augment ho sakta hai. Kuch teams ne bataya hai ki unke retrieval systems tab best kaam karte hain jab data question-and-answer format me organize ho.

Agar document multiple chunks me split hai to kuch chunks me woh context nahi hoga jo retriever ko samajhne me madad kare ki chunk kis baare me hai. Isse avoid karne ke liye har chunk ko original document ke context se augment karo — jaise original document ka title aur summary. Anthropic ne AI models se short context (aam taur pe 50–100 tokens) generate karwaya jo chunk ko explain karta hai aur original document se uska relationship batata hai. Prompt tha: document aur chunk deke "Please give a short succinct context to situate this chunk within the overall document for the purposes of improving search retrieval of the chunk. Answer only with the succinct context and nothing else." Generated context har chunk ke aage prepend kar diya jata hai, aur augmented chunk retrieval algorithm se index hota hai (Figure 6-5, "Introducing Contextual Retrieval", Anthropic, 2024).

Retrieval solution evaluate karna

Retrieval solution evaluate karte time ye factors dhyaan me rakho: kaunse retrieval mechanisms support karta hai — kya hybrid search support karta hai? Vector database hai to kaunse embedding models aur vector search algorithms support karta hai? Data storage aur query traffic dono me kitna scalable hai — tumhare traffic patterns ke liye kaam karta hai? Data index karne me kitna time lagta hai — bulk me kitna data add/delete kar sakte ho ek saath? Alag retrieval algorithms ke liye query latency kya hai? Managed solution hai to pricing structure kya hai — document/vector volume pe based hai ya query volume pe? Is list me enterprise functionalities shamil nahi hain jaise access control, compliance, data plane aur control plane separation.

RAG beyond texts — multimodal aur tabular data

Ab tak text-based RAG systems discuss hue — external data sources text documents hain. Lekin external data sources multimodal aur tabular bhi ho sakte hain.

  • Multimodal RAG: generator multimodal ho to uska context sirf text documents se nahi, images, videos, audio se bhi augment ho sakta hai. Example: query "What's the color of the house in the Pixar movie Up?" — retriever Up ke ghar ki picture fetch karke model ko answer karne me madad kar sakta hai (Figure 6-6). Images ke metadata (titles, tags, captions) hon to unse retrieve kar sakte ho — image tab retrieve hoti hai jab uska caption query se relevant mana jaye. Images ko content ke basis pe retrieve karna ho to multimodal embedding model chahiye jo images aur texts dono ke embeddings generate kar sake — jaise CLIP (Radford et al., 2021): (1) saare data (texts aur images) ke CLIP embeddings generate karke vector database me store karo, (2) query ka CLIP embedding generate karo, (3) vector database me query embedding ke close saare images aur texts dhoondho.
  • RAG with tabular data: zyada tar applications unstructured data (texts, images) ke saath tabular data se bhi kaam karti hain. Workflow classic RAG se significantly alag hai. Example: imaginary ecommerce site Kitty Vogue ka order table Sales (Table 6-3: Order ID, Timestamp, Product ID, Product, Unit price, Units, Total — jaise Fruity Fedora, $18, 1 unit). Sawaal: "How many units of Fruity Fedora were sold in the last 7 days?" — system ko table query karni hai saare Fruity Fedora orders ke liye aur units sum karne hain. SQL query: SELECT SUM(units) AS total_units_sold FROM Sales WHERE product_name = 'Fruity Fedora' AND timestamp >= DATE_SUB(CURDATE(), INTERVAL 7 DAY). Workflow (Figure 6-7): (1) Text-to-SQL: user query aur table schemas ke basis pe determine karo ki kaunsi SQL query chahiye — text-to-SQL semantic parsing ka example hai (Chapter 2); (2) SQL execution: SQL query execute karo; (3) Generation: SQL result aur original user query ke basis pe response generate karo. Bahut se tables hon jinki schemas model ke context me fit na hon to intermediate step chahiye jo predict kare ki har query ke liye kaunse tables use karne hain. Text-to-SQL wahi generator kar sakta hai jo final response generate karta hai, ya specialized text-to-SQL model. Yahan se sawaal banta hai — model ko aur tools dene se capabilities aur improve hongi? Tool use agentic pattern ki core characteristic hai, jo agla section hai.
Yaad rakho: RAG system ki quality ko component by component aur end to end — dono tareeke se evaluate karo: retrieval quality, final outputs, aur embeddings. Aur retrieval me term-based aur embedding-based ka combination (hybrid search) aksar kisi ek se behtar hota hai.
sql — Text-to-SQL example: Fruity Fedora sales — as printed in the book (no code file for this example in the repo) (GitHub: https://github.com/chiphuyen/aie-book)
SELECT SUM(units) AS total_units_sold
FROM Sales
WHERE product_name = 'Fruity Fedora'
AND timestamp >= DATE_SUB(CURDATE(), INTERVAL 7 DAY);
SOURCESource: Huyen, AI Engineering, O'Reilly, Chapter 6 — RAG and Agents
← Previous06 · RAG and Agents→ Next06.2 · Agents — Tools aur Planning
06.2Chapter 6 · RAG and Agents

Agents — Tools aur Planning

Intelligent agents ko bahut se log AI ka ultimate goal mante hain. Stuart Russell aur Peter Norvig ki classic book Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach (1995) AI research ke field ko hi "the study and design of rational agents" ke roop me define karti hai. Foundation models ki unprecedented capabilities ne pehle unimaginable agentic applications ka darwaza khol diya hai — autonomous, intelligent agents jo hamare assistants, coworkers aur coaches ban sakein: website banana, data gather karna, trip plan karna, market research, customer account manage karna, data entry automate karna, interview ki taiyari, candidates interview karna, deal negotiate karna — possibilities endless lagti hain aur potential economic value enormous hai.

Note: AI-powered agents ek emerging field hai — inhe define, develop aur evaluate karne ke liye koi established theoretical framework nahi hai. Ye section existing literature se framework banane ki best-effort attempt hai, aur field ke saath evolve hoga. Baaki book ke comparison me ye section zyada experimental hai. Agents naye lagte hain, lekin woh is book me pehle aaye concepts pe built hain — self-critique, chain-of-thought aur structured outputs.

Agent kya hai — overview

"Agent" term bahut se engineering contexts me use hota hai — software agent, intelligent agent, user agent, conversational agent, reinforcement learning agent. Definition: agent woh hai jo apne environment ko perceive kar sakta hai aur us environment pe act kar sakta hai. Matlab agent ko characterize karta hai uska environment aur uske actions ka set.

  • Environment use case se define hoti hai: game khelne wala agent (Minecraft, Go, Dota) ka environment woh game hai; internet scrape karne wale agent ka environment internet hai; cooking robot ka environment kitchen hai; self-driving car agent ka environment road system aur uske aas-paas ke areas hain.
  • Actions ka set agent ke tools se augment hota hai. Tum roz interact karne wale bahut se generative AI-powered applications agents hain, simple tools ke saath — ChatGPT ek agent hai: web search kar sakta hai, Python code execute kar sakta hai, images generate kar sakta hai. RAG systems bhi agents hain — text retrievers, image retrievers aur SQL executors unke tools hain.
  • Environment aur tools ke beech strong dependency hai: environment determine karta hai ki agent potentially kaunse tools use kar sakta hai (chess game me sirf valid chess moves possible hain), aur tool inventory restrict karta hai ki agent kis environment me operate kar sakta hai (robot ka ekmatra action swimming hai to woh sirf water environment me rahega). Figure 6-8 me SWE-agent (Yang et al., 2024) dikhaya hai — GPT-4 pe built coding agent, environment computer hai (terminal aur file system), actions hain navigate repo, search files, view files, edit lines.

AI agent me AI brain hai jo received information (task aur environment se feedback) process karta hai, task achieve karne ke liye actions ka sequence plan karta hai, aur determine karta hai ki task accomplish hua ya nahi. Kitty Vogue wale tabular RAG example ko lo — ye ek simple agent hai jiske 3 actions hain: response generation, SQL query generation, SQL query execution. Query: "Project the sales revenue for Fruity Fedora over the next three months" — agent ye sequence perform kar sakta hai: (1) reason karo ki task kaise accomplish karein — future sales predict karne ke liye pehle last 5 years ke sales numbers chahiye; (2) SQL query generation invoke karo last 5 years ke sales numbers ke liye; (3) SQL query execution invoke karo; (4) tool outputs pe reason karo — numbers insufficient lag sakte hain (missing values ki wajah se), past marketing campaigns ki information bhi chahiye; (5) SQL query generation past marketing campaigns ke liye; (6) SQL query execution; (7) reason karo ki nayi information projection ke liye sufficient hai, phir projection generate karo; (8) reason karo ki task successfully complete ho gaya.

Non-agent use cases ke comparison me agents ko typically zyada powerful models chahiye, 2 reasons se: compound mistakes — agent ko task accomplish karne ke liye multiple steps karne padte hain, aur overall accuracy steps badhne pe kam hoti hai (per step accuracy 95% ho to 10 steps ke baad overall 60%, 100 steps ke baad sirf 0.6%); higher stakes — tools ke access se agents zyada impactful tasks kar sakte hain, lekin koi bhi failure zyada severe consequences de sakta hai. Bahut steps wala task chalane me time aur paisa lagta hai — lekin agents autonomous ho sakte hain to bahut saara human time bacha sakte hain, isliye unki cost worthwhile ho sakti hai.

Environment diya ho to agent ki success uske tool inventory aur uske AI planner ki strength pe depend karti hai. Pehle tools dekhte hain, phir planning.

Tools — 3 categories

System ko agent hone ke liye external tools ki zaroorat nahi hai — lekin bina external tools ke agent ki capabilities limited hongi. Akele model typically ek action perform kar sakta hai — LLM text generate kar sakta hai, image generator images generate kar sakta hai. External tools agent ko vastly zyada capable bana dete hain. Tools agent ko environment perceive karne aur uspe act karne — dono me madad karte hain. Perceive karne wale actions read-only hote hain, act karne wale write actions hote hain. Agent ke paas tools ka set uski tool inventory hai. Zyada tools matlab zyada capabilities — lekin jitne zyada tools, unhe samajhna aur achhe se use karna utna challenging. Sahi set dhoondhne ke liye experimentation zaroori hai ("Tool selection" aage).

1. Knowledge augmentation (context construction)

Relevant context model ke response quality ke liye kitna important hai, ye book ab tak convince kar chuki hogi. Is category ke tools agent ki knowledge augment karte hain — kuch pehle discuss ho chuke hain: text retriever, image retriever, SQL executor. Aur potential tools: internal people search, inventory API (alag products ka status return kare), Slack retrieval, email reader. Bahut se aise tools model ko organization ke private processes aur information se augment karte hain; tools public information bhi de sakte hain, khaas taur pe internet se.

Web browsing ChatGPT jaise chatbots me incorporate hone wali earliest aur most anticipated capabilities me se ek thi. Web browsing model ko stale hone se rokta hai — model tab stale ho jata hai jab uski training data outdated ho jaye. Training data last week tak cut off hai to is week ki information wale sawaal tabhi answer kar payega jab woh information context me di jaye. Bina web browsing ke model weather, news, upcoming events, stock prices, flight status nahi bata sakta. Web browsing umbrella term hai saare internet-access tools ke liye — web browsers aur specific APIs jaise search APIs, news APIs, GitHub APIs, social media APIs (X, LinkedIn, Reddit). Web browsing se agent up-to-date information reference karke behtar responses generate karta hai aur hallucinations kam karta hai — lekin ye agent ko internet ke cesspools ke liye bhi khol deta hai. Internet APIs carefully select karo.

2. Capability extension

Doosri category ke tools AI models ki inherent limitations address karte hain — performance boost dene ka easy tareeka. Example: AI models math me notorious tareeke se kharab hain — 199,999 divided by 292 poochho to model likely fail karega, lekin calculator ke saath ye calculation trivial hai. Model ko arithmetic me achha train karne ki koshish karne se bahut zyada resource-efficient hai use calculator ka access de dena. Doosre simple tools: calendar, timezone converter, unit converter (lbs se kg), translator (un languages ke liye jinme model achha nahi hai).

Zyada complex lekin powerful tools hain code interpreters — model ko code samajhne ke liye train karne ki jagah code interpreter ka access do taaki woh code execute kar sake, results return kar sake, ya code ke failures analyze kar sake. Isse agents coding assistants, data analysts, aur research assistants ban sakte hain jo experiments chalane ke liye code likh ke results report karte hain. Lekin automated code execution ke saath code injection attacks ka risk hai (Chapter 5, "Defensive Prompt Engineering") — users ko safe rakhne ke liye proper security measures crucial hain.

External tools text-only ya image-only model ko multimodal bana sakte hain — sirf text generate karne wala model text-to-image model ko tool ke roop me use karke texts aur images dono generate kar sakta hai. Agent ka AI planner decide karta hai ki text generation invoke kare, image generation, ya dono — ChatGPT texts aur images dono isliye generate kar sakta hai kyunki woh DALL-E ko image generator ke roop me use karta hai. Agents code interpreter se charts aur graphs generate kar sakte hain, LaTeX compiler se math equations render kar sakte hain, ya browser se HTML code se web pages render kar sakte hain. Similarly, sirf text inputs process karne wala model image captioning tool se images process kar sakta hai, transcription tool se audio, aur OCR (optical character recognition) tool se PDFs padh sakta hai.

Tool use sirf prompting ya finetuning se compare karke model ki performance significantly boost kar sakta hai. Chameleon (Lu et al., 2023) dikhata hai ki 13 tools se augmented GPT-4-powered agent kai benchmarks pe GPT-4 alone ko outperform karta hai — tools the knowledge retrieval, query generator, image captioner, text detector, Bing search. ScienceQA (science question answering benchmark) pe Chameleon ne best published few-shot result ko 11.37% improve kiya; TabMWP (Tabular Math Word Problems, Lu et al., 2022) pe accuracy 17% improve ki.

3. Write actions

Ab tak read-only actions discuss hue jo model ko data sources se padhne dete hain. Lekin tools write actions bhi perform kar sakte hain — data sources me changes karna. SQL executor data table retrieve kar sakta hai (read) lekin use change ya delete bhi kar sakta hai (write). Email API email padh sakti hai lekin respond bhi kar sakti hai. Banking API current balance retrieve kar sakti hai lekin bank transfer bhi initiate kar sakti hai.

Write actions se system bahut zyada kar sakta hai — poora customer outreach workflow automate kar sakte ho: potential customers research karo, contacts dhoondho, emails draft karo, pehli emails bhejo, responses padho, follow up karo, orders extract karo, databases ko naye orders se update karo. Lekin AI ko automatically hamari zindagi alter karne ki ability dena frightening hai. Jaise intern ko production database delete karne ki authority nahi deni chahiye, waise unreliable AI ko bank transfers initiate karne ki permission nahi deni chahiye. System ki capabilities aur security measures pe trust crucial hai — bad actors se protection ensure karni hai jo system ko harmful actions karne ke liye manipulate kar sakte hain.

Jab author logon se autonomous AI agents ke baare me baat karti hai to aksar koi self-driving cars ka example deta hai — "Kya hoga agar koi car hack karke tumhe kidnap kar le?" Self-driving car example visceral lagta hai kyunki usme physicality hai, lekin AI system physical presence ke bina bhi harm kar sakta hai — stock market manipulate karna, copyrights churana, privacy violate karna, biases reinforce karna, misinformation aur propaganda failana, aur bhi bahut kuch (Chapter 5). Ye saari concerns valid hain, aur AI leverage karne wali har organization ko safety aur security seriously lena chahiye. Lekin iska matlab ye nahi hai ki AI systems ko kabhi real world me act karne ki ability nahi deni chahiye — agar hum machine pe trust karke space me ja sakte hain, to ummeed hai ek din security measures itne sufficient honge ki autonomous AI systems pe trust kar sakein. Waise bhi insaan bhi fail ho sakte hain — author personally average stranger se drive karwane ki jagah self-driving car pe zyada trust karegi.

Jaise sahi tools insaanon ko vastly zyada productive bana dete hain — Excel ke bina business aur cranes ke bina skyscraper banana soch sakte ho? — waise hi tools models ko bahut zyada tasks accomplish karne dete hain. Bahut se model providers apne models ke saath tool use support karte hain, ek feature jise aksar function calling kehte hain. Aage jaake expect karo ki wide set of tools ke saath function calling zyada tar models me common hoga.

Planning

Foundation model agent ke heart me woh model hai jo task solve karne ke liye responsible hai. Task ko uske goal aur constraints se define kiya jata hai — example: San Francisco se India 2-week trip schedule karni hai $5,000 budget me — goal hai 2-week trip, constraint hai budget. Complex tasks ko planning chahiye. Planning process ka output hai plan — task accomplish karne ke liye steps outline karne wala roadmap. Effective planning ke liye model ko task samajhna, use achieve karne ke alag options consider karna, aur sabse promising option chunna padta hai. Planning mushkil hai — computational problem ke roop me well studied hai, cover karne ke liye kai volumes chahiye; yahan sirf surface cover hogi.

Planning overview — decouple planning from execution

Kisi task ko decompose karne ke bahut se tareeke ho sakte hain, lekin saare successful outcome nahi denge; sahi solutions me bhi kuch zyada efficient hote hain. Query: "How many companies without revenue have raised at least $1 billion?" — 2 options: (1) saari companies dhoondho jinhe revenue nahi hai, phir amount raised se filter karo; (2) saari companies dhoondho jinhone kam se kam $1 billion raise kiya hai, phir revenue se filter karo. Doosra option zyada efficient hai — bina revenue wali companies $1 billion raise karne wali companies se vastly zyada hain. Intelligent agent ko option 2 chunna chahiye.

Planning ko execution ke saath same prompt me couple kar sakte ho — model ko prompt do, step by step sochne ko kaho (chain-of-thought prompt), phir woh steps ek hi prompt me execute karo. Lekin agar model 1,000-step plan bana de jo goal accomplish hi nahi karta, to bina oversight ke agent ghanton woh steps chala sakta hai, API calls pe time aur paisa waste karke, jab tak tumhe realize ho ki woh kahin nahi ja raha hai. Isse bachne ke liye planning ko execution se decouple karo: pehle agent se plan generate karwao, aur sirf plan validate hone ke baad use execute karo. Plan ko heuristics se validate kar sakte ho — invalid actions wale plans eliminate karo (plan me Google search chahiye aur agent ke paas Google Search access nahi hai to plan invalid hai), ya X steps se zyada wale plans eliminate karo. Plan ko AI judges se bhi validate kar sakte ho — model se poochho ki plan reasonable lagta hai ya kaise improve karein. Plan bura evaluate ho to planner se doosra plan generate karwao; plan achha ho to execute karo. Plan ke tools involve hon to function calling invoke hogi. Plan execute karne ke outputs ko phir evaluate karna hoga. Plan poore task ke liye end-to-end plan hona zaroori nahi hai — kisi subtask ke liye chhota plan bhi ho sakta hai (Figure 6-9).

Ab tumhare system me 3 components hain: plans generate karne wala, plans validate karne wala, aur plans execute karne wala. Har component ko agent mano to ye ek multi-agent system hai. Process fast karne ke liye plans sequentially generate karne ki jagah kai plans parallel me generate karke evaluator se sabse promising chunwa sakte ho — ye latency/cost trade-off hai, kyunki multiple plans ek saath generate karne se extra cost aayegi.

Planning ke liye task ke peeche ki intent samajhni padti hai — user is query se kya karna chahta hai? Intent samajhne me intent classifier madad karta hai — Chapter 5 ("Break Complex Tasks into Simpler Subtasks") ke hisaab se intent classification doosre prompt ya is task ke liye train kiye gaye classification model se ki ja sakti hai. Intent classification mechanism ko multi-agent system ka ek aur agent mana ja sakta hai. Intent jaan ne se agent sahi tools pick kar sakta hai — customer support me billing wali query ho to user ke recent payments retrieve karne wala tool chahiye; password reset wali query ho to documentation retrieval chahiye. Kuch queries agent ke scope se bahar ho sakti hain — intent classifier ko unhe IRRELEVANT classify karna chahiye taaki agent politely reject kar sake, impossible solutions banane me FLOPs waste karne ki jagah.

Ab tak assume kiya ki agent teeno stages automate karta hai — plans generate karna, validate karna, execute karna. Reality me humans kisi bhi stage me involve ho sakte hain — process me madad karne aur risks mitigate karne ke liye. Human expert plan de sakta hai, plan validate kar sakta hai, ya plan ke parts execute kar sakta hai. Complex tasks jinme agent ko poora plan generate karne me trouble ho, unme human expert high-level plan de sakta hai jise agent expand kar sake. Risky operations (database update, code change merge) wale plans me system explicit human approval maang sakta hai ya humans ko execute karne de sakta hai. Iske liye clearly define karna hoga ki har action ke liye agent ko kitna automation level allowed hai.

Summary me task solve karne me ye processes hote hain (reflection mandatory nahi hai, lekin agent ki performance significantly boost karta hai): (1) Plan generation: task accomplish karne ka plan banao — manageable actions ka sequence, is process ko task decomposition bhi kehte hain; (2) Reflection aur error correction: generated plan evaluate karo — bura plan ho to naya generate karo; (3) Execution: plan me outline kiye actions lo — aksar specific functions call karna; (4) Reflection aur error correction: action outcomes milne pe unhe evaluate karo aur determine karo ki goal accomplish hua ya nahi — mistakes identify aur correct karo; goal complete na ho to naya plan generate karo. Plan generation aur reflection ki techniques tum pehle dekh chuke ho — "think step by step" kehna matlab task decompose karne ko kehna; "verify if your answer is correct" kehna matlab reflect karne ko kehna.

Foundation models as planners — kya LLMs plan kar sakte hain?

Ye ek open question hai ki foundation models kitni achhi tarah plan kar sakte hain. Bahut se researchers mante hain ki foundation models, kam se kam autoregressive language models pe built, plan nahi kar sakte. Meta ke Chief AI Scientist Yann LeCun unequivocally kehte hain ki autoregressive LLMs plan nahi kar sakte (2023). Article "Can LLMs Really Reason and Plan?" me Kambhampati (2023) argue karte hain ki LLMs knowledge extract karne me great hain lekin planning me nahi — LLMs ki planning abilities claim karne wale papers LLMs se extract ki gayi general planning knowledge ko executable plans se confuse kar dete hain: "The plans that come out of LLMs may look reasonable to the lay user, and yet lead to execution time interactions and errors."

Lekin bahut si anecdotal evidence hai ki LLMs poor planners hain, phir bhi unclear hai ki ye isliye hai kyunki hum LLMs ko sahi tareeke se use karna nahi jaante, ya kyunki LLMs fundamentally plan nahi kar sakte. Planning core me ek search problem hai — goal tak jaane wale alag paths me search karo, har path ke outcome (reward) predict karo, aur sabse promising outcome wala path pick karo. Aksar ye bhi determine karna padta hai ki goal tak pahunchne wala koi path hai hi nahi. Search me aksar backtracking chahiye — ek step pe 2 possible actions A aur B hon; action A lene ke baad aisi state me pahuncho jo promising nahi hai, to previous state pe backtrack karke action B lena padega.

Kuch log argue karte hain ki autoregressive model sirf forward actions generate kar sakta hai, backtrack karke alternate actions generate nahi kar sakta — isliye autoregressive models plan nahi kar sakte. Lekin ye necessarily sach nahi hai — action A wala path execute karne ke baad agar model determine kare ki ye path sense nahi banata, to woh action B use karke path revise kar sakta hai, effectively backtracking kar sakta hai. Model hamesha start over karke doosra path bhi chun sakta hai. Ye bhi possible hai ki LLMs poor planners isliye hain kyunki unhe plan karne ke liye zaroori toolings nahi di gayi hain. Plan karne ke liye sirf available actions jaanna kaafi nahi hai — har action ka potential outcome bhi jaanna zaroori hai. Example: pahad chadhna hai, potential actions hain right mudo, left mudo, peeche mudo, ya seedha jao — lekin agar right mudne se cliff se gir jaoge to woh action consider nahi karna chahoge. Technically, ek action tumhe ek state se doosri state me le jata hai, aur action lena hai ya nahi ye decide karne ke liye outcome state jaanna zaroori hai. Matlab model se sirf actions ka sequence generate karwana kaafi nahi hai, jaise popular chain-of-thought prompting technique karti hai. Paper "Reasoning with Language Model is Planning with World Model" (Hao et al., 2023) argue karta hai ki LLM, duniya ke baare me itni information contain karne ki wajah se, har action ka outcome predict kar sakta hai — aur is outcome prediction ko incorporate karke coherent plans generate kar sakta hai. Agar AI plan nahi bhi kar sakti, to bhi woh planner ka part ho sakti hai — LLM ko search tool aur state tracking system se augment karke planning me madad ki ja sakti hai.

FM planners vs RL planners

Agent RL (reinforcement learning) me bhi core concept hai — Wikipedia RL ko define karta hai as field "concerned with how an intelligent agent ought to take actions in a dynamic environment in order to maximize the cumulative reward". RL agents aur FM agents bahut tareekon se similar hain — dono ko unke environments aur possible actions se characterize kiya jata hai. Main difference hai planners kaise kaam karte hain: RL agent me planner ko RL algorithm se train kiya jata hai — is training me bahut time aur resources lag sakte hain. FM agent me model hi planner hai — model ko planning capabilities improve karne ke liye prompt ya finetune kar sakte ho, aur aam taur pe kam time aur kam resources lagte hain. Lekin koi cheez FM agent ko performance improve karne ke liye RL algorithms incorporate karne se nahi rokti — author ko lagta hai ki long run me FM agents aur RL agents merge ho jayenge.

Plan generation — prompt se

Model ko plan generator banane ka simplest tareeka hai prompt engineering. Example: Kitty Vogue ke customers ko products ke baare me seekhne me madad karne wala agent — 3 external tools: retrieve products by price, retrieve top products, retrieve product information. Plan generation ke liye prompt (illustration ke liye, production prompts likely zyada complex honge): SYSTEM PROMPT — "Propose a plan to solve the task. You have access to 5 actions: get_today_date(), fetch_top_products(start_date, end_date, num_products), fetch_product_info(product_name), generate_query(task_history, tool_output), generate_response(query). The plan must be a sequence of valid actions." Examples: Task "Tell me about Fruity Fedora" — Plan: [fetch_product_info, generate_query, generate_response]; Task "What was the best selling product last week?" — Plan: [fetch_top_products, generate_query, generate_response]; phir Task: {USER INPUT} — Plan:

Is example me 2 cheezein note karo: (1) plan format — functions ki list jinki parameters agent infer karta hai — agent control flow structure karne ke bahut se tareekon me se ek hai; (2) generate_query function task ki current history aur most recent tool outputs leke response generator ko feed karne wali query generate karta hai — har step ka tool output task ki history me add hota hai. User input "What's the price of the best-selling product last week" ho to generated plan aisa ho sakta hai: (1) get_time(), (2) fetch_top_products(), (3) fetch_product_info(), (4) generate_query(), (5) generate_response().

Har function ke liye exact parameters pehle se predict karna mushkil hai, kyunki woh aksar previous tool outputs se extract hote hain. Pehla step get_time() output de "2030-09-13", to agent reason kar sakta hai ki agle step ke parameters hone chahiye: retrieve_top_products(start_date="2030-09-07", end_date="2030-09-13", num_products=1). Aksar function ke exact parameter values determine karne ke liye sufficient information nahi hoti — user poochhe "What's the average price of best-selling products?" to unclear hai: user kitne best-selling products dekhna chahta hai? Last week ke, last month ke, ya all time ke? Matlab models ko frequently guess karna padta hai, aur guesses galat ho sakte hain. Action sequence aur associated parameters dono AI models generate karte hain, isliye hallucinate ho sakte hain — hallucinations se model invalid function call kar sakta hai ya valid function ko galat parameters ke saath call kar sakta hai. Model ki performance improve karne ki general techniques se planning capabilities bhi improve kar sakte ho. Agent ko planning me behtar banane ke approaches: better system prompt likho zyada examples ke saath; tools aur unke parameters ki better descriptions do taaki model unhe behtar samjhe; functions ko rewrite karo taaki simple ho jayein — complex function ko 2 simple functions me refactor karo; stronger model use karo — aam taur pe stronger models planning me behtar hote hain; plan generation ke liye model finetune karo.

Function calling

Bahut se model providers apne models ke liye tool use offer karte hain, effectively unke models ko agents bana dete hain. Tool ek function hai — tool invoke karna isliye aksar function calling kehlata hai. Alag model APIs alag tareeke se kaam karti hain, lekin aam taur pe function calling aise kaam karta hai: (1) tool inventory create karo — saare tools declare karo jo model use karna chahta ho; har tool ko uske execution entry point (function name), parameters aur documentation (function kya karta hai, kaunse parameters chahiye) se describe karo; (2) specify karo ki agent kaunse tools use kar sakta hai — alag queries ko alag tools chahiye ho sakte hain, isliye bahut si APIs har query ke liye declared tools ki list specify karne deti hain. Kuch APIs tool use ko aur control karne deti hain: required (model ko kam se kam ek tool use karna hi hai), none (model ko koi tool use nahi karna chahiye), auto (model decide karta hai kaunse tools use karne hain). Function calling Figure 6-10 me illustrate hai (pseudocode, multiple APIs ke representative hone ke liye; specific API use karne ke liye uski documentation dekho).

Query di gayi ho to agent automatically decide karta hai ki kaunse tools use karne hain aur unke parameters kya honge. Kuch function calling APIs ensure karti hain ki sirf valid functions generate hon — lekin correct parameter values guarantee nahi kar sakti hain. Example: user query "How many kilograms are 40 pounds?" — agent decide kar sakta hai ki use lbs_to_kg tool chahiye, ek parameter value 40 ke saath. Agent ka response aisa dikh sakta hai: ModelResponse(finish_reason='tool_calls', message=chat.Message(content=None, role='assistant', tool_calls=[ToolCall(function=Function(arguments='{"lbs":40}', name='lbs_to_kg'), type='function')])). Is response se tum lbs_to_kg(lbs=40) function evoke kar sakte ho aur uske output se users ko response generate kar sakte ho. Agents ke saath kaam karte time hamesha system se poochho ki woh har function call ke liye kaunse parameter values use kar raha hai. In values ko inspect karo taaki sure ho sako ki woh sahi hain.

Planning granularity

Plan ek roadmap hai — roadmap alag granularity levels ka ho sakta hai. Ek saal ka plan karna hai to quarter-to-quarter plan month-to-month plan se higher-level hai, jo week-to-week plan se higher-level hai. Yahan planning/execution trade-off hai: detailed plan generate karna mushkil hai lekin execute karna aasan hai; higher-level plan generate karna aasan hai lekin execute karna mushkil hai. Is trade-off ko circumvent karne ka approach hai hierarchically plan karna: pehle planner se high-level plan generate karwao (quarter-to-quarter), phir har quarter ke liye same ya alag planner se month-to-month plan generate karwao.

Ab tak ke saare plan examples me exact function names use hue hain, jo bahut granular hai. Problem ye hai ki agent ki tool inventory time ke saath badal sakti hai — get_time() function rename hoke get_current_time() ho sakta hai. Tool badle to prompt aur saare examples update karne padenge. Exact function names use karne se planner ko alag use cases me reuse karna bhi mushkil ho jata hai jahan tool APIs alag hain. Aur agar model ko purani tool inventory pe plan generate karne ke liye finetune kiya tha to nayi tool inventory pe dobara finetune karna padega. Is problem se bachne ke liye plans natural language me generate kar sakte ho, jo domain-specific function names se higher-level hai. Query "What's the price of the best-selling product last week" ho to agent ko aisa plan output karne ko kaho: (1) get current date, (2) retrieve the best-selling product last week, (3) retrieve product information, (4) generate query, (5) generate response. Natural language use karne se plan generator tool API changes ke liye robust ho jata hai — model mostly natural language pe train hua hai to use natural language me plans samajhne aur generate karne me behtar hoga aur hallucinate karne ki possibility kam hogi. Downside hai ki har natural language action ko executable commands me translate karne ke liye translator chahiye — lekin translating planning se bahut simple task hai aur weaker models se kam hallucination risk ke saath kiya ja sakta hai. (Chameleon (Lu et al., 2023) is translator ko program generator kehta hai.)

Complex plans — control flows

Ab tak ke plan examples sequential the: plan me agla action hamesha previous action complete hone ke baad execute hota hai. Actions execute karne ka order control flow kehlata hai. Sequential sirf ek type ka control flow hai; doosre types hain parallel, if statement aur for loop (Figure 6-11):

  • Sequential: task A complete hone ke baad task B execute karna — likely kyunki task B task A pe depend karta hai. Example: SQL query tabhi execute ho sakti hai jab woh natural language input se translate ho chuki ho.
  • Parallel: tasks A aur B ek saath execute karna. Example: query "Find me best-selling products under $100" — agent pehle top 100 best-selling products retrieve kare, aur har product ke liye uski price retrieve kare.
  • If statement: previous step ke output ke basis pe task B ya task C execute karna. Example: agent pehle NVIDIA ki earnings report check karta hai; us report ke basis pe decide karta hai ki NVIDIA stocks sell karne hain ya buy karne hain.
  • For loop: task A ko repeat karte rehna jab tak specific condition meet na ho. Example: prime number milne tak random numbers generate karte rehna.

Traditional software engineering me control flows ki conditions exact hoti hain. AI-powered agents me AI models control flows determine karte hain. Non-sequential control flows wale plans generate karna aur unhe executable commands me translate karna — dono zyada mushkil hain. Agent framework evaluate karte time check karo ki woh kaunse control flows support karta hai — example: system ko 10 websites browse karni hon to kya woh simultaneously kar sakta hai? Parallel execution users ko perceived latency significantly kam kar sakta hai.

Reflection aur error correction

Best plans ko bhi constantly evaluate aur adjust karna padta hai taaki success ka chance maximize ho. Reflection agent operate karne ke liye strictly necessary nahi hai, lekin agent succeed kare iske liye necessary hai. Reflection task process me kai jagah useful ho sakta hai: user query milne ke baad (request feasible hai ya nahi evaluate karo), initial plan generation ke baad (plan sense banata hai ya nahi), har execution step ke baad (sahi track pe hai ya nahi), aur poora plan execute hone ke baad (task accomplish hua ya nahi determine karo). Reflection aur error correction 2 alag mechanisms hain jo saath kaam karte hain — reflection insights generate karta hai jo errors uncover karne me madad karte hain.

Reflection same agent se self-critique prompts se kar sakte ho, ya alag component se — jaise specialized scorer: ek model jo har outcome ke liye concrete score output karta hai. ReAct (Yao et al., 2022) ne pehli baar reasoning aur action ko interleave karna propose kiya — ye agents ke liye common pattern ban gaya. Yao et al. ne "reasoning" term se planning aur reflection dono ko encompass kiya. Har step pe agent ko apni thinking explain karne ko (planning), actions lene ko, phir observations analyze karne ko (reflection) kaha jata hai, jab tak agent task ko finished na mane. Agent ko typically examples se prompt kiya jata hai ki woh is format me outputs generate kare: Thought 1: ... Act 1: ... Observation 1: ... (continue jab tak reflection determine na kare ki task finished hai) ... Thought N: ... Act N: Finish [Response to query]. Figure 6-12 me ReAct framework follow karne wale agent ka example hai jo HotpotQA (Yang et al., 2018) ke question ka jawab de raha hai — multi-hop question answering ka benchmark. Reflection ko multi-agent setting me bhi implement kar sakte ho: ek agent plans banata hai aur actions leta hai, doosra agent har step ya kuch steps ke baad outcome evaluate karta hai. (Ye reinforcement learning ki actor-critic (AC) agent method (Konda aur Tsitsiklis, 1999) ki yaad dilata hai.)

Agar agent ka response task accomplish karne me fail ho jaye to agent ko prompt karo ki reflect kare ki woh kyun fail hua aur kaise improve kare. Is suggestion ke basis pe agent naya plan generate karta hai — isse agents apni galtiyon se seekhte hain. Example: code generation task hai, evaluator evaluate karta hai ki generated code 1/3 test cases fail karta hai. Agent reflect karta hai ki fail hone ka reason ye hai ki usne all-negative arrays ko account me nahi liya. Actor phir naya code generate karta hai, all-negative arrays ko account me leke. Ye approach Reflexion (Shinn et al., 2023) ne li thi — is framework me reflection 2 modules me separate hai: evaluator jo outcome evaluate karta hai, aur self-reflection module jo analyze karta hai ki kya galat hua. Figure 6-13 me Reflexion agents ke examples hain (Reflexion GitHub repo se). Authors ne "trajectory" term se ek plan ke har step pe evaluation aur self-reflection ke baad propose ki gayi nayi trajectory ko refer kiya.

Plan generation ke comparison me reflection implement karna relatively easy hai aur surprisingly achha performance improvement la sakta hai. Downside hai latency aur cost — thoughts, observations aur kabhi-kabhi actions generate karne me bahut tokens lagte hain, jo cost aur user-perceived latency badhate hain, khaas taur pe bahut intermediate steps wale tasks me. Agents ko format follow karne ke liye nudge karne ke liye ReAct aur Reflexion dono ke authors ne prompts me plenty examples use kiye — isse input tokens compute karne ki cost badhti hai aur doosri information ke liye available context space kam hoti hai.

Tool selection

Tools aksar task ki success me crucial role play karte hain, isliye tool selection me careful consideration chahiye. Agent ko kaunse tools dene hain, ye environment aur task pe depend karta hai, lekin AI model pe bhi depend karta hai jo agent ko power karta hai. Best set of tools select karne ka koi foolproof guide nahi hai. Agent literature me tool inventories ki wide range hai — Toolformer (Schick et al., 2023) ne GPT-J ko 5 tools seekhne ke liye finetune kiya; Chameleon (Lu et al., 2023) 13 tools use karta hai; Gorilla (Patil et al., 2023) ne agents ko 1,645 APIs me se sahi API call select karne ke liye prompt karne ki koshish ki.

Zyada tools matlab zyada capabilities — lekin jitne zyada tools, unhe efficiently use karna utna mushkil hai. Ye insaanon jaisa hai — tools ka bada set master karna mushkil hota hai. Tools add karne ka matlab tool descriptions bhi add karna hai, jo model ke context me fit na hon. Jaise AI applications banate time bahut se decisions, tool selection me bhi experimentation aur analysis chahiye. Kuch cheezein jo madad kar sakti hain: alag sets of tools ke saath agent ka performance compare karo; ablation study karo — dekho ki ek tool inventory se hata dene pe agent ki performance kitni girti hai; agar tool hataane se performance drop nahi hota to use hata do; un tools ko dhoondho jinpe agent frequently mistakes karta hai — agar extensive prompting aur finetuning ke baad bhi agent tool use karna nahi seekh pata to tool ko badlo; tool calls ka distribution plot karo — kaunse tools sabse zyada use hote hain, kaunse sabse kam (Figure 6-14: Chameleon me GPT-4 aur ChatGPT ke tool use patterns me farak).

Lu et al. (2023) ke experiments 2 points demonstrate karte hain: (1) alag tasks ko alag tools chahiye — ScienceQA (science question answering) TabMWP (tabular math problem-solving) se bahut zyada knowledge retrieval tools pe rely karta hai; (2) alag models ki alag tool preferences hoti hain — GPT-4 ChatGPT se wider set of tools select karta hai; ChatGPT image captioning prefer karta hai, GPT-4 knowledge retrieval prefer karta hai. Agent framework evaluate karte time ye bhi evaluate karo ki woh kaunse planners aur tools support karta hai — alag frameworks alag categories ke tools pe focus karte hain. Example: AutoGPT social media APIs (Reddit, X, Wikipedia) pe focus karta hai, jabki Composio enterprise APIs (Google Apps, GitHub, Slack) pe focus karta hai. Tumhari needs time ke saath likely badlengi, isliye evaluate karo ki apne agent me naye tools incorporate karna kitna aasan hai.

Insaan sirf diye gaye tools use karke hi productive nahi hote — woh simple tools se progressively zyada powerful tools create bhi karte hain. Kya AI apne initial tools se naye tools create kar sakti hai? Chameleon (Lu et al., 2023) tool transition ka study propose karta hai — tool X ke baad agent kitna likely hai ki tool Y call kare? Figure 6-15 me tool transition tree ka example hai — agar 2 tools frequently saath me use hote hain to unhe combine karke ek bada tool bana sakte ho. Agar agent ko ye information pata ho to agent khud initial tools combine karke continually zyada complex tools build kar sakta hai. Voyager (Wang et al., 2023) ek skill manager propose karta hai jo agent ke acquire kiye gaye naye skills (tools) ko baad me reuse ke liye track karta hai — har skill ek coding program hai. Jab skill manager determine karta hai ki nayi skill useful hai (jaise kyunki usne agent ko task accomplish karne me successfully madad ki), to woh use skill library me add karta hai (conceptually tool inventory jaisa). Is skill ko baad me doosre tasks ke liye retrieve karke use kar sakte ho.

Yaad rakho: Agent ki success 2 cheezon pe depend karti hai — tool inventory aur planner ki strength. Plan ko execution se alag karo, sirf validated plans execute karo, aur function calls ke parameter values ko hamesha inspect karo.
SOURCESource: Huyen, AI Engineering, O'Reilly, Chapter 6 — RAG and Agents
