06.3Chapter 6 · RAG and Agents

Agent Failure Modes, Evaluation aur Memory

Evaluation ka matlab hai failures detect karna. Agent jitna complex task perform karta hai, utne zyada possible failure points hote hain. Chapters 3 aur 4 me discuss hue saare AI applications ke common failure modes ke alawa, agents ke unique failures hote hain — planning, tool execution aur efficiency ki wajah se. Kuch failures pakadna aasan hai, kuch mushkil. Agent ko evaluate karne ke liye uske failure modes identify karo aur measure karo ki har failure mode kitni baar hota hai.

Author ne in alag failure modes ko illustrate karne ke liye ek simple benchmark banaya hai, jo book ke GitHub repository pe hai. Agent benchmarks aur leaderboards bhi hain, jaise Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard, AgentOps evaluation harness aur TravelPlanner benchmark.

Planning failures

Planning mushkil hai aur kai tareekon se fail ho sakti hai. Planning failure ka sabse common mode hai tool use failure — agent aisa plan generate karta hai jisme ye errors me se ek ya zyada hon:

  • Invalid tool: plan me bing_search hai, lekin bing_search agent ki tool inventory me hai hi nahi.
  • Valid tool, invalid parameters: lbs_to_kg ko 2 parameters ke saath call karta hai, jabki use sirf ek parameter lbs chahiye.
  • Valid tool, incorrect parameter values: lbs_to_kg ko ek parameter lbs ke saath call karta hai, lekin value 100 use karta hai jabki 120 honi chahiye thi.

Planning failure ka doosra mode hai goal failure — agent goal achieve karne me fail ho jata hai. Ye isliye ho sakta hai kyunki plan task solve nahi karta, ya task solve karta hai lekin constraints follow kiye bina. Example: model se San Francisco se Hanoi 2-week trip plan karne ko kaho $5,000 budget me — agent San Francisco se Ho Chi Minh City ki trip plan kar de, ya San Francisco se Hanoi ki 2-week trip plan kar de jo budget se way over ho.

Ek common constraint jo agent evaluation me aksar overlook hoti hai, woh hai time. Bahut se cases me agent kitna time leta hai, ye kam matter karta hai — tum agent ko task assign karke tab check kar sakte ho jab woh done ho. Lekin bahut se cases me agent time ke saath less useful ho jata hai — agent se grant proposal prepare karne ko kaho aur woh grant deadline ke baad finish kare to agent zyada helpful nahi hai.

Planning failure ka ek interesting mode reflection me errors ki wajah se hota hai — agent convinced ho jata hai ki usne task accomplish kar liya hai jabki usne nahi kiya. Example: agent se 50 logon ko 30 hotel rooms me assign karne ko kaho — agent sirf 40 logon ko assign karke insist kare ki task accomplish ho gaya.

Planning failures ke liye agent evaluate karne ka ek option hai planning dataset banana — har example ek tuple hai (task, tool inventory). Har task ke liye agent se K plans generate karwao aur ye metrics compute karo: (1) saare generated plans me se kitne valid hain? (2) kisi task ke liye valid plan paane ke liye agent ko average kitne plans generate karne padte hain? (3) saare tool calls me se kitne valid hain? (4) invalid tools kitni baar call hote hain? (5) valid tools invalid parameters ke saath kitni baar call hote hain? (6) valid tools incorrect parameter values ke saath kitni baar call hote hain? Agent ke outputs me patterns analyze karo — agent kis types ke tasks pe zyada fail karta hai? Tumhara hypothesis kya hai kyun? Agent kis tools pe frequently mistakes karta hai? Kuch tools agent ke liye use karna mushkil ho sakte hain — challenging tool use karne ki ability ko better prompting, zyada examples ya finetuning se improve kar sakte ho. Agar sab fail ho jaye to tool ko kisi easier tool se swap karne pe consider karo.

Tool failures

Tool failures tab hote hain jab sahi tool use hota hai, lekin tool ka output galat hota hai. Ek failure mode hai jab tool hi galat outputs deta hai — image captioner galat description return karta hai, ya SQL query generator galat SQL query return karta hai. Agar agent sirf high-level plans generate karta hai aur translation module involved hai har planned action ko executable commands me translate karne me, to failures translation errors ki wajah se bhi ho sakte hain.

Tool failures isliye bhi ho sakte hain kyunki agent ke paas task ke liye sahi tools hi nahi hain. Obvious example: task me internet se current stock prices retrieve karne hain, aur agent ke paas internet access hi nahi hai. Tool failures tool-dependent hote hain — har tool ko independently test karna chahiye. Hamesha har tool call aur uske output ko print out karo taaki unhe inspect aur evaluate kar sako. Translator ho to use evaluate karne ke liye benchmarks banao. Missing tool failures detect karne ke liye samajhna chahiye ki kaunse tools use hone chahiye — agar agent kisi specific domain pe frequently fail karta hai to ho sakta hai usme us domain ke tools ki kami ho. Human domain experts ke saath kaam karo aur observe karo ki woh kaunse tools use karenge.

Efficiency

Agent valid plan generate karke sahi tools se task accomplish kar sakta hai, lekin inefficient ho sakta hai. Agent ki efficiency evaluate karne ke liye ye cheezein track karo:

  • Task complete karne ke liye agent ko average kitne steps chahiye?
  • Task complete karne me agent ki average cost kitni hai?
  • Har action typically kitna time leta hai? Koi actions khaas taur pe time-consuming ya expensive hain?

In metrics ko apne baseline se compare kar sakte ho — baseline doosra agent ya human operator ho sakta hai. AI agents ko human agents se compare karte time dhyaan rakho ki humans aur AI ke modes of operations bahut alag hain — jo humans ke liye efficient hai woh AI ke liye inefficient ho sakta hai, aur vice versa. Example: 100 web pages visit karna human agent ke liye inefficient hai jo ek time pe sirf ek page visit kar sakta hai, lekin AI agent ke liye trivial hai jo saare web pages ek saath visit kar sakta hai.

Memory — 3 mechanisms

RAG aur agents dono bahut saari information se deal karte hain, jo aksar underlying model ki maximum context length se zyada hoti hai. Isliye ek memory system chahiye jo model ke context ko supplement karke saari information handle karne me madad kare. Memory mechanisms model ko information retain aur utilize karne dete hain. Memory system khaas taur pe knowledge-rich applications jaise RAG aur multi-step applications jaise agents ke liye useful hai. RAG system memory pe rely karta hai apne augmented context ke liye, jo multiple turns me aur information retrieve karne pe badhta hai. Agentic system ko memory chahiye instructions, examples, context, tool inventories, plans, tool outputs, reflections aur bhi bahut kuch store karne ke liye. RAG aur agents memory pe zyada demands rakhte hain, lekin memory kisi bhi AI application ke liye beneficial hai jise information retain karni ho.

AI model ke typically 3 main memory mechanisms hote hain:

  • Internal knowledge: model khud ek memory mechanism hai — training data se seekha gaya knowledge retain karta hai. Ye internal knowledge tab tak nahi badalti jab tak model update na ho. Model har query me is knowledge ko access kar sakta hai.
  • Short-term memory: model ka context ek memory mechanism hai. Conversation ke previous messages ko model ke context me add kar sakte ho, jisse model unhe leverage karke future responses generate kar sakta hai. Model ka context uski short-term memory mana jata hai kyunki woh tasks (queries) ke across persist nahi karta. Access karna fast hai, lekin capacity limited hai — isliye ye aksar current task ke liye sabse important information store karne ke liye use hoti hai.
  • Long-term memory: external data sources jinhe model retrieval se access kar sakta hai, jaise RAG system me — ye model ki long-term memory mani jati hai, kyunki ye tasks ke across persist kar sakti hai. Model ki internal knowledge se alag, long-term memory ki information ko model update kiye bina delete kiya ja sakta hai.

Insaanon ke paas bhi similar memory mechanisms hain — saans lena tumhari internal knowledge hai (tum typically bhoolte nahi ho ki saans kaise lete hain, jab tak serious trouble na ho), short-term memory me woh information hai jo tum abhi kar rahe ho uske liye immediately relevant hai (jaise abhi mile hue vyakti ka naam), aur long-term memory books, computers, notes se augment hoti hai. Kaunsa memory mechanism kis data ke liye use karna hai, ye uski frequency of use pe depend karta hai — saare tasks ke liye essential information ko training ya finetuning se model ki internal knowledge me incorporate karo; rarely needed information ko long-term memory me rakho; short-term memory immediate, context-specific information ke liye reserve rakho (Figure 6-16).

Memory system ke benefits

  • Session ke andar information overflow manage karna: task execute karte time agent bahut saari nayi information acquire karta hai, jo agent ki maximum context length se zyada ho sakti hai. Excess information ko long-term memories wale memory system me store kar sakte ho.
  • Sessions ke beech information persist karna: AI coach practically useless hai agar har baar advice chahiye ho to poori life story dobara explain karni pade. AI assistant annoying hoga agar woh tumhari preferences bhool jata rahe. Conversation history ka access agent ko tumhare liye actions personalize karne deta hai — book recommendations maango aur model yaad rakhe ki tumhe pehle The Three-Body Problem pasand aayi thi, to woh similar books suggest kar sakta hai.
  • Model ki consistency boost karna: mujhse subjective question do baar poochho, jaise joke ko 1–5 rate karo — main zyada likely consistent answers doonga agar mujhe apna previous answer yaad ho. Similarly, AI model apne previous answers reference kar sake to future answers ko consistent rehne ke liye calibrate kar sakta hai.
  • Data structural integrity maintain karna: text inherently unstructured hai, isliye text-based model ke context me stored data unstructured hai. Table ko context me line-by-line feed kar sakte ho, lekin koi guarantee nahi hai ki model samjhega ki ye table hai. Structured data store karne wala memory system data ki structural integrity maintain karne me madad karta hai — agent se potential sales leads dhoondhne ko kaho to agent leads store karne ke liye Excel sheet leverage kar sakta hai; sequence of actions store karne ke liye queue leverage kar sakta hai.

Memory management — add aur delete

AI models ke liye memory system typically 2 functions se banta hai: memory management (kaunsi information short-term aur long-term memory me store karni hai) aur memory retrieval (long-term memory se task se relevant information retrieve karna). Memory retrieval RAG retrieval ke similar hai, kyunki long-term memory ek external data source hai — is section me focus memory management pe hai. Memory management typically 2 operations se banta hai: memory add karna aur delete karna. Agar memory storage limited na ho to deletion zaroori nahi hai — long-term memory ke liye ye kaam kar sakta hai, kyunki external memory storage relatively cheap aur easily extensible hai. Lekin short-term memory model ki maximum context length se limited hai, isliye use strategy chahiye ki kya add karna hai aur kya delete karna hai.

Long-term memory short-term memory ka overflow store karne ke liye use ho sakti hai. Ye operation ispe depend karta hai ki short-term memory ke liye kitni space allocate karni hai. Kisi query ke liye model me input hone wala context short-term memory aur long-term memory se retrieved information — dono se banta hai. Model ki short-term capacity isliye isse determine hoti hai ki context ka kitna hissa long-term memory se retrieved information ke liye allocate karna hai — example: agar context ka 30% reserve hai to model short-term memory ke liye context limit ka maximum 70% use kar sakta hai. Jab ye threshold reach ho jaye, overflow ko long-term memory me move kar sakte ho.

Memory management AI applications ke liye unique nahi hai — ye saare data systems ka cornerstone raha hai, aur memory efficiently use karne ke liye bahut si strategies develop hui hain:

  • FIFO (first in, first out): sabse simple strategy — jo pehle short-term memory me add hua, woh pehle external storage me move hoga. Conversation lambi hote hi OpenAI jaise API providers conversation ki shuruaat remove karna shuru kar sakte hain. LangChain jaise frameworks N last messages ya N last tokens retain karne dete hain. Lambi conversation me ye strategy assume karti hai ki early messages current discussion ke liye kam relevant hain — lekin ye assumption fatally galat ho sakti hai. Kuch conversations me earliest messages me sabse zyada information hoti hai, khaas taur pe jab early messages conversation ka purpose state karte hain. (Human conversations me opposite bhi sach ho sakta hai, agar pehle kuch messages pleasantries hon.) FIFO implement karna straightforward hai, lekin isse model important information ka track kho sakta hai.
  • Redundancy remove karna: zyada sophisticated strategies redundancy remove karti hain. Human languages me redundancy hoti hai clarity badhane aur potential misunderstandings compensate karne ke liye — redundancy automatically detect karne ka tareeka ho to memory footprint significantly kam ho jayega. Ek tareeka hai conversation ka summary use karna — summary same ya doosre model se generate kar sakte ho. Summarization, named entities track karne ke saath, tumhe bahut aage le ja sakti hai. Bae et al. (2022) ne isse ek step aage badhaya — summary milne ke baad authors nayi memory construct karna chahte the, memory ko us key information se join karke jo summary ne miss kar di thi. Authors ne classifier develop kiya jo memory ki har sentence aur summary ki har sentence ke liye determine karta hai ki sirf ek, dono, ya koi bhi nayi memory me add karni chahiye.
  • Reflection approach (Liu et al., 2023): har action ke baad agent se 2 cheezein karne ko kaho — (1) abhi generate hui information pe reflect karo, (2) determine karo ki ye nayi information memory me insert karni chahiye, existing memory ke saath merge karni chahiye, ya kisi doosri information ko replace karni chahiye — khaas taur pe agar doosri information outdated hai aur nayi information se contradict karti hai. Contradicting pieces of information milne pe kuch log nayi wali rakhna chunte hain; kuch log AI models se judge karwate hain ki kaunsi rakhni hai. Contradiction ko kaise handle karna hai, ye use case pe depend karta hai — contradictions hone se agent confuse ho sakta hai, lekin woh alag perspectives se draw karne me bhi madad kar sakta hai.

Usage-based strategies, jaise least frequently used information remove karna, zyada challenging hain, kyunki ye jaanne ka tareeka chahiye ki model ne kisi information ko kab use kiya.

Yaad rakho: Agent ko evaluate karne ke liye pehle uske failure modes likho — planning, tools, efficiency — phir har failure mode ko measure karo. Aur memory ko 3 layers me socho: internal knowledge (training), short-term memory (context) aur long-term memory (retrieval) — har information ko uski use frequency ke hisaab se sahi layer me rakho.
SOURCESource: Huyen, AI Engineering, O'Reilly, Chapter 6 — RAG and Agents

07Chapter 7 · Finetuning

Finetuning

Finetuning ka matlab hai — ek pehle se trained model ko aur train karke apne specific task ke liye adapt karna. Prompting model ko instructions deti hai, finetuning model ke weights ko hi badal deti hai. Is chapter me kab finetune karein, kab nahi, aur RAG vs finetuning ka faisla kaise karein — ye sab seekhenge.

Finetuning kya hai?

Finetuning me tum ek base model se shuru karte ho jisme kuch capabilities pehle se hain, par tumhare task ke liye poori nahi. Goal ye hai ki model tumhare specific task par achha perform kare.

Ye transfer learning ka ek tareeka hai — ek task se seekha hua knowledge doosre related task me transfer karna. Jaise piano bajana seekhne se doosra instrument seekhna aasan ho jata hai, waise hi text completion par pre-train hua model legal question answering ya text-to-SQL jaise tasks ke liye adapt ho sakta hai.

  • Sample efficiency: scratch se train karne ke liye lakhon examples chahiye hote, finetuning me aksar sirf kuch sau examples kaafi hote hain — kyunki zyada kuch model pehle se jaanta hai.
  • Unlocking capabilities: InstructGPT paper ke hisaab se finetuning aksar model ki woh capabilities unlock karta hai jo prompting se nikaalna mushkil hota hai.
  • Feature-based transfer: finetuning ke alawa ek aur tareeka hai — model se features (embeddings) nikaal kar unpar doosra model chalana. Computer vision me ye bahut common hai, jaise ImageNet par trained model se features nikaal kar object detection karna.

Finetuning ke types

Pre-training ke baad jo bhi training hoti hai, woh finetuning hai. Iske kai forms hain:

  • Continued pre-training (self-supervised finetuning): mehngi annotated data se pehle, saste task-related raw data par model ko aur train karo. Jaise legal QA ke liye pehle raw legal documents par, phir (question, answer) pairs par. Vietnamese summarization ke liye pehle Vietnamese text par.
  • Supervised finetuning (SFT): high-quality (input, output) pairs se train karna — input instruction ho sakta hai, output open-ended (summarization) ya close-ended (classification) ho sakta hai. Isse model human usage aur preference se align hota hai.
  • Infilling finetuning: next token predict karne ki jagah blank bharna — text editing aur code debugging ke liye bahut useful. Autoregressively pre-trained model ko bhi infilling ke liye finetune kar sakte ho.
  • Preference finetuning: reinforcement learning se model ko aise responses generate karna sikhana jo human preference ko maximize karein. Iske liye (instruction, winning response, losing response) format ka comparative data chahiye.
  • Long-context finetuning: model ki context length badhana — iske liye architecture change karna padta hai, jaise positional embeddings adjust karna. Ye baaki techniques se mushkil hai, aur model chhoti sequences par degrade bhi ho sakta hai. Code Llama ne isi se context 4,096 se 16,384 tokens tak badhaya tha.

Model developers bhi finetune karte hain (post-training, release se pehle) aur application developers bhi. Application developer aksar pehle se post-trained model ko finetune karta hai — model jitna refined hoga aur tumhare task se relevant hoga, utna kam kaam tumhe karna padega.

Kab finetune karein — Reasons to finetune

  • Quality badhana: general aur task-specific dono capabilities improve karna — khaas taur par specific output structure/format follow karna, jaise JSON ya YAML.
  • Domain-specific gaps: model standard SQL to achha convert karta hai, par kam common SQL dialect me fail hota hai — us dialect ke data par finetune karo. Customer-specific queries par bhi yehi logic lagta hai.
  • Bias mitigation: carefully curated data se model ke biases ko counter karna — jaise female CEOs wale dataset se gender bias kam karna. BERT-like models par women authors ya African authors ke text se finetuning se bias kam hua tha.
  • Chhote model ko bada banana: chhota finetuned model bade out-of-the-box model ko hara sakta hai. Grammarly ke finetuned Flan-T5 models ne GPT-3 ke text-editing variant ko haraya tha, 60x chhote hone ke bawjood, sirf 82,000 (instruction, output) pairs se.
  • Distillation: bade model ka behaviour chhote model me distill karna — bade model se generated data par chhota model train karo (detail Chapter 8 me).

Kab finetune NA karein

  • Ek task sudhrega, doosre bigdenge: sirf ek task par finetune karne se model doosre tasks par degrade ho sakta hai. Example: changing orders par finetune karo to product recommendations aur general feedback par performance gir sakti hai. Solution: saare tasks par finetune karo, ya alag-alag tasks ke liye alag models use karo, ya models ko merge karo.
  • Upfront investment bahut zyada: data, hardware aur ML talent — teeno chahiye. Annotated data slow aur mehnga hai, khaas taur par domain expertise wale tasks me.
  • ML knowledge chahiye: optimizer, learning rate, overfitting/underfitting, evaluation — ye sab samajhna padta hai. Frameworks automate karte hain, par debug tumhe hi karna hai.
  • Serving aur maintenance: finetuned model ko serve kaise karoge — khud host ya API? Aur naye base models tezi se aa rahe hain — agar naya base model tumhare finetuned model ko hara de, to kab switch karoge? Iska policy aur budget pehle se tay karo.
  • Pehle prompting try karo: bahut baar log kehte hain prompting kaam nahi kar rahi, par jaanch par pata chalta hai ki prompt experiments hi minimal aur unsystematic the — instructions unclear, examples representative nahi, metrics poorly defined. Prompt refine karne par kaam ho jata hai.
Yaad rakho: domain-specific model hamesha jeetta nahi. BloombergGPT (50B params, $1.3–2.6M compute) ko GPT-4-0314 ne financial benchmarks par haraya tha — FiQA sentiment me 87.15 vs 75.07, ConvFinQA me 76.48 vs 43.41. General-purpose models jaise-jaise capable hote ja rahe hain, domain tasks me bhi behtar hote ja rahe hain.

Finetuning vs RAG — form vs facts

Prompting se max fayda nikaalne ke baad sawal aata hai — RAG ya finetuning? Jawab is par depend karta hai ki model ki failure information-based hai ya behavior-based.

  • Information-based failure → RAG: model ke paas information hi nahi hai (private data), ya information outdated hai (Taylor Swift ke albums 10 vs 11). Ovadia et al. (2024) ne dikhaya ki current events wale QA me RAG ne finetuning ko haraya — aur RAG + base model ne RAG + finetuned model ko bhi haraya.
  • Behavior-based failure → Finetuning: output factually sahi hai par irrelevant hai, ya expected format follow nahi karta. Jaise HTML code generate kiya par compile nahi hua, ya technical specs me detail missing hai. Semantic parsing (natural language → JSON jaise structured format) aksar finetuning mangta hai, khaas taur par kam common syntaxes ke liye.
  • Short me: finetuning form ke liye hai, RAG facts ke liye. RAG hallucinations kam karta hai; finetuning syntax aur style sikhata hai. Low-quality data se finetuning hallucinations badha bhi sakta hai.
  • Dono ek saath bhi chal sakte hain: Ovadia et al. ke experiment me finetuned model par RAG lagane se MMLU par 43% cases me aur improvement mila — par 57% cases me RAG alone se behtar nahi tha.

Adaptation workflow — step by step

Evaluation criteria aur evaluation pipeline pehle define karo (Chapter 4) — har step par wahi pipeline progress naapegi:

  1. Prompting alone: Chapter 5 ki best practices se, prompts ko systematically version karte hue.
  2. Examples add karo: prompt me 1–50 examples, use case par depend karta hai.
  3. Missing information ho to RAG: simple term-based retrieval (BM25) se shuru karo — relevant knowledge add karte hi improvement dikhna chahiye.
  4. Failure mode ke hisaab se aage badho: information failure bani rahe to advanced RAG (embedding-based retrieval); behavioral issues (irrelevant, malformatted, unsafe responses) hon to finetuning. Embedding retrieval inference complexity badhata hai, finetuning model development complexity — inference unchanged rehta hai.
  5. Dono combine karo aur bhi performance ke liye.

Ek aur purana fayda: finetuning se token usage optimize hota tha — examples prompt me daalne ki jagah model par finetune kar do, prompt chhota ho jata hai. Prompt caching ke aane se ye fayda kam ho gaya hai, par context length ki limit prompt me abhi bhi hai, finetuning me nahi.

Yaad rakho: finetuning aur prompting mutually exclusive nahi hain. Real-world problems me aksar dono chahiye hote hain — aur prompting ke experiments se jo evaluation pipeline, annotation guideline aur experiment tracking banti hai, wahi finetuning ki seedhi banti hai.

07.1Chapter 7 · Finetuning

Memory Bottlenecks — Backprop, Math, Quantization

Finetuning ki sabse badi chunauti hai memory. Foundation models itne bade hain ki naive finetuning ek single GPU ki memory me fit hi nahi hoti. Is section me samjhenge ki memory kahan kharch hoti hai — backpropagation, memory math, numerical formats aur quantization — kyunki yahi samajh PEFT jaise techniques ko samajhne ki chaabi hai.

Key takeaways (poora section skip karna ho to ye yaad rakho)

  1. Memory inference aur finetuning dono me bottleneck hai — finetuning me bahut zyada, kyunki training ka tareeka hi aisa hai.
  2. Memory footprint ke main contributors: parameters ki sankhya, trainable parameters ki sankhya, aur numerical representation.
  3. Jitne zyada trainable parameters, utni zyada memory. Trainable parameters kam karo to memory kam hoti hai — yahi PEFT ki motivation hai.
  4. Quantization matlab model ko zyada bits wale format se kam bits wale format me convert karna. 13B params ka model FP32 (4 bytes/weight) me 52 GB, 2 bytes/weight me 26 GB.
  5. Inference aam taur par kam se kam bits me hoti hai — 16, 8, hatta ki 4 bits.
  6. Training numerical precision ke prati sensitive hai, isliye training aam taur par mixed precision me hoti hai — kuch operations 32-bit me, kuch 16-bit ya 8-bit me.

Backpropagation aur trainable parameters

Trainable parameter woh parameter hai jo finetuning ke dauran update ho sakta hai. Pre-training me saare parameters update hote hain, inference me koi nahi, finetuning me kuch ya saare. Jo parameters unchanged rehte hain, woh frozen kehlate hain.

Neural networks aam taur par backpropagation se train hote hain. Har training step ke do phases hote hain:

  1. Forward pass: input se output compute karna.
  2. Backward pass: forward pass ke signals se weights update karna.

Backward pass, high level par, aise kaam karta hai:

  1. Computed output ko expected output (ground truth) se compare karo. Antar ko loss kehte hain.
  2. Har trainable parameter ka loss me contribution compute karo — is value ko gradient kehte hain. Har trainable parameter ke liye ek gradient value hoti hai. Gradient zyada ho to parameter ko zyada adjust karna chahiye.
  3. Gradient ke hisaab se parameter values adjust karo — kitna adjust karna hai, ye optimizer tay karta hai. Common optimizers: SGD (stochastic gradient descent) aur Adam. Transformer models me Adam sabse zyada use hota hai.

Isi liye har trainable parameter ke saath extra values aati hain — uska gradient aur uske optimizer states. Jitne zyada trainable parameters, utni zyada memory.

Memory math — inference ke liye

Model ki memory footprint model, workload aur optimization techniques par depend karti hai. Rough estimate ke formulas:

  • Weights: N × M — N = parameter count, M = har parameter ke liye memory. 13B-parameter model, 2 bytes per parameter → 13B × 2 = 26 GB sirf weights ke liye.
  • Activations + KV vectors: sequence length aur batch size ke saath linearly badhte hain. Aam taur par weights ka ~20% maan lo, to total N × M × 1.2 — 13B model ke liye 26 × 1.2 = 31.2 GB.
  • 70B model: 2 bytes per parameter par sirf weights ke liye 140 GB chahiye. Model bada hote hi memory bottleneck ban jata hai.

Memory math — training ke liye

Training memory = model weights + activations + gradients + optimizer states.

Har trainable parameter ke liye gradient ke liye 1 value, plus optimizer states ke liye 0–2 values chahiye:

  • Vanilla SGD: koi state nahi (0 values).
  • Momentum optimizer: 1 value per trainable parameter.
  • Adam optimizer: 2 values per trainable parameter.

Example — 13B model, saare parameters trainable, Adam, 2 bytes per value: gradients + optimizer states = 13B × 3 × 2 bytes = 78 GB. Sirf 1B trainable parameters hon to ye sirf 6 GB hota hai. Yahi antar PEFT ko powerful banata hai.

Ek aur baat: activations ki memory weights se bhi badi ho sakti hai. Activations ko gradient computation ke liye store karna padta hai, aur bade models me ye weights ko dwarf kar deti hai. Solution hai gradient checkpointing (activation recomputation) — activations store karne ki jagah zaroorat padne par dobara compute karo. Memory kam hoti hai, par training time badh jata hai kyunki recomputation hoti hai.

Numerical representations — FP, BF16, INT

Har value ko represent karne ke liye kitni memory lagti hai, ye uske numerical format par depend karta hai:

  • FP32 — 32 bits (4 bytes), single precision. FP64 — 64 bits (8 bytes), double precision; NumPy/pandas ka default, par neural networks me rarely use hota hai. FP16 — 16 bits (2 bytes), half precision.
  • BF16 (BFloat16) — Google ne TPUs ke liye banaya; TF32 (TensorFloat-32) — NVIDIA ne GPUs ke liye banaya (naam 32 hai par asal me 19 bits ka hai).
  • INT8 / INT4 — integer formats, inference me tezi se popular ho rahe hain.
  • Har float format me 1 bit sign ke liye hota hai, baaki bits range (exponent) aur precision (significand) me batte hote hain. Zyada range bits = wider range; zyada precision bits = zyada accurate value. Jaise 10.1234 ko 2 decimal digits wale format me 10.12 karna precision khona hai.
  • BF16 vs FP16: dono 16 bits ke hain, par BF16 ke paas range ke liye zyada bits hain, precision ke liye kam. BF16 bade values represent kar sakta hai jo FP16 me out-of-bound (INF) ho jayenge, par BF16 kam precise hai — 1234.56789 FP16 me 1235.0 hota hai (0.035% change), BF16 me 1232.0 (0.208% change).
Yaad rakho: model ko usi format me load karo jiske liye woh intended hai. Llama 2 ke weights BF16 me the, par bahut teams ne FP16 me load kar liya aur quality kharab paakar pareshan hui. Galat format model ko significantly badal sakta hai.

Quantization — kam bits, kam memory

Quantization matlab values ko lower-precision format me convert karna. Strictly bolen to quantization tabhi kehte hain jab target integer ho, par practice me har precision reduction ko quantization kaha jata hai. 10B-parameter model 32-bit me 40 GB, 16-bit me sirf 20 GB.

Kya quantize karein: jo sabse zyada memory kha raha hai — weights ya activations. Weight quantization zyada common hai kyunki uska performance par impact stable aur kam hota hai. Kab quantize karein: training ke dauran ya training ke baad. Post-training quantization (PTQ) — model ko fully train karne ke baad quantize karna — sabse common hai, aur application developers ke liye sabse relevant.

Inference quantization

  • Pehle standard 32-bit (FP32) tha; late 2010s se 16-bit common ho gaya, phir 8-bit aur 4-bit. Dettmers et al. ne LLMs ko 8 bits (LLM.int8()) aur 4 bits (QLoRA) me quantize kiya.
  • Mixed precision serving: jahan possible ho wahan kam precision, jahan zaroori ho wahan zyada. Apple (2024) ne 2-bit aur 4-bit ka mixture use kiya — average 3.5 bits per weight. NVIDIA Blackwell architecture 4-bit float inference support karta hai.
  • 8 bits se neeche minifloat formats (FP8, FP4) ya integer formats (INT8, INT4) use hote hain.
  • Limit: 1 bit per value se kam nahi ja sakte. BinaryConnect, Xnor-Net aur BitNet ne 1-bit try kiya. Microsoft ka BitNet b1.58 sirf 1.58 bits per parameter use karta hai aur 3.9B params tak 16-bit Llama 2 jaisi performance deta hai.
  • Fayde: kam memory ke saath bada batch size, aur computation bhi tez (32-bit addition me 32t time, 16-bit me 16t) — isliye latency aur training time dono kam hote hain. Par format conversion ka extra computation kabhi-kabhi latency badha bhi sakta hai.
  • Nuksaan: har conversion chhota sa value change karta hai, aur bahut saare chhote changes bada performance change kar sakte hain. Range se bahar ki value infinity ya arbitrary value ban sakti hai.
  • PyTorch, TensorFlow aur Hugging Face transformers me PTQ kuch lines of code me free milta hai. Edge devices (TensorFlow Lite, PyTorch Mobile) par to quantized inference hi chalta hai.

Training quantization

Training ke dauran quantization PTQ jitni common nahi hai, par traction badh raha hai. Iske do alag goals hain:

  1. Low precision me achha perform karne wala model banana — taaki PTQ se quality degrade na ho.
  2. Training time aur cost kam karna — kam memory se saste hardware par train karo ya same hardware par bada model train karo.
  • Quantization-aware training (QAT): training ke dauran low-precision (e.g. 8-bit) behaviour simulate karo, taaki model low precision me high-quality output dena seekh le. Par QAT training time kam nahi karta — computations abhi bhi high precision me hote hain, simulation ka extra kaam time badha bhi sakta hai.
  • Direct low-precision training: dono goals achieve kar sakta hai. Character.AI (2024) ne models poori tarah INT8 me train kiye — training/serving precision mismatch khatam, efficiency bhi badhi. Par backpropagation low precision ke prati sensitive hai — chhote rounding changes compound hote hain, loss ki precise computation zaroori hai.
  • Mixed precision training: weights ki ek copy high precision me rakho, gradients aur activations low precision me. Ya sensitive weights high precision me, less-sensitive low precision me (LLM-QAT: weights aur activations 4-bit, embeddings 16-bit). Automatic Mixed Precision (AMP) ye setting automatically kar sakta hai.
  • Different phases, different precision: model high precision me train karo, finetune low precision me — foundation models ke saath ye bahut common hai.
Yaad rakho: inference memory ka formula N × M × 1.2 hai, training memory = weights + activations + gradients + optimizer states. Quantization M ko kam karta hai, PEFT trainable parameters ko kam karta hai — dono milkar finetuning ko affordable banate hain.
SOURCESource: Huyen, AI Engineering, O'Reilly, Chapter 7 — Finetuning

07.2Chapter 7 · Finetuning

Finetuning Techniques — PEFT, Merging, Multi-Task

Full finetuning me saare parameters update hote hain — 7B model ke liye Adam ke saath sirf weights + gradients + optimizer states ke liye 56 GB chahiye, jo most consumer GPUs (12–24 GB, high-end 48 GB) se zyada hai. Isi liye memory-efficient techniques aayi — sabse pehle PEFT, phir LoRA, aur phir model merging.

Full finetuning se partial finetuning tak

  • Full finetuning: trainable parameters = total parameters. Training se farak sirf itna hai ki training randomized weights se shuru hoti hai, finetuning pehle se trained weights se.
  • Partial finetuning: sirf kuch parameters update karo — jaise 10 layers me se sirf aakhri layer finetune karo (trainable 10%). Output ke paas wale layers zyada task-specific hote hain, pehle wale general features capture karte hain, isliye aakhri layers finetune karna common hai.
  • Par partial finetuning parameter-inefficient hai: BERT-large par GLUE benchmark ke barabar performance ke liye ~25% parameters update karne padte the (Houlsby et al., 2019).
  • CPU offloading: memory ko GPUs se CPUs par offload karna (DeepSpeed) — hardware memory ko efficiently use karne ka tareeka, footprint kam karne ka nahi.

PEFT — Parameter-Efficient Finetuning

PEFT ka idea Houlsby et al. (2019) ne diya: model me sahi jagah par additional parameters insert karo, aur sirf unhe update karo. Unhone BERT ke har transformer block me do adapter modules insert kiye, original parameters frozen rakhe, sirf adapters update kiye.

  • Result: GLUE par full finetuning se sirf 0.4% peeche, sirf 3% trainable parameters ke saath.
  • Downside: adapters extra layers add karte hain, isliye inference latency badh jati hai — forward pass me extra computational steps.
  • PEFT sirf parameter-efficient nahi, sample-efficient bhi hai: full finetuning ko tens of thousands–millions examples chahiye, kuch PEFT methods kuch hazaar examples me hi strong performance de dete hain.
  • PEFT ki koi fixed threshold nahi hai — aam taur par woh technique parameter-efficient maani jati hai jo full finetuning ke kareeb performance de, several orders of magnitude kam trainable parameters ke saath.

PEFT techniques — do buckets

1. Adapter-based methods (additive methods): model weights me additional modules add karte hain.

  • LoRA (Hu et al., 2021) — sabse popular, detail neeche.
  • BitFit (Zaken et al., 2021) — LoRA ke aas-paas aaya.
  • IA3 (Liu et al., 2022) — efficient mixed-task batching, multi-task finetuning ke liye attractive; kuch cases me LoRA aur full finetuning se bhi behtar.
  • LongLoRA (Chen et al., 2023) — attention-modification se context length expand karta hai.

2. Soft prompt-based methods: architecture me parameters add karne ki jagah input processing badalte hain — special trainable tokens (soft prompts) input tokens ke saath feed karte hain.

  • Hard prompt vs soft prompt: hard prompts human-readable hote hain ("I", "write", "a") aur static/not trainable; soft prompts continuous vectors (embeddings jaise) hote hain, human-readable nahi, aur backpropagation se optimize ho sakte hain.
  • Soft prompting prompt engineering aur finetuning ke beech ka crossover hai — hard + soft prompts ek saath use ho sakte hain.
  • Prefix-tuning (Li aur Liang, 2021) — har transformer layer par soft prompt tokens prepend karta hai. Prompt tuning (Lester et al., 2021) — sirf embedded input par prepend karta hai. P-Tuning (Liu et al., 2021) — inke beech ka variant. Faraksirf itna hai ki soft prompts kahan insert hote hain — PEFT frameworks inhe out of the box implement karte hain.
  • Popularity check: Hugging Face PEFT repo ke 1,000+ open issues (Oct 2024) ka analysis dikhata hai ki LoRA dominate karta hai; soft prompts kam common hain, par un logon me interest badh raha hai jo prompt engineering se zyada customization chahte hain par full finetuning nahi karna chahte.

LoRA — Low-Rank Adaptation

LoRA (Hu et al., 2021) original adapter method se alag hai: ye extra layers add nahi karta, balki aise modules use karta hai jo original layers me merge back ho sakte hain — isliye koi extra inference latency nahi.

Weight matrix W (dimension n × m) par LoRA aise kaam karta hai:

  1. Chhoti matrices ka dimension chuno — r (LoRA rank). Do matrices banao: A (n × r) aur B (r × m). Inka product WAB wahi dimension ka hota hai jo W ka hai.
  2. WAB ko original W me add karke naya matrix W' banao: W' = W + (α/r) × WAB. Hyperparameter α tay karta hai ki WAB kitna contribute kare.
  3. Finetuning ke dauran sirf A aur B update karo. W intact rehta hai.

Low-rank factorization: badi matrix ko do chhoti matrices ke product me factorize karo. 9 × 9 matrix (81 params) ko 9 × 1 aur 1 × 9 matrices (18 params) me factorize kar sakte ho. Rank jitna zyada, utni zyada information preserve hoti hai — factorization lossy hai, ye approximation hai.

  • GPT-3 par LoRA ne full finetuning ke barabar ya behtar performance di, sirf ~4.7M trainable parameters (0.0027%) ke saath.
  • LoRA kyun kaam karta hai? LLMs ke bahut parameters hote hain, par unki intrinsic dimension bahut low hoti hai. Pre-training implicitly intrinsic dimension ko minimize karta hai — aur bade models ki intrinsic dimension pre-training ke baad aur bhi low hoti hai. Matlab pre-training downstream tasks ke liye compression framework ki tarah kaam karta hai. Isi liye chhote parameters aur chhote data se finetuning possible hai.
  • Pre-training me LoRA kyun nahi? Low-rank pre-training chhote scale par kaam karta hai (SqueezeNet ne AlexNet-level accuracy 50x kam parameters me di). ReLoRA 1.3B tak, GaLore 1B par full-rank jaisi aur 7B par promising performance deta hai. Ho sakta hai full-rank pre-training hi intrinsic dimension ko itna kam karne ke liye zaroori ho ki low-rank factorization kaam kare.

LoRA configurations — kahan apply karein, rank kitna ho

  • LoRA khaas taur par transformer models ke liye hai. Sabse common: attention ke chaar weight matrices — query (Wq), key (Wk), value (Wv), output projection (Wo). Aam taur par ek type ke saare matrices par uniformly apply karte hain.
  • GPT-3 175B par 18M trainable parameters ka budget (0.01%) tha. Options: ek matrix rank 8, do matrices rank 4, ya chaaro matrices rank 2. Chaaro matrices rank 2 ne WikiSQL aur MultiNLI par best performance di. Sirf do matrices chunni hon to query aur value aam taur par best hote hain.
  • Feedforward matrices par bhi LoRA lagane se aur fayda milta hai — Databricks ko sabse bada boost saare feedforward layers par LoRA lagane se mila. Feedforward LoRA attention LoRA ka complement ho sakta hai.
  • Rank r: chhota r (4–64) aam taur par kaafi hota hai. r badhane se performance badhti nahi — aur zyada r overfitting bhi kar sakta hai. Kuch cases me bada r zaroori hota hai (Raschka ko r = 256 par best performance mili). Kuch frameworks max rank 32 allow karte hain.
  • Alpha (α): ratio α:r aam taur par 1:8 se 8:1 ke beech hota hai. r chhota ho to α bada, r bada ho to α chhota — best combination ke liye experimentation zaroori hai.

LoRA adapters serve karna

LoRA serve karne ke do tareeke hain:

  1. Merge karke serve karo: A aur B ko original model me merge karke naya matrix W' banao. Koi extra latency nahi. Ek LoRA model serve karna ho to ye behtar hai.
  2. Alag rakh kar serve karo: W, A, B separate rakhte hue inference ke dauran merge karo. Extra latency aati hai, par multi-LoRA serving ke liye behtar hai.

Multi-LoRA example: 100 customers, har ek ke liye alag finetuned model, same base model. W = 4096 × 4096 (16.8M params), rank 8 → A+B = 65,536 params. Option 1 (merge): 100 full matrices = 1.68B params store karne padenge. Option 2 (alag): 1 full matrix + 100 adapters = 23.3M params. Task switch karna bhi tez hota hai — poora weight matrix load karne ki jagah sirf adapter load karo.

  • Apple ne ek hi 3B base model ko alag iPhone features ke liye multiple LoRA adapters se adapt kiya, quantization ke saath on-device serve kiya.
  • LoRA adapters share aur reuse ho sakte hain — Hugging Face aur AdapterHub par publicly available adapters milte hain.
  • Catch: LoRA full finetuning jitni strong performance nahi deta, aur implement karna zyada mushkil hai (model architecture samajhna aur code modify karna). Popular base models ke liye PEFT frameworks (Hugging Face PEFT, Axolotl, unsloth, LitGPT) out of the box support dete hain.

Quantized LoRA — QLoRA

LoRA adapter ki memory model weights ke mukable minimal hoti hai (13B model: weights 26 GB, LoRA adapter sirf 6.55 MB). Isliye LoRA parameters kam karne se zyada fayda nahi — weights ko quantize karna zyada effective hai.

  • QLoRA (Dettmers et al., 2023): weights 4-bit me store karo (NF4 format — pre-trained weights aam taur par normal distribution follow karte hain, median zero), forward/backward pass ke liye BF16 me dequantize karo. Paged optimizers GPU memory khatam hone par data CPU-GPU ke beech transfer karte hain. Result: 65B model ek single 48 GB GPU par finetune ho gaya. Guanaco family (Llama 7B–65B) GPT-4 se peeche par ChatGPT se aage rahi (Elo ratings, May 2023).
  • Limitation: NF4 quantization mehnga hai — quantization/dequantization se training time badh sakta hai.
  • Doosre quantized LoRA works: QA-LoRA, ModuLoRA, IR-QLoRA.

Model merging aur multi-task finetuning

Finetuning ek model ko tailor karta hai; model merging multiple models ko combine karke ek naya, zyada useful model banata hai. Merged model ko aage finetune bhi kar sakte ho, par bina GPU ke bhi merging ho sakti hai — isliye indie developers ke liye attractive hai.

  • Value kahan se aati hai: behtar performance (do models jo alag-alag 60% questions answer karte hain, merge hokar 80% kar sakte hain) ya kam memory footprint (do tasks ke do models ko ek model me merge karna, khaas taur par adapters ko).
  • Multi-task finetuning ke 3 tareeke: (1) Simultaneous — saare tasks ka dataset ek saath finetune karo; zyada data aur training chahiye. (2) Sequential — ek ke baad ek task finetune karo; catastrophic forgetting ka risk — naya task seekhte hue purana bhool jata hai. (3) Merging — har task par alag-alag parallel finetune karo, phir merge karo; sequential learning nahi, isliye forgetting kam.
  • On-device deployment: phones, laptops, cars, smartwatches par memory limited hoti hai — multiple models ki jagah ek merged model. Privacy (data device se bahar na jaye) aur unreliable internet ke cases me bhi zaroori, aur inference cost bhi kam hoti hai.
  • Federated learning: multiple devices same model ko alag data par train karte hain, phir copies ko merge karke ek naya base model banate hain.
  • Ensembling vs merging: ensembling outputs combine karta hai (har model intact rehta hai, majority vote) — performance badhti hai par inference cost bhi badhti hai (har request par multiple inference calls). Merging parameters combine karta hai — ek hi model banta hai. Hugging Face Open LLM Leaderboard ke top models me bahut se merged models hain.

Merging approaches — summing, layer stacking, concatenation

1. Summing — weights ko add karna:

  • Linear combination: weighted average — Merge(A, B) = (WAA + WBB) / (WA + WB). Model soups ne dikhaya ki multiple finetuned models ke weights average karne se accuracy badhti hai, inference time badhe bina. Same base model par finetune hue models ke liye sabse effective — task vectors (finetuned model minus base model) ka concept: task vectors add karke capabilities combine karo, subtract karke undesirable behaviours (jaise facial recognition ya biases) hatao — ise task arithmetic kehte hain.
  • SLERP (Spherical Linear Interpolation): do vectors ko sphere ki surface par shortest path ke along merge karo. Interpolation factor 0–1 ke beech: 0.5 se kam pehle vector ke kareeb, 0.5 exactly beech me. Sirf do vectors ek baar me merge hote hain — zyada models ke liye sequentially merge karo.
  • Pruning redundant parameters (TIES / DARE): finetuning me bahut se parameters sirf thoda sa change hote hain aur performance me contribute nahi karte — redundant hain. Yadav et al. ne dikhaya ki top 20% task vector parameters rakhne se 100% jitni performance milti hai. Merge karne se pehle redundant parameters prune karne se merged model ki quality significantly badhti hai — jitne zyada models merge karne hon, pruning utni hi important.

2. Layer stacking (passthrough / franken-merging): alag-alag models ki layers ko ek ke upar ek stack karo. Unique architectures aur parameter counts bante hain; aam taur par aage finetuning chahiye hoti hai.

  • Goliath-120B: do finetuned Llama 2-70B models (Xwin aur Euryale) se bana — har model se 80 me se 72 layers liye.
  • MoE banana (Sparse Upcycling): pre-trained model ki certain layers ki multiple copies banao, router add karo jo har input ko sabse suitable copy par bheje, phir merged model + router ko aur train karo. Together AI ne chhah kamzor models ko mix karke Mixture-of-Agents banaya jo kuch benchmarks me GPT-4o ke barabar tha.
  • Model upscaling (depthwise scaling): bada model chahiye ho to scratch se train karne ki jagah existing model se bada banao. SOLAR 10.7B ek 7B model (32 layers) se bana: model ki copy banao, kuch layers sum karo aur baaki stack karo — 16 layers sum karne par 32 × 2 − 16 = 48 layers — phir upscaled model ko aur train karo.

3. Concatenation: parameters ko add karne ki jagah concatenate karo — merged component ke parameters constituent components ke sum hote hain. Do LoRA adapters (rank r1 aur r2) concatenate karne par merged adapter ka rank r1 + r2 hota hai. Recommended nahi hai — memory footprint kam nahi hota, alag models serve karne ke barabar hai, aur incremental performance extra parameters ke layak nahi hoti.

Yaad rakho: LoRA ka fayda modularity hai — ek base model, bahut saare chhote adapters. Merging ka fayda flexibility hai — alag-alag finetuned models ko ek model me jodna. Dono milkar multi-task, multi-customer aur on-device use cases ko practical banate hain.

07.3Chapter 7 · Finetuning

Finetuning Tactics

Finetuning ka actual process mushkil nahi hai — frameworks bahut kuch handle kar lete hain. Mushkil hai uske aas-paas ka context: kaunsa base model, kaunsi method, kaunsa framework, aur hyperparameters kaise tune karein. Ye section practical tactics deta hai.

Base model chunna — progression aur distillation paths

Chapter 4 ke model selection criteria (size, license, benchmark performance) finetuning par bhi lagte hain. Explore karte waqt sabse powerful model se shuru karo jo afford kar sako — agar strongest model bhi achha result na de, to weaker models bhi nahi denge. Agar strongest kaam kar jaye, to weaker models ko benchmark karke dekho.

Progression path (OpenAI best practices):

  1. Finetuning code test karo sabse saste aur tez model par — code sahi kaam kar raha hai ya nahi, ye check karo. (Author ki kahani: ek baar model raat bhar train hua, phir 8 ghante baad crash hua kyunki checkpoint save karne wala folder exist hi nahi karta tha.)
  2. Data test karo middling model par finetune karke. Agar zyada data par bhi training loss kam na ho, to kuch galat hai.
  3. Best model par kuch aur experiments karo — performance ko kitna aage push kar sakte ho, dekho.
  4. Saare models par training run karke price/performance frontier map karo, aur jo model sense banaye use chuno.

Distillation path:

  1. Chhote dataset aur sabse strong model se shuru karo. Strong base model ko achhi performance ke liye kam data chahiye.
  2. Is finetuned model se zyada training data generate karo.
  3. Is naye dataset se sasta model train karo.

Kyunki finetuning aam taur par prompt engineering ke baad aata hai, tab tak tumhe alag-alag models ke behaviours ki achhi samajh ho chuki hoti hai — apna finetuning development path usi samajh par plan karo.

Finetuning method chunna

  • LoRA jaise adapter methods cost-effective hain, par full finetuning jitni performance nahi dete. Shuru me LoRA try karo, full finetuning baad me.
  • Data volume: full finetuning ke liye aam taur par kam se kam hazaaron examples chahiye, aksar bahut zyada. PEFT methods chhote dataset (kuch sau examples) par bhi achhi performance de sakte hain. Chhota dataset ho to full finetuning LoRA ko hara bhi na paye.
  • Kitne models serve karne hain: LoRA se multiple models efficiently serve hote hain jo same base model share karte hain — ek full model serve karo. Full finetuning me har model ke liye poora model serve karna padta hai.

Finetuning frameworks aur APIs

  • Finetuning APIs: data upload karo, base model chuno, finetuned model pao. Model providers, cloud providers aur third-party providers dete hain. Limitation: sirf supported base models, aur saare knobs expose nahi hote. Quick aur easy ke liye achha, customization chahne walon ke liye frustrating.
  • Finetuning frameworks: LLaMA-Factory, unsloth, PEFT, Axolotl, LitGPT — adapter-based techniques ke liye wide support. Full finetuning ke liye bahut se base models apna open source training code GitHub par dete hain. Llama Police ke paas frameworks aur model repos ki comprehensive list hai.
  • Compute: khud finetune karoge to compute provision karna padega. Adapter techniques ke liye mid-tier GPU kaafi ho sakta hai. Zyada compute chahiye ho to aisa framework chuno jo tumhare cloud provider se seamlessly integrate ho.
  • Distributed training: ek se zyada machines par finetune karna ho to DeepSpeed, PyTorch Distributed ya ColossalAI jaise frameworks chahiye.

Hyperparameters — learning rate

Learning rate tay karta hai ki har learning step me parameters kitni tezi se change hon. Learning ko goal tak pahunchne ka raasta mano to learning rate step size hai: step bahut chhota ho to pahunchne me bahut time lagega; bahut bada ho to goal ko overshoot kar doge aur model kabhi converge nahi karega.

  • Universal optimal learning rate nahi hota. Aam taur par 1e-7 se 1e-3 ke beech experiment karo. Common practice: pre-training ke end ka learning rate lekar use 0.1–1 ke beech ke constant se multiply karo.
  • Loss curve se hints: loss curve bahut fluctuate kare to learning rate bahut bada hai. Loss stable hai par dheere kam ho raha hai to learning rate bahut chhota hai. Learning rate ko utna badhao jitna loss curve stable rahe.
  • Learning rate schedules: training ke dauran learning rate vary karo — shuru me bada, end me chhota. Ye tay karne wale algorithms ko learning rate schedules kehte hain.

Hyperparameters — batch size aur gradient accumulation

Batch size tay karta hai ki har step me model kitne examples se seekh kar weights update kare.

  • Bahut chhota batch (8 se kam) unstable training de sakta hai. Bada batch alag-alag examples ke signals aggregate karta hai — zyada stable aur reliable updates.
  • Bada batch training ko tez karta hai, par zyada memory chahiye hoti hai. Batch size hardware se limited hoti hai — yahi cost vs efficiency trade-off hai.
  • Gradient accumulation: compute bottleneck ki wajah se aksar sirf chhote batch use ho pate hain, jo unstable updates dete hain. Solution: har batch ke baad weights update karne ki jagah kai batches ke gradients accumulate karo, aur jab kaafi reliable gradients jama ho jayein tab ek baar weights update karo.

Hyperparameters — epochs aur prompt loss weight

Number of epochs: ek epoch matlab training data par ek poora pass. Har example kitni baar train hoga, ye epochs tay karte hain.

  • Chhote datasets ko zyada epochs chahiye: millions examples wale dataset ke liye 1–2 epochs kaafi ho sakte hain, hazaaron examples wale dataset ko 4–10 epochs ke baad bhi improvement dikh sakta hai.
  • Training loss vs validation loss: dono steadily kam ho rahe hon to aur epochs (aur data) fayda denge. Training loss kam ho raha ho par validation loss badh raha ho to model overfit kar raha hai — epochs kam karo.

Prompt loss weight: instruction finetuning me har example me prompt + response hota hai, aur dono loss me contribute kar sakte hain. Par inference me prompt user deta hai, model ko sirf response generate karna hota hai — isliye response tokens ka loss me contribution prompt tokens se zyada hona chahiye.

  • Weight 100% ho to prompt aur response barabar seekhte hain; 0% ho to model sirf responses se seekhta hai. Aam taur par default 10% hota hai — prompt se thoda seekho, response se zyada.
Yaad rakho: finetuning karna aasan hai, uske liye data jutana mushkil hai. Frameworks training process handle kar lete hain aur sensible default hyperparameters bhi suggest karte hain — asli mehnat ye tay karne me hai ki finetune karna bhi chahiye ya nahi, kis model par, aur kis data se. Agla chapter wahi data ki chunauti par hai.

08Chapter 8 · Dataset Engineering

Dataset Engineering

Model ki quality uske training data ki quality par depend karti hai. Duniya ki best ML team, infinite compute ke saath bhi, achha model finetune nahi kar sakti agar data hi nahi hai. Dataset engineering ka goal hai — allocated budget ke andar aisa dataset banana jo best model train karne de.

Data-centric AI vs model-centric AI

  • Model-centric AI: models ko behtar karke performance badhana — nayi architectures, bade models, nayi training techniques.
  • Data-centric AI: data ko behtar karke performance badhana — nayi data processing techniques aur high-quality datasets, jinse kam resources me behtar models train hon.
  • Pehle benchmarks model-centric the — ImageNet jaise fixed dataset par best model train karo. Ab data-centric benchmarks aaye hain — same model, best dataset banao. Andrew Ng ne 2021 me data-centric AI competition launch kiya (incorrect labels fix karo, edge cases add karo, data augment karo).
  • DataComp (2023): CLIP model train karne ke liye best dataset banao — standardized script se train karke 38 downstream tasks par evaluate karo. 2024 me language models (412M–7B) ke liye bhi aisa hi competition hua. Doosre benchmarks: DataPerf aur dcbench.
  • Reality me progress ke liye dono me investment chahiye — model aur data dono.

Data ki importance badhne ka ek sign: GPT-3 (2020) ke contribution list me sirf 2 log data collecting/filtering/dedup par credited the; GPT-4 (2023) me 80 log alag-alag data processes par credited the — aur isme contracted data annotators shamil nahi hain. ChatML format jaise simple cheez par bhi 11 log lage the, jinme kai senior researchers the.

Data curation ka flow — linear nahi hai

Chapter me pehle data curation (kya data chahiye, kitna, quality ka matlab kya hai), phir data synthesis aur processing techniques aati hain. Ye steps linear nahi hain — tumhe baar-baar peeche jaakar steps ke beech aana-jana padega.

  • Alag training phases ko alag capabilities sikhani hoti hain, isliye alag datasets chahiye: pre-training me quantity tokens me naapi jati hai, supervised finetuning me examples me. Par high level par curation principles same hain.
  • Ye chapter post-training data par focus karta hai (application developers ke liye zyada relevant), par pre-training se mile lessons bhi shamil karta hai jahan woh insightful hon.
  • Best practices aur automation tools hain, par data ka kaam mostly toil, tears, and sweat hi rehta hai — data roles ab dedicated ho gaye hain: data labelers, dataset creators, data quality engineers.

Kis format ka data chahiye?

Kya data chahiye, ye task aur jo behaviour sikhana hai, us par depend karta hai:

  • Self-supervised finetuning: data ke sequences chahiye.
  • Instruction finetuning: (instruction, response) format.
  • Preference finetuning: (instruction, winning response, losing response) format.
  • Reward model: preference finetuning jaisa format, ya ((instruction, response), score) format.

Training data me woh behaviours dikhne chahiye jo model ko seekhne hain. Complex behaviours sikhana khaas taur par mushkil hai:

  • Chain-of-thought (CoT): step-by-step responses wala data chahiye. "Scaling Instruction-Finetuned Language Models" ne dikhaya ki CoT responses finetuning data me shamil karne se CoT tasks par accuracy kuch tasks me lagbhag double ho gayi. Par multi-step responses likhna tedious hai — final answer dena aasan hai, step-by-step samjhana mushkil. Isliye CoT datasets kam common hain.
  • Tool use: domain experts se tool use data banwana padta hai — har prompt ek task, response woh actions jo task karne ke liye chahiye. Experts se poochhne par steps miss ho sakte hain (faulty memory, ya steps unimportant lagte hain) — isliye humans ko observe karna zaroori hota hai. Aur jo human ke liye efficient hai, woh AI ke liye efficient ho, zaroori nahi — human browser kholkar search karta hai, model search API ko ek request bhejkar saare results process kar leta hai. Isliye tool use data ke liye simulations aur synthetic techniques par bharosa karna padta hai.
  • Tool use formats: normal conversation me user aur AI ek-ek message lete hain, par tool use me AI ko ek turn me multiple messages generate karne pad sakte hain — ek code interpreter ko, ek user ko. Llama 3 ne iske liye multi-message chat format banaya: message headers jo source aur destination batate hain, aur special termination tokens jo human aur AI turns ki shuruaat batate hain.
  • Single-turn vs multi-turn: single-turn data individual instructions ka jawab sikhata hai, multi-turn data tasks solve karna sikhata hai — intent clarify karna, corrections lena. Single-turn aasan hai, multi-turn ke liye purpose-built scenarios ya lambi interactions chahiye.
  • Unlearning bhi curation hai: galat behaviours wala data hatao bhi. Example: chatbot arrogant lagta hai — "statement sahi hai, par style improve kar sakte hain" kehkar unsolicited rewriting deta hai. Investigation me pata chala training data me unsolicited suggestions wale examples the — unhe hatane aur fact-checking bina rewriting wale naye examples lane ki request daali gayi.
Yaad rakho: data curation ke 3 core criteria hain — quality, coverage, quantity. Cooking analogy: data ingredients hain — quality matlab ingredients ki quality (kharab ingredients se achha khana nahi banega), coverage matlab sahi mix (cheeni na zyada na kam), quantity matlab kitne ingredients chahiye. Detail agle section me.
SOURCESource: Huyen, AI Engineering, O'Reilly, Chapter 8 — Dataset Engineering
← Previous07.3 · Finetuning Tactics→ Next08.1 · Data Quality, Coverage aur Quantity
08.1Chapter 8 · Dataset Engineering

Data Quality, Coverage aur Quantity

Dataset design ke 3 core criteria hain — quality, coverage, quantity. Headlines me quantity aati hai, par chhota sa high-quality dataset bade noisy dataset ko hara sakta hai. Is section me teeno ko detail me samjhenge.

Data quality — chhota achha data, bade kharab data se behtar

  • Yi model family ke creators ne paya: 10,000 carefully crafted instructions lakhon noisy instructions se behtar hain.
  • LIMA (Less Is More for Alignment): 65B Llama model, sirf 1,000 carefully curated prompts/responses par finetune hua, GPT-4 ke barabar ya usse behtar answers 43% cases me de paya (human annotators ke hisaab se). Downside: itne kam data se model product-grade models jitna robust nahi hota.
  • Llama 3 team bhi is nateeje par pahunchi — aur unhone paya ki human-generated data errors aur inconsistencies ke prati zyada prone hai, khaas taur par nuanced safety policies ke liye. Isliye unhone AI-assisted annotation tools banaye.

High-quality data ka matlab hai — data tumhara kaam efficiently aur reliably karne me madad kare. Aam taur par high-quality data ki 6 characteristics hoti hain:

  • Relevant: examples task se relevant hon. Aaj ke legal questions ke liye 19th century ka legal dataset relevant nahi hai — par 19th century ke legal system ke baare me task ho to wahi dataset highly relevant hai.
  • Aligned with task requirements: annotations task ki requirements se align hon. Factual consistency chahiye to annotations factually correct hon; creativity chahiye to creative hon; score + justification chahiye to dono hon; concise answers chahiye to concise hon. "Aligned" shabd "accurate" ki jagah isliye use hua hai kyunki accurate jawab hamesha woh nahi hota jo user chahta hai.
  • Consistent: examples aur annotators ke beech consistent hon. Do annotators same example ko bahut alag annotate na karein. Essays ko 1–5 score karna ho to same score wale essays same quality ke hone chahiye. Inconsistent annotations model ko confuse karti hain. Iske liye achhi annotation guideline zaroori hai.
  • Correctly formatted: saare examples model ke expected format me hon. Redundant formatting tokens learning me interfere karte hain — scraped reviews se HTML tags hatao. Trailing white spaces, new lines, inconsistent casing, numerical formats se bacho.
  • Sufficiently unique: duplicates biases aur data contamination laate hain. "Sufficiently" isliye kyunki har use case alag level ka duplication tolerate kar sakta hai.
  • Compliant: saari internal aur external policies (laws, regulations) ke compliant hon. PII use karna allowed nahi hai to data me PII nahi hona chahiye.

Data coverage (diversity)

Training data ko un problems ki range cover karni chahiye jo model se solve karne ki ummeed hai. Users apni problems alag-alag tareekon se express karte hain — data ko woh diverse usage patterns capture karne chahiye.

  • Agar kuch users detailed instructions dete hain aur kuch chhoti, to dono tarah ki instructions data me honi chahiye. User queries me typos aam hon to typos wale examples bhi hone chahiye. Multiple programming languages support karni hon to un saari languages ka data hona chahiye.
  • Har application ke diversity ke alag dimensions hote hain: French-to-English tool ko language diversity nahi, topic/length/style diversity chahiye; global customers wale chatbot ko domain diversity nahi, linguistic aur cultural diversity chahiye.
  • NVIDIA ke Nemotron ke liye researchers ne task diversity, topic diversity aur instruction diversity par focus kiya — alag output formats, alag output lengths, open-ended aur yes-or-no answers. Par "The Data Addition Dilemma" ne dikhaya ki kabhi-kabhi zyada heterogeneous data add karne se performance kharab bhi ho sakti hai.
  • Llama 3: architecture purane Llama se zyada alag nahi tha — performance gains "primarily driven by improvements in data quality and diversity as well as by increased training scale" the.
  • Llama 3 data mix (domain): pre-training me general knowledge (English) 50%, math/reasoning 25%, coding 17%, multilingual 8%; SFT me 52.66% / 21.19% / 14.89% / 3.01% + exam-like 8.14% + long context 0.11%; preference finetuning me general knowledge 81.99%, math 5.89%, coding 6.93%, multilingual 5.19%. Pre-training aur SFT me math+reasoning+code milakar lagbhag aadha data hai — internet ka itna hissa math/code nahi hai. High-quality code aur math data par annealing (learning rate dheere-dheere kam karte hue zyada code/math data se training) benchmarks par performance boost karta hai — code/math data natural language text se reasoning badhane me zyada effective hai. Preference finetuning me code+math sirf 12.82% hai, kyunki goal real user preferences ka distribution reflect karna hai.
  • Sahi data mix kaise tay karein? Simple tareeka: real-world application usage ko reflect karne wala mix chuno. Ya experiments karo — Meta ne scaling law experiments kiye: har candidate mix par chhote models train karke bade model ki performance predict ki, aur best-guess mix chuna.
  • Experiment (Zhou et al., 2023): 7B model ko 2,000 examples ke 3 datasets par train kiya — (1) high-quality par diverse nahi, (2) diverse par low-quality, (3) diverse aur high-quality dono. Teesra model dono se behtar raha — quality aur diversity dono chahiye.

Data quantity — kitna data chahiye?

"Kitna data chahiye?" ye poochhna "kitna paisa chahiye?" jaisa hai — jawab har situation me alag hai. Ek extreme par Jeremy Howard aur Jonathan Whitaker ne dikhaya ki LLMs ek hi example se seekh sakte hain; doosre extreme par teams ne millions examples se finetune kiya hai. Reference ke liye: Llama 2 ko 2 trillion tokens, Llama 3 ko 16 trillion tokens par train kiya gaya — har example 2,000 tokens ka ho to ye 1 billion aur 15 billion examples ke barabar hai.

Quantity ko influence karne wale 3 factors (quality aur diversity ke alawa):

  • Finetuning technique: full finetuning ko PEFT (jaise LoRA) se orders of magnitude zyada data chahiye. Tens of thousands–millions (instruction, response) pairs hon to full finetuning try karo; sirf kuch sau–hazaar examples hon to PEFT best hai.
  • Task complexity: product review positive/negative classify karna simple hai — kam data chahiye. Financial filings par question answering complex hai — bahut zyada data chahiye.
  • Base model ki performance: base model desirable performance ke jitna kareeb hoga, utne kam examples chahiye. Bade base models behtar hote hain, isliye unhe finetune karne ke liye kam examples chahiye — pre-training se ulta, jahan bade models ko zyada data chahiye.

OpenAI finetuning guide ka experiment: 100 examples par advanced models ne finetuning ke baad bahut behtar performance di (kyunki out of the box bhi behtar the). 550,000 examples par paanchon models ki performance lagbhag barabar ho gayi. Matlab: chhota data ho to advanced models par PEFT karo; bada data ho to chhote models par full finetuning karo.

Chhote dataset se shuru karo

  • Bada dataset curate karne se pehle 50 examples ka chhota, well-crafted dataset try karo. Agar desirable performance mil jaye to great. Clear improvement dikhe to aur data se aur improvement ki ummeed karo. Koi improvement na dikhe to bada dataset rarely kaam karta hai.
  • Par jaldi conclude mat karo: hyperparameters (learning rate bahut high/low), data quality, poorly crafted prompts — bahut si cheezein results ko affect karti hain. Zyadatar cases me 50–100 examples par finetuning ke baad improvement dikhna chahiye.
  • Performance gain curve: dataset ke subsets (25%, 50%, 100%) par model finetune karke performance vs dataset size plot karo. Steep slope matlab data double karne se bada fayda; plateau matlab fayda chhota. Aam taur par diminishing returns hote hain — pehle 1,000 examples accuracy 10 points badhayein, agle 1,000 sirf 5 points.
  • Diversity bhi scale karti hai: Chung et al. (2022) ne dikhaya ki finetuning tasks 9 se 282 badhane par performance significantly badhi; 282 ke baad gains plateau hone lage, par 1,836 tasks tak positive incremental improvements milte rahe. Diversity task types, topics aur expected output formats (JSON, yes-or-no) me reflect hoti hai.
  • High-quality data ki zaroorat kam karne ke 3 tareeke: (1) Self-supervised → supervised: pehle legal documents par self-supervised finetune karo, phir (question, answer) pairs par. (2) Less-relevant → relevant: pehle tweet sentiment par finetune karo, phir product sentiment par. (3) Synthetic → real: pehle AI-synthesized data par finetune karo, phir real data par — par ye mushkil hai, do alag finetuning jobs coordinate karne padte hain, aur galat kiya to sirf high-quality data se finetune karne se bura model ban sakta hai.
  • Ossification: bahut zyada training data ho to scratch se train karna finetuning se behtar ho sakta hai — pre-training weights ko ossify (freeze) kar deti hai, woh finetuning data par utna adapt nahi kar pate. Chhote models ossification ke prati zyada susceptible hote hain.
  • Budget bhi matter karta hai: $10,000 budget aur $2 per example ho to max 5,000 examples. Data par zyada kharch karoge to compute ke liye kam bachega, aur vice versa.
Yaad rakho: quality aur diversity quantity se kam important nahi hain. 1,000 carefully curated examples (LIMA) GPT-4 ko 43% cases me takkar de sakte hain, aur diverse + high-quality dataset sirf diverse ya sirf high-quality dataset se behtar model deta hai. Pehle 50 examples se shuru karo, phir gain curve dekhkar decide karo ki aur data chahiye ya nahi.
SOURCESource: Huyen, AI Engineering, O'Reilly, Chapter 8 — Dataset Engineering
