08.2Chapter 8 · Dataset Engineering

Data Acquisition aur Annotation

Dataset banane ka goal hai — quality aur diversity ke saath kaafi bada dataset, user privacy ka samman aur regulations ka compliance. Data acquisition ke tareeke hain: public data source karna, proprietary data khareedna, annotate karna, aur synthesize karna. Is section me acquisition aur annotation ki strategy samjhenge.

Sabse important source: tumhara apna application data

Apne application ka data ideal hota hai — perfectly relevant aur task se aligned, kyunki woh exactly usi distribution ka hota hai jiski tumhe parwah hai. Ye kisi aur source se achieve karna bahut mushkil hai. User-generated data user content, system-generated usage data, ya user feedback ho sakta hai. Agar tum data flywheel bana lo — users ka data product ko continually improve kare — to tumhe bada advantage milega. User feedback system kaise design karein, ye Chapter 10 me hai.

Apna data banane me invest karne se pehle available datasets check karo. Data marketplaces me open source aur proprietary dono tarah ka data hai — kabhi-kabhi koi dataset exactly tumhari zaroorat ka mil jata hai. Aksar mix-and-match approach hota hai — ek dataset multiple sources aur channels se banta hai. Example — (instruction, response) dataset banane ka process:

  1. Available datasets me desirable characteristics wala ek promising dataset dhoondho — maan lo 10,000 examples.
  2. Low-quality instructions hatao — maan lo 9,000 examples bachte hain.
  3. Low-quality responses wale instructions alag rakho — maan lo 3,000 aise examples. Bache 6,000 high-quality instruction + high-quality response examples.
  4. 3,000 high-quality instructions ke responses manually likho — ab total 9,000 high-quality examples.
  5. Topic X ke liye data kam lage to 100 instruction templates manually banao, AI se in 10 templates se 2,000 instructions synthesize karwao.
  6. 2,000 synthetic instructions manually annotate karo — ab total 11,000 examples.

Ye oversimplification hai — asal me aur bhi steps hote hain: annotations helpful na lagein to guidelines update karke re-annotate karna, factually incorrect annotations ko fact-check karne ke liye doosre annotators hire karna, ek template se 100 instructions banane se diversity kharab ho to zyada templates aur kam instructions per template banana, aur aise hi bahut kuch.

Public datasets kahan dhoondhein — 10 resources

Available data ka fayda uthao, par us par kabhi poora bharosa mat karo — data ko thoroughly inspect aur validate karo. Dataset ka license hamesha check karo, aur samjho ki data kahan se aaya hai. Commercial use allow karne wala license bhi ho sakta hai, par uska ek hissa aise source se aaya ho jo allow na karta ho.

  1. Hugging Face aur Kaggle — har ek par lakhon datasets.
  2. Google Dataset Search — wonderful aur underrated.
  3. Governments — open data ke great providers. Data.gov par lakhon datasets, data.gov.in par tens of thousands.
  4. University of Michigan ICPSR (Institute for Social Research) — tens of thousands social studies ka data.
  5. UC Irvine Machine Learning Repository aur OpenML — purane repositories, har ek par kai hazaar datasets.
  6. Open Data Network — tens of thousands datasets search kar sakte ho.
  7. Cloud providers — chhota sa open datasets ka collection host karte hain; sabse notable AWS Open Data.
  8. ML frameworks — TensorFlow datasets jaise chhote pre-built datasets framework use karte hue load kar sakte ho.
  9. Evaluation harness tools — Eleuther AI ka lm-evaluation-harness 400+ benchmark datasets host karta hai, average 2,000+ examples per dataset — PEFT finetuning ke liye kaafi bade.
  10. Stanford Large Network Dataset Collection — graph datasets ke liye great repository.

Annotation — guidelines sabse mushkil hissa

Aksar apna data annotate karna padta hai. Annotation mushkil sirf process ki wajah se nahi hai, balki clear annotation guidelines banane ki complexity ki wajah se bhi hai. Explicitly batana padta hai ki achha response kaisa dikhta hai, aur kya use achha banata hai. Kya response correct par unhelpful ho sakta hai? Score 3 aur 4 me kya farak hai?

  • LinkedIn jaise teams ne bataya ki annotation guidelines unke AI engineering pipeline ke sabse challenging parts me se ek thi. Bahut log aadhe raaste me careful annotation chhod dete hain, ummeed karte hain ki model khud sahi responses figure out kar lega. Strong models kabhi-kabhi succeed bhi kar jate hain, par is par bharosa karna bahut applications ke liye risky hai.
  • Achhi khabar: ye guidelines evaluation data wali guidelines hi hain (Chapter 4). Isi liye evaluation guidelines aur data par zyada time invest karna chahiye. Agar lucky rahe to evaluation examples ko augment karke ya seed examples banakar naya data synthesize kar sakte ho — agle section me yehi aata hai.
Yaad rakho: data acquisition strategy ek growing research field hai — diye gaye budget me specific requirements meet karne wala dataset best tareeke se kaise acquire karein. Pehle available datasets check karo, phir apne application ka data flywheel banao, aur annotation guidelines ko evaluation guidelines jitna hi seriously lo.
SOURCESource: Huyen, AI Engineering, O'Reilly, Chapter 8 — Dataset Engineering
← Previous08.1 · Data Quality, Coverage aur Quantity→ Next08.3 · Data Augmentation, Synthesis aur Distillation
08.3Chapter 8 · Dataset Engineering

Data Augmentation, Synthesis aur Distillation

Data, compute aur talent ke saath AI ki sabse mushkil chunauti hai. Data ko programmatically generate karna industry ka long-term goal raha hai. Augmentation existing (real) data se naya data banata hai, synthesis real data ki properties mimic karne wala data generate karta hai. AI ke aane se ye dono ab bahut powerful ho gaye hain.

Augmentation vs synthesis

  • Data augmentation: existing real data se naya data — jaise billi ki real photo ko flip karke nayi photo banana.
  • Data synthesis: real data jaisi properties wala data generate karna — jaise mouse ke web page par movement simulate karke bot movements ka data banana.
  • Dono ka goal data creation automate karna hai, isliye terms kabhi-kabhi interchangeably use hote hain. Is chapter me "data synthesis" aksar dono ke liye use hota hai.
  • Artificially generated data ka software engineering me lamba history hai — Faker aur Chance jaise libraries testing ke liye fake data (names, addresses, phone numbers, emails) generate karti hain. Jaise shipping addresses parse karne wale program ko test karne ke liye alag-alag countries/states ke alag formats wale addresses generate karo.
  • AI ab human-generated data se indistinguishable data generate kar sakta hai — doctor's notes, contracts, financial statements, product descriptions, images, video commercials. Synthetic data human data ko poori tarah replace nahi karta — aksar human + AI data ka mix best value deta hai.

Data synthesis kyun? — 5 reasons

  • Quantity badhana: scale par data produce karo. Real-world data scarce ho (rare weather, deep sea exploration, self-driving accidents) to synthesis hi rasta hai. Zyada data, theory me, models ko wider range of tasks par generalize karne me madad karta hai.
  • Coverage badhana: targeted characteristics wala data generate karo — bahut chhote ya bahut lambe texts, toxic detection ke liye toxic phrases wali conversations (ya toxic real data ho to safe data), adversarial examples, rare class ke liye data (class imbalance). TrueTeacher (Gekhman et al., 2022) ne LLMs se factually inconsistent summaries generate karke factual inconsistency detect karne wale models train kiye. Anthropic ne 154 alag AI behaviours (personality, political views, ethical stances, social biases) test karne wale datasets synthesize kiye — head-to-head me LM-written datasets human-written ke kareeb, kabhi-kabhi usse behtar paye gaye.
  • Quality badhana: kabhi-kabhi synthetic data human data se behtar hota hai. Tool use data me humans aur AI ke operation modes alag hain; complex math problems me AI average human expert se zyada complex questions generate kar sakta hai. Preference data me bhi AI zyada consistent aur reliable ratings de sakta hai — har human apne aap me consistent ho sakta hai, par alag-alag logon me mood aur motivation se performance vary karti hai.
  • Privacy concerns mitigate karna: healthcare me real patient records use karna mushkil ya impossible hai — synthetic patient records banao jinme sensitive information na ho. Insurance me real claims ki jagah synthetic claims use karo.
  • Model distillation: chhota model bade model ka behaviour imitate kare — distilled model bade model se generated data par train hota hai (detail neeche).

Traditional techniques — rule-based aur simulation

Rule-based synthesis: predefined rules aur templates se data generate karo. Credit card transaction template lo aur Faker jaise random generator se har field bharo (Transaction ID, Date, Time, Amount, Merchant, Category, Location, Payment Method, Status, Description). Fraud detection models pehle aise synthetic data par train hote hain, phir real data milta hai. Templates se invoices, resumes, tax forms, bank statements, contracts, configuration files jaise structured documents bhi bante hain, aur regular expressions aur math equations jaise grammar/syntax wala data bhi. DeepMind ne AlphaGeometry ko 100 million synthetic examples par train kiya.

  • Simple transformations: images ko rotate, crop, scale, erase karo — flipped billi ki photo phir bhi billi hi hai. AlexNet paper ne ImageNet augment karke iski usefulness dikhayi. Text me word ko similar word se replace karo — "She's a fantastic nurse" se "She's a great nurse". Similar words dictionary se ya word embeddings ki closeness se dhoondho.
  • Bias mitigation: gendered words ko opposite se replace karo — "she" → "he", "nurse" ke saath "doctor", "Mr. Alex Wang" → "Ms. Alexa Wang", "mom" → "dad", "Emily" → "Mohammed".
  • Perturbation: data me noise add karke naya data banao. Ek pixel change karne se 67.97% CIFAR-10 aur 16.04% ImageNet test images misclassify ho sakti hain (One Pixel Attack). Perturbed data par train karne se model ki performance aur robustness dono badhti hain. ImageNet-C aur ImageNet-P ne 15 common corruptions (brightness, snow, contrast, noise) apply kiye. Text me BERT training me 1.5% tokens random words se replace kiye gaye — chhota sa performance boost mila.
  • Sophisticated visual augmentation: Snap ne characters ko alag skin colors, body types, hairstyles, clothes, facial expressions ke saath synthesize karke unrepresented corner cases aur implicit biases mitigate kiye.

Simulation: real world me experiment karna mehnga ya khatarnak ho to virtual environment me simulate karo. Self-driving car highway par ghode se kaise react karegi — asli ghoda chhodna khatarnak hai, simulation me test karo (CARLA, Waymo SimulationCity, Tesla ka San Francisco simulation). Robot ko coffee pour karna sikhana ho to alag-alag joint movements simulate karo, sirf successful scenarios se train karo.

  • Simulations se multiple experiments kam cost me, bina accidents aur physical damage ke. Simulation me kaam karne wala robot real world me kaam na bhi kare, par simulation me fail hone wala real world me bhi fail hoga. Simulations real world ke simplifications hain — Sim2Real subfield simulation-trained algorithms ko real world me adapt karne par focus karta hai.
  • Tool use data ke liye simulations: diye gaye query par alag-alag action sequences simulate karo, execute karo, outcomes validate karo — sabse efficient sequence ko annotated response banao. Rare events (company IPO, bankruptcy, material defects, extreme weather) ke liye bhi simulations invaluable hain.

AI-powered synthesis

  • AI simulating programs/humans: StableToolBench ne dikhaya ki AI se APIs simulate karo bina actual calls kiye — costly ya slow API calls ki jagah simulated outcomes use karo. OpenAI ne Dota 2 bot ko self-play se train kiya — simulator se bot roz ~180 saal ke games khelta tha. DeepMind ne AlphaGo ke liye self-play se millions Go games ka data collect kiya. Self-play general agents ke liye bhi kaam karta hai — ek AI customer bane, doosri customer support agent, alag-alag negotiation strategies test karo.
  • Paraphrasing aur translation: "How to reset my password?" se AI 3 naye queries banata hai — "I forgot my password", "How can I change my password?", "Steps to reset passwords". Yu et al. ne MATH aur GSM-8K ke 15,000 examples rewrite karke MetaMath banaya — lagbhag 400,000 examples — aur is par trained models ne bade models ko math benchmarks par haraya. High-resource languages ka data low-resource languages (Quechua, Lao) me translate karo. Back-translation se quality verify karo: English X → Lao Y → wapas English X'. X' aur X bahut alag hon to translation Y kharab hai. AI programming languages bhi translate kar sakta hai.
  • Llama 3 back-translation: code snippets se AI ne explanations/documentation generate kiye, phir unse wapas code generate kiya — sirf tabhi explanation/documentation use ki jab generated code original ke faithful ho.
  • Pre-training vs post-training: synthetic data post-training me zyada deliberately include hota hai, kyunki post-training data (instruction aur preference) produce karna sabse zyada effort mangta hai. Pre-training ka goal knowledge badhana hai, aur AI existing knowledge ko naye formats me synthesize kar sakta hai, par naya knowledge synthesize karna mushkil hai. Phir bhi internet AI-generated content se bhar raha hai, to internet data par pre-trained models pehle se hi synthetic data par train ho rahe hain. Cosmopedia — 25-billion-token synthetic textbooks, blog posts, stories, WikiHow articles, Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct se generate kiye gaye.
  • Preference data synthesis: AI judge se better response chunna — Chapter 3 me covered. Model ke biases (jaise first-position bias) ka khayal rakho: NVIDIA researchers ne AI judge se do baar poocha, response order swap karke — sirf tabhi (prompt, winning, losing) triplet valid maana jab dono baar same winner chuna gaya.

Instruction data synthesis

Instruction finetuning me har example me instruction + response hota hai. AI instructions, responses, ya dono synthesize kar sakta hai:

  • Instruction generation: topics, keywords ya instruction types ki list se shuru karo, har item ke liye kuch instructions generate karo. Ya templates se shuru karo, har template se kuch examples generate karo. Topic list aur templates bhi AI generate kar sakta hai.
  • Response generation: har instruction ke liye ek ya zyada responses generate karo.
  • UltraChat: ChatGPT se 30 topics generate karwaye (technology, food, fashion, nature, education, finance, travel...), har topic ke 30–50 subtopics, phir un subtopics ke liye instructions aur responses generate karwaye — multi-turn dialogue dataset bana.
  • Alpaca: Stanford researchers ne Self-Instruct seed dataset ke 175 (instruction, response) examples se shuru kiya, phir GPT-3 (text-davinci-003) se 52,000 pairs generate karwaye.
  • Reverse instruction: lambi, high-quality responses generate karna AI ke liye mushkil hai — lamba response, zyada hallucination ka chance. Solution ulta karo: existing long-form high-quality content (stories, books, Wikipedia articles) lo, aur AI se prompts generate karwao jo aisa content elicit karein. Isse responses human-generated (high-quality) rehte hain, hallucinations avoid hote hain. Bootstrapping loop (Li et al., 2023): (1) chhote seed examples se weak model train karo, (2) weak model se existing high-quality content ke liye instructions generate karo, (3) is naye high-quality instruction data par weak model finetune karo, (4) desirable performance milne tak repeat karo — theory me model khud ko continually improve kar sakta hai.
  • Long-context finetuning ke liye: lambe documents ko chhote chunks (8K tokens se kam) me todo, har chunk ke liye (question, answer) pairs generate karo, phir har pair ke liye original long document ko context banakar train karo — model extended context use karna seekhta hai.
  • Llama 3 coding data pipeline: (1) AI se diverse topics par programming problem descriptions generate karo, (2) har problem + language ke liye solution generate karo (good programming rules aur CoT reasoning shamil karke quality badhao), (3) parsers/linters se syntactic errors pakdo, (4) unit tests (AI se generate kiye) se runtime errors pakdo, (5) fail hone par model ko revise karne ko prompt karo — original problem + faulty solution + parser/linter/test feedback dekar; sirf saare checks pass karne wale examples final SFT dataset me aaye. ~20% solutions pehle incorrect the par self-correct ho gaye. (6) Code ko alag languages me translate karo, tests fail karne wale ko filter out karo. (7) Code ke baare me conversations (explanation, documentation) generate karo, back-translation verification fail karne walon ko filter out karo. Total: 2.7 million+ synthetic coding examples Llama 3.1 ke SFT ke liye.

Data verification — synthetic data ko kaise check karein

  • Quality measure karne ke tareeke wahi hain jo AI outputs evaluate karne ke — functional correctness aur AI judges. Ye techniques general training data par bhi lagti hain.
  • Log wahi data synthesize karte hain jo verify kar sakte hain (evaluation-driven development, Chapter 4) — isiliye coding examples sabse zyada synthesized hote hain: code execution aur back-translation se programmatically verify ho sakte hain.
  • AI verifiers: general-purpose AI judge ya specialized scorer. Har example ko 1–5 score do ya good/bad classify karo, ya model ko quality requirements batakar check karwao ki example unhe meet karta hai ya nahi. Factual consistency ke liye Chapter 4 ki factual inconsistency detection techniques use karo.
  • Creative checks: synthetic data real data jaisa hona chahiye to AI content detector train karo — real aur synthetic aasani se distinguish ho jayein to synthetic data achha nahi hai. Academic work jaisa hona chahiye to classifier train karo jo predict kare ki paper NeurIPS me accept hoga ya nahi — clear rejects discard karo. Topic detect karke irrelevant topics wale examples hatao. Sab examples similar pattern follow karte hon to anomaly detection se outliers dhoondho.
  • Heuristic filtering: empty ya bahut chhote examples hatao, bahut lambe ko truncate karo ya hatao, keywords/user/author/date/metadata/source se filter karo. Self-Instruct authors ne filter kiya: repetitive examples, bahut lambi ya bahut chhoti instructions, same instruction par alag responses, output input ka repetition ho.
  • Ultimate test real-world performance hai — kya synthetic data model ki performance improve karta hai? Bahut se models ke liye is test ko synthetic data pass kar chuka hai.

Limitations of AI-generated data — 4 badi problems

  • Quality control: AI data low quality ka ho sakta hai — "garbage in, garbage out". Agar quality verify nahi kar sakte to log synthetic data use karne me hesitate karenge. Reliable evaluation methods aur metrics develop karna essential hai.
  • Superficial imitation: "The False Promise of Imitating Proprietary LLMs" ne dikhaya ki imitation models teacher ki style mimic karne me achhe hote hain, par factual accuracy aur training data se bahar generalize karne me struggle karte hain. Imitation hallucination bhi sikha sakta hai — teacher complex math solve kar sakta hai, uske solutions par student ko train karna use aise answers produce karna sikhata hai jo solutions jaise dikhte hain, bhale student solve kar hi na paye. Human annotations me bhi yehi issue ho sakta hai — labeler apne knowledge se answer de, jo model ke paas nahi hai.
  • Model collapse: recursively AI-generated data par train karne se models me irreversible defects aate hain, performance degrade hoti hai (Shumailov et al., 2023 — "The Curse of Recursion"). AI probable events zyada generate karta hai (cancer na hona) aur improbable events kam (cancer hona) — iterations ke saath probable events over-represented aur rare events under-represented ho jate hain, model rare events bhool jata hai. Gerstgrasser et al. (2024) kehte hain synthetic + real data mix karne se collapse avoid ho sakta hai, par koi definitive ratio recommendation nahi hai. Kuch experiments me synthetic data ~1 million samples tak saturation ke bina kaam karta hai, aur Nemotron-4 340B-Instruct ne instruction + preference finetuning me 98% synthetic data use kiya — par ye sirf ek model iteration ke experiments the. Data feedback loops biases bhi amplify kar sakte hain (Taori aur Hashimoto, 2023).
  • Obscure data lineage: AI generation data lineage chhupa deta hai. Model X se data generate karke apna model train karo — agar X copyright-violating data par train hua tha, to tumhara model bhi copyright violate kar sakta hai. Ya benchmark B par tumhara model strong perform kare, par X bhi B par train hua ho to result contaminated hai. Clear lineage ke bina commercial viability assess karna ya performance par bharosa karna mushkil hai.

Model distillation

Model distillation (knowledge distillation) — chhota model (student) bade model (teacher) ko mimic karna seekhta hai (Hinton et al., 2015). Traditionally goal hota hai deployment ke liye chhota, tez model banana jo teacher jaisi performance retain kare. DistilBERT ne BERT ka size 40% kam kiya, 97% language understanding retain ki, aur 60% tez hua. Student scratch se train ho sakta hai (DistilBERT) ya pre-trained model se finetune ho sakta hai (Alpaca — Llama-7B ko text-davinci-003 ke examples par finetune kiya, teacher ka 4% size).

  • License warning: sab models distill nahi kiye ja sakte — bahut se licenses apne outputs se doosre models (khaas taur par competing models) train karne par rok lagate hain.
  • Synthetic instruction data aksar LoRA jaise adapter techniques ke saath use hota hai — BuzzFeed ne Flan-T5 ko LoRA + text-davinci-003 ke examples se finetune karke inference cost 80% kam ki.
  • Har synthetic training distillation nahi hoti: student teacher se bada aur powerful bhi ho sakta hai. Reverse instruction bootstrapping ek example hai. NVIDIA ka Nemotron-4: pehle 340B base model pre-train kiya, phir Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct (56B MoE) se generated instruction + preference data par finetune kiya — resulting Nemotron-4-340B-Instruct ne teacher ko kai tasks par haraya.
  • Llama 3 paper kehta hai: zyada competent model ke data par train karne se performance significantly badhti hai, par indiscriminately self-generated data par train karne se performance badhti nahi, degrade bhi ho sakti hai. Sirf verified synthetic data use karke hi model khud ke generated data se continually improve ho paya.
Yaad rakho: synthetic data quantity, coverage, quality, privacy aur distillation — paanchon reasons se attractive hai. Par use verify kiye bina train mat karo, aur human data ko poori tarah replace karne ki ummeed mat rakho: model collapse, superficial imitation aur obscure lineage real risks hain. Best value aksar human + AI data ke mix se milti hai.

← Previous08.2 · Data Acquisition aur Annotation→ Next08.4 · Data Processing — Inspect, Dedup, Clean, Format
08.4Chapter 8 · Dataset Engineering

Data Processing — Inspect, Dedup, Clean, Format

Data acquire karne ke baad use model ki requirements ke hisaab se process karna padta hai — inspect, deduplicate, clean/filter, aur format. Bade data par har step me ghante, kabhi din lag sakte hain. Is section me har step aur efficiency ke tips samjhenge.

Efficiency tips — pehle ye padho

  • Order flexible hai: steps jis order me time aur compute bachaye, us order me karo. Cleaning har example par zyada time le to pehle duplicates hatao, phir clean karo. Deduplication cleaning se zyada time le to pehle low-quality data filter karo.
  • Pehle trial runs karo: processing scripts ko poore data par lagane se pehle validate karo ki woh sahi kaam karte hain.
  • Data ko in place change mat karo: original data ki copy rakho — (1) tumhe ya kisi aur team ko data ko alag tareeke se process karna pad sakta hai doosre applications ke liye, (2) scripts me bugs data corrupt kar sakte hain.
  • Model papers padhna helpful hai jo dataset details disclose karte hain — unme curation, generation aur processing ke great tips milte hain.

Inspect data — pehle data ko dekho

Raw dataset gather karne ke baad pehla kaam hai inspect karna — quality ka sense lena. Data kahan se aaya hai? Kaise process hua hai? Kis aur kaam me use hua hai? Statistics nikalo aur distributions plot karo:

  • Tokens ka distribution (kaunse tokens common hain), input lengths, response lengths. Koi special tokens use ho rahe hain? Topics aur languages ka distribution kya hai? Tumhare task se kitne relevant hain?
  • Creative statistics use karo: Microsoft researchers ne GPT-3 vs GPT-4 generations compare karne ke liye (verb, direct object, noun) pairs aur response length ke distributions use kiye — GPT-4 ke verb-noun pairings zyada diverse the aur responses lambe hote the. Ye analysis data evaluate karne ke liye bhi useful hai, models ke liye bhi.
  • Distributions ko data source, time, annotator ke hisaab se plot karo. Kaunse question patterns lambe/chhote responses ya high/low scores lete hain? Outliers hain? Unki wajah kya hai? Unke saath kya karna hai?
  • Agar scores normal distribution follow karne chahiye to kya saare annotators ke scores normal distribution follow karte hain? Kuch annotators bahut chhote responses dete hain ya high scores ki taraf biased hote hain — unke annotations ke saath kya karna hai, tumhe decide karna hai.
  • Har example ki ek se zyada annotations hon to inter-annotator disagreement compute karo. Conflicting annotations wale examples check karo aur conflicts resolve karo.
  • Data exploration tools use karo, par woh manual inspection ki jagah nahi le sakte. Har project me sirf 15 minute data ko ghoorne se aisi insight milti hai jo ghanton ki headache bacha sakti hai. OpenAI co-founder Greg Brockman ne tweet kiya tha: "Manual inspection of data has probably the highest value-to-prestige ratio of any activity in machine learning." Kuch queries khud annotate karke dekho ki tumhari annotations di gayi annotations se match karti hain ya nahi — isse annotations ki trustworthiness ka sense milta hai. Responses ko fact-check karo. Examples kitne unique hain? Same query par alag responses, ya same response par alag queries to nahi hain?

Deduplicate data — duplicates kyun kharab hain

Duplicated data data distribution ko skew karta hai aur model me biases introduce karta hai. Toy example: dataset me "red pencil → $20" 3 baar ho, to model galat conclusion nikaal sakta hai ki saare red items expensive hone chahiye. Duplications test set contamination bhi karte hain — duplicate ka ek copy train set me aur doosra test set me chala jaye.

  • Anthropic study: 0.1% data ko 100 baar repeat karne se 800M-parameter model ki performance 400M-parameter model jitni degrade ho gayi, bhale baaki 90% training tokens unique rahe. Performance kharab na bhi ho to duplicates time aur compute waste karte hain.
  • Duplication ke types (documents me): whole document duplications (same document ek se zyada baar), intra-document duplications (same paragraph ek document me do baar), cross-document duplications (same popular quote kai documents me).
  • Definition tumhari hai: duplication document level, paragraph level, sentence level ya token level par dekho? Exact match chahiye ya 80% overlap kaafi hai? Same items alag order me hon to lists duplicates hain ya nahi?
  • Deduplication ke tareeke: (1) Pairwise comparison — har example ka har doosre example se similarity score compute karo (exact match, n-gram match, fuzzy match, semantic similarity — Chapter 3) — bade datasets par mehnga hai. (2) Hashing — examples ko buckets me hash karo, sirf same bucket walon me check karo (MinHash, Bloom filter). (3) Dimensionality reduction — pehle data ki dimensions kam karo, phir pairwise comparison karo; vector search ki techniques (Chapter 6) yahan bhi kaam aati hain.
  • Libraries: dupeGuru, Dedupe, datasketch, TextDistance, TheFuzz, deduplicate-text-datasets. Author ki lazyNLP library bhi Bloom filter se overlap estimation aur deduplication support karti hai.

Clean aur filter data

  • Extraneous formatting tokens hatao: internet se scraped datasets me HTML tags common hain — model ko HTML tags par train nahi karna to unhe hatao. Databricks ne paya ki extraneous Markdown aur HTML tokens hatane se model ki accuracy 20% badhi aur input token lengths 60% kam hui.
  • Non-compliant data hatao: PII, sensitive data, copyrighted data, toxic data. Chapter 4 ki techniques madad karti hain. Woh fields hatao jo use karna allowed nahi hai — zip code, name, gender.
  • Low-quality data hatao: "Data verification" wali techniques se low-quality data detect karo. Manual inspection yahan khaas taur par important hai — data ko ghoorne se patterns dikhte hain jo low-quality data detect karne ke heuristics ban sakte hain. Non-obvious heuristic example: Kern et al. (2024) ne paya ki annotation session ke second half me ki gayi annotations lower quality ki hoti hain — shayad annotator boredom ya fatigue ki wajah se.
  • Filter karna (agar data zaroorat se zyada ho): active learning se woh examples chuno jo model ko seekhne me sabse helpful hon; importance sampling se woh examples dhoondho jo task ke liye sabse important hon. Inki efficiency is par depend karti hai ki har training example ki importance evaluate karne ka achha tareeka hai ya nahi. Meta researchers ne data pruning par paper me conclude kiya ki achhe data-pruning metrics modern deep learning ke resource costs significantly kam kar sakte hain.

Format data — chat template sahi hona chahiye

Dedup aur clean karne ke baad data ko us format me lana hai jo finetune karne wala model expect karta hai. Har model apna tokenizer aur specific chat template use karta hai (Chapter 5). Galat chat template me data daalne se model me strange bugs aate hain.

  • Supervised finetuning me data aam taur par (instruction, response) format me hota hai. Instructions ko (system prompt, user prompt) me decompose kar sakte ho.
  • Prompt engineering se finetuning par graduate hone par instructions alag hote hain: finetuning me instructions me task descriptions ya examples ki zaroorat nahi hoti — kaafi training examples hon to model task ka expected behaviour examples se hi seekh leta hai.
  • Example — food classification: base model ke liye 3-shot instruction thi — "Label the following item as either edible or inedible. Item: burger, Label: edible; Item: car, Label: inedible; Item: mushroom, Label: edible; Item: {INPUT}, Label:" — finetuning me ye 3 examples training examples ban jate hain (burger → edible, car → inedible, mushroom → edible). Finetuned model ke liye prompt sirf "{INPUT} -->" jaisa chhota sa ho sakta hai — base model wale prompt se bahut chhota. Isliye input tokens ki chinta ho to finetuning cost manage karne ka ek tareeka hai.
  • Alag-alag finetuning data formats finetuned model ki performance ko affect karte hain — best format dhoondhne ke liye experiments helpful hote hain.
  • Finetuned model use karte waqt prompts training data ke format se match karne chahiye. Training data "burger -->" format me ho to ye prompts problems karenge: "burger" (end arrow missing), "Item: burger -->" (extra prefix), "burger --> " (extra space appended).
Yaad rakho: dataset banane ke principles simple hain — pehle socho ki model ko kaunse behaviours seekhne hain, phir aisa dataset design karo jo woh behaviours dikhaye. Par execution intricate hai: annotation mushkil hai, guidelines banana aur bhi mushkil; data generation automate karna mushkil hai, verification automate karna aur bhi mushkil. Data ko 15 minute ghoorna, scripts ko trial run par test karna, aur original data ki copy rakhna — ye chhoti aadatein badi bachte hain.
SOURCESource: Huyen, AI Engineering, O'Reilly, Chapter 8 — Dataset Engineering

09Chapter 9 · Inference Optimization

Inference Optimization

Naye models aate-jate rehte hain, par ek cheez hamesha relevant rahegi — unhe behtar, sasta aur tez banana. Ab tak book ne models ko behtar banane ki techniques discuss ki; ye chapter unhe tez aur sasta banane par hai. Model achha ho par slow ho to users patience kho denge — jaise next-day stock price prediction model jo har outcome compute karne me 2 din le. Model bahut mehnga ho to ROI worth nahi hoga.

Optimization 3 levels par hoti hai

  • Model level: trained model ka size kam karo ya zyada efficient architectures banao — jaise transformer me attention mechanism ke computation bottlenecks hatana.
  • Hardware level: zyada powerful hardware design karo.
  • Service level: inference service model ko diye gaye hardware par chalata hai, user requests accommodate karta hai, hardware-specific optimization incorporate karta hai, aur usage/traffic patterns dekhkar resources efficiently allocate karta hai taaki latency aur cost kam hon.
  • Isi liye inference optimization interdisciplinary field hai — model researchers, application developers, system engineers, compiler designers, hardware architects aur data center operators ka collaboration.
  • Ye chapter bottlenecks aur unhe overcome karne ki techniques par hai — mostly model aur service level, AI accelerators ka overview bhi. Kabhi-kabhi technique jo model ko tez karti hai, cost bhi kam karti hai (precision kam karna model ko chhota aur tez banata hai). Par aksar trade-offs hote hain — best hardware model ko tez chalayega par zyada cost par.
  • Open source models ki availability badhne se zyada teams apni inference services bana rahi hain. Khud techniques implement na bhi karo to unhe samajhna inference services aur frameworks evaluate karne me madad karta hai.

Inference overview — inference server aur inference service

  • Training matlab model banana; inference matlab model ko use karke diye gaye input ke liye output compute karna. Inference me sirf forward pass hota hai, training me forward + backward dono (Chapter 7).
  • Inference server: production me woh component jo model inference chalata hai — available models host karta hai, necessary hardware tak access rakhta hai, applications (user prompts) se requests ke hisaab se resources allocate karke appropriate models execute karta hai aur responses users ko return karta hai.
  • Inference service: isse bada hai — requests receive, route aur possibly preprocess bhi karta hai, phir inference server tak pahunchata hai. OpenAI aur Google jaise model APIs inference services hain. Inhe use karo to is chapter ki most techniques implement nahi karni padengi; khud model host karo to inference service build, optimize aur maintain karna tumhari zimmedari hai.
  • Training vs inference cost: model provider ke liye model tabhi sense banata hai jab inference se recover hone wala paisa training cost se zyada ho — T <= p × N (T = total training cost, p = per inference price, N = beche ja sakne wale inference calls). Model jitna zyada production me use hoga, provider inference cost utna kam kar sakta hai.

Computational bottlenecks — compute-bound vs memory bandwidth-bound

Optimization matlab bottlenecks identify karke unhe address karna. Do main computational bottlenecks hain:

  • Compute-bound: task complete hone ka time computation se decide hota hai. Example: password decryption — encryption break karne ke intensive mathematical calculations.
  • Memory bandwidth-bound (memory-bound): task system ke andar data transfer rate se constrained hota hai — jaise memory aur processors ke beech data movement ki speed. Example: data CPU memory me ho aur model GPUs par train ho raha ho to CPU se GPU data move karne me bahut time lagta hai.
  • Terminology ambiguity: "memory-bound" kuch log memory capacity ke liye bhi use karte hain — hardware me task handle karne ke liye kaafi memory na ho (OOM, out-of-memory error). Par task ko chhote pieces me split karke ise mitigate kar sakte ho — splitting computation slow kar deti hai kyunki CPU-GPU data transfer time lagta hai. Isliye capacity limitation asal me bandwidth ke baare me hi hai. System background wale log memory-bound se bandwidth-bound samajhte hain, AI background wale capacity-bound.
  • Arithmetic intensity: ek operation compute-bound hai ya memory bandwidth-bound, ye uski arithmetic intensity se classify hota hai — per byte memory access par kitne arithmetic operations. "Roofline" paper (Williams et al., 2009) ne ye concepts diye. NVIDIA Nsight jaise profiling tools roofline chart dikhate hain jo batata hai ki workload compute-bound hai ya memory bandwidth-bound — chart roof jaisa dikhta hai isliye ye naam hai.
  • Compute-bound workload ko zyada chips ya zyada FLOP/s wale chips se tez kar sakte ho; memory bandwidth-bound workload ko zyada bandwidth wale chips se.

LLM inference — prefill aur decode

  • Prefill: model input tokens ko parallel process karta hai. Ek saath kitne tokens process ho sakte hain, ye hardware kitne operations execute kar sakta hai, usse limited hai — isliye prefill compute-bound hai. Prefill effectively initial KV cache populate karta hai.
  • Decode: model ek baar me ek output token generate karta hai. Har step me bade matrices (model weights) GPUs me load karne padte hain, jo data load karne ki speed se limited hai — isliye decode memory bandwidth-bound hai.
  • Prefill aur decode ke computational profiles alag hain, isliye production me inhe aksar alag machines par decouple kar dete hain (detail ch9-service me).
  • Context length, output length aur request batching strategies bottlenecks ko affect karte hain. Lamba context aam taur par memory bandwidth-bound workload banata hai, par clever optimization techniques is bottleneck ko hata sakti hain.
  • Image generators jaise Stable Diffusion ki inference aam taur par compute-bound hoti hai, autoregressive language models ki memory bandwidth-bound. Aaj transformer architecture aur accelerator technologies ki limitations ki wajah se bahut se AI/data workloads memory bandwidth-bound hain — future software/hardware advancements inhe compute-bound bana sakti hain.

Online vs batch inference APIs

  • Online APIs: latency ke liye optimize — requests aate hi process hoti hain. Chatbots aur code generation jaise customer-facing use cases inhe use karte hain.
  • Batch APIs: cost ke liye optimize — strict latency requirements na hon to batch APIs par bhejo, zyada efficient processing hoti hai. Higher latency se zyada optimization techniques possible hoti hain — requests ko ek saath batch karna, sasta hardware use karna. Google Gemini aur OpenAI dono batch APIs par 50% cost reduction dete hain, par turnaround time hours me hota hai, seconds/minutes me nahi.
  • Online APIs bhi requests batch kar sakti hain jab tak latency significantly impact na ho. Asli farak sirf itna hai ki online API low latency par focus karti hai, batch API high throughput par.
  • Batch APIs ke ideal use cases: synthetic data generation; periodic reporting (Slack messages summarize karna, social media par brand mentions ka sentiment analysis, customer support tickets analyze karna); naye customers onboard karna (unke saare uploaded documents process karna); naye model par migrate karna (saara data reprocess karna); bade customer base ke liye personalized recommendations/newsletters generate karna; organization ka data reindex karke knowledge base update karna.
  • Foundation models ki batch API traditional ML ki batch inference se alag hai: traditional ML me online matlab requests aane ke baad predictions compute karo, batch matlab requests aane se pehle predictions precompute karo (jaise recommendation systems me saare users ke liye recommendations pehle se generate karna). Foundation models me inputs open-ended hote hain — saare user prompts predict karna mushkil hai, isliye precompute possible nahi hai. Sirf system prompt pehle se pata hota hai.
  • Streaming mode: APIs by default complete response return karti hain, par autoregressive decoding me poora response aane me time lagta hai. Streaming mode me har token generate hote hi return hota hai — first token ka wait kam ho jata hai. Downside: response dikhane se pehle use score nahi kar sakte, isliye users ko bad responses dikh sakte hain — par risk detect hote hi response ko retrospectively update ya remove kar sakte ho.

Performance metrics — latency, TTFT, TPOT

User perspective se central axis latency hai (response quality model ki property hai, inference service ki nahi). Application developers ko throughput aur utilization bhi dekhne padte hain, kyunki woh cost decide karte hain.

  • Latency: user query bheje us se lekar complete response milne tak ka time. Streaming mode me isse break karte hain:
  • TTFT (Time to First Token): query bhejne ke baad pehla token kitni jaldi generate hota hai. Ye prefill step ka duration hai, input length par depend karta hai. Conversational chatbots ke liye TTFT instantaneous hona chahiye; lambe documents summarize karne ke liye users zyada wait karne ko tayyar hote hain.
  • TPOT (Time Per Output Token): pehle token ke baad har output token kitni jaldi generate hota hai. Har token 100 ms le to 1,000 tokens ka response 100 s lega. Streaming me TPOT human reading speed se tez hona chahiye, bahut zyada tez hone ki zaroorat nahi — tez reader 120 ms/token padhta hai, to ~120 ms TPOT (6–8 tokens/second) most use cases ke liye kaafi hai.
  • TBT / ITL (Time Between Tokens / Inter-token Latency): output tokens ke beech ka time. Total latency = TTFT + TPOT × (output tokens ki sankhya).
  • Same total latency, alag user experience: instant first tokens + beech me lamba wait, vs pehle token ke liye thoda wait + phir tez generation — users kya prefer karte hain, ye user studies se pata chalta hai. Prefill se decode ki taraf compute shift karke TTFT kam karke TPOT badha sakte ho, ya vice versa.
  • Time to publish: CoT ya agentic queries me model intermediate steps generate karta hai jo user ko dikhte nahi — model ke perspective se pehla token step 1 me generate hota hai, user ke perspective se TTFT step 3 ke final output ke pehle token tak bahut lamba hota hai. Isi liye kuch teams "time to publish" metric use karti hain — pehle token jo user dekhta hai, uska time.
  • Average misleading ho sakta hai: 10 requests ke TTFT 100, 102, 100, 100, 99, 104, 110, 90, 3000, 95 ms hon to average 390 ms hoga — service asal se slow lagegi, jabki ek outlier (network error ya bahut lamba prompt) ne average bigada hai. Percentiles dekho: p50 (median), p90, p95, p99. TTFT values ko input lengths ke against plot karna bhi helpful hai.

Throughput aur goodput

  • Throughput: inference service saare users/requests me kitne output tokens per second generate kar sakta hai (tokens/s, TPS). Kuch teams input + output tokens dono count karti hain, par prefill aur decode ke bottlenecks alag hain aur modern servers me decoupled hote hain, isliye input aur output throughput alag count karne chahiye. Modifier ke bina throughput ka matlab output tokens hota hai.
  • Throughput ko completed requests se bhi naap sakte hain — requests per second (RPS), ya foundation models ke liye requests per minute (RPM), kyunki ek request complete hone me seconds lag sakte hain. Providers concurrent requests zyada bhejne par throttle bhi kar sakte hain.
  • Throughput seedha cost se juda hai: system $2/h cost kare aur throughput 100 tokens/s ho to cost ~$5.556 per 1M output tokens hoti hai. Har request average 200 output tokens generate kare to 1,000 requests decode karne ki cost $1.11. Prefill cost alag se: $2/h hardware 100 requests/minute prefill kare to 1,000 requests prefill karne ki cost $0.33. Total cost per 1,000 requests = $1.11 + $0.33 = $1.44.
  • Achha throughput model, hardware aur workload par depend karta hai — chhote models aur high-end chips se zyada throughput. Consistent input/output lengths wale workloads optimize karna aasan hai. Token count tokenizer par depend karta hai, isliye alag models ke throughput ko seedha compare karna approximate hi hota hai — cost per request se compare karna behtar hai.
  • Latency/throughput trade-off: batching throughput badhata hai par latency bhi. LinkedIn AI team ke hisaab se TTFT aur TPOT sacrifice karne ko tayyar hon to throughput double ya triple karna uncommon nahi hai. Sirf throughput aur cost par focus karne se user experience kharab ho sakta hai.
  • Goodput: SLO (software-level objective) satisfy karne wale requests per second. Example: SLO ho TTFT max 200 ms aur TPOT max 100 ms; service 100 requests/minute complete kare par sirf 30 SLO satisfy karein to goodput 30 requests/minute hai.

Utilization — GPU utilization, MFU, MBU

  • nvidia-smi GPU utilization: GPU kitne time actively tasks process kar raha tha, iska percentage. 10 ghante me 5 ghante active ho to 50%. Par actively processing karna efficiently processing karna nahi hai — 100 operations/second capable GPU 1 operation/second karke bhi 100% utilization report kar sakta hai. Ye metric zyada useful nahi hai.
  • MFU (Model FLOP/s Utilization): observed throughput (tokens/s) / theoretical maximum throughput (peak FLOP/s par). Chip peak par 100 tokens/s generate kar sakta ho par tumhari service me 20 tokens/s kare to MFU 20% hai.
  • MBU (Model Bandwidth Utilization): achievable memory bandwidth ka kitna percentage use ho raha hai. LLM inference me used bandwidth = parameter count × bytes/param × tokens/s. Example: 7B model FP16 (2 bytes/param) par 100 tokens/s → 7B × 2 × 100 = 700 GB/s. A100-80GB (theoretical 2 TB/s) par MBU = 700 GB/s ÷ 2,000 GB/s = 35%. (Book me is example ke liye 70% print hai, jo arithmetic se match nahi karta — 700/2000 = 35% hi hota hai.) Quantization yahan important hai — kam bytes per parameter matlab kam bandwidth consumption.
  • Throughput aur MBU/MFU ke beech linear relationship hai, isliye kuch log throughput ko hi MBU/MFU ke liye use karte hain.
  • Compute-bound workloads me MFU zyada, MBU kam; bandwidth-bound me MFU kam, MBU zyada. Training ki MFU inference se zyada hoti hai (predictable workloads, behtar batching). Inference me prefill ki MFU decode se zyada hoti hai. Training me 50% se upar MFU aam taur par achha mana jata hai, par achieve karna mushkil hai. PaLM paper ke examples: GPT-3 21.3%, Gopher 32.5%, Megatron-Turing NLG 30.2%, PaLM 46.2%.
  • Llama 2-70B FP16 par MBU concurrent users badhne ke saath decrease hota hai — computational load badhne se workload bandwidth-bound se compute-bound ki taraf shift hota hai.
  • Utilization track karna efficiency samajhne me helpful hai, par goal highest utilization wale chips lena nahi hai — asal goal jobs ko tez aur sasta karna hai. Utilization zyada ho par cost aur latency dono badh jayein to koi fayda nahi.

AI accelerators — GPU, TPU aur memory hierarchy

  • Accelerator matlab specific type ke computational workload ko accelerate karne ke liye design kiya gaya chip. AI accelerator AI workloads ke liye hai. Dominant type GPUs hain, sabse bada economic driver NVIDIA hai. AI models aur hardware ka development hamesha intertwined raha hai — 1970s me sufficiently powerful computers ki kami first AI winter ka ek kaaran thi; 2012 me AlexNet ki popularity ka ek kaaran GPUs se neural networks train karna tha (thousands CPUs ki jagah couple GPUs).
  • CPU vs GPU: CPUs general-purpose hain — kuch powerful cores (high-end consumer machines me 64 tak), high single-thread performance, OS/I-O/complex sequential processes ke liye achhe. GPUs parallel processing ke liye — hazaaron chhote, kam powerful cores, independent calculations ke liye optimize. ML workloads ka zyada hissa matrix multiplication hai, jo highly parallelizable hai (neural network ke 90%+ floating point operations).
  • Doosre accelerators: AMD ke naye GPUs, Google TPU (Tensor Processing Unit), Intel Habana Gaudi, Graphcore IPU, Groq LPU, Cerebras Wafer-Scale Engine, aur bahut se. Inference ke liye specialized chips emerging theme hai — survey ke hisaab se inference deployed AI systems ke ML costs ka 90% tak ho sakta hai, training cost se zyada. Training ko backpropagation ki wajah se zyada memory chahiye aur lower precision me karna mushkil hai, aur throughput par focus hota hai; inference latency minimize karna chahta hai. Isliye inference chips lower precision aur tez memory access ke liye optimize hote hain, badi memory capacity ke liye nahi — examples: Apple Neural Engine, AWS Inferentia, MTIA (Meta Training and Inference Accelerator), Edge TPU, NVIDIA Jetson Xavier. Kuch chips specific architectures (transformer) ke liye specialized hain.
  • Compute units: chips me alag-alag data types ke liye specialized compute units hote hain — scalars, vectors, tensors. GPUs traditionally vector operations support karte the, modern GPUs me matrix/tensor computations ke liye tensor cores hain; TPUs tensor operations ko primary compute primitive banakar design kiye gaye hain.
  • Computational capabilities — FLOP/s: chip ek second me kitne floating-point operations kar sakta hai. Precision zyada ho to operations kam — 32-bit numbers add karna 16-bit se lagbhag double computation mangta hai. H100 SXM: TF32 989, BF16 1,979, FP16 1,979, FP8 3,958 teraFLOP/s (sparsity ke saath).
  • Memory hierarchy (3 levels): (1) CPU memory (DRAM) — sabse kam bandwidth, 25–50 GB/s; laptops me 16–64 GB, high-end workstations me 1 TB+. (2) GPU HBM (high-bandwidth memory) — GPU ke paas dedicated memory, 256 GB/s se 1.5 TB/s+ bandwidth; consumer GPU me 24–80 GB. CPUs DDR SDRAM (2D structure) use karte hain, high-end GPUs HBM (3D stacked structure) — isliye GPU memory zyada mehngi hoti hai. (3) GPU on-chip SRAM — L1/L2 (kabhi L3) caches, register files, shared memory; 10 TB/s se zyada speed, par size chhota — aam taur par 40 MB ya kam. GPU optimization ka bada hissa isi memory hierarchy ka best use karna hai. PyTorch/TensorFlow fine-grained memory access control nahi dete — isliye CUDA, OpenAI Triton aur ROCm (AMD ka CUDA alternative) jaise GPU programming languages me interest badh raha hai.
  • Power consumption: A100 me 54 billion transistors, H100 me 80 billion. H100 peak par ek saal chale to ~7,000 kWh consume karta hai — average US household ki annual consumption 10,000 kWh hai. Electricity compute scale karne ka bottleneck hai. TDP (thermal design power) maximum heat hai jo cooling system ko dissipate karna hai typical workloads par; maximum power draw iska lagbhag 1.1–1.5x hota hai. Cloud use karo to cooling/electricity ki chinta nahi, par environment impact samajhne ke liye numbers useful hain.
  • Accelerators chunna — 3 sawaal: (1) Kya hardware tumhare workloads chala sakta hai? (2) Kitna time lagega? (3) Kitni cost hogi? FLOP/s, memory size aur memory bandwidth pehle do sawaalon ka jawab dete hain. Compute-bound workloads ke liye zyada FLOP/s wale chips, memory-bound ke liye zyada bandwidth aur memory wale chips.
Yaad rakho: LLM inference me prefill compute-bound hai, decode memory bandwidth-bound hai. TTFT prefill se, TPOT decode se aata hai. Throughput cost batata hai, goodput SLO-satisfying requests batata hai, aur MFU/MBU batate hain ki hardware kitna efficiently use ho raha hai — par aakhir me matter ye karta hai ki jobs tez aur saste me hon, utilization numbers nahi.
SOURCESource: Huyen, AI Engineering, O'Reilly, Chapter 9 — Inference Optimization
← Previous08.4 · Data Processing — Inspect, Dedup, Clean, Format→ Next09.1 · Model Optimization
09.1Chapter 9 · Inference Optimization

Model Optimization

Model-level optimization model ko modify karke use zyada efficient banata hai — isse model ka behaviour badal sakta hai. Transformer + autoregressive language models ki 3 characteristics inference ko resource-intensive banati hain: model size, autoregressive decoding, aur attention mechanism. Is section me teeno ke solutions samjhenge.

Model compression — quantization, distillation, pruning

  • Quantization (Chapter 7): model ki precision kam karke memory footprint kam karo aur throughput badhao. Weight-only quantization sabse popular approach hai — use karna aasan, bahut se models par out of the box kaam karta hai, extremely effective. 32 bits se 16 bits karne par memory footprint aadha ho jata hai. Par hum quantization ki limit ke kareeb hain — 1 bit per value se kam nahi ja sakte.
  • Distillation (Chapter 8): chhota model bade model ka behaviour mimic karna seekhta hai — bade model jaisa behaviour kam parameters me capture karna possible hai.
  • Pruning: do meanings hain — (1) neural network ke poore nodes remove karna (architecture change, parameters kam), (2) predictions ke liye least useful parameters ko zero set karna (total parameters same, non-zero parameters kam — model sparse ho jata hai, storage kam aur computation tez). Pruned models ko as-is use kar sakte ho ya remaining parameters adjust karne ke liye aur finetune kar sakte ho.
  • Pruning ke encouraging results hain — Frankle aur Carbin (2019) ne dikhaya ki kuch trained networks ke non-zero parameters 90%+ kam kiye ja sakte hain, accuracy compromise kiye bina. Pruning promising architectures discover karne me bhi madad karta hai. Par practice me pruning kam common hai — karna mushkil hai (original architecture samajhna padta hai), performance boost aksar doosre approaches se kam hota hai, aur sab hardware sparse models ka fayda uthane ke liye design nahi hain.
  • Warning: inference service providers alag-alag optimization techniques use karte hain, isliye same Llama models ki performance alag providers par benchmarks me thodi alag hoti hai (Cerebras, 2024 ka experiment). Optimization model ka behaviour badal sakta hai.

Autoregressive decoding bottleneck — speculative decoding

Autoregressive models ek ke baad ek token generate karte hain. Har token 100 ms le to 100 tokens ka response 10 s lega. Ye slow hi nahi, mehnga bhi hai — output token ki cost input token se lagbhag 2–4x hoti hai, aur Anyscale ke experiment me ek output token ka latency par wahi impact tha jo 100 input tokens ka. Speculative decoding (speculative sampling) is bottleneck ko todta hai:

  1. Ek tez par kam powerful model (draft/proposal model) K tokens ka sequence generate karta hai: xt+1, xt+2, …, xt+K.
  2. Target model (jis model ko tum use karna chahte ho) in K tokens ko parallel verify karta hai.
  3. Target model draft tokens ka sabse lamba subsequence accept karta hai, left se right, jise woh use karne ko agree karta hai.
  4. Maan lo target model ne j tokens accept kiye. Phir target model ek extra token generate karta hai: xt+j+1. Phir process step 1 se repeat hota hai.

Koi draft token accept na ho to loop me sirf 1 token generate hota hai; saare accept hon to K+1 tokens generate hote hain. Agar saare draft sequences reject ho jayein to target model ko response generate karne ke saath verify bhi karna padta hai — latency badh sakti hai. Par 3 insights ki wajah se ye avoid hota hai:

  • Tokens verify karna generate karne se tez hota hai — verification parallelizable hai, generation sequential. Speculative decoding decoding ke computation profile ko prefill jaisa bana deta hai.
  • Output sequence me kuch tokens predict karne me aasan hote hain — kamzor draft model bhi inhe sahi predict kar sakta hai, isliye acceptance rate high hoti hai.
  • Decoding memory bandwidth-bound hai, isliye idle FLOPs hote hain jo free verification ke liye use ho sakte hain. (Agar MFU pehle se maxed out ho to speculative decoding ka sense kam hai.)
  • Acceptance rates domain-dependent hain — code jaise structured texts me zyada hoti hain. K bada ho to target model ke verifying calls kam hote hain par draft tokens ki acceptance rate low hoti hai. Draft model kisi bhi architecture ka ho sakta hai, ideally target model ke saath same vocabulary aur tokenizer share kare. Custom draft model train kar sakte ho ya existing weaker model use kar sakte ho.
  • Example: Chinchilla-70B ko speed up karne ke liye DeepMind ne 4B-parameter draft model train kiya — draft model token 8x tez generate karta tha (1.8 ms/token vs 14.1 ms/token), overall response latency aadhe se zyada kam ho gayi, response quality compromise kiye bina. T5-XXL par bhi similar speed-up mila.
  • Implement karna relatively aasan hai (PyTorch me ~50 lines), quality change nahi karta, isliye vLLM, TensorRT-LLM aur llama.cpp jaise popular inference frameworks me incorporate ho gaya hai.

Inference with reference — input se copy karo

Aksar response ko input ke tokens reference karne hote hain — jaise attached document ke baare me poochho to model document ka chunk verbatim repeat kare, ya code me bugs fix karne ko kaho to model zyada tar original code reuse kare, sirf minor changes ke saath. In repeated tokens ko generate karwane ki jagah input se copy kyun na kar lein? Yahi inference with reference ka core idea hai.

  • Speculative decoding jaisa hai, par draft tokens model se generate karwane ki jagah input se select karte hain. Key challenge: har decoding step par context se sabse relevant text span identify karne ka algorithm — simplest option woh text span dhoondhna jo current tokens se match kare.
  • Extra model ki zaroorat nahi hai, par sirf un scenarios me useful hai jahan context aur outputs me significant overlap ho — retrieval systems, coding, multi-turn conversations. Yang et al. (2023) ke paper me aise use cases me 2x generation speedup mila.

Parallel decoding — sequential dependency todna

Draft tokens se generation tez karne ki jagah, kuch techniques sequential dependency ko hi todne ki koshish karti hain — existing sequence x1…xt se xt+1, xt+2, …, xt+k ek saath generate karo. Ye kaam kar sakta hai kyunki existing sequence ka knowledge aksar agle kuch tokens predict karne ke liye kaafi hota hai — jaise "the cat sits" ke baad, ye jane bina ki agla token "on", "under" ya "behind" hai, tum predict kar sakte ho ki uske baad wala word "the" hoga.

  • Lookahead decoding (Fu et al., 2024): same decoder se parallel tokens generate karo, Jacobi method se verify karo — (1) K future tokens parallel generate karo, (2) context ke saath coherence/consistency verify karo, (3) fail karne wale tokens ko regenerate/adjust karo, baaki ko aggregate mat karo. Model tokens ko refine karta rehta hai jab tak saare pass na kar jayein. Is family ko Jacobi decoding bhi kehte hain.
  • Medusa (Cai et al., 2024): original model ko multiple decoding heads se extend karo — har head ek chhoti neural network layer hai jo specific position ka future token predict karne ke liye train ki jati hai. Original model next token xt+1 predict karta hai, k-th head token xt+k+1 predict karegi. Heads original model ke saath train hoti hain, par original model frozen rehta hai. Tree-based attention mechanism se tokens verify aur integrate karte hain — har head har position ke liye kai options deta hai, options ko tree-like structure me organize karke sabse promising combination select karte hain. NVIDIA ne claim kiya ki Medusa ne HGX H200 GPUs par Llama 3.1 token generation 1.9x tak boost ki.
  • Sequential dependency circumvent karne ka perspective appealing hai, par parallel decoding intuitive nahi hai, aur Medusa jaise techniques implement karna challenging ho sakta hai.

Attention mechanism optimization — KV cache

Next token generate karne ke liye saare previous tokens ke key aur value vectors chahiye hote hain. Har step par unhe dobara compute karne ki jagah KV cache me store karke reuse karo — naye token ke key/value vectors compute karke cache me add karte jao. KV cache sirf inference me use hota hai, training me nahi — training me saare tokens pehle se pata hote hain, isliye next token generation ek saath compute ho sakta hai.

  • Attention computations sequence length ke saath O(n²) badhte hain; KV cache size linearly badhta hai — sequence length aur batch size ke saath. Google ke paper ke hisaab se 500B+ model, multi-head attention, batch size 512, context length 2048 par KV cache total 3TB hota hai — model weights se 3x bada.
  • KV cache size formula: 2 × B × S × L × H × M — B = batch size, S = sequence length, L = transformer layers ki sankhya, H = model dimension, M = numerical representation ki memory (FP16/FP32). Example: Llama 2 13B (40 layers, model dimension 5,120), batch 32, sequence 2,048, 2 bytes per value → 2 × 32 × 2,048 × 40 × 5,120 × 2 = 54 GB.
  • KV cache size hardware storage se limited hai — long context applications ke liye bottleneck. Bada cache load karne me time bhi lagta hai, strict latency wale applications ke liye problem hai.

Bucket 1 — Attention mechanism redesign (training/finetuning me hi possible, kyunki architecture change hoti hai):

  • Local windowed attention: saare previous tokens ki jagah sirf fixed size window ke nearby tokens par attend karo — effective sequence length fixed window ho jati hai, KV cache aur attention computation dono kam. Average sequence 10,000 tokens ho aur window 1,000 ho to KV cache 10x kam. Local attention ko global attention ke saath interleave kar sakte ho — local nearby context capture kare, global document bhar ki task-specific information.
  • Cross-layer attention: adjacent layers ke beech key-value vectors share karo — 3 layers same KV share karein to KV cache 3x kam.
  • Multi-query attention (MQA): saare query heads ke beech key-value vectors share karo.
  • Grouped-query attention (GQA): MQA ka generalization — query heads ko chhote groups me daalo, KV pairs sirf same group ke heads ke beech share karo. Query heads aur KV pairs ke beech flexible balance milta hai.
  • Character.AI example: unki average conversation 180 messages ki hoti hai — KV cache size inference throughput ka primary bottleneck tha. MQA + local/global attention interleaving + cross-layer attention se KV cache 20x se zyada kam hua — memory ab bade batch sizes serve karne me bottleneck nahi rahi.

Bucket 2 — KV cache size optimize karna:

  • PagedAttention (vLLM): KV cache ko non-contiguous blocks me divide karke memory management optimize karta hai — fragmentation kam, flexible memory sharing, LLM serving efficiency badhti hai. Isi liye vLLM itna popular hua.
  • Doosri techniques: KV cache quantization, adaptive KV cache compression, selective KV cache.

Bucket 3 — Attention computation ke liye kernels likhna:

  • FlashAttention (Dao et al., 2022): transformer model me commonly use hone wale kai operations ko fuse karke ek kernel banaya, jo unhe tez chalata hai.

Kernels aur compilers

Kernels specific hardware accelerators (GPUs, TPUs) ke liye optimize kiye gaye specialized code pieces hain — computationally intensive routines jo baar-baar, aksar parallel execute hone hain. Matrix multiplication, attention computation, convolution — sab ke specialized kernels hain.

  • Kernel likhne ke liye hardware architecture ki gehri samajh chahiye — memory hierarchy (caches, global memory, shared memory, registers) aur data access/movement. Kernels low-level languages me likhe jate hain — CUDA (NVIDIA GPUs), Triton (OpenAI ki custom kernels likhne ki language), ROCm (AMD GPUs).
  • Pehle kernel writing dark art thi, kuch log hi karte the — chip makers ke optimization engineers, frameworks ke kernel engineers. Ab demand badhne se zyada AI engineers seekh rahe hain; bahut se great online tutorials hain.
  • 4 common kernel techniques: (1) Vectorization — loop me ek data element ki jagah memory me contiguous multiple elements ek saath process karo, data I/O kam karo. (2) Parallelization — input array ko independent chunks me divide karke alag cores/threads par ek saath process karo. (3) Loop tiling — loop me data accessing order ko hardware ki memory layout aur cache ke liye optimize karo — hardware-dependent hai, CPU ke liye efficient tiling GPU par kaam na kare. (4) Operator fusion — multiple operators ko ek pass me combine karo taaki redundant memory access bache; jaise same array par operate karne wale do loops ko ek me fuse karo. Operator fusion ke liye model ke specific operators aur architecture ki gehri samajh chahiye.
  • Kernels hardware architecture ke liye optimize hote hain — nayi architecture aaye to naye kernels chahiye. FlashAttention pehle NVIDIA A100 ke liye bana tha, FlashAttention-3 H100 ke liye aaya.
  • Compilers: model script operations ki series specify karta hai; hardware par chalane ke liye use us hardware ki compatible language me convert karna padta hai — is process ko lowering kehte hain, aur jo tool lowering karta hai use compiler kehte hain. Lowering ke dauran jahan possible ho, operations ko specialized kernels me convert karte hain taaki target hardware par tez chalein.
  • Compiler examples: standalone tools — Apache TVM, MLIR (Multi-Level Intermediate Representation); frameworks me integrated — torch.compile (PyTorch), XLA (TensorFlow se, open source version OpenXLA), TensorRT (NVIDIA GPUs ke liye optimize). AI companies ke apne compilers aur proprietary kernels bhi hote hain — apne workloads ko competitors se tez aur sasta chalana competitive advantage hai, isliye bahut companies apne kernels ko trade secret manti hain.

Case study — PyTorch se Llama-7B throughput

PyTorch team ne Llama-7B par ye optimization steps apply karke throughput improvement dikhayi (A100 GPU, 80 GB memory): (1) torch.compile se model ko zyada efficient kernels me compile karo, (2) model weights ko INT8 me quantize karo, (3) aur quantize karke INT4 me karo, (4) speculative decoding add karo. Ye unclear tha ki in steps se model ki output quality par kya impact pada.

Yaad rakho: model-level optimization me quantization (generally sab models par kaam karta hai), speculative decoding, aur attention/KV cache optimization sabse impactful hain. Har technique ka apna trade-off hai — quantization aur pruning quality badal sakte hain, speculative decoding quality change kiye bina tez karta hai, aur kernels likhna hardware-specific mehnat mangta hai.
SOURCESource: Huyen, AI Engineering, O'Reilly, Chapter 9 — Inference Optimization
← Previous09 · Inference Optimization→ Next09.2 · Inference Service Optimization
09.2Chapter 9 · Inference Optimization

Inference Service Optimization

Service-level optimization models ko modify nahi karta — sirf ye badalta hai ki model kaise serve hota hai. Isliye output quality change nahi honi chahiye. Goal hai fixed resources (compute aur memory) aur dynamic workloads (alag-alag models wale user requests) ke saath resources efficiently allocate karke latency aur cost optimize karna.

Batching — sabse aasan cost saver

Production me inference service ko ek saath multiple requests mil sakti hain. Har request ko alag process karne ki jagah aas-paas aane wale requests ko ek saath batch karo — throughput significantly badhta hai. Analogy: har request ko alag car me bhejna vs sabko ek bus me daalna — bus zyada log move kar sakti hai, par har vyakti ki journey lambi bhi ho sakti hai. Intelligently karo to latency par impact minimal hota hai.

  • Static batching: fixed number ke inputs ko ek batch me group karo. Bus ki tarah jo tab tak wait karti hai jab tak saari seats na bhar jayein. Drawback: batch ka pehla request aakhri request aane tak wait karta hai, chahe aakhri kitna bhi late aaye.
  • Dynamic batching: har batch ke liye maximum time window set karo. Batch size 4 aur window 100 ms ho to server batch ko tab process karta hai jab 4 requests aa jayein ya 100 ms beet jayein — jo pehle ho. Bus ki tarah jo fixed schedule par ya full hone par nikalti hai. Latency control me rehti hai, pehle wale requests baad walon ke liye hold nahi hote. Downside: batches hamesha full nahi hote, compute waste ho sakta hai.
  • Continuous batching (in-flight batching): naive batching me saare batch requests complete hone ke baad hi responses return hote hain — LLMs me ek request 10 tokens generate kare aur doosri 1,000, to chhota response lambe response ka wait karta hai. Continuous batching (Orca paper, Yu et al., 2022) me batch ke responses complete hote hi users ko return kar dete hain. Batch me ek request complete hote hi uski jagah nayi request add kar sakte ho — batching continuous ho jati hai. Bus ki tarah jo ek passenger drop karke turant doosre ko pick kar leti hai, occupancy maximize karne ke liye.

Prefill aur decode ko decouple karna

Prefill compute-bound hai, decode memory bandwidth-bound hai. Dono ko same machine par chalane se woh resources ke liye inefficiently compete karte hain aur TTFT aur TPOT dono significantly slow ho jate hain. GPU pehle se prefilling aur decoding ko peak capacity ke kareeb handle kar raha ho to ek aur decoding job handle kar sakta hai, par nayi query add karne ka matlab ek prefilling job bhi add karna hai — aur ek prefilling job existing decoding jobs se computational resources drain karke unka TPOT slow kar deta hai.

  • Disaggregation: prefill aur decode operations ko alag instances (alag GPUs) par assign karo. DistServe aur "Inference Without Interference" papers ne dikhaya ki kai popular LLMs aur applications ke liye isse processed requests ka volume significantly badhta hai, latency requirements adhere karte hue. Prefill instances se decode instances tak intermediate states transfer karne ka communication overhead modern GPU clusters me high-bandwidth connections (jaise node ke andar NVLink) ki wajah se substantial nahi hai.
  • Ratio: prefill instances : decode instances ka ratio workload characteristics aur latency requirements par depend karta hai. Input sequences aam taur par lambe hon aur TTFT prioritize karna ho to ratio 2:1 se 4:1 ho sakta hai. Input sequences chhote hon aur TPOT prioritize karna ho to ratio 1:2 se 1:1 ho sakta hai.

Prompt caching — overlapping segments ko reuse karo

Application me bahut se prompts ke overlapping text segments hote hain. Prompt cache in overlapping segments ko store karke reuse karta hai — ek baar process karo, baar-baar use karo. Sabse common overlapping segment system prompt hai: prompt cache ke bina har query ke saath system prompt process karna padta hai, cache ke saath sirf pehli query ke liye. Ise context cache ya prefix cache bhi kehte hain.

  • Use cases: lambe documents se related queries (book ya codebase — document ek baar cache karo, saari queries me reuse karo); lambi conversations (pehle ke messages process karke cache karo, future messages predict karte waqt reuse karo).
  • Impact: system prompt 1,000 tokens ka ho aur application roz 1 million API calls generate kare to prompt cache roz ~1 billion repetitive input tokens process karne se bachata hai. Par free nahi hai — KV cache ki tarah prompt cache size bhi bahut bada ho sakta hai aur memory leta hai. Model API ke bina implement karna significant engineering effort mangta hai.
  • Provider offerings: Google Gemini prompt caching deta hai — cached input tokens par regular tokens ke mukable 75% discount, par cache storage ke liye extra charge ($1.00 per 1 million tokens per hour). Anthropic prompt caching 90% tak cost savings aur 75% tak latency reduction ka promise karta hai (cached context jitna lamba, savings utni zyada). Anthropic ke numbers: book ke saath chat (100,000-token cached prompt) — TTFT 11.5 s se 2.4 s (−79%), cost −90%; many-shot prompting (10,000-token prompt) — TTFT 1.6 s se 1.1 s (−31%), cost −86%; multi-turn conversation (10-turn, lamba system prompt) — TTFT ~10 s se ~2.5 s (−75%), cost −53%.
  • llama.cpp me bhi prompt caching hai, par lagta hai ki woh sirf whole prompts cache karta hai aur same chat session ke queries ke liye kaam karta hai.

Parallelism — replica, tensor, pipeline, context, sequence

Accelerators parallel processing ke liye design kiye gaye hain, aur parallelism strategies high-performance computing ki backbone hain. Kai nayi strategies develop ho rahi hain; yahan kuch reference ke liye hain. Ek optimization technique me multiple parallelism strategies combine ho sakti hain.

  • Replica parallelism: sabse straightforward — serve karne wale model ki multiple replicas banao. Zyada replicas se ek saath zyada requests handle kar sakte ho, par zyada chips lagenge. Alag sizes ke models (8B, 13B, 34B, 70B) ko alag memory capabilities wale GPUs (24 GB, 40 GB, 48 GB, 80 GB) par fit karna bin-packing problem hai — fixed chips hon to har model ki kitni replicas aur kis GPU par, ye decide karna; fixed replicas hon to kaunse chips khareedein taaki cost minimize ho. Training me isi technique ko data parallelism kehte hain.
  • Model parallelism: model itna bada ho ki ek machine me fit na ho to use multiple machines par split karo. Sabse common inference approach tensor parallelism (intra-operator parallelism) hai — operator me involved tensors ko multiple devices par partition karo, operator ko chhote pieces me todkar parallel execute karo. Example: do matrices multiply karte waqt ek matrix ko columnwise split karo. Do fayde: (1) single machine me na fit hone wale bade models serve karna possible hota hai, (2) latency kam hoti hai — par extra communication overhead latency benefit kam kar sakta hai.
  • Pipeline parallelism: model ki computation ko distinct stages me divide karke har stage alag device ko assign karo. Data model se flow karte hue har stage ek part process karta hai, jabki doosre stages subsequent parts process karte hain — overlapping computations. Batch ko chhote micro-batches me split karte hain — ek micro-batch ek machine par process hone ke baad uska output model ke agle part par agle machine ko pass hota hai. Bade models multiple machines par serve karna possible hota hai, par har request ki total latency badh jati hai (pipeline stages ke beech extra communication) — isliye strict latency wale applications me pipeline parallelism avoid karke replica parallelism prefer karte hain. Training me pipeline parallelism commonly use hota hai kyunki throughput badhata hai.
  • Context parallelism: input sequence ko hi alag devices par split karke separately process karo — pehla half machine 1 par, doosra half machine 2 par.
  • Sequence parallelism: poore input ke liye chahiye operators ko machines par split karo — jaise attention machine 1 par process ho aur feedforward machine 2 par. Dono context aur sequence parallelism lambi input sequences ko efficiently process karne ke liye develop kiye gaye the.
Yaad rakho: service-level techniques model ko intact rakhkar serve karne ka tareeka badalti hain. Sabse impactful techniques aam taur par hain — quantization, tensor parallelism (latency kam + bade models serve karna), replica parallelism (implement karna relatively straightforward), aur attention mechanism optimization. Technique ka chunaav workload par depend karta hai: lambi context wale workloads ke liye KV caching zyada important hai, lambe overlapping prompt segments ya multi-turn conversations ke liye prompt caching crucial hai.
SOURCESource: Huyen, AI Engineering, O'Reilly, Chapter 9 — Inference Optimization
