10Chapter 10 · AI Engineering Architecture and User Feedback

AI Engineering Architecture and User Feedback

Ab tak book ne foundation models ko specific applications ke liye adapt karne ki alag-alag techniques cover ki hain. Ye chapter un techniques ko ek saath jodkar successful products banana sikhata hai — aur phir user feedback se unhe continually improve karna.

Gradual approach — simplest architecture se shuru karo

AI engineering techniques aur tools ki range dekhkar sahi chunna overwhelming lag sakta hai. Is chapter ka approach gradual hai: sabse simple architecture se shuru karo, uski challenges highlight karo, aur dheere-dheere components add karke unhe address karo.

  • Sabse simple architecture: application query receive karti hai, model ko bhejti hai, model response generate karta hai, response user ko return hota hai. Koi context augmentation nahi, koi guardrails nahi, koi optimization nahi. "Model API" box third-party APIs (OpenAI, Google, Anthropic) aur self-hosted models dono ko refer karta hai. Self-hosted models ke liye inference server banana Chapter 9 me hai.
  • Is simple architecture se components add karne ka process aisa dikhta hai:
  1. Context input enhance karo — model ko external data sources aur tools ka access do information gather karne ke liye.
  2. Guardrails lagao — system aur users ko protect karne ke liye.
  3. Model router aur gateway add karo — complex pipelines support karne aur security badhane ke liye.
  4. Caching se latency aur costs optimize karo.
  5. Complex logic aur write actions add karo — system ki capabilities maximize karne ke liye.

Ye chapter production me commonly dekha jaane wala progression follow karta hai, par har application ki needs alag hoti hain — jo order tumhare application ke liye sense banaye, wahi follow karo. Monitoring aur observability, jo quality control aur performance improvement ke liye integral hain, process ke end me discuss ki jayengi. Orchestration — saare components ko ek saath chain karna — uske baad aata hai.

Architecture validate hui hai, par har application alag hai

Full-fledged AI architecture complex ho sakti hai. Yahan propose ki gayi architecture multiple companies me validate hui hai aur wide range ki applications ke liye general hai, par certain applications deviate kar sakti hain. AI applications diverse hone ke bawjood bahut se common components share karte hain — isi liye ek common architecture banana possible hai.

User feedback — data flywheel ka source

Application ko users ke saamne laaye bina ye pata lagana impossible hai ki woh apna goal achieve kar rahi hai ya nahi. User feedback product development guide karne ke liye hamesha invaluable raha hai, par AI applications ke liye uska role aur bhi crucial hai — feedback models improve karne ke liye data ka source hai.

  • Conversational interface users ke liye feedback dena aasan banata hai, par developers ke liye signals extract karna mushkil. Is chapter me conversational AI feedback ke alag-alag types aur feedback collect karne ka system design karne ka tareeka discuss hoga — sahi feedback collect karna, user experience hurt kiye bina.
  • User feedback proprietary data hai, aur data competitive advantage hai. Achhe se design kiya gaya user feedback system data flywheel (Chapter 8) banane ke liye zaroori hai. Feedback se models ko individual users ke liye personalize bhi kar sakte ho aur future iterations train bhi kar sakte ho.
  • Data scarce hote ja raha hai, isliye proprietary data pehle se zyada valuable hai. Jo product jaldi launch karke users attract karta hai, woh data gather karke models continually improve kar sakta hai, competitors ke liye catch up karna mushkil ho jata hai.
  • Privacy yaad rakho: user feedback user data hai. Use leverage karne me wahi cautions chahiye jo kisi bhi data ke liye chahiye. User privacy respect karo — users ko pata hona chahiye ki unka data kaise use ho raha hai.
Yaad rakho: har additional component system ko zyada capable, safe ya fast bana sakta hai, par complexity aur naye failure modes bhi badhata hai. Isi liye architecture gradual banao — zaroorat padne par ek component add karo, aur monitoring ko design ka hissa banao, afterthought nahi.
SOURCESource: Huyen, AI Engineering, O'Reilly, Chapter 10 — AI Engineering Architecture and User Feedback
← Previous09.2 · Inference Service Optimization→ Next10.1 · Architecture — 5 Steps
10.1Chapter 10 · AI Engineering Architecture and User Feedback

Architecture — 5 Steps

AI application ki architecture ek step me nahi banti — woh dheere-dheere badhti hai. Is section me 5 steps hain: context enhance karo, guardrails lagao, router aur gateway add karo, caches se latency kam karo, aur agent patterns + write actions add karo.

Step 1 — Enhance context

Platform ka pehla expansion aam taur par context construct karne ke mechanisms add karna hota hai — system ko har query ka jawab dene ke liye relevant context banane ki ability dena. Context retrieval mechanisms (text, image, tabular data retrieval — Chapter 6) ya tools (web search, news, weather, events jaise APIs) se construct ho sakta hai.

  • Context construction foundation models ke liye feature engineering jaisi hai — model ko output produce karne ke liye necessary information deti hai. Output quality me central role ki wajah se context construction lagbhag universally model API providers support karte hain — OpenAI, Claude, Gemini files upload karne aur tools use karne dete hain.
  • Par providers ki context construction support alag hoti hai: kitne types ke documents aur kitne upload kar sakte ho, isme limitations ho sakti hain. Specialized RAG solution vector database jitne documents upload karne de sakta hai, generic model API sirf chhoti sankhya me. Frameworks retrieval algorithms aur configurations (jaise chunk sizes) me bhi differ karte hain. Tool use me bhi supported tools ke types aur execution modes (parallel function execution, long-running jobs) differ karte hain.

Step 2 — Guardrails lagao

Guardrails risks mitigate karte hain aur tumhe aur tumhare users ko protect karte hain. Jahan bhi risk exposure ho, wahan guardrails lagane chahiye. Aam taur par guardrails inputs aur outputs ke aas-paas hote hain.

Input guardrails — 2 risks:

  • Private information external APIs ko leak hona: employee company secret ya user ki private info prompt me copy karke third-party API ko bhej de (Samsung employee ne ChatGPT me Samsung ki proprietary info daal di thi); developer company ki internal policies/data system prompt me daal de; tool internal database se private info retrieve karke context me add kar de. Third-party APIs use karte waqt leaks ko airtight tareeke se eliminate karna possible nahi hai, par mitigate kar sakte ho — sensitive data detect karne wale tools se. Common sensitive data classes: personal information (ID numbers, phone numbers, bank accounts), human faces, company IP ya privileged info se associated keywords/phrases. Bahut se detection tools AI use karke identify karte hain ki string valid home address jaisi lagti hai ya nahi. Query me sensitive info mile to 2 options: poori query block karo, ya sensitive info remove karo — jaise phone number ko [PHONE NUMBER] placeholder se mask karo; response me placeholder aaye to PII reverse dictionary se unmask karo.
  • Bad prompts jo system compromise karein: prompt hacks aur unse defense Chapter 5 me hain. Risks mitigate kar sakte ho, fully eliminate kabhi nahi kar sakte — models responses generate karne ka tareeka aur unavoidable human failures ki wajah se.

Output guardrails — 2 functions: output failures catch karo, aur har failure mode ko handle karne ki policy specify karo.

  • Quality failures: malformatted responses (expected JSON ki jagah invalid JSON), factually inconsistent (hallucinated) responses, generally bad responses (essay likhne ko kaha aur essay hi kharab hai). Quality failures Chapter 4 me, security failures Chapter 5 me discuss hue hain.
  • Security failures: toxic responses (racist, sexual, illegal content), private/sensitive info wale responses, remote tool/code execution trigger karne wale responses, brand-risk responses (tumhari company ya competitors ko mischaracterize karna).
  • Sabse aasan failure: model empty response return kare jab nahi karna chahiye tha.
  • False refusal rate bhi track karo: system bahut secure bhi ho sakta hai — legitimate requests bhi block kar de, user workflows interrupt ho, frustration badhe.

Failure handling — retry, parallel calls, human fallback:

  • Bahut se failures simple retry logic se mitigate hote hain — AI models probabilistic hote hain, dobara try karne par alag response mil sakta hai. Empty response ho to X baar try karo jab tak nonempty na mile; malformatted ho to try karte raho jab tak correctly formatted na mile.
  • Retry se extra latency aur cost aati hai — har retry ek aur API call hai, aur failure ke baad retry karne par user-perceived latency double ho jati hai. Latency kam karne ke liye calls parallel me karo — har query ko ek saath do baar model ko bhejo, do responses me se behtar chuno. Redundant API calls badhti hain, latency manageable rehti hai.
  • Humans par fallback: tricky requests humans ko transfer karo — jaise specific phrases wali queries human operators ko. Kuch teams specialized model se decide karti hain kab transfer karna hai — ek team sentiment analysis model se anger detect hote hi transfer karti hai; doosri team certain number of turns ke baad transfer karti hai taaki users loop me na fasein.

Guardrail implementation — trade-offs:

  • Reliability vs latency: kuch teams ne bataya ki latency zyada important hai — guardrails application ki latency significantly badha sakte hain, isliye unhone implement hi nahi kiye.
  • Streaming mode me problem: stream completion me naye tokens generate hote hi user ko stream hote hain, wait kam hota hai. Par partial responses evaluate karna mushkil hai, isliye unsafe responses guardrails ke block karne se pehle users tak stream ho sakte hain.
  • Self-host vs third-party APIs: third-party APIs aam taur par bahut se guardrails out of the box dete hain, isliye tumhe kam implement karne padte hain. Self-hosting me requests bahar nahi bhejti, isliye input guardrails ki zaroorat kam hoti hai.
  • Guardrails kai levels par: model providers apne models me guardrails dete hain (safety vs flexibility balance karte hue — restrictions model ko safe banati hain par specific use cases ke liye kam usable bhi). Application developers bhi guardrails implement kar sakte hain (Chapter 5 ki defenses). Out-of-the-box solutions: Meta Purple Llama, NVIDIA NeMo Guardrails, Azure PyRIT, Azure AI content filters, Perspective API, OpenAI content moderation API. Inputs aur outputs ke risks overlap karte hain, isliye ek guardrail solution aam taur par dono ko protect karta hai. Model gateways bhi guardrail functionalities dete hain (agle step me).
  • Architecture me scorers ko Model APIs ke neeche rakha gaya hai, kyunki scorers aksar AI-powered hote hain (bhale generative models se chhote aur tez hon) — par scorers output guardrails box me bhi ho sakte hain.

Step 3 — Model router aur gateway add karo

Applications grow karte hue zyada models involve karte hain — routers aur gateways complexity aur costs manage karne me madad karte hain.

Router: ek model sab queries ke liye use karne ki jagah alag types ki queries ke liye alag solutions. Fayde: (1) specialized models specific queries par general-purpose model se behtar perform kar sakte hain — ek model technical troubleshooting me specialized, doosra billing me; (2) cost bachat — simple queries saste models ko route karo.

  • Intent classifier: router aam taur par user ka intent predict karta hai, phir query ko appropriate solution par route karta hai. Customer support chatbot example: password reset chahiye to FAQ page par route karo; billing mistake correct karni hai to human operator ko; technical issue troubleshoot karna hai to troubleshooting-specialized chatbot ko.
  • Intent classifier out-of-scope conversations rok sakta hai — inappropriate query ho to stock response se politely decline karo, API call waste kiye bina. Example: "upcoming election me tum kisko vote doge?" par chatbot kahe "As a chatbot, I don't have the ability to vote. If you have questions about our products, I'd be happy to help."
  • Ambiguous queries detect karke clarification maang sakta hai — "Freezing" query par system poochhe "Do you want to freeze your account or are you talking about the weather?"
  • Doosre routers: agent ke liye next-action predictor (code interpreter use kare ya search API?); memory system wale model ke liye router predict kare ki memory hierarchy ke kis part se information pull karni hai. Example: user ne Melbourne mention karne wala document attach kiya, phir poochha "What's the cutest animal in Melbourne?" — model ko decide karna hai ki attached document par rely kare ya internet search kare.
  • Intent classifiers aur next-action predictors foundation models ke upar implement ho sakte hain. Bahut teams GPT-2, BERT, Llama 7B jaise chhote language models adapt karti hain; kuch aur bhi chhote classifiers scratch se train karti hain. Routers fast aur cheap hone chahiye taaki multiples use karne par bhi extra latency/cost significant na ho.
  • Context limits: alag context limits wale models ko route karte waqt query ka context adjust karna pad sakta hai. 1,000-token query 4K context limit wale model ke liye slated ho, phir web search 8,000-token context le aaye to ya context truncate karo, ya query ko bade context limit wale model ko route karo.
  • Routing aam taur par retrieval se pehle hoti hai — router decide karta hai ki query in-scope hai ya nahi, aur retrieval chahiye ya nahi. Retrieval ke baad bhi routing ho sakti hai — jaise query human operator ko route karni hai ya nahi. Par routing → retrieval → generation → scoring bahut zyada common pattern hai.

Gateway: model gateway intermediate layer hai jo organization ko alag-alag models se unified aur secure tareeke se interface karne deta hai.

  • Unified interface: self-hosted models aur commercial APIs ke peeche wale models — sab ke liye ek interface. Code maintain karna aasan — model API change ho to sirf gateway update karo, us par depend karne wali saari applications nahi.
  • Access control aur cost management: sabko organizational tokens dene ki jagah sirf gateway ka access do — centralized, controlled point of access. Fine-grained access controls — kaunsa user/application kis model ko access kar sakta hai. API calls ka usage monitor aur limit karo — abuse roko, costs manage karo.
  • Fallback policies: rate limits ya API failures (jo unfortunately common hain) se nipatne ke liye — primary API unavailable ho to alternative models ko route karo, thodi der baad retry karo, ya failures gracefully handle karo. Application bina interruption chalta rahe.
  • Requests/responses gateway se flow karte hain, isliye yahan load balancing, logging, analytics bhi implement kar sakte ho. Kuch gateways caching aur guardrails bhi dete hain.
  • Off-the-shelf gateways: Portkey AI Gateway, MLflow AI Gateway, Wealthsimple LLM Gateway, TrueFoundry, Kong, Cloudflare. Gateway implement karna relatively straightforward hai — simple wrapper se shuru kar sakte ho.
  • Isi tarah ka abstraction layer tools ke liye (tool gateway) bhi useful ho sakta hai, par ye abhi common pattern nahi hai isliye book me discuss nahi hai.

Step 4 — Caches se latency kam karo

Caching software applications me latency aur cost kam karne ke liye lambe time se integral hai. Inference caching techniques (KV caching, prompt caching) Chapter 9 me hain; yahan system caching par focus hai — 2 major mechanisms: exact caching aur semantic caching.

Exact caching: cached items sirf tab use hote hain jab exact wahi item request ho. Example: user product summarize karne ko kahe to system check kare ki is exact product ka summary cache me hai ya nahi — ho to fetch karo, nahi to summarize karke cache karo. Embedding-based retrieval me bhi use hota hai — query pehle se vector search cache me ho to cached result fetch karo.

  • Multi-step queries (chain-of-thought) aur time-consuming actions (retrieval, SQL execution, web search) wale queries ke liye khaas taur par appealing hai.
  • Implementation: fast retrieval ke liye in-memory storage; memory limited hai isliye PostgreSQL, Redis ya tiered storage bhi use kar sakte ho speed aur storage capacity balance karne ke liye.
  • Eviction policy crucial hai: LRU (Least Recently Used), LFU (Least Frequently Used), FIFO (first in, first out). Query ko kitne time cache me rakhna hai, ye is par depend karta hai ki woh dobara call hone ki kitni sambhavna hai. User-specific queries ("What's the status of my recent order?") doosre users reuse nahi karenge, isliye cache nahi karni chahiye. Time-sensitive queries ("How's the weather?") bhi cache karne ka sense nahi hai. Kuch teams classifier train karti hain jo predict kare ki query cache karni chahiye ya nahi.
  • Data leak ka risk: ecommerce site par user X poochhe "What is the return policy for electronics products?" — return policy user ki membership par depend karti hai, system X ki info retrieve karke X ki info wala response generate karta hai, aur use generic question samajhkar cache kar deta hai. Baad me user Y wahi question poochhe to cached result return hota hai — X ki information Y ko reveal ho jati hai.

Semantic caching: cached items tab bhi use hote hain jab woh incoming query se sirf semantically similar hon, identical na hon. Ek user poochhe "What's the capital of Vietnam?" — jawab "Hanoi". Doosra user poochhe "What's the capital city of Vietnam?" — semantically same question, wording thodi alag. Semantic caching pehle query ka answer reuse kar sakta hai. Similar queries reuse karne se cache hit rate badhti hai aur cost kam ho sakti hai — par model ki performance kam ho sakti hai.

  • Kaam karne ke liye reliable tareeka chahiye ye determine karne ka ki do queries similar hain ya nahi — common approach semantic similarity (Chapter 3): (1) har query ki embedding generate karo, (2) vector search se cached embedding dhoondho jiska similarity score sabse zyada ho (maan lo X), (3) X similarity threshold se zyada ho to cached query similar maani jati hai, cached results return karo; nahi to current query process karo aur use embedding + results ke saath cache karo. Iske liye cached queries ki embeddings store karne ke liye vector database chahiye.
  • Value dubious hai: bahut se components failure-prone hain — high-quality embeddings, functional vector search, reliable similarity metric. Sahi similarity threshold set karna tricky hai, bahut trial and error chahiye. System incoming query ko doosri query jaisa samajh le to cached response incorrect hoga.
  • Semantic cache time-consuming aur compute-intensive bhi ho sakta hai (vector search). Cache hit rate high ho to bhi worthwhile ho sakta hai — par complexities add karne se pehle efficiency, cost aur performance risks evaluate karo.

Step 5 — Agent patterns aur write actions add karo

Ab tak ki applications fairly simple hain — har query sequential flow follow karti hai. Par Chapter 6 ke agentic patterns se application flow zyada complex ho sakta hai — loops, parallel execution, conditional branching.

  • System output generate karne ke baad determine kar sakta hai ki task accomplish nahi hua aur aur information gather karne ke liye ek aur retrieval chahiye. Original response, naye retrieved context ke saath, same model ya alag model me pass hoti hai — ye loop banata hai.
  • Write actions: model ke outputs se write actions invoke ho sakte hain — email compose karna, order place karna, bank transfer initialize karna. Write actions system ko environment me directly changes karne dete hain — system vastly zyada capable banta hai, par significantly zyada risks bhi aate hain. Model ko write actions ka access utmost care ke saath dena chahiye.
  • Har additional component system ko zyada capable, safe ya fast bana sakta hai, par complexity bhi badhata hai aur naye failure modes laata hai, jinhe debug karna mushkil hota hai kyunki failure ke bahut se potential points hote hain. Isi liye agla section observability par hai.
Yaad rakho: components ko modular aur maintainable rakhne ke liye alag karna zaroori hai, par separation fluid hai — components functionalities me overlap kar sakte hain. Guardrails inference service me, model gateway me, ya standalone component ke roop me implement ho sakte hain.
Poora code dekho — model gateway (Ch 10, Architecture)
python — Model gateway (OpenAI + Gemini unified wrapper) — as printed in the book; book kehta hai ye functional nahi hai, sirf idea ke liye (no code file for this example in the repo) (GitHub: https://github.com/chiphuyen/aie-book)
import google.generativeai as genai
import openai
def openai_model(input_data, model_name, max_tokens):
openai.api_key = os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"]
response = openai.Completion.create(
engine=model_name,
prompt=input_data,
max_tokens=max_tokens
)
return {"response": response.choices[0].text.strip()}
def gemini_model(input_data, model_name, max_tokens):
genai.configure(api_key=os.environ["GOOGLE_API_KEY"])
model = genai.GenerativeModel(model_name=model_name)
response = model.generate_content(input_data, max_tokens=max_tokens)
return {"response": response["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]}
@app.route('/model', methods=['POST'])
def model_gateway():
data = request.get_json()
model_type = data.get("model_type")
model_name = data.get("model_name")
input_data = data.get("input_data")
max_tokens = data.get("max_tokens")
if model_type == "openai":
result = openai_model(input_data, model_name, max_tokens)
elif model_type == "gemini":
result = gemini_model(input_data, model_name, max_tokens)
return jsonify(result)
SOURCESource: Huyen, AI Engineering, O'Reilly, Chapter 10 — AI Engineering Architecture and User Feedback

10.2Chapter 10 · AI Engineering Architecture and User Feedback

Monitoring, Observability aur Orchestration

Observability kisi product ki afterthought nahi honi chahiye — woh design ka integral hissa hai. Product jitna complex hoga, observability utni hi crucial hogi. Is section me monitoring, observability aur orchestration samjhenge — foundation models par bane applications ke liye kya unique hai.

Monitoring vs observability

  • Monitoring: system ke external outputs ko track karke figure out karna ki andar kuch galat hua hai — koi guarantee nahi hai ki external outputs se pata chalega ki kya galat hua.
  • Observability: stronger assumption — system ki internal states ko uske external outputs ke knowledge se infer kiya ja sakta hai. Observable system me kuch galat ho to logs aur metrics dekhkar pata lagana chahiye ki kya galat hua, bina system me naya code ship kiye. Observability matlab system ko aise instrument karna ki runtime ki kaafi information collect aur analyze ho, taaki kuch galat ho to woh bataye ki kya galat hua.
  • Is book me "monitoring" matlab system ki information track karna, "observability" matlab instrument, track aur debug karne ki poori process.
  • Observability universal software engineering practice hai — badi industry hai, established best practices aur bahut se proprietary/open source solutions hain (sabse bade observability companies — Datadog, Splunk, Dynatrace, New Relic — ki aggregate market cap ~$100 billion ke kareeb hai). Wheel reinvent karne ki jagah, yahan focus foundation model applications ke liye unique cheezon par hai.

Monitoring ka goal aur 3 quality metrics

Monitoring ka goal evaluation jaisa hi hai: risks mitigate karna aur opportunities discover karna. Mitigate karne wale risks: application failures, security attacks, drifts. Discover karne wali opportunities: application improvement aur cost savings. Monitoring accountability bhi deta hai — system ki performance ki visibility.

  • MTTD (mean time to detection): kuch bura ho to detect karne me kitna time lagta hai?
  • MTTR (mean time to response): detect karne ke baad resolve karne me kitna time lagta hai?
  • CFR (change failure rate): changes/deployments ka kitna percentage failures me result karta hai jinhe fix ya rollback karna pade. CFR na pata ho to platform ko redesign karne ka time hai taaki woh zyada observable bane.
  • High CFR ka matlab zaroori nahi ki monitoring system kharab hai — evaluation pipeline par dobara sochna chahiye taaki bad changes deploy hone se pehle pakde jayein. Evaluation aur monitoring ko closely kaam karna chahiye: evaluation metrics monitoring metrics me translate hone chahiye (evaluation me achha karne wala model monitoring me bhi achha kare), aur monitoring me detect hue issues evaluation pipeline me feed hone chahiye.

Metrics — failure modes ke aas-paas design karo

Metrics khud goal nahi hain — metric ka purpose hai batana ki kuch galat hua hai aur improvement ke opportunities identify karna. Pehle samjho ki kaunse failure modes catch karne hain, phir unke aas-paas metrics design karo. Example: hallucination nahi chahiye to aisi metrics design karo jo hallucination detect karein — jaise output context se infer ho sakta hai ya nahi. API credit burn nahi karna to API costs se related metrics track karo — input/output tokens per request, cache ki cost aur cache hit rate.

  • Format failures (sabse aasan): JSON expect karo to kitni baar invalid JSON output aata hai, aur unme se kitne aasani se fix ho sakte hain (missing closing bracket aasan hai, missing expected keys mushkil).
  • Open-ended generations: factual consistency aur generation quality metrics (conciseness, creativity, positivity) — bahut se AI judges se compute ho sakte hain.
  • Safety: toxicity metrics, inputs/outputs me private/sensitive info detect karo. Guardrails kitni baar trigger hote hain, system kitni baar answer karne se refuse karta hai — ye track karo. Abnormal queries bhi detect karo — interesting edge cases ya prompt attacks reveal ho sakte hain.
  • Conversational signals se model quality: users generation ko beech me kitni baar rokte hain? Average turns per conversation kitna hai? Average tokens per input kitne hain — users zyada complex tasks ke liye use kar rahe hain ya concise prompts seekh rahe hain? Average tokens per output — kuch models zyada verbose hain? Output token distribution time ke saath kaise change ho raha hai — model zyada ya kam diverse ho raha hai?
  • RAG components: retrieval quality context relevance aur context precision se evaluate karo. Vector database ko storage aur query time se evaluate karo.
  • Business north star se correlation: metrics ko DAU (daily active user), session duration, subscriptions jaise north star metrics se correlate karo. Strongly correlated metrics north star improve karne ke ideas dete hain; bilkul uncorrelated metrics batate hain kis par optimize nahi karna hai.
  • Latency metrics (Chapter 9): TTFT, TPOT, total latency — har user ke hisaab se track karo taaki dekho ki system zyada users ke saath kaise scale karta hai.
  • Cost metrics: queries ki sankhya, input/output tokens ka volume (tokens per second, TPS). Rate limits wali API use karo to requests per second track karo taaki allocated limits me raho aur service interruptions avoid karo.
  • Spot checks vs exhaustive checks: spot checks subset sample karke issues jaldi identify karte hain; exhaustive checks har request evaluate karke comprehensive view dete hain. System ki requirements aur available resources par depend karta hai — dono ka combination balanced strategy deta hai.
  • Breakdown by axes: metrics ko users, releases, prompt/chain versions, prompt/chain types aur time ke hisaab se todkar dekho — performance variations samajhne aur specific issues identify karne me madad milti hai.

Logs aur traces — metrics ne bataya kuch galat hai, logs batate hain kya hua

Metrics aggregated hote hain — system ki events ki information ko time ke saath condense karte hain. Ek jhalak me batate hain ki system kaisa kar raha hai. Par bahut se sawaalon ka jawab metrics nahi de sakte — jaise activity me spike dekhkar "kya ye pehle bhi hua hai?" Logs iska jawab dete hain. Production me debugging process aisa dikhta hai:

  1. Metrics batate hain ki 5 minute pehle kuch galat hua, par kya hua ye nahi batate.
  2. 5 minute pehle ke events ke logs dekhkar figure out karo ki kya hua.
  3. Logs ke errors ko metrics se correlate karo taaki confirm ho ki sahi issue identify kiya hai.
  • Log everything: saari configurations log karo — model API endpoint, model name, sampling settings (temperature, top-p, top-k, stopping condition), prompt template. User query, model ko bheja gaya final prompt, output, intermediate outputs log karo. Tool calls aur tool outputs log karo. Component kab start hua, kab end hua, kab crash hua — ye bhi log karo. Har log piece ko tags aur IDs do taaki pata chale ki log system me kahan se aaya hai.
  • Fast detection ke liye metrics jaldi compute hone chahiye; fast response ke liye logs readily available aur accessible hone chahiye. Logs 15 minute delayed hon to 5 minute pehle hue issue ko track karne ke liye logs ka wait karna padega.
  • Logs bahut jaldi bade ho jate hain — automated log analysis aur log anomaly detection ke bahut se tools AI-powered hain. Manual processing impossible hai, par production data ko roz manually inspect karna useful hai — Shankar et al. (2024) ne paya ki developers ki good/bad outputs ki perception zyada data interact karne par badalti hai, jisse woh prompts rewrite karke achhe responses ki chance badhate hain aur evaluation pipeline update karke bad responses pakadte hain.
  • Traces: logs disjointed events ki series hain; traces related events ko link karke transaction/process ki poori timeline banate hain — har step kaise connect hota hai, start se finish tak. AI application me trace user query bhejne se lekar final response return hone tak ki poori process reveal karta hai — system ne kya actions liye, kaunse documents retrieve kiye, model ko final prompt kya bheja gaya, har step me kitna time laga aur cost kya lagi (agar measurable ho). LangSmith me request trace visualize hoti hai. Ideally har query ko step-by-step trace kar sakna chahiye — query fail ho to exact step pinpoint kar sako jahan galat hua: query incorrectly process hui, retrieved context irrelevant tha, ya model ne galat response generate kiya.

Drift detection — system ke kitne parts badal sakte hain

  • System prompt changes: system prompt prompt template par bana ho aur template update ho jaye; coworker typo fix kar de. Simple logic se catch karna kaafi hai ki application ka system prompt change hua hai.
  • User behavior changes: time ke saath users technology ke hisaab se apna behaviour adapt karte hain — log Google Search par behtar results ke liye queries frame karna seekh gaye, articles ko search me rank karwana seekh gaye, self-driving cars wale areas me log self-driving cars ko bully karke right of way lena seekh gaye. Tumhare users bhi behtar results ke liye apna behaviour badlenge — jaise responses concise banane ke liye instructions likhna seekh jayein, response length dheere-dheere kam ho jaye. Sirf metrics dekhkar root cause obvious nahi hoga — investigation chahiye.
  • Underlying model changes: API se model use kar rahe hon to API unchanged rahe, par underlying model update ho sakta hai. Model providers hamesha updates disclose nahi karte — detect karna tumhara kaam hai. Same API ke alag versions performance par significant impact daal sakte hain — Chen et al. (2023) ne GPT-4 aur GPT-3.5 ke March 2023 vs June 2023 versions me benchmark scores me notable differences dekhe. Voiceflow ne GPT-3.5-turbo-0301 se GPT-3.5-turbo-1106 par switch karne par 10% performance drop report kiya.

AI pipeline orchestration — components ko chain karna

AI application fairly complex ho sakti hai — multiple models, kai databases se data retrieval, tools ki wide range. Orchestrator specify karne me madad karta hai ki alag-alag components end-to-end pipeline banane ke liye ek saath kaise kaam karte hain. Data components ke beech seamlessly flow kare, ye ensure karta hai. High level par orchestrator 2 steps me kaam karta hai:

  • Components definition: orchestrator ko batao ki system kaunse components use karta hai — alag-alag models, retrieval ke liye external data sources, system use kar sakne wale tools. Model gateway model add karna aasan banata hai. Evaluation aur monitoring ke tools bhi bata sakte ho.
  • Chaining: chaining basically function composition hai — alag functions (components) ko combine karna. User query receive karne se lekar task complete karne tak ke steps batate ho. Example steps: (1) raw query process karo, (2) processed query ke hisaab se relevant data retrieve karo, (3) original query + retrieved data combine karke model ke expected format me prompt banao, (4) model prompt ke hisaab se response generate kare, (5) response evaluate karo, (6) response achha ho to user ko return karo, nahi to query ko human operator ko route karo.
  • Orchestrator components ke beech data pass karne ke liye responsible hai. Toolings deni chahiye jo ensure karein ki current step ka output agle step ke expected format me ho. Data flow disrupt ho (component failures ya data mismatch failures) to notify karna chahiye.
  • AI pipeline orchestrator general workflow orchestrator (Airflow, Metaflow) se alag hai.
  • Strict latency requirements wale application ke pipeline design karte waqt jitna possible ho parallel me karo — jaise routing component (query kahan bhejni hai) aur PII removal component ek saath ho sakte hain.
  • Orchestration tools: LangChain, LlamaIndex, Flowise, Langflow, Haystack. Retrieval aur tool use common application patterns hain, isliye bahut se RAG aur agent frameworks bhi orchestration tools hain.
  • Pehle bina orchestrator ke build karo: project shuru karte hi orchestrator par jump karna tempting hai, par pehle application bina orchestrator ke banao. Har external tool additional complexity lata hai. Orchestrator system ke kaam karne ke critical details abstract kar sakta hai, jisse system ko samajhna aur debug karna mushkil ho jata hai.
  • Orchestrators evaluate karte waqt 3 aspects: (1) Integration aur extensibility — kya orchestrator tumhare existing ya future components support karta hai? Llama model use karna ho to check karo ki support hai ya nahi. Har cheez support karna impossible hai, isliye extensibility bhi dekho — specific component support na kare to change karna kitna mushkil hai? (2) Complex pipelines ka support — applications complex hote jayein to branching, parallel processing, error handling jaise advanced features chahiye honge. (3) Ease of use, performance, scalability — intuitive APIs, comprehensive documentation, strong community support learning curve kam karte hain. Hidden API calls karne wale ya latency add karne wale orchestrators avoid karo. Applications, developers aur traffic badhne par scale karne ki ability ensure karo.
Yaad rakho: metrics batate hain ki kuch galat hua, logs batate hain kya hua, traces batate hain kahan hua. MTTD, MTTR aur CFR se observability ki quality naapo — aur evaluation ko monitoring se jodo, taaki bad changes deploy hone se pehle pakde jayein aur monitoring ke issues evaluation me feed hon.
SOURCESource: Huyen, AI Engineering, O'Reilly, Chapter 10 — AI Engineering Architecture and User Feedback
← Previous10.1 · Architecture — 5 Steps→ Next10.3 · User Feedback aur Epilogue
10.3Chapter 10 · AI Engineering Architecture and User Feedback

User Feedback aur Epilogue

User feedback software applications me hamesha 2 tareekon se critical raha hai — application ki performance evaluate karna aur uski development inform karna. AI applications me feedback ka role aur bhi bada hai: feedback proprietary data hai, aur data competitive advantage hai. Is section me conversational feedback extract karna, feedback design karna, aur uski limitations samjhenge — phir book ka epilogue.

Explicit vs implicit feedback

  • Explicit feedback: users feedback ke explicit requests ke jawab me dete hain — thumbs up/thumbs down, upvote/downvote, star rating, ya "Did we solve your problem?" ka yes/no. Explicit feedback fairly standard hai — kisi se poochhne ke tareeke limited hain ki use kuch pasand aaya ya nahi. Isliye explicit feedback behtar samajha jata hai.
  • Implicit feedback: user actions se infer ki gayi information — jaise kisi ne recommended product khareed liya to recommendation achhi thi. Kya implicit feedback mana jaye, ye har application me user kya actions kar sakta hai, us par depend karta hai — application-dependent hai. Foundation models nayi duniya ki applications enable karte hain, aur unke saath implicit feedback ke naye genres bhi.
  • Conversational interface users ke liye feedback dena aasan banata hai — users achhe behaviours encourage kar sakte hain aur errors correct kar sakte hain, waise hi jaise daily dialogues me feedback dete hain. User AI ko directions dene ke liye jo language use karta hai, woh application ki performance aur user ki preference dono ke baare me feedback convey kar sakti hai.
  • Trip planning example: AI Sydney me 3 nights ke liye 3 hotels suggest karta hai — Historic Rocks Boutique Hotel (~$400/night, The Rocks), Stylish Surry Hills House Hotel (~$200/night, Surry Hills), Chill Bondi Beachside Hotel (~$300/night, Bondi Beach). User ka response preference reveal karta hai: "Yes book me the one close to galleries" matlab art me interest; "Is there nothing under $200?" matlab price-conscious preference aur assistant abhi user ko samajh nahi paya.
  • Conversations se feedback 3 kaam me use hota hai: (1) Evaluation — application monitor karne ke metrics derive karo, (2) Development — future models train karo ya unki development guide karo, (3) Personalization — application ko har user ke liye personalize karo.
  • Conversational feedback ChatGPT se pehle bhi active research area tha — RL community late 2010s se natural language feedback se RL algorithms ko seekhane ki koshish kar rahi thi; Amazon Alexa, Spotify voice control, Yahoo! Voice jaise early conversational AI applications me bhi interest tha.

Natural language feedback — messages ki content se signals

Early termination: user response ko beech me terminate kar de — generation halfway rokna, app se exit karna (web/mobile), voice assistant ko stop kehna, ya agent ko hanging chhod dena (agent ke option par respond hi na karna) — likely conversation achhi nahi chal rahi hai.

Error correction: user follow-up "No, …" ya "I meant, …" se shuru kare to model ka response likely off the mark hai. Users requests rephrase karke correct karne ki koshish karte hain — rephrase attempts heuristics ya ML models se detect ho sakte hain. Users specific cheezein bhi point out karte hain jo model ko alag karni chahiye thi — jaise story summarize karne me character confuse ho jaye to user kahe "Bill is the suspect, not the victim" — model ko feedback lekar summary revise karni chahiye.

  • Action-correcting feedback agentic use cases me khaas taur par common hai — user agent ko zyada optional actions ki taraf nudge karta hai: "You should also check XYZ GitHub page", "Check the CEO's X profile".
  • Users model se explicit confirmation bhi maang sakte hain — "Are you sure?", "Check again", "Show me the sources". Iska matlab zaroori nahi ki model galat jawab de raha hai — ho sakta hai answers me woh detail na ho jo user chahta hai, ya model par general distrust ho.
  • Kuch applications users ko model ke responses directly edit karne deti hain — model code generate kare aur user us code ko correct kare to ye bahut strong signal hai ki edited code theek nahi tha. User edits preference data ka valuable source bhi hain — original generated response losing response, edited response winning response — (query, winning response, losing response) format me preference finetuning ke liye use hota hai.

Complaints: users aksar outputs ke baare me complain karte hain bina correct kiye — answer galat, irrelevant, toxic, lengthy, detail ki kami, ya bas bad hai. FITS dataset (Feedback for Interactive Talk & Search, Xu et al., 2022) ko automatically cluster karke 8 feedback groups mile (Yuan et al., 2023):

  • Group 1 (26.54%): apni demand phir se clarify karna. Group 2 (16.20%): complain karna ki bot (1) question ka jawab nahi deta, (2) irrelevant information deta hai, ya (3) user se khud answer dhoondhne ko kehta hai. Group 3 (16.17%): specific search results point out karna jo question ka jawab de sakte hain. Group 4 (15.27%): suggest karna ki bot ko search results use karne chahiye. Group 5 (11.27%): batana ki answer (1) factually incorrect hai ya (2) search results me grounded nahi hai. Group 6 (9.39%): point out karna ki bot ka answer specific/accurate/complete/detailed nahi hai. Group 7 (4.17%): point out karna ki bot apne answers me confident nahi hai aur hamesha "I am not sure" ya "I don't know" se shuru karta hai. Group 8 (0.99%): repetition/rudeness ke baare me complain karna.
  • Bot user ko kaise fail karta hai, ye samajhna use behtar banane ke liye crucial hai — verbose answers pasand nahi to prompt change karke bot ko concise banao; detail ki kami hai to zyada specific hone ko prompt karo.

Sentiment: complaints bina reason bataye general negative sentiments (frustration, disappointment, ridicule) bhi ho sakti hain — jaise "Uggh". Conversations ke dauran user ke sentiments analyze karne se bot ki performance ki insights mil sakti hain. Kuch call centers calls ke dauran users ki awaaz track karte hain — user zor se bolne lage to kuch galat hai; conversation angry shuru hokar happily end ho to issue resolve hua hoga. Model ke responses se bhi feedback infer ho sakta hai — model ka refusal rate important signal hai: "Sorry, I don't know that one" ya "As a language model, I can't do …" kahe to user likely unhappy hai.

Doosre conversational feedback — actions se signals

  • Regeneration: bahut si applications users ko doosra response generate karne deti hain, kabhi alag model se. Regeneration choose karna matlab pehla response se satisfied nahi hain — par ho sakta hai pehla response adequate ho aur user options compare karna chahta ho. Creative requests (image/story generation) me ye khaas taur par common hai. Usage-based billing wale applications me regeneration signals zyada strong hote hain — users idle curiosity ke liye extra paise kharch karke regenerate nahi karenge. Kuch applications regeneration ke baad explicitly poochhti hain ki naya response pehle se behtar hai ya bura — ye better/worse data preference finetuning ke liye use hota hai.
  • Conversation organization: conversations ko delete, rename, share, bookmark karna bhi signals hain. Conversation delete karna pretty strong signal hai ki conversation bad thi — jab tak embarrassing conversation na ho jise user apna trace hatana chahta ho. Rename karna suggest karta hai ki conversation achhi hai par auto-generated title kharab hai.
  • Conversation length: turns per conversation commonly tracked signal hai. Positive hai ya negative, ye application par depend karta hai. AI companions ke liye lambi conversation matlab user conversation enjoy kar raha hai; customer support jaise productivity chatbots ke liye lambi conversation matlab bot users ki issues resolve karne me inefficient hai.
  • Dialogue diversity: conversation length ko dialogue diversity ke saath interpret karo — distinct token ya topic count se measure hoti hai. Conversation lambi ho par bot kuch lines repeat karta rahe to user loop me fasa hua ho sakta hai.
  • Explicit vs implicit trade-off: explicit feedback interpret karna aasan hai, par users se extra effort mangta hai. Bahut se users ye extra kaam nahi karna chahte, isliye explicit feedback sparse ho sakta hai, khaas taur par chhote user base wale applications me. Explicit feedback response biases se bhi suffer karta hai — unhappy users complain karne ke zyada likely hote hain, feedback asal se zyada negative dikhta hai. Implicit feedback zyada abundant hai — kya implicit feedback mana jaye, ye sirf tumhari imagination se limited hai — par noisier hai. Signals interpret karna challenging hai — conversation share karna negative bhi ho sakta hai, positive bhi. Ek friend mostly tab share karta hai jab model ne glaring mistakes ki hon, doosra friend useful conversations coworkers ke saath share karta hai. Users ko study karna important hai taaki samjho ki woh har action kyun karte hain. Zyada signals add karne se intent clarify ho sakta hai — jaise user link share karne ke baad question rephrase kare to likely conversation expectations meet nahi kar payi.

Feedback design — kab aur kaise collect karein

Kab collect karein: feedback user journey ke dauran collect kiya ja sakta hai aur karna chahiye. Users ke paas feedback dene ka option hona chahiye, khaas taur par errors report karne ke liye, jab bhi zaroorat ho. Feedback collection option nonintrusive hona chahiye — user workflow me interfere nahi karna chahiye.

  • Shuruaat me: user ne abhi sign up kiya ho to feedback application ko user ke liye calibrate karne me madad karta hai. Face ID app pehle tumhara face scan karti hai; voice assistant wake words recognize karne ke liye tumse sentence padhne ko kehta hai; language learning app skill level gauge karne ke liye kuch questions poochhti hai. Kuch applications ke liye calibration necessary hai, doosron ke liye initial feedback optional hona chahiye kyunki woh product try karne me friction banata hai. User preference specify na kare to neutral option par fall back karo aur time ke saath calibrate karo.
  • Jab kuch bura ho: model hallucinate kare, legitimate request block kare, compromising image generate kare, ya respond karne me bahut time le to users tumhe notify kar sakein. Options do: response downvote karo, same model se regenerate karo, ya doosre model par switch karo. Users conversational feedback bhi de sakte hain — "You're wrong", "Too cliche", "I want something shorter". Ideally product galti kare tab bhi users apne tasks accomplish kar sakein — model product galat categorize kare to users category edit kar sakein. AI ke saath collaborate karne do; na ho to humans ke saath collaborate karne do. Bahut se customer support bots conversation drag hone ya users frustrated lagne par human agents ko transfer offer karte hain. Inpainting human-AI collaboration ka example hai — image generation me user image ke region select karke prompt se bataye ki use kaise behtar banana hai (DALL-E example) — users ko behtar results milte hain aur developers ko high-quality feedback.
  • Jab model ki confidence low ho: model action ke baare me uncertain ho to user se feedback maangkar confidence badhao. Paper summarize karne ka request ho aur model uncertain ho ki user short high-level summary chahta hai ya detailed section-by-section summary, to model dono summaries side by side output kar sakta hai (maan lo do summaries generate karne se latency nahi badhti) — user choose kare ki kaunsi prefer karta hai. Aise comparative signals preference finetuning ke liye use hote hain. Side-by-side comparison ka production example ChatGPT ke do responses ka comparison hai.
  • Do poore responses side by side dikhana matlab explicit feedback maangna — users ke paas dono padhne ka time na ho ya thoughtful feedback dene ki parwah na ho, to votes noisy ho sakte hain. Google Gemini sirf har response ki shuruaat dikhata hai — user jis response ko padhna chahta hai use click karke expand karta hai. Full ya partial responses side by side dikhane se zyada reliable feedback milta hai, ye unclear hai — events me poochhne par responses conflicted the.
  • Photo organization app example: app automatically photos tag karti hai taaki "Show me all the photos of X" jaise queries ka jawab de sake. Do log same hain ya nahi, is par unsure ho to Google Photos user se feedback maangta hai.
  • Jab kuch achha ho: users thumbs up, favoriting ya sharing se satisfaction express kar sakte hain. Par Apple ki human interface guideline positive aur negative dono feedback maangne ke against warn karti hai — application ko by default achhe results produce karne chahiye; achhe results par feedback maangna users ko impression de sakta hai ki achhe results exceptions hain. Phir bhi bahut log mante hain ki users ke paas amazing cheez par feedback dene ka option hona chahiye — popular AI product ke product manager ne bataya ki positive feedback batata hai ki users ko kaunse features itne pasand hain ki woh enthusiastic feedback dete hain — isse team chhote se high-impact features par concentrate kar sakti hai, bahut se minimal-value features par spread karne ki jagah. Feedback requests ki frequency limit karke clutter/annoyance manage karo — jaise bade user base me ek baar me sirf 1% users ko request dikhao. Users ka percentage jitna chhota, feedback biases ka risk utna bada — par kaafi bade pool se feedback meaningful product insights de sakta hai.

Kaise collect karein: feedback user ke workflow me seamlessly integrate hona chahiye. Feedback dena aasan hona chahiye, bina extra kaam ke. Feedback collection user experience disrupt nahi karni chahiye aur ignore karna aasan hona chahiye. Users ko achha feedback dene ke incentives hone chahiye.

  • Midjourney — good feedback design ka often-cited example: har prompt par 4 images generate karta hai aur options deta hai — (1) kisi image ka unscaled version generate karo, (2) kisi image ki variations generate karo, (3) regenerate karo. Teeno options alag signals dete hain: option 1 aur 2 batate hain ki 4 photos me se kaunsi user ko sabse promising lagi — option 1 strongest positive signal, option 2 weaker positive signal; option 3 signal karta hai ki koi photo kaafi achhi nahi hai. Par users existing photos achhi hone par bhi regenerate kar sakte hain, bas ye dekhne ke liye ki aur kya possible hai.
  • GitHub Copilot: drafts ko final texts se lighter colors me dikhata hai — users Tab key se suggestion accept kar sakte hain ya type karte rehkar ignore kar sakte hain — dono feedback dete hain.
  • Standalone apps ki challenge: ChatGPT aur Claude jaise standalone AI applications users ke daily workflow me integrated nahi hain, isliye high-quality feedback collect karna mushkil hai — GitHub Copilot jaise integrated products ki tarah nahi. Gmail email draft suggest kare to Gmail track kar sakta hai ki draft use hua ya edit hua; ChatGPT se email likhwaya to ChatGPT nahi janta ki generated email asal me bheja gaya ya nahi.
  • Feedback ke saath context chahiye: sirf thumbs up/down product analytics ke liye helpful hai — kitni baar log happy/unhappy hain, ye calculate karne ke liye. Deeper analysis ke liye feedback ke aas-paas ka context chahiye — jaise pichhle 5–10 dialogue turns. Is context se figure out kar sakte ho ki kya galat hua. Par ye context explicit user consent ke bina possible nahi ho sakta, khaas taur par agar context me PII ho. Isi liye kuch products service agreements me terms include karte hain jo unhe analytics aur product improvement ke liye user data access karne dete hain. Aise terms na hon to feedback user data donation flow se jud sakta hai — users se feedback submit karte waqt recent interaction data share karne ke liye checkbox tick karne ko kaha jata hai.
  • Users ko batayo ki feedback kaise use hota hai: feedback se product ko user ke liye personalize karte ho, general usage statistics collect karte ho, ya naya model train karte ho? Users ko motivate karta hai ki woh zyada aur behtar feedback dein. Privacy ki chinta ho to reassure karo ki unka data models train karne ke liye use nahi hoga ya device se bahar nahi jayega (sirf tabhi jab ye sach ho).
  • Users se impossible mat maango: comparative signals collect karte waqt users se do aise options ke beech choose karne ko mat kaho jinhe woh samajhte nahi hain. Author ek baar stump ho gaye jab ChatGPT ne statistical question ke do possible answers me se choose karne ko kaha — "I don't know" ka option hona chahiye tha, kyunki mathematical question ka sahi answer preference ka matter nahi hona chahiye.
  • Icons aur tooltips: options samajhne me madad karein to add karo. Confusing design avoid karo — ambiguous instructions noisy feedback deti hain. Luma feedback form me angry emoji (1-star rating) wahan tha jahan 5-star rating honi chahiye thi — positive reviews wale users ne galti se use pick kar liya, aur negative feedback padhne par author confuse ho gaye jab responses positive the par star ratings 1/5 thi.
  • Feedback private ya public: user ko kuch pasand aaye to kya ye information doosre users ko dikhani hai? Early days me Midjourney ka feedback (image upscale karna, variations generate karna, regenerate karna) public tha. Visibility user behaviour, user experience aur feedback ki quality par profound impact dalti hai. Users private me zyada candid hote hain — judge hone ka chance kam hota hai — isse higher-quality signals milte hain. 2024 me X (Twitter) ne "likes" private kar diye — Elon Musk ne claim kiya ki likes ki sankhya me significant uptick aaya. Par private signals discoverability aur explainability kam karte hain — likes chhupane se users apne connections ke liked tweets nahi dhoondh sakte, aur X unke follow kiye logon ke likes par tweets recommend kare to users confuse ho sakte hain ki certain tweets feed me kyun aaye.

Feedback limitations — biases aur degenerate feedback loops

Feedback free lunch nahi hai — uski apni limitations hain.

  • Leniency bias: log items ko warranted se zyada positively rate karte hain — conflict avoid karne, nice hone, ya easiest option chunne ke liye. Jaldi me ho aur app transaction rate karne ko kahe — transaction se happy nahi ho, par pata hai ki negative rate karne par reasons dene padenge, to positive choose karke kaam khatam kar lo. 5-star scale par 4–5 stars achhe experience ke liye hote hain, par users 5 stars dene ke liye pressured feel karte hain, 4 stars tab dete hain jab kuch galat ho. Uber (2015) me average driver rating 4.8 thi, 4.6 se neeche scores drivers ko deactivation ke risk me daalte the. Bias dealbreaker nahi hai — Uber ka goal achhe drivers ko bure se differentiate karna hai, aur rating system isme madad karta hai. Apne user ratings ka distribution dekho taaki bias detect ho. Zyada granular feedback chahiye to low ratings se judi strong negative connotation hatao — numbers 1–5 dikhane ki jagah options dikhao: "Great ride. Great driver", "Pretty good", "Nothing to complain about but nothing stellar either", "Could've been better", "Don't match me with this driver again".
  • Randomness: users aksar random feedback dete hain — malice se nahi, motivation ki kami se. Do lambe responses side by side dikhao to users dono padhna nahi chahte aur randomly ek par click kar dete hain. Midjourney me bhi users randomly ek image choose karke variations generate kar sakte hain.
  • Position bias: option kis position par present kiya gaya hai, ye uski perception ko influence karta hai — users pehli suggestion par doosri se zyada likely click karte hain. Pehli suggestion par click karne ka matlab zaroori nahi ki woh achhi suggestion hai. Mitigation: suggestions ki positions randomly vary karo, ya model banao jo suggestion ki true success rate uski position ke hisaab se compute kare.
  • Preference bias: side-by-side comparison me log lambe response ko prefer kar sakte hain, bhale woh kam accurate ho — length inaccuracies se aasan dikhti hai. Recency bias: do answers compare karte waqt log aakhri wala answer prefer karte hain. Apne user feedback ko inspect karo taaki biases uncover hon — biases samajhne se feedback ko sahi interpret kar sakoge aur misleading product decisions avoid kar sakoge.
  • Degenerate feedback loop: feedback incomplete hai — feedback sirf us par milta hai jo users ko dikhate ho. User feedback se model ka behaviour modify karne wale system me degenerate feedback loops arise ho sakte hain — predictions khud feedback ko influence karti hain, feedback model ke agle iteration ko influence karta hai, initial biases amplify hote hain. Video recommendation example: upar rank karne wale videos pehle dikhte hain, zyada clicks milte hain, system ka belief reinforce hota hai ki woh best picks hain. Video A aur B me shuru me minor difference ho, par A thoda upar rank hua, zyada clicks mile, system use boost karta raha — time ke saath A ki ranking soar kar gayi, B peeche reh gaya. Ise "exposure bias", "popularity bias" ya "filter bubbles" kehte hain — well-studied problem hai.
  • Degenerate loop product ka focus aur user base badal sakta hai — shuru me kuch users cat photos pasand karne ka feedback dein, system zyada cat photos generate kare, cat lovers attract hon, aur zyada feedback dein ki cat photos achhe hain, system aur zyada cats generate kare — jaldi hi application cat haven ban jati hai. Cat photos example hain, par wahi mechanism racism, sexism, explicit content preference jaise biases bhi amplify kar sakta hai.
  • User feedback par train karne se conversational agent sycophant (chaplus) bhi ban sakta hai — Sharma et al. (2023) ne dikhaya ki human feedback par trained AI models users ko woh dene lagte hain jo users chahte hain, bhale woh sabse accurate ya beneficial na ho — user ke view se match karne wale responses present karne ki tendency badh jati hai.
  • User feedback user experience improve karne ke liye crucial hai, par indiscriminately use karne se biases perpetuate ho sakte hain aur product destroy ho sakta hai. Feedback ko product me incorporate karne se pehle uski limitations aur potential impact samajh lo.

Epilogue — tumne kar dikhaya

Book me 150,000+ words, 160 illustrations, 250 footnotes aur 975 reference links the — aur tumne ise poora padh liya. Seekhne ke liye time nikaal pana ek privilege hai, aur author grateful hain ki tumne apna valuable learning time is book ko diya.

  • Technical writing ka sabse mushkil hissa sahi answers dhoondhna nahi hai, sahi questions poochhna hai. Book likhne se author ko aise questions poochhne ki inspiration mili jo fun aur useful discoveries ki taraf le gaye — ummeed hai book ne tumhare andar bhi interesting questions jagaye honge.
  • Foundation models ke upar pehle se hi incredible applications bane hain, aur ye sankhya future me exponentially badhegi. AI engineering ke zyada systematic approaches — jaise is book me introduce kiye gaye — development process ko aasan banayenge aur aur bhi applications enable karenge.
  • AI engineering me bahut si challenges hain. Sab fun nahi hain, par sab growth aur impact ke opportunities hain. Author se reach out kar sakte ho — X par @chipro, LinkedIn par /in/chiphuyen, ya email huyenchip.com/communication par. Aur resources ke liye book ka GitHub repository hai: github.com/chiphuyen/aie-book.
Yaad rakho: user feedback data flywheel ka fuel hai — par woh biased, noisy aur incomplete hota hai. Feedback design product ki zimmedari samajhkar engineers aksar overlook kar dete the; ab AI engineers khud is process me involve ho rahe hain taaki unhe woh data mile jo models ko continually improve karne ke liye chahiye. Chapter 1 ka idea yahi hai — traditional ML engineering ke mukable AI engineering product ke zyada kareeb aa rahi hai, kyunki data flywheel aur product experience competitive advantages ban gaye hain.
SOURCESource: Huyen, AI Engineering, O'Reilly, Chapter 10 — AI Engineering Architecture and User Feedback

F1Ant me · Interview FAQs
Interview FAQs
AI engineering interviews (current era) ke liye — foundation models se lekar architecture tak, 37 sawaal-jawaab. Har jawaab isi book ke concepts par aadharit hai.
Q01 AI Engineering kya hai — aur ML Engineering se kaise alag hai?
AI Engineering foundation models (LLMs/LMMs) ke upar applications banana hai — prompt engineering, context construction, RAG, agents, parameter-efficient finetuning. ML Engineering traditional ML models par hai — tabular data annotation, feature engineering, model training from scratch. AI Engineering me model training kam, model ko application se jodna zyada hota hai. Dono ek hi system me saath bhi aate hain.
Q02 Foundation model aur LLM me kya farak hai?
LLM sirf language ke liye trained model hai. Foundation model bada term hai — LLMs aur large multimodal models (LMMs) dono ko cover karta hai, jo text ke saath image, audio, video bhi samajhte hain. Foundation model wo base model hai jise alag-alag applications ke liye adapt karte hain.
Q03 AI application banana chahiye ya nahi — ye kaise tay karein?
Use case evaluation se: kya problem real hai? Kya AI se fayda hoga? Kya expectations realistic hain? Kya data available hai? Aur sabse important — kya ye rules se solve nahi ho sakta? Agar rules se ho sakta hai, to AI mat lagao. Milestone planning aur maintenance ka kharcha bhi pehle se socho.
Q04 AI Engineering Stack ki 3 layers kya hain?
Neeche se upar: 1) Infrastructure layer — compute, GPUs, model hosting. 2) Model layer — foundation models, finetuning, evaluation. 3) Application layer — prompts, RAG, agents, user interface. Har layer ke apne trade-offs hain; application developer ko teeno samajhne padte hain, par har layer me expert hona zaroori nahi.
Q05 Training data me kya-kya matter karta hai?
Teen cheezein: quality (saaf, sahi data), coverage (har tarah ke examples), quantity (kaafi examples). Multilingual models ko alag-alag bhashaon ka data chahiye; domain-specific models ko us domain ka data. Data hi model ki capability ki hadd tay karta hai — achha data, achha model.
Q06 Model architecture aur model size ka kya role hai?
Architecture (jaise transformer) batata hai ki model information kaise process karta hai. Size (parameters) capacity batata hai — bada model zyada seekh sakta hai, par train aur run karna mehenga hai. Scaling laws kehte hain ki size, data aur compute saath badhao to performance badhti hai — par diminishing returns bhi hote hain.
Q07 Supervised finetuning (SFT) aur preference finetuning me kya farak hai?
SFT me model ko sahi jawab wale examples dikha kar train karte hain — "ye input, ye output". Preference finetuning (jaise RLHF/DPO) me model ko do outputs me se behtar wala chunna sikhate hain — human preference se. SFT model ko task sikhata hai; preference finetuning uske behavior ko human expectations ke kareeb laata hai.
Q08 Sampling kya hai — temperature, top-p, top-k ka kya matlab hai?
Sampling wo process hai jisse model next token chunta hai. Temperature distribution ko control karta hai — 0 matlab hamesha sabse likely token (greedy), zyada matlab zyada random. Top-k sirf top k tokens me se chunta hai; top-p (nucleus) un tokens me se chunta hai jinki cumulative probability p tak ho. Creative kaam me temperature zyada, factual kaam me kam rakho.
Q09 Test-time compute kya hai?
Inference ke time zyada compute kharch karke behtar jawab paana — jaise chain-of-thought (model ko step-by-step sochne do), self-consistency (kai baar sample karke majority lo), ya tree search. Trade-off: latency aur cost badhti hai, par accuracy bhi badhti hai. Mushkil reasoning tasks me test-time compute training se zyada effective ho sakta hai.
Q10 Structured outputs kyun zaroori hain?
Kyunki applications ko model se JSON ya fixed format chahiye hota hai — free-form text parse karna risky hai. Structured outputs (JSON mode, function calling, constrained decoding) guarantee karte hain ki output valid format me aaye. Bina iske, ek galat bracket bhi poora pipeline tod sakta hai.
Q11 Perplexity kya hai aur isse kya pata chalta hai?
Perplexity language modeling ka basic metric hai — model text ko kitna achhe se predict karta hai, ye naapti hai. Formula: exp(average negative log-likelihood). Kam perplexity = behtar prediction. Par dhyaan rakho: perplexity sirf language modeling ke liye hai — ye nahi batati ki model tumhara task achhe se karega.
Q12 Exact evaluation aur AI as a judge me kya farak hai?
Exact evaluation me jawab ko reference se word-by-word ya rule se milate hain — jaise functional correctness (code chalta hai ya nahi). Ye sirf wahan kaam karta hai jahan ek sahi jawab ho. AI as a judge me ek model dusre model ke output ko score karta hai — open-ended tasks (writing, summaries) ke liye. Judge bhi biased ho sakta hai, isliye human evaluation se cross-check karo.
Q13 AI as a judge ke biases kya hain?
Position bias — pehle dikhaya gaya output jeet jata hai. Verbosity bias — lamba jawab behtar lagta hai. Self-enhancement bias — judge apne jaise outputs ko zyada pasand karta hai. Bachav: position swap karke evaluate karo, length normalize karo, aur multiple judges use karo.
Q14 Evaluation pipeline design karne ke 3 steps kya hain?
Step 1: system ke har component ko alag evaluate karo (retrieval, generation, tools alag-alag). Step 2: evaluation guideline banao — kya achha hai, ye likh kar tay karo. Step 3: evaluation methods aur data define karo — kis metric se, kis data par, kitni baar. Bina guideline ke evaluation subjective ho jata hai.
Q15 Model selection kaise karein — build vs buy?
Pehle criteria tay karo: capability, cost, latency. Phir public benchmarks se shortlist karo, par apne data par khud evaluate karo — public benchmark tumhara use case nahi hai. Build vs buy: agar model tumhara core differentiator hai to build karo; nahi to API use karo. Chhota model bhi kaafi ho sakta hai — bada model hamesha behtar nahi hota.
Q16 Prompt engineering kya hai — aur iske best practices kya hain?
Model se behtar output paane ke liye prompt likhne ki kala. Best practices: clear aur explicit instructions likho; kaafi context do; complex task ko chhote subtasks me todo; model ko sochne ka time do (chain-of-thought); prompts ko iterate karo aur version karo. Prompt ko code ki tarah treat karo — test karo, version karo.
Q17 Zero-shot, few-shot aur chain-of-thought me kya farak hai?
Zero-shot: sirf instruction, koi example nahi — simple tasks ke liye. Few-shot: 2-3 examples ke saath — format ya style sikhane ke liye. Chain-of-thought: model ko step-by-step reasoning karne ko kaho — multi-step math/logic ke liye. CoT se accuracy badhti hai par tokens (cost) bhi badhte hain.
Q18 Context length aur context efficiency kya hai?
Context length wo maximum tokens hai jo model ek baar me dekh sakta hai. Context efficiency ka matlab hai ki us context ko kitne achhe se use kar rahe ho — bekaar context bharna cost badhata hai aur performance gira sakta hai. Relevant context chuno, irrelevant hatao. "Lost in the middle" problem: lambi context me beech ki information model bhool jata hai.
Q19 Prompt injection aur jailbreaking kya hain?
Prompt injection: user input me chhupa hua instruction jo model ko uske system prompt ke against kaam karwata hai — jaise "ignore previous instructions". Jailbreaking: model ke safety guardrails ko tod kar mana hua content nikalwana. Bachav: input validation, output filtering, system prompt ko user input se alag rakhna, aur guardrails lagana.
Q20 RAG kya hai aur ye kyun kaam karta hai?
Retrieval-Augmented Generation: user ke sawal par pehle relevant documents retrieve karo (search), phir unhe model ke context me daal kar jawab generate karo. Ye kaam karta hai kyunki model ko external knowledge milti hai — hallucinations kam hote hain, aur model ko har baar retrain nahi karna padta. RAG ki quality retrieval par tiki hoti hai.
Q21 RAG me retrieval algorithms kaunse hain?
Keyword search (BM25) — exact words match karta hai, fast hai. Semantic search (embeddings) — matlab match karta hai, synonyms pakadta hai. Hybrid — dono ko combine karta hai (aksar sabse behtar). Retrieval optimization: chunking, embedding quality, reranking. Galat retrieval ho to RAG galat jawab dega — garbage in, garbage out.
Q22 Agent kya hai — aur RAG se kaise alag hai?
Agent wo system hai jo khud plan banata hai, tools use karta hai, aur multi-step tasks poore karta hai — jaise research karke report banana. RAG sirf ek step hai (retrieve + generate). Agent me planning, tool use, memory aur evaluation bhi hota hai. Agent = LLM + tools + planning + memory.
Q23 Agent ke failure modes kya hain?
Planning fail ho jana (galat plan), tool galat use karna, context bhool jana, loop me phas jana (wahi kaam dobara), aur error se recover na kar paana. Evaluation: har step ko alag test karo, aur end-to-end bhi. Agent ko hamesha human oversight ke saath deploy karo — poori autonomy risky hai.
Q24 Agent me memory kyun zaroori hai?
Kyunki bina memory ke agent har turn pe sab kuch bhool jata hai. Short-term memory (conversation history) aur long-term memory (past interactions, user preferences) — dono chahiye. Memory se agent context banaye rakhta hai aur behtar decisions leta hai. Par memory me bhi galat ya purani information aa sakti hai — isliye memory ko bhi manage karo.
Q25 Finetuning kab karein aur kab nahi?
Karein jab: model ko specific style/format/behavior chahiye; ya task par base model consistently fail ho raha ho. Nahi karein jab: prompt engineering ya RAG se kaam ho jaye; ya data kam ho (overfitting hoga); ya model ka behavior unpredictable ho jaye. Finetuning mehenga hai — pehle simple solutions try karo.
Q26 PEFT aur LoRA kya hain?
Parameter-Efficient Finetuning: poora model train karne ki jagah sirf chhota sa hissa train karo. LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) sabse popular PEFT hai — model ke weights ko freeze karke sirf chhote low-rank matrices train karte hain. Fayda: memory aur compute bahut kam lagta hai, aur original model safe rehta hai. 7B model ek consumer GPU par finetune ho sakta hai.
Q27 Quantization kya hai aur kab use karein?
Model ke weights ko kam precision me store karna — jaise FP32 (4 bytes) se INT8 (1 byte) ya INT4. Fayda: model chhota hota hai, memory kam lagti hai, inference fast hota hai. Nuksaan: thodi accuracy kam ho sakti hai. Use karo jab: model deploy karna hai aur latency/cost matter karti hai. Training me quantization alag technique hai (QAT) — inference me PTQ common hai.
Q28 Model merging aur multi-task finetuning kya hain?
Model merging: do finetuned models ke weights ko mila kar ek model banana — jaise ek model coding me achha, dusra writing me, dono ko merge karo. Multi-task finetuning: ek model ko kai tasks par ek saath train karna — tasks ek dusre se seekhte hain. Dono se ek hi model kai kaam kar sakta hai, par tasks ke beech interference bhi ho sakta hai.
Q29 Dataset engineering me sabse important kya hai?
Data quality, coverage aur quantity — teeno. Quality: saaf, sahi labels. Coverage: har tarah ke examples (edge cases samet). Quantity: kaafi examples, par quality se zyada quantity kabhi nahi. Data acquisition aur annotation mehenga hai — isliye data synthesis (AI se data banana) aur distillation (bade model se chhote ko sikhana) bhi use hote hain.
Q30 Data synthesis aur model distillation kya hain?
Data synthesis: AI se naya training data banana — jaise bade model se examples generate karwana. Fayda: sasta aur fast; nuksaan: synthetic data me bade model ka bias aa sakta hai. Model distillation: bade teacher model ke outputs se chhote student model ko train karna — chhota model bade jaisa perform kare, par fast aur sasta ho.
Q31 Data deduplication kyun zaroori hai?
Kyunki duplicate data se model wahi examples baar-baar dekh kar unhe yaad kar leta hai (memorization) — evaluation bhi galat ho jata hai agar test data training me aa jaye. Deduplicate karne se training fast hoti hai aur evaluation honest rehti hai. Exact duplicates ke saath near-duplicates bhi hatao (semantic similarity se).
Q32 Inference optimization ke main tareeke kya hain?
Do levels: Model optimization — quantization, pruning, distillation (model ko chhota/fast banana). Inference service optimization — batching, KV-cache, prefix caching, speculative decoding, continuous batching (server ko efficient banana). Pehle measure karo (TTFT, TPOT, throughput), phir bottleneck par optimize karo.
Q33 TTFT aur TPOT kya hain?
TTFT (Time To First Token): request ke baad pehla token aane me kitna time — user ko lagta hai ki system respond kar raha hai. TPOT (Time Per Output Token): har token ke beech ka time — streaming speed. Dono user experience ke liye zaroori hain; TTFT latency, TPOT throughput se juda hai.
Q34 AI Engineering Architecture ke 5 steps kya hain?
Step 1: Context enhance karo (RAG, memory). Step 2: Guardrails lagao (input/output safety). Step 3: Model router aur gateway lagao (request ko sahi model par bhejo). Step 4: Latency kam karo caches se (KV-cache, semantic cache). Step 5: Agent patterns add karo (multi-step tasks). Ye steps ek production AI system ki backbone hain.
Q35 User feedback kaise collect karein aur use karein?
Conversational feedback: user ke follow-up messages, corrections, thumbs up/down se seekho. Feedback design: feedback dena aasan banao (ek click), aur specific banao (kya galat tha?). Limitations: feedback biased ho sakta hai (sirf naraz users dete hain), aur noisy bhi. Feedback ko evaluation data me badlo, phir usse model improve karo — yehi continuous improvement loop hai.
Q36 AI application me monitoring kya-kya dekhna chahiye?
Latency, cost, error rate, aur output quality — chaaro. Monitoring: metrics track karo, alerts lagao (accuracy drop, cost spike). Observability: har request ko trace karo (prompt, retrieved docs, model output) taaki galti ki root cause mil sake. Bina monitoring ke production me kya ho raha hai, ye pata hi nahi chalega.
Q37 Hallucination kya hai aur isse kaise kam karein?
Jab model confident hoke galat information de — jaise aisi reference batana jo exist hi nahi karti. Kam karne ke tareeke: RAG se ground truth do; model ko "pata nahi" kehna sikhao; output ko verify karo (fact-checking, citations); temperature kam rakho factual tasks me. Hallucination poori tarah khatm nahi hoti — isliye critical tasks me human review rakho.
